article_content: The glare of a low-lying sun — a recurring issue for drivers each October — has contributed to an average of 28 road deaths per year since 2010, according to data from the AA. Around 3,900 road users are injured annually due to sun dazzle, with drivers in northwest England most affected, the AA reports. The motoring organization highlighted these figures as sunrise and sunset shift into morning and evening rush hours leading up to the clocks going back on Sunday, October 26. One particularly dangerous stretch is the M4 motorway, which runs in a straight west-east line from south Wales to London, exposing commuters to blinding sun both in the morning and evening. In northwest England, 2.2 people are killed or injured per reported sun-dazzle incident — significantly higher than the national average of 1.4. Yorkshire and Humberside also face elevated risks, with a rate of 1.6. AA President Edmund King warned that vulnerable road users — including joggers, dog walkers, pedestrians, cyclists, and horse riders — are increasingly active during the fading evening light before daylight saving ends. 'All road users must be fully aware of the dangers of twilight driving,' King said. Research based on 2004 UK pedestrian casualty data shows that 10.8% of the 5,566 pedestrians killed or seriously injured were walking or running with their backs to traffic, compared to just 5.9% facing oncoming vehicles. European studies indicate that head-on crashes involving lorries nearly quadruple during twilight conditions. While up to 10% of truck accidents — including rollovers and rear-end collisions — occur at twilight, up to 40% of head-on collisions between cars happen when the sun is low in the sky, often on rural roads.

Kèk 3,900 moun ki itilize voie yo te blese chak ane a rezilta de layèl sou lèn, ak endyen yo nan nòdwès Angleterre ki pi fòman afe, se konsa AA di. Organizasyon otomobilis la te mete an avant chif sa yo pandan levè ak kouche solèy yo te deplase nan peyod yo maten ak swa a pwochen dimanch 26 oktòb. Yon zòn ki pi dangereyòz se M4, otojwenn ki al nan direksyon ouest-est soti nan Suid Uel ak rive nan Londre, ki fè yon fòmasyon pou konduktè yo jwenn lèn fèt maten ak swa. Nan nòdwès Angleterre, 2.2 moun mouri oswa blese pou chak akidan rapòte de layèl sou lèn — anpil plis pase moyenn nasyonal ki se 1.4. Yòrkshir ak Hùmbèsid toujou gen yon taux elève, 1.6. 'Tout moun ki itilize voie yo dwe konnen riske yo nan tan twilaj,' King te di. Etid ki te fèt sou donnè 2004 pou viktim peyizon yo monre ke 10.8% nan 5,566 peyizon ki mouri oswa blese gravman te mache oswa koure ak dos yo tounen anba machin yo, konsa ke se 5.9% ki te fèy sou machin yo. Etid Ewopeyen yo montre ke taux akidan kòlizyon avan-avan ki envolven lòri yo a preske kwa doublé nan kondisyon twilaj. article_content: Treasurer Joe Hockey has pushed back against speculation that he may be replaced by Malcolm Turnbull, stating that the pressure he faces is greater than that of any treasurer in the past 15 years. He emphasized that his ministerial colleagues share responsibility for communicating the budget to the public. Reports from the Daily Telegraph suggest growing support among senior government figures for Turnbull to assume the treasurer role if political support remains stable heading into next year. On Channel Seven’s Sunrise, Hockey acknowledged the difficulty of his role, noting that advocating fiscal discipline often meets resistance—even from colleagues. 'Everyone wants Joe to succeed,' said one anonymous colleague. 'But to say there isn’t a problem is barking mad. The backbench wants Malcolm.' Prime Minister Tony Abbott publicly defended Hockey on Thursday, calling him one of Australia’s greatest treasurers. 'Joe bounces back—and that’s exactly what he’s doing now,' Abbott told ABC’s 7.30. While sources confirm that discussions about a possible cabinet reshuffle have occurred, they stress there is 'no push to get rid of Joe.' One insider added: 'If he has a great summer, he’ll come back a hero.' Hockey’s recent controversies—including being filmed smoking cigars the night before the budget release and likening the $7 GP co-payment to the cost of beer and cigarettes—have fueled public criticism and intensified speculation.

Li te mete ak jwenn kòlèg yo ansanm responsab pou fè konprann bujè a an publik. article_content: A harrowing cellphone video captures a Colorado family’s desperate escape from a wildfire that erupted unexpectedly near their home. In the dim, smoke-choked darkness, a child’s trembling voice asks, 'Daddy? Where’s Mom?' As flames lick the sky, Doug Gulick calmly reassures his son, Kaleb: 'We’re going to make it.' His wife, Kim Olson, who was driving ahead, briefly stopped in panic, fumbling for headlights and questioning whether to flee or turn back — until a neighbor’s car shot past, urging her forward. The fire, now known as the Lower North Fork Fire, began as a controlled burn conducted by the Colorado State Forest Service — but it spiraled out of control, consuming over 4,100 acres, killing two elderly residents, and leaving one person missing. At least 27 homes have been destroyed or damaged. In response, Colorado Governor John Hickenlooper immediately halted all state-managed prescribed burns on public lands and contracted properties until safety protocols can be reviewed. Firefighters continue battling the blaze, having dropped more than 4,100 gallons of retardant, while search teams scour the wreckage for the missing woman. Despite the devastation, Olson says her home still stands, with firefighters now stationed on her driveway, dousing lingering embers. 'We’re still hoping for the best,' she said. The victims, Samuel and Linda Lucas, aged 77 and 76, were found close together — one inside, one outside — their fate raising urgent questions about evacuation timing and warning systems.

article_content: As South Africa celebrates its historic win at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, host nation France is also celebrating a major economic victory. The France 2023 Organising Committee anticipates €40 million in net profits, all of which will be reinvested into rugby through community programs, infrastructure upgrades, and grassroots development across the country. This optimism is well-founded: over 2.5 million tickets were sold for the tournament, priced between €10 and €950. With an estimated 600,000 international visitors, each staying an average of two weeks, the event is projected to inject approximately $1 billion (€940 million) into the French economy. Broadcasting rights have already delivered strong returns. TF1, one of France’s leading media outlets, reported over €350 million in advertising revenue in September — a 9.7% increase largely fueled by the Rugby World Cup. For context, the 2019 Rugby World Cup in Japan set a record with a $2.93 billion (€2.75 billion) economic impact, according to Ernst & Young. Yet rugby still pales in scale compared to football. While the Rugby World Cup ranks among the world’s top 20 sporting events, the FIFA World Cup sits firmly in the top three — generating roughly $7.5 billion for organizers in Qatar 2022, versus an estimated $500 million for World Rugby in 2023. Revenue for the Rugby World Cup comes primarily from broadcasting, followed by sponsorships and ticket/merchandise sales. Broadcast deals cover live matches, highlights, news segments, and social media content — all dependent on global viewership. As Professor Simon Chadwick of Skema Business School notes, while rugby draws hundreds of millions of viewers, football and the Olympics command billions — making them vastly more attractive to sponsors and investors. Rugby union turned professional only in 1995, but its global footprint is expanding. Interest is rising in the United States and even China, where new teams and leagues are emerging. Private equity firms, especially from North America, are beginning to take notice. Given that the U.S. accounts for one-third of global sports revenue, this shift could be transformative. Long-term success hinges on cultivating young fans. As Chadwick explains, early exposure — whether through a first game, team, or player — creates lifelong loyalty. However, today’s children are increasingly introduced to sports through video games. EA’s FIFA franchise, which earned $7.4 billion in 2023, shows how digital platforms shape fandom. Future rugby engagement may depend less on live matches and more on virtual experiences. Even quirky cultural moments matter. Obano, a French giraffe at the zoo, correctly predicted France’s opening match and their game against Namibia. Though playful, such stories draw media attention and boost public interest. With €45 million wagered online during the first three weeks, gambling remains a powerful driver of engagement in Europe. For many, Obano’s ‘predictions’ served as an entry point — and some of those new viewers may become lifelong rugby fans. Today, nearly 9 million people play rugby regularly in over 130 countries. As the sport continues to grow, so too does its commercial appeal. While we can’t predict the future — unless, of course, you’re Obano — the signs point to a brighter, more inclusive, and financially robust era for rugby.

Sikses long tan an depandan sou fòme fan yo jeun. Kòm Chadwick te ekspike, eksposisyon prékòz — ki ta fèt atravè yon premye match, ekip, oswa jwètè — kreye loyauté pou tout lan. Kounye a, preske 9 milyon moun jwe règbi regyèlman an plis pase 130 peyi. Kòm spòt la ap grandi, interè investisè yo toujou ap grandi. Nou pa kapab pwojete avenir an — sa se pa kòm Obano a — men signa yo montre yon avenir ki pi klè, pi inkliziv ak pi fort ekonomikman pou règbi a.

article_content: A WWII-era parachute mine, discovered tangled in a fisherman’s net off the coast of Herne Bay in Kent, was safely detonated by Royal Navy explosive specialists on July 19, 2013. Fisherman Ben Cooper pulled the 70-year-old device from the sea during a routine fishing trip, bringing it two miles toward shore before authorities intervened. With the mine resting in just four meters of water, the Navy’s bomb disposal team from Portsmouth conducted a controlled explosion at approximately 3 p.m., sending a towering column of water more than 80 feet into the air. The Coastguard had established a one-mile safety zone, but officials noted the location was ideal — far from busy shipping routes, eliminating the need for traffic rerouting. This event echoes other recent finds across Britain: in March, two men were seen removing a suspected Cold War bomb from Dorset’s Warbarrow Bay, while in April, a young homeowner in north Wales unearthed a 16-pound artillery shell hidden in his kitchen cupboard. These incidents underscore how remnants of past conflicts continue to surface in everyday life.

Pèchè Ben Cooper te tirè lòt 70 ane a nan mòt la pandan yon tòm pèchaj kouran, epi li te ramène l deu mil nan direksyon kòst la avan otôritè yo te entèvni. Ak minè a an reyèlman kat mèt dèwòt, ekipaj detonnasyon nava yo nan Portsmouth te fè yon eksplòsyon kontwòle a pwen envènman 3 mwa, ki te pwodwi yon kolòn dlo ki monte plis pase 80 pèt nan lè a. Coastguard te kreye yon zòn sekirite yon mil, men ofisye yo te observe ke sitwayen an te idéal — lòt kòs lòt kote vòyaj nava, ki te enkli yon beswen pou chanjman trajè. Evènman sa yo montre koman restes konfli yo te kontinye montre yo nan laj daily.

article_content: On Tuesday, President Barack Obama will deliver his fourth State of the Union address — the 224th such address in U.S. history. However, this will mark only the 80th time a sitting president has given the speech before a joint session of Congress. In earlier eras, presidents typically sent written messages to Congress, which were then read aloud. Obama is the first and only African-American president to address a joint session or joint meeting of Congress. While other Black international leaders — such as Nelson Mandela in 1990 and 1994, and Liberian President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf in 2006 — have spoken before Congress, none held the U.S. presidency. By the numbers: Woodrow Wilson delivered the most speeches before Congress — 26 — while Franklin D. Roosevelt holds the record for most State of the Union addresses overall, with 12. Ten were delivered in person; two were submitted in writing, one of which he broadcast over the radio as a 'fireside chat.' Two U.S. presidents never delivered any form of State of the Union or annual message: William Henry Harrison, who died 31 days after taking office, and James Garfield, who served only 199 days. Radio broadcasts began in 1923 with Calvin Coolidge’s address, though Warren Harding’s 1922 message was the first ever aired — albeit to a tiny audience, including First Lady Florence Harding, who listened from the White House during her recovery. Television debuted with Harry Truman’s 1947 address. Lyndon B. Johnson shifted the speech to prime time on January 4, 1965, to maximize viewership. George W. Bush made history again in 2002 by webcasting the address live online, followed by the first high-definition broadcast in 2004. The only time a State of the Union was postponed was in 1986, when Ronald Reagan delayed his speech following the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster. He instead spoke to the nation from the Oval Office that evening. Bill Clinton’s 2000 address remains the longest on record at 1 hour, 28 minutes, and 49 seconds, per the American Presidency Project. Written messages, like those from Jimmy Carter, William Howard Taft, and Truman, were often lengthy. In contrast, George Washington’s 1790 address was just 833 words and likely lasted under 10 minutes.

Apre kantite yo: Woodrow Wilson te pote plis adres la avèk Konsèy la — 26 — men Franklin D. Roosevelt se ki gen plis adres Etat de Nasyon yo — 12. Dix te pote yo an presans, de te transmete yo an ekri, yon nan yo te difize sou radio tankou yon 'chat devan fèy.' Bush te fè yon histori lòt fwa nan 2002 avèk difizyon live sou entènèt, epi apre sa, difizyon HD premye fwa nan 2004. Se sèl fwa Etat de Nasyon te reta: nan 1986, Ronald Reagan te reta adres li a aprè eksplodyon navet espas Challenger. Li te pote yon adres a nasyon an nan Bòk Ovale a sa nwit-lan. Kontrèman, adres George Washington nan 1790 te sèlman 833 mo, epi li te pataje moun yo anndan 10 minit.

article_content: Brian Cashman, General Manager of the New York Yankees, is enduring intense public scrutiny amid allegations from Louise Neathway, who claims they had an affair, that she became pregnant, and that he pressured her to have an abortion. Cashman denies the relationship but admits to paying her $6,000, stating he was stalked and blackmailed. Neathway, 36, sent Cashman disturbing emails—including an ultrasound image—threatening to expose the alleged pregnancy unless he paid for an abortion. She also falsely claimed to work for MI6 to deter retaliation. These communications, along with hundreds of texts, formed the basis of her arrest on charges of stalking, harassment, and grand larceny. Cashman’s wife, Mary, filed for divorce on January 31, 2012, one day before Neathway’s arrest, citing irreparable damage to their marriage. She is seeking joint custody of their two children, half of their $3.7 million Darien mansion, and permanent alimony. This marks the second alleged affair during their marriage. The Yankees organization has publicly backed Cashman, affirming their full confidence in his leadership. At a press conference at the team’s spring training camp in Tampa, Cashman emphasized his commitment to his job, saying, 'I have a professional life and a personal life—I will continue to do my job to the best of my ability.' Neathway has a long history of harassment dating back to 1988, involving multiple victims across three states. Her ex-husband, Jason Bump, described her as a 'psychopath' and confirmed there is an active protection order against her. Former associates report similar patterns of threats, phone hacking, and false claims of miscarriages or abortions. In a controversial move, Cashman contacted Neathway’s mother and urged her to have her daughter involuntarily committed, citing concerns about her mental health. A psychiatrist consulted during the meeting reportedly agreed Neathway posed a serious risk and advised calling 911. Additionally, Cashman wrote a professional reference letter for Neathway in 2011 on Yankees letterhead, describing her as a 'tireless contributor' with 'respect and admiration' from colleagues—a fact now under scrutiny given the circumstances.

article_content: Throughout my decades at BP — rising from trainee to chief executive — I lived in two worlds. One was visible: the polished image of a corporate titan. The other was hidden: my truth as a gay man. When I lied under oath to shield my private life, those worlds shattered. I lost everything I’d built. Looking back, I wish I’d found the courage to be open while leading BP. I carry that regret daily. That’s why I wrote 'The Glass Closet' and launched GlassCloset.org — to help others avoid the pain I endured. Real inclusion doesn’t happen by accident. It starts at the top. CEOs must treat LGBTQ+ equity not as an HR side project, but as a core leadership responsibility. Measure it. Reward it. Hold leaders accountable. Events like Pride sponsorships or employee networks? Helpful, but not enough. Lasting change demands clear goals, measurable outcomes, and real consequences. True leadership means acting — relentlessly — not just speaking. Hidden lives come at a cost. Employees distracted by fear aren’t performing at their best. As Peter Sands of Standard Chartered said, the unseen toll on productivity and morale is real. When people can be themselves, they thrive — and so does the business. Straight colleagues are the key. They’re the majority, and their everyday actions — like not assuming everyone is straight, or asking about partners without hesitation — send powerful signals. Tiny shifts in language and behavior can mean the world to someone living in silence. Role models matter. I didn’t have one. And because of that, I couldn’t be one for others. Sharing stories — like those on GlassCloset.org — shows people it’s possible to survive, succeed, and stay true. And we can’t stop at our home offices. In 77 countries, being gay is still a crime. But companies like IBM refuse to weaken their inclusion policies anywhere — even in hostile regions. That’s not naive idealism. It’s quiet resistance. It tells governments and employees alike: dignity isn’t negotiable. You don’t have to change the law to change the culture — but you must create spaces where people dare to breathe freely.
translated_content: Pandan lavi mwen nan BP — monte nan rang yo nan tan k ap pase — mwen te viv dan de monn. Yon anpil te vwa: imaj fini yon dirijan korporatif. Lòt la te kache: verite mwen tankou yon gason ki gay. Lè mwen te di yon fòm pa vre pou proteje vid mwen, de monn sa yo te kase. Mwen te pèdi tout sa mwen te konstwi. Konsidere aryè, mwen ta vle te gen kouraj pou mwen te ouvri mwen lè mwen te dirije BP. Mwen akòmanse rezèl sa a jodi a. Se pou sa mwen te ekri 'The Glass Closet' epi mwen te kreye GlassCloset.org — pou aji lòt moun yo evite doule mwen te ressenti. Inklizyon reyèl pa genyen pa fèt. Sa k ap kòmanse an top. Dirijan yo dwe traite ekite LGBTQ+ tankou yon responsabilite lide, pa yon projè sekondè. Mesire li. Rejwadi li. Fè dirijan yo reponsab. Evenman tankou sponsorship Pride oswa rezo enplwaye? Benen, men pa sifiyan. Chanjman durab lekòl gen bezwen objektif klè, rezilta mezire, ak sanksyon reyèl. Dirijans reyèl se fè aksyon — anpil — pa sèlman pale. Viv kache gen yon kout. Enplwaye ki distre pa peyè pa fèt yo nan maksimom. Tankou Peter Sands nan Standard Chartered te di, kout kache sou prodktivite epi mora yo reyèl. Lè moun yo kapab ete yo menm, yo prospere — epi biznis lan tou. Kolèg yo ki pa gay se klé a. Yo se majo rite, ak aksyon yo jounen a — tankou pa presume tout moun se hétéro, oswa mande sou konpani yo sans hesitasyon — pwomèt signifikasyon anpil. Piti chanjman nan lang ak konpòtman yo ka vini anpil pou yon moun ki viv nan silans. Modèl yo enpotan. Mwen pa te gen yon. Epi pandan sa a, mwen pa te kapab gen pou lòt moun. Partaj istwa yo — tankou yo sou GlassCloset.org — montre moun yo se posib pou yo sibvi, reyeni, epi rete fidèl. Epi nou pa dwe kite nou an pati nòt. Dan 77 peyi, ete gay se yon krim. Men kompani tankou IBM refize alèz politik inklizyon yo n’importe kote ki gen yo — menm nan zòn ki difisil. Se pa ideyalis moun pa konprann. Se rezistans silans. Se di gouvenman ak enplwaye yo: dignite a pa negosyab. Ou pa dwe chanje lòt pou chanje kilti — men ou dwe kreye espas kote moun yo kapab poul avèk libète.

article_content: It’s been over eight years since Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, and Rupert Grint first boarded the Hogwarts Express — and since then, their lives have been inseparable from the world of Harry Potter. Now, as the final films wrap up, they’re facing a new reality: life after magic. Radcliffe admits the franchise gave him purpose; without it, he might never have pursued acting as a career. At just 11, he landed the lead role after minor roles in British productions, and today, he’s earned millions per film — but his true passion lies beyond the screen. On Broadway and in London’s West End, he stunned audiences as the troubled Alan Strang in 'Equus,' even stripping bare on stage — a bold move that proved he’s more than just the boy who lived. Meanwhile, Emma Watson has traded her Hogwarts robes for runway lights. With magazine covers from Teen Vogue to Elle and a major campaign for Burberry, the 19-year-old has become a fashion symbol — a surprising pivot from bookish witch to global style icon. Yet, like Hermione, she’s grounded in learning: she plans to begin university in the U.S. this fall. Reflecting on her journey, she wishes she’d relaxed more and enjoyed the ride — but she’s still driven, still curious. Rupert Grint, ever the quiet wildcard, doesn’t have a clear roadmap ahead. ‘I’ve been doing this my whole life,’ he says, sounding both nostalgic and uncertain. Though he started with no experience — even submitting hip-hop lyrics to win Ron Weasley’s role — he’s quietly built a diverse filmography, from family comedies to edgy thrillers. His next project, 'Wild Target,' alongside Emily Blunt, hints at a future full of surprises. Director David Yates notes that 'Half-Blood Prince' mirrors the cast’s own adolescence — blending tender romance with chilling violence. As the characters matured, so did the stories. But perhaps the real magic isn’t in the spells — it’s in the bond between the three leads. Radcliffe says they’ve kept each other humble, reminding one another that the person fans admire on screen isn’t the same as the person behind the curtain. In a world obsessed with celebrity, their friendship has been their anchor.

An 11 an, li te jwenn lòt prinsipal la aprè roler moun ki pi piti yo nan pwodiksyon britanik yo, epi kounye a, li te kouri milyon dola pou chak fim — menm pasyon li vre a se lòt pafè a. Sou Broadway ak an West End Lond, li te fèt moun yo avèk Alan Strang, yon gason ki te malad mental, menm si li te enlèv tout vètman yo sou etaj la — yon aksyon ki te montre li se plis pase timoun ki te viv. Mwenm, Emma Watson te chanje robe Hogwarts yo pou peyis yo. Avèk kouver ti Vogue ak Elle, ak yon kampan maje pou Burberry, timoun 19 an sa a te fèt yon simbòl mod — yon pousè ki san fèy nan ant tif konsèy ak istilis global. Menm jan ak Hermione, li gen yon pousè pou lekti: li te konfime ke li pral kòmanse kolej la nan Etazini aki sa a. Li reflechi sou jwenn lavi li, li ta vle di jwenn yo yo te pèmèt yo pou pi fasil ak pi plezi — men li toujou entèrese, toujou kourajè. Rupert Grint, toujou yon moun ki pa gen plan klè, pa gen okenn ide kisa li pral fè. 'Mwen te fè sa tout lavi mwen an,' li di, genyen yon sèn nóstalji ak incertitud. Menm si li te kòmanse san ekspèryans — menm avèk yon lirik hip-hop pou jwenn lòt Ron Weasley — li te konstwi yon karrièr diversifikè, nan komedi famyal yo ak thriller ki pi enpotan. Fim ki vin aprè li, 'Wild Target,' ak Emily Blunt, montre yon avenir ki ka gen plizyè sèn. Direktè David Yates di ke 'Half-Blood Prince' reflete jwenn timoun yo — melanj tanmòz ak vyolets. Pandan karakter yo te evolye, istwa yo tou. Menm, pèti magi pa se nan magi yo — se nan kònnèksyon an ant twa moun sa yo. Radcliffe di yo te pèmèt yo rete modeste, raple yo ke moun ki admiré yo sou ekràn pa menm moun ki se lèt la. An yon mond ki obseye avèk fama, kònnèksyon yo te ankoraj yo.

article_content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has authorized Israel’s security forces to use 'all necessary measures' to locate three teenage boys who went missing in the West Bank after allegedly being kidnapped. The teens, who were last seen leaving their religious school on Thursday night, have not been heard from since. An extremist group calling itself Dawlat al-Islam — reportedly linked to ISIS — distributed flyers claiming responsibility in Hebron. Israeli intelligence agencies are investigating the claim, though no definitive proof of direct ISIS involvement has been established. In a televised address, Netanyahu stated unequivocally that the abduction was carried out by a terrorist organization and emphasized that the Palestinian Authority bears responsibility for the safety of individuals in areas under its jurisdiction. He urged Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas to do everything possible to help secure the teens’ safe return. Palestinian officials, however, rejected this assertion. Adnan Demeiri, spokesperson for the Palestinian security services, countered that the incident occurred in an area under full Israeli military control, making Israel responsible for security there. One of the missing teens is a U.S. citizen. U.S. officials, including Ambassador Dan Shapiro, have been notified. Secretary of State John Kerry has spoken with Abbas and plans to speak with Netanyahu as well. Israeli soldiers have conducted extensive searches across the West Bank, particularly around Hebron, where a burned-out vehicle linked to the case was discovered and is now under forensic examination. The Shin Bet intelligence agency initially issued a media blackout, but later permitted limited reporting after confirming the American citizenship of one victim. The disappearances come at a fragile moment in regional politics — shortly after the formation of a Palestinian unity government combining Fatah and Hamas. While Israel and the West classify Hamas as a terrorist organization due to its history of violence against civilians, Hamas has long called for the abduction of Israelis, and past incidents have occurred. Despite repeated warnings from Israeli authorities against hitchhiking, the practice remains common. The military says it has thwarted numerous attempted abductions in recent years. Families and communities, especially in the settlements where the teens live, are in deep distress, holding prayer vigils and demanding swift action.

Famè ak kominisite, piti piti nan koloni kote timoun yo rete, yo soufri anpil, yo fè prier pou yo ak demands aksyon rapid.

article_content: In August 2009, Robert Wilson, a 49-year-old taxi driver and devoted caregiver to his wife, who has lived with a lifelong disability since childhood, suffered a devastating spinal injury during a team-building exercise at Clyne Farm Centre in Mayals, Wales. While descending a 10-foot fireman’s pole in wet conditions, he landed awkwardly on his back, fracturing a vertebra. He was airlifted to hospital and underwent major surgery, but the injury permanently impaired his mobility and ability to continue working or providing full-time care. Wilson, who weighed 13.5 stone and described himself as unfit, voiced concerns before the attempt. He remembered the 24-year-old instructor telling him, 'Just give the pole a big hug,' without offering any safety guidance tailored to the slippery surface. The court found no evidence that he released his grip or performed recklessly—claims labeled 'entirely fanciful' by the judge. Mrs Justice Swift delivered a strong verdict in Wilson’s favor, calling him a 'thoroughly genuine and honest individual' and dismissing the instructor as an unconvincing witness. Although the center’s operator, Geoff Haden, argued the course had been safely used by over 300,000 people—including many children—over two decades, the judge held that past safety did not absolve the failure to provide proper instruction for this specific activity. In February 2013, the High Court ordered Haden to pay Wilson £167,514 in compensation. This included £25,000 for pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life, along with funds to cover lost wages and ongoing support needs. Wilson, now a full-time caregiver for his wife and their four-year-old son, continues to live with the consequences of an injury the court determined was entirely preventable.

Lè li te desann sou yon pòl fèy 10 pous nan kondisyon mouye, li te tomè malenwatè sou dòt li, fèn yon vètebra. Li te envoye ak helikoptè a hopital ak te fè yon operasyon mòd, men lesyon sa a te afekte permanentèman mobilite ak kapasite li pou travay ak kare aseptè. Li te sonje instriktris 24 an yo te di l, 'Donne pòl la yon bon embras', san yo te bay okenn direksyon sekirite adaptè pou sol mouye. Kòt la te jwenn pasen yon preuve ke li te lache presyon an oswa fè yon aksyon temèt—klam yo te dekri tankou 'totalman fantsè' pa jij. Jij Mrs Justice Swift te rend yon desizyon fòt pou Wilson, li te dekri l tankou 'yon moun trè veritab ak onesti' ak refize instriktris tankou témoin pa konvainkant. Menm si operatè sentè a, Geoff Haden, te argiman ke kours la te itilize pa plis pase 300,000 moun—konsa yon mòd timoun—pandan de zèk, jij la te deklare ke sikilité antérie a pa eksime defa ilizib pou fè yon instruksyon adikat pou aksivite sa a. Fevriye 2013, Kòt Nivo Enpotan te obligè Haden pou paie Wilson 167,514 £ nan domaj. Sa ki enkli 25,000 £ pou doule, soufrans ak pèd konsèn, ak fònd pou pèd revni ak beswen sòti. Wilson, ki moun kare aseptè pou fèm li ak fèt 4 an an, ap kontinye viv avèk konsekans lesyon sa a, ki te konsidere totalman evitab.

article_content: An Iranian teenage girl, Armita Geravand, who was injured weeks ago on Tehran’s Metro while not wearing a headscarf, has died, state media reported on Saturday. Her death follows more than a month in a coma and comes on the heels of the one-year anniversary of Mahsa Amini’s death — a case that triggered nationwide protests. Geravand’s Oct. 1 injury and subsequent death risk reigniting public outrage, especially as women across Tehran and other cities continue to defy Iran’s mandatory hijab law as an act of protest against the theocratic regime. Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency confirmed Geravand’s death but offered no context regarding the broader unrest tied to hijab enforcement. What occurred in the moments after Geravand boarded the train remains unclear. A friend told Iranian state television that she hit her head on the platform, but the video footage shown — taken outside the train car — was obstructed by a bystander. Moments later, her unconscious body was carried away. State TV did not release any footage from inside the train, despite the fact that most metro cars are equipped with multiple CCTV cameras monitored by security staff. Geravand’s parents appeared on state media, suggesting her injury resulted from a sudden drop in blood pressure, a fall, or possibly both. Activists abroad allege she may have been pushed or attacked for refusing to wear the hijab. They are calling for an independent investigation by the United Nations’ fact-finding mission on Iran, citing the government’s history of pressuring families and broadcasting coerced confessions. The Associated Press has been unable to verify the exact cause of her injuries. The Hengaw Organization for Human Rights, which previously published a photo of Geravand in a coma, reiterated its call for an international probe, accusing the Islamic Republic of systematically concealing the truth. 'Over the past 28 days, the Islamic Republic has attempted to distort the narrative around the death of this teenage girl,' Hengaw claimed. Geravand was injured at the Meydan-E Shohada Metro station in southern Tehran. Rumors about possible assault circulated widely online — details omitted in IRNA’s official report. IRNA stated: 'Due to severe brain damage, the victim remained in a coma and passed away a few minutes ago.' According to her doctors, a sudden drop in blood pressure led to a fall, resulting in brain trauma, prolonged seizures, reduced cerebral oxygenation, and cerebral edema. Geravand’s injury coincides with the return of Iran’s morality police — long linked to Amini’s death — and legislative efforts to impose harsher penalties for violations of the hijab rule. Internationally, her case has drawn renewed criticism of Iran’s treatment of women and its enforcement of compulsory headscarves.
translated_content: Yon timoun fanm Iranyen, Armita Geravand, ki te vannè lèkòl nan mètèy de Teheran, san kafe, te mouri, pou yo te di sa nan medya etatik samedi. article_content: When you hear 'Thanksgiving and apps,' your mind likely jumps to stuffing and cranberry sauce—not smartphone tools. But in late 2011, if there was a task tied to the holiday, someone had probably built an app for it. Thanksgiving isn’t just a meal—it’s a full-on operation: cooking experiments, awkward family dynamics, and the scramble for Black Friday bargains. It’s no wonder people turned to technology for help—even if they’re not rooting for the Detroit Lions (yes, they were better in 2011, but old habits stick). To make your day smoother, here are a few standout apps worth checking out. No need to thank us—just save us a drumstick. And if everything goes sideways—burnt turkey, runaway dogs, or a toddler who painted the dog purple—don’t panic. Apps like OpenTable, UrbanSpoon, or Foodspotting can guide you to a last-minute Chinese buffet or cozy diner instead. Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade app gives you everything you’d want whether you’re in Manhattan or curled up on the couch: participant schedules, historical tidbits, live traffic cams, and even restroom locations for those brave enough to join the crowd. Don’t forget to keep an eye out for Snoopy! For serious cooks, The Professional Chef app—a $49.99 iPad-exclusive tool from the Culinary Institute of America—is packed with video lessons, 750+ images, interactive notes, and over 1,000 recipes. A free chapter is included upon download, with additional chapters available for $2.99 each. Looking for a budget-friendly option? Epicurious is free and just as useful. Need to keep the kids occupied while you’re juggling pots and pans? The free Thanksgiving Coloring Book lets children paint turkeys, pilgrims, and pumpkins with 60 vibrant colors. Shake the device to reset, then save or share their masterpieces via email or social media. Looking for mindless fun? Turkey Plucker is a silly, free game where you swipe to pluck feathers off a cartoon turkey. It’s not deep—but then again, neither is Thanksgiving afternoon after three slices of pie. And for the early-risers and coupon warriors: T.G.I. Black Friday delivers real-time deals from Best Buy, Target, Sears, and more—with alerts, personalized lists, and online shopping options. Because yes, some of us are already thinking about next-day sales while still chewing on stuffing.
translated_content: Kòm ou mande 'Tèkivòs ak aplikasyon', ou pènse sans doute a yon repas, pa yon aplikasyon. Menm jan an, nan fin 2011, si gen yon bagay ki te konèk ak fèt sa a, yon moun te kapab kreye yon aplikasyon pou li. Tèkivòs pa sèlman yon repas—li se yon operasyon ki fèt: eksperyans kokenn, relasyon difisil ak fami ak chache okazyon pou Black Friday. Se pa etranj ke moun yo te fèy sou teknoloji pou yo aji—menm si ou pa ap espere pou Lions de Detroit (wi, yo te pi bon an 2011, men tradisyon yo reziste). Pou fè jounen ou pi fasil, men yon ti lis aplikasyon yo ki vale peye. Pa bezwen merci nou... se yon pati de drumstick pou nou ki bay. Epi si tout bagay pa t al byen—poul brule, chyen Bumpus ki vini, oswa yon timoun ki te warn chen ou vyolet—pa panike. Aplikasyon tankou OpenTable, UrbanSpoon, oswa Foodspotting ka mennen ou nan yon restoran pou yon repas Chine oswa yon lòt opsyon. Aplikasyon Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade ap pèmèt ou konnen tout bagay, ke ou al nan rilèt New York oswa ou fèt sou sofa w: lis paticipan, historik, videyo kamera trafik, ak pozisyon latrin pou sa ki al nan foule. Pa oublie regarde pou Snoopy! Pou kokenn ki enplike, aplikasyon The Professional Chef—$49.99, sèlman pou iPad—kreye pa Culinary Institute of America, li gen videyo instruksyon, 750+ foto, anotasyon interaktif, ak plis pase 1000 rekèt. Yon chapit gratis disponib pou telechaje, ak chapit ki ka achte pou $2.99 chak. Ou vle yon opsyon ki pa chè? Epicurious se gratis epi toujou egzak. Ou bezwen yon bagay pou fè timoun yo okipe pandan ou ap jwe pot ak pan? Aplikasyon Thanksgiving Coloring Book gratis pou timoun yo kolori poul, citrouy, ak pèlgrim yo avèk 60 koulè vif. Sekèl aparèy la pou rese sete, epi anrejistre oswa pètèt travay yo sou mail oswa rezo sosyal. Ou vle yon jwèt ki pa enplike? Turkey Plucker se yon jwèt gratis ou ap swip pou retire plim nan yon poul kouti. Li pa enplike... men se pa enplike nonplis jounen Tèkivòs aprè twa tranche de gatye. Epi pou sa ki leve tôt pou konsom: T.G.I. Black Friday ap afiche okazyon real-time nan Best Buy, Target, Sears, ak lòt, avèk alèt, lis pèsonèl, ak opsyon pou achte an ligne. Paske wi, kèk moun deja pènse sou okazyon lèn an pandan yo ap manje gatye yo.

article_content: Off the coast of Tasmania, Australian divers have captured extraordinary footage of the Pyrostremma spinosum — a rare, glowing, tube-like sea creature nicknamed the 'Unicorn of the Sea'. Stretching up to 30 meters long — roughly the length of two double-decker buses — this organism is made up of thousands of tiny, interconnected animals called zooids, each just a few millimeters in size. Together, these zooids beat in unison to pull seawater through the pyrosome’s hollow body, filtering out plankton for food before expelling the filtered water out the opposite end. Classified as planktonic, pyrosomes drift freely in open ocean waters, rarely coming near shore. That makes sightings like this one — filmed by Michael Baron of the Eaglehawk Dive Centre near the Tasman Peninsula — exceptionally rare. Baron also recorded nearby salps, creatures that look similar but are composed of fewer, much larger individuals and can form dense swarms that serve as vital food for marine life. According to marine biologist Rebecca Helm of Deep Sea News, pyrosomes resemble sci-fi collectives like the Borg from Star Trek or the clone armies of Star Wars — eerie, synchronized, and slightly unsettling. Yet despite their alien appearance, they’re surprisingly fragile. One diver likened touching one to brushing against a feather boa. These gentle giants don’t hunt or chase; they simply float, filter, and glow — a quiet marvel of evolution in the deep blue.
translated_content: Anndan kòt Tasmanie, divè akstralen yo te kapte yon fòmaj ekstraordinè nan Pyrostremma spinosum — yon kriyati mòdèl tièb, ki gen yon fòm tub, ki rele 'Unicòn dè Oseàn'. Li ka poulè 30 mèt long — enviròn longè de bwi ak de lèt la — epi li fèt nan milyèn ti kriyati ki rele zoòid, chak fèt kèk milimèt. Ansèm, zoòid sa yo bat sou yon sèl fason pou tir eau mè a atravè korpi touf pyrosom la, pou filtre plankton yo pou manje, avèk rejete eau ki te filtre a lòt end. Klasifiké kòm planktonik, pyrosom yo dèrèt libman nan oseàn ouvè, rariman ap pwoche kòt. Sa fè yon vèwizyon tankou sa a — fèt pa Michael Baron nan Eaglehawk Dive Centre apre Tasman Peninsula — ekstèmement rari. Baron tou jwenn salp yo, kriyati ki sanble anpil men ki fèt nan moun ki pi gwo, epi ki kapab fòme gwo poul pou sèvi kòm plisman pou fòm mòdèl. Anndan biologis maren Rebecca Helm nan Deep Sea News, pyrosom yo sanble ak kolektif siyens fiks tankou Borg nan Star Trek oswa lòm klòn nan Star Wars — trè etranj, sinkrònizé, ak yon ti piti angoisse. Menm si aparans yo alèn, yo se trè frijil. Yon divè te konpare tanpèt yo ak yon pètèt pèl. Moun gwo sa yo pa chache oswa pousye; yo sèlman dèrèt, filtre, ak lòm — yon mervey ak evolision nan dèpèn oseàn an.

article_content: In a story that blends digital serendipity with old-fashioned determination, 24-year-old Belgian student Victor Van Rossem flew more than 8,000 kilometers to Austin, Texas — all because Facebook suggested he become friends with a man he’d never met. Neal D. Retke, 49, appeared in Van Rossem’s feed with only one shared connection, but something about Retke’s photos — his wild beard, surreal artwork of mythological beasts, and oddball charm — pulled Van Rossem in. When online messages went unanswered, Van Rossem didn’t give up. Instead, he teamed up with his friend Bran Van Bree, packed a camera, and turned their quest into a grassroots mission: handing out posters across Austin, wearing T-shirts that read 'Neal D Retke for President!', and asking strangers if they’d seen him. After a week of searching, a tip led them to a local book signing. There, they finally met the man behind the profile. 'We were nervous,' Van Rossem recalled. 'But he just laughed and said, 'Well, you found me.' It felt like he’d been waiting.' What followed wasn’t just a meeting — it was a three-week friendship filled with laughter, art, and deep conversations. The duo documented everything, and now their short film lives on Vimeo. Van Rossem says Retke isn’t just a Facebook friend anymore — he’s someone he truly considers a friend. And next summer, Retke might even visit Belgium.

Neal D. Retke, 49 an, te parèt nan fèd li avèk sèl yon konnèksyon komèn, men kosèk foton Retke — barb li long, peinti sou kriyatir mitolojik ak karaktè egzantrik li — te fè Van Rossem vin entrige. Lè mesaj digital yo pa reponn, Van Rossem pa abandone. Li te jwenn bèl Bran Van Bree, te pran kamera a, epi te fè yon kampagne lokal: distribiye afich yo sou routh Austin, mete tish ki di 'Neal D Retke pou Prezidan!', epi demann moun ki pase si yo konn li. Aprè yon semèn rekèch, yon tip te mennen yo nan yon sèten siyèn liv. Lè sa a, yo te rejwenn moun ki te dèyè profi a. 'Nou te nèv,' Van Rossem te raple. 'Men li te rire epi di, 'Bon, ou te trove m.' Li te sanse li te atann nou.' Sa ki te swiv pa sèlman yon reyinyon — se te yon tri wèk amitye ki pèmèt rire, art, ak konvèrsasyon pwofond. Dyò ki te fèt yo te dokumente, epi fim kout yo genyen sou Vimeo. Van Rossem di Retke pa sèlman yon amie Facebook an — li se yon moun ki lè l ta gen yon bon amie. Epi lété prochain, Retke ka vini vizite Beljik.

article_content: For decades, the idea that the French are naturally unfaithful has been a cliché — but recent surveys suggest there may be some truth to it. A 2024 study by Ifop, commissioned by the extramarital dating platform Gleeden, reveals that 52% of French men and 33% of French women have admitted to being unfaithful in their relationships. Even more striking, 36% of all French adults say they would consider cheating if they were certain they’d never be discovered. This marks a significant rise from the 1970s, when only 19% of French people reported infidelity — a figure that has more than doubled in five decades. The data also points to specific demographics most prone to cheating: professional men over the age of 50 (66%) and men with left-leaning political views (45%). Yet despite these behaviors, 63% of respondents believe it’s still possible to remain deeply in love with a partner who has been unfaithful. Interestingly, the rise in infidelity is linked to societal changes — more women in the workforce, greater access to private communication through technology, and the normalization of digital flirtation. Adding a layer of political irony, former President François Hollande saw a surge in public approval — jumping from 26% to 31% — after news broke of his relationship with actress Julie Gayet. His then-partner, Valérie Trierweiler, reportedly expressed willingness to forgive him if he formally ended the affair. Meanwhile, reports in France’s Journal du Dimanche claim Hollande and Gayet are deeply committed to each other. These findings align with a 2013 Pew Research Center study, which showed France as one of the least morally outraged nations regarding infidelity. Only 47% of French respondents considered cheating morally wrong — far lower than in the UK (55%), Germany (60%), Spain (64%), Italy (65%), and especially the U.S. (84%). French sociologists suggest this reflects a broader cultural acceptance of emotional complexity and personal freedom in relationships — not necessarily a lack of values, but a different framework for evaluating loyalty.

Etid Ifop ki te fèt pou platform ekstra-mariyal Gleeden montre ke 52% gason Fransè yo ak 33% fanm yo te rekonèt ke yo te fèt nan relasyon yo. Pi enpotan anko, 36% moun Fransè yo di yo ta kapab fèt si yo te sèkire yo pa ta janm detekte. Sa reprezante yon pwogres enpotan pa kote an 1970, se 19% moun Fransè yo ki te deklare yo te fèt — chif sa a te doublé an senk desenn. Donnè yo montre tou ke demografi ki pi probable fèt se: gason profesyonèl ki pi vje pase 50 an (66%) ak gason ki gen vizyon politik gwo gwo (45%). Menm si sa a, 63% respondan yo di se posib pou yo kontinye aimer jwenn moun yo ki te fèt. Interezan an, poulman fèt la se lèkòl chanjman sosyal — plis fanm nan mache travay, akse pi fasil sou teknoloji pou komunikasyon prive ak normalizasyon flirte digital. Ajoute yon elèmènt ironi politik, presidan fransè a eks-Prezidan François Hollande te wè yon poulman nan popilayite li — monte nan 26% pou 31% — aprè nouvo a te piblike sou relasyon li ak aktè Julie Gayet. article_content: Wearing Lycra has long been seen as a fashion faux pas — but for cyclist Tim Burton, not wearing it nearly got him stopped by police. In Keynsham, Somerset, an officer suspected his £500 bicycle had been stolen because he was dressed in jeans and a t-shirt, not cycling gear. Officer PC Keith James of Avon and Somerset Police explained that the absence of Lycra and a helmet made the bike seem too valuable for someone in casual clothes to own. After checking the bike’s serial number and confirming Burton was the rightful owner, the officer let him go. Burton later posted about the incident on Twitter, joking that he’d been pulled over for 'not wearing Lycra.' He noted he was clipped in, wearing clean shoes, and even wondered if he just didn’t look 'hipster enough.' He added that he appreciated the police’s efforts to tackle local bike thefts, which had included multiple shed break-ins. James, himself a cyclist, admitted the situation was unusual but emphasized that protecting property is a priority. Burton concluded the story with good-natured humor: 'Jeans and a tee are so last season.' The article also traces Lycra’s history: invented in 1959 by DuPont chemists and marketed as Spandex, it became synonymous with cycling culture — giving rise to terms like 'MAMIL' (Middle-Aged Man in Lycra) and 'Lycra Louts' for aggressive riders.

article_content: While New York and London never truly rest, much of the world’s internet goes quiet after sunset. New research from the University of Southern California reveals a striking pattern: across large swaths of Africa, Russia, and Australia, online activity surges during the day and nearly vanishes at night—like a living rhythm tied to daylight. In contrast, countries like the United States, the United Kingdom, India, and East Asia stay wired around the clock. To map this phenomenon, researchers sent automated signals—known as 'pings'—to over 3.7 million IP address ranges every 11 minutes over two months. These pings, which detect active devices without accessing data, revealed glowing hotspots of connectivity in urban centers and dim zones in rural or restricted areas. Pink and red areas on the map indicate dense device activity; blue and black suggest minimal or no response. Texas-based expert John Matherly, creator of the Shodan search engine, helped visualize this global footprint. His team found that while most signals targeted routers, personal devices like iPhones and Android phones also occasionally responded. The full mapping process took over 17 hours—five to collect data and twelve to render the visualization. Some regions appear darker than they should. For instance, China’s vast digital presence is largely hidden due to its state-enforced 'Great Firewall,' which blocks external pings. Similarly, many organizations deliberately silence these signals for security reasons. Experts believe nighttime dips in usage may stem from limited infrastructure, reliance on dial-up connections that are turned off overnight, or efforts to save electricity. Understanding these natural patterns isn’t just curious—it’s critical. When networks go dark, it’s hard to tell if it’s a planned pause or a dangerous outage, like those seen after Hurricane Sandy in New York. Professor John Heidemann of USC notes, 'This is among the first studies to link policy and behavior in global internet use. By learning how the network normally sleeps, we can better detect when it’s truly broken.' In a separate but related effort, the privacy service IVPN mapped internet freedom globally using a 2013 Freedom House report. Countries were labeled 'free' (white), 'partly free' (pink), or 'not free' (red) based on censorship, access barriers, and rights violations. China, Iran, and Syria ranked lowest. But while this map sheds light on digital rights, its age limits its current relevance.
translated_content: Menm New York ak London pa janm dòmi, men tout fòs entènèt mondyal la pral fèm epi yo dòmi chak nwit. Rechèch ki fèt pa Universite Southern California montre yon schèm frappant: nan gran pati Afrik, Rousi ak Awstralye, aktivite entènèt monte jodi a epi anfòm nan nwit—tankou yon ritm vivan ki liye ak jou a. Kontrèman, peyi tankou Etazini, Royaume Uni, Inde ak Asya Lòsòl yo kontinye enkonnèk ak tout tan. Pou mape sa a, rechèchè yo te envwaye sinèy automatik—konnen kòm 'pings'—sou plis pase 3.7 milyon blok IP chak 11 minit pandan de mwens. Pings sa yo, ki detekte apereyans sans akse ak dat yo, te revele zòn ki lumiye nan vil yo ak zòn ki fèm nan zòn riral oswa rezon ki restrèn. Zòn kolor pank ak wouj montre yon dènsite eleman enkonnèk elektwonik yo; zòn blan ak nwa montre yon aktivite ki pi piti oswa pa gen okenn repons. Espesyalis teksas John Matherly, kreyatè machin rechèch Shodan, te ede mape sa a. Ekip la te jwenn ke plis pase 90% sinèy yo te envwaye sou routè, men apereyans pèsonèl tankou iPhone ak Android yo te reponn tou. Pwoses total la te pran plis pase 17 è a—5 è pou kole donnè ak 12 pou kreye mape a. Kèk zòn patache yo patache plis pase yo dwe. Pa egzanp, prezenn digita la vòlèman Chine a se maske pa 'Great Firewall' li a, ki bloke pings ekstèn. Anplis, kèk organizasyon yo fèmen sinèy sa yo pou sekirite. Espesyalis yo kroire ke chwaj pwogres la nan nwit la ka rezilta de infrastrakti ki limit, pouvwa dial-up ki fèm nan nwit, oswa enpotans elektrisite. Konesans pou sa a pati se pa sèlman enteresan—li se esansyèl. Lè rezo a fèm, li difisil pou konprann si li se yon pòz pa plan oswa yon defa ki dangere, tankou sa yo te genyen aprè Uragan Sandy nan New York. Profesè John Heidemann nan USC di, 'Sa a se yon nan premye etid ki lye politik ak komòtman nan entènèt mondyal. Lè ou konnen kòman rezo a dòmi, ou kapab rekonèt pi rapid kote li veritabman defèt.' Nan yon lòt efò ki rela, sèvis privase IVPN te mape libète entènèt mondyal la sou baz rapò Freedom House 2013. Peyi yo te klasifye kòm 'lib' (blan), 'pi piti lib' (pank), oswa 'pa lib' (wouj) selon kantite senzòr, bariyè akès ak violasyon dro. Chine, Iràn ak Sirie te klase pi ba. Menm si mape sa a montre libète digita, dat li a limite valè li a pou jounen jodi a.

article_content: It’s almost predictable: within moments of the State of the Union beginning, the president delivers a glowing summary of the nation’s condition. Last year, Barack Obama confidently proclaimed, 'The state of our union is stronger.' But should we really wait for his polished optimism? After all, presidents have a vested interest in painting the brightest picture possible. So instead of waiting, CNN turned to its own reporters, analysts, and political experts to give a clearer, unfiltered snapshot of where America stood as 2014 began. Their take? The economy is inching forward, but wealth gains are concentrated among the top earners. Obama and his team are preparing to rely heavily on executive actions to push through priorities amid congressional gridlock. Meanwhile, Congress might show rare signs of cooperation — not out of unity, but because it’s an election year. The military, despite the end of major wars, is still under financial pressure as Washington shifts toward a leaner, tech-driven force. On the global stage, the U.S. remains active, but doubts linger about whether its influence is waning, even as it deepens ties in Asia and mediates Middle East tensions. Domestically, national security is being reshaped by new threats and public outrage over surveillance disclosures. And as the speech neared, political insiders from both parties offered divergent views on where the country is headed.
translated_content: C’est preski imòtan: nan mounmèn ki piti piti aprè kòmansman discou Etat de l’Unyon, prezidan lan ap fè yon rezime plis souvwa. Lan dènye ane, Barack Obama te deklare ak konfyan: 'Etat de nòt inyon pi for.' Men, eske nou vle vreman attendi optimism lan poli? Aprè tout, prezidan yo gen yon intèrè pou fè yon imaj ki pi bèl posib. Alòs, plis pou attendi, CNN te tounen sou rapòte yo, analis yo ak ekspè politik yo pou bay yon imaj ki pi klè, san filtre, ki montre kote Amerik la te ye lè 2014 te kòmansé. Kisa yo te di? Ekonomi a ap avanse, men pwofit yo se sèlman yo ki gen plis la ki profite. Obama ak ekip la ap prepar pou sèvi ak ordi ekzekitif pou pousye priorit yo nan kontèks blokaj lejislatif. Menm tan sa, Kongres la ka montre yon ti kantite kòoperasyon — pa paske yo se yon sèl, men paske se ane eleksyon an. Armi a, malgre fini gwè yo maje, li toujou sou pression finansye paske Washington ap chaje pou yon arme ki pi lek, ki pi teknolojik. Sou scene mondyal, Etazini a toujou aktif, men gen anpil doub sou si influans li a ap faiblir, menm tan li ap fòtifye lòt lòt yo nan Asya ak mwayennmò a. Domestikman, sekirite nasyonal la ap chanje avèk menas ak nouvo ak reyaksyon publik sou divulgasyon program espionaj yo. Epi lè discou a te pwoche, ekspè politik yo de deu pati yo te bay aviz diferan sou kote peyi a ap ale.

article_content: The Dutch man suspected in the 2005 disappearance of Natalee Holloway has sued the Chilean government for more than $13 million, alleging his human rights were violated when Chile extradited him last year to Peru to face charges related to the death of a Peruvian woman. 'The lawsuit is against the Chilean government for violating Joran van der Sloot's basic human rights,' his Peruvian lawyer, Aldo Cotrina, told In Session. The suit was filed on September 4 with the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights in Washington. 'Maybe they won't accept my analysis in Peru, because they feel this is how things have always been done,' said Cotrina, who is based in New York. 'But I believe there are universal human rights, and we must respect them. We cannot say that because someone is accused of killing a person, their rights can be completely ignored.' Cotrina said van der Sloot’s former attorney, Maximo Altez, contacted him in July 2010 about filing a complaint. The two met the following month to begin researching grounds for the lawsuit, based on claims that van der Sloot’s rights were violated in June 2010, when Chile expelled him to Peru. Cotrina expects to complete next week a similar filing against the Peruvian government. Van der Sloot, 24, faces trial on murder and robbery charges beginning January 6 in Peru. He is accused of killing 21-year-old Stephany Flores in his Lima hotel room in 2009. Police say he stole money and bank cards from her wallet and fled to Chile, where he was arrested days later. The 13-page lawsuit states that no international arrest warrant had been issued against van der Sloot, yet Chilean authorities arrested him anyway. However, documents from Peru’s Ministry of the Interior indicate that Peruvian police had requested his arrest; Interpol offices in both countries and Chile’s Ministry of the Interior were notified. The lawsuit further alleges van der Sloot was not given adequate time to appeal his expulsion — a violation of his rights. Yet correspondence between Chile’s and Peru’s Ministries of the Interior shows both governments believed the expulsion complied with the Southern Common Market (Mercosur) treaty, which permits cross-border cooperation in criminal matters. Documents obtained by In Session on TruTV — a sister network to CNN — show the expulsion order cited a police report dated May 13, 2010. Van der Sloot’s lawyer notes he did not enter Chile until May 31, suggesting a possible clerical error. The lawsuit claims Chilean police denied van der Sloot access to a phone, computer, legal counsel, or a translator — all alleged rights violations. However, Interpol documents obtained by In Session reveal van der Sloot voluntarily gave a statement in English to Chilean police, claiming he and Flores had been attacked in Lima and fled fearing for his life. Van der Sloot was once the prime suspect in the 2005 disappearance of Natalee Holloway, an Alabama teenager who vanished during a graduation trip to Aruba. He was arrested twice but never charged in connection with her case, which remains unsolved. He also faces extradition to the United States. In June 2010, a federal grand jury in Alabama indicted him on charges of wire fraud and extortion after allegations emerged that he attempted to extort $250,000 from Holloway’s mother. Authorities believe he used the $25,000 he received to travel to Peru and attend a poker tournament, where he met Flores.
translated_content: Homme holandè ki soupeze pou disparisyon Natalee Holloway an 2005 te fèt yon plenn kontre gouvernman Chili pou plis pase 13 milyon dola, anplante ke dwa moun li te vyolette lè Chili te ekspòte li an 2010 pou Pèv la pou li fèt jwenn yo pou mouri yon moun Pèvyan. 'Plenn an se kontre gouvernman Chili pou violasyon dwa moun fondamantal yo nan Joran van der Sloot,' avoka Pèvyan li, Aldo Cotrina, te di In Session. Plenn an te depoze 4 septanm 2010 nan Kominisyon Amerikèn an pou Dwa Home nan Washington. 'Poukisa pa gen poum pa aksepte analiz mwen an an Pèv, paske yo panse sa se mod ki te toujou itilize,' te di Cotrina, ki rezide nan New York. 'Menm jan mwen panse yo gen dwa moun universèl yo, epi nou dwe respekte dwa sa yo. Nou pa ka di kote yon moun te akuzé de mouri yon lòt, tout dwa li yo dwe vyolette.' Cotrina te di avoka anpil antye Joran van der Sloot, Maximo Altez, te kontakte li jyè 2010 pou fèt plenn an, epi yo te wè l mwa ki pwochen pou yo kòmanse etidye baz pou plenn an, sou baze akuzasyon yo ke dwa moun van der Sloot te vyolette jyè 2010, lè Chili te ekspòte li an Pèv. Cotrina pral fini yon dokiman ki anndan yon semèn ki pwochen pou li depoze kontra gouvernman Pèv. Van der Sloot, 24 an, ta jwenn yon tiral pou akuzasyon mouri ak vol ki ta dwe kòmanse 6 janvye an Pèv. Li akuzé de mouri Stephany Flores, 21 an, nan chamb li nan Lima an 2009. Pòl la di li te pran lajan ak kard ban ki te nan pòtfe li epi li te fèt Chili, lè li te areste kèk jou pi fò. Plenn ki gen 13 paj an di ke pa te gen mande arest internasyonal pou van der Sloot, men pòl Chili te areste li tout poul. Menm tan, dokiman nan Ministè Pèvyan an pou Entrieyè te montre ke pòl Pèvyan te demann arest li; Ofis Interpol nan Pèv ak Chili epi Ministè Entrieyè Chili te avèse. Plenn an anplante tou ke van der Sloot pa te pèmèt pou yo apel ekspòtasyon li — sa se yon violasyon dwa moun fondamantal yo. Menm tan, korespondans ki te genyen ant Ministè Entrieyè Chili ak Ministè Entrieyè Pèv montre ke ofisyèl yo te panse ekspòtasyon li te legal sou trate Mercosur, ki pèmèt koperasyon internasyonal nan afè kriminel. Dokiman yo te resevwa pa In Session sou TruTV — rezo sèvè a CNN — ki montre ordi ekspòtasyon an te cite rapò pòl daté 13 me 2010. Avoka van der Sloot te obseve ke li pa te al Chili tan 31 me. Plenn an anplante ke pòl Chili pa te pèmèt van der Sloot itilize telefòn, oswa ordinate, oswa avoka, oswa interpretè — tout sa yo se violasyon dwa moun. Menm tan, dokiman Interpol resevwa pa In Session montre ke van der Sloot te donnen yon déklarasyon an angle ak pòl Chili, ki di li ak Flores te atake nan Lima epi li te fèt peyiz la. Van der Sloot te yon sospèk pime nan disparisyon Natalee Holloway, timoun Alabam ki disparèt me 2005 lè li te fèt yon tiyèn nan Aruba. Li te areste de fwa, men pa te janm akuzé nan afè sa a ki pa rezoud. Li toujou te gen yon akuzasyon ekstradisyon pou Etazini. Jyè 2010, yon gran juri federal nan Alabam te akuzé li pou frai elektronik ak ekstorsyon aprè yo te konnen ke li te eseye ekstorsyon 250.000 dola nan mèm Natalee Holloway. Autorite yo panse li te itilize 25.000 dola li te resevwa pou li al Pèv epi paticipe nan yon tournoi pòk, lè li te kenbe Flores.

article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) — Taliban leaders are holding Saudi-brokered talks with the Afghan government to end the country’s bloody conflict — and are severing ties with al-Qaeda, sources close to the historic discussions told CNN. King Abdullah of Saudi Arabia hosted meetings between the Afghan government and the Taliban, according to a source. The Taliban, which has intensified attacks on the U.S.-led coalition since being ousted from power in 2001 for harboring Osama bin Laden’s terrorist network, participated in four days of talks hosted by King Abdullah. These talks — the first of their kind aimed at resolving Afghanistan’s protracted conflict — mark a significant shift in Saudi Arabia’s foreign policy, as it now directly engages with former adversaries while bypassing Pakistan, a key U.S. ally often accused of failing to curb militant activity on its soil. According to the source, fugitive Taliban leader Mullah Mohammed Omar — high on the U.S. military’s most-wanted list — was not present, but his representatives emphasized that he no longer maintains ties with al-Qaeda. While details of this split have never been publicly confirmed before, the claims align with earlier reports from insiders familiar with Omar and the Taliban. This round of talks, said to have taken two years of behind-the-scenes diplomacy to arrange, is viewed as the first step toward a negotiated end to the war. Saudi Arabia’s involvement is driven by rising casualties among coalition troops and escalating violence that has also claimed numerous civilian lives. A Saudi source familiar with the talks confirmed their occurrence and stressed Riyadh’s serious commitment to facilitating dialogue. A second round is scheduled for two months from now. Both the Afghan government and the Taliban believe military victory is unattainable, according to the Saudi source. Saudi officials also fear Iran may exploit U.S. difficulties in Afghanistan, as it has in Iraq. Several Afghan sources say Iranian officials and diplomats, while investing in businesses and education projects, are actively lobbying Afghan politicians. Coalition commanders routinely accuse Iran of arming the Taliban, and Western diplomats privately allege Tehran is undermining U.S. interests in Afghanistan. Saudi sources cite perceived Iranian expansionism as one of their top regional concerns. The talks, held in Mecca from September 24 to 27, included 11 Taliban delegates, two Afghan government officials, a representative of former mujahideen commander and U.S. foe Gulbadin Hekmatyar, and three others. King Abdullah broke his fast during Eid al-Fitr — marking the end of Ramadan — with the 17-member Afghan delegation, a symbolic gesture signaling his dedication to peace. Saudi Arabia was one of only three countries to recognize the Taliban regime in the 1990s, but severed relations after Omar refused to hand over bin Laden. Described as an icebreaker, all parties agreed that dialogue — not war — is the only viable path forward. Further talks are expected in Saudi Arabia, involving this core group and additional stakeholders.
translated_content: LOND, Angleter (CNN) — Dirijè Taliban yo ap fè nègosyasyon broukè pa Saoudi pou fini konfli sanguin nan peyi a — ak yo ap kase tout lajè yo avèk al-Qaeda, sòs ki tou pre nègosyasyon historik sa a te di CNN. Rwa Abdoulah d’Arabie Saoudite te akòmòde mèteng nan ant gouvenman Afganistan ak Taliban, tankou yon sòs te di. Taliban, ki te anplisye atak yo sou koalisyon dirije pa Etazini, aprè yo te ekspulsé yo nan 2001 pou yo te abrite rezo teroristik Osama bin Laden, te paticipe nan kat jou nègosyasyon ki te akòmòde pa Rwa Abdoulah. Nègosyasyon sa yo — premye kounya ki vize rezoud konfli long Afganistan an — markè yon chanjman sinifikan nan politik ekstènèl Arabie Saoudit, ki ap jwenn direkteman ak anmèn yo te envimis yo anvan, tout enpòtan yo ap evite Pakistàn, yon alie klè Etazini ki souvan akuzé pa gen pa fè ase pou kontwole aktivite miltan yo sou teritoa yo. Konsa sòs la di, dirijè Taliban ki fèt Mullah Mohammed Omar — ki sou lis pi renomè yo nan armée Etazini — pa te prezan, men represantan yo te mete a jèn ke li pa gen plis lajè avèk al-Qaeda. Menm si detay koupe sa a pa janm te konfime publikman anvan, kliyè sa yo kòrèl ak rapòt anvan sòs ki konnen bien Mullah Omar ak Taliban. Nègosyasyon sa a, ki te pran de ane nègosyasyon sekre pou li pèmèt, se vwe kòm premie etap pou yon fin negociye nan konfli a. Paticipasyon Arabie Saoudit la te pousè pa kantite mort ki monte nan troup koalisyon an ak vyolets ki pase, ki te tue tou plizyè sivil. Yon sòs Saoudit ki konnen nègosyasyon yo te konfime ke yo te fèt, epi te mete a jèn komitmèn Rijad la pou fasilite dialog. Yon dezyèm roud lan pral fèt dan de mwa. Gouvenman Afganistan ak Taliban yo te konvini ke viktwar militè pa posib, tankou sòs Saoudit la di. Dirijè Saoudit yo tou fèy ke Iràn ka profite de fèbès Etazini nan Afganistan, tankou li fèt nan Irak. Plizyè sòs Afgan ki konnen aktivite Iràn nan Afganistan di ke ofisyal ak diplòmà Iràn, ki investi nan biznis ak edikasyon, ap lobyè politisien nan Kaboul. Komandan koalisyon yo souvan akuzè Iràn d’armi Taliban, ak diplòmà Owest priye sipoze ke Iràn ap travay kontra intèrè Etazini nan Afganistan. Sòs Saoudit yo cite ekspansionis Iràn kòm yon inquietid moun moun yo. Nègosyasyon yo te fèt nan La Mekke, nan 24-27 septanm, ak 11 delegè Taliban, 2 ofisyal gouvenman Afganistan, yon represantan ki te dirijè mujahidin ak ennemi Etazini Gulbadin Hekmatyar, ak 3 lòt. Rwa Abdoulah te brise jeûn li nan fèt Eid al-Fitr — ki endike fin mwa Ramadàn — avèk delegasyon Afgan 17 moun, yon gest simbolik ki montre komitmèn li pou pè. Arabie Saoudit te yon nan tripi sefè ki te rekonèt regime Taliban nan ane 1990, men yo te kase relasyon yo aprè Omar refize remet bin Laden. Deskri yon brèch glas, tout pati yo te aksèpte ke dialog — pa gèr — se sèl solisyon posib pou konfli a. Nègosyasyon lòt yo pral fèt nan Arabie Saoudit, avèk gròp sa a ak lòt.

article_content: Seoul, South Korea (CNN) — Relatives separated since 1953 reunited for the first time on Saturday at a South Korean-built tourism resort in North Korea, despite rising tensions between the two nations. Elderly men in suits and women in traditional Korean silk hanboks sat at numbered tables in a large restaurant. Many burst into tears; some spoke, exchanged photographs, while others simply clutched hands and stared in silence at faces unseen for six decades. The families had been torn apart by the Korean War (1950–1953). In Seoul, scenes from the reunion at Mount Kumgang aired on television in a press room. 'We have held a memorial service for you every year,' said South Korean Yi Jong-sool to his North Korean elder brother, Yi Jong-ryeol, 90. 'I can't believe you are alive.' The oldest South Korean participant, Kim Lye-jong, 96, embraced her North Korean daughter, Woo Jong-hye, 71. Goh Yoon-sob, 81, from North Korea met his son Koh Bae-il, 63, from the South — the two had been separated when the son was just three. They held hands and shared photographs; the son remained speechless as his father spoke. 'Our mother waited for you,' said South Korean Yi Yun to his older brother Yi Hwa-chun, 81. 'But she passed away last year. If only she had lived one more year...' Kang Kyung-won, 79, from North Korea sat across from his younger sister Kang Byong-sun from the South. She dabbed her eyes with a handkerchief, unable to speak. Remarkably, four South Korean soldiers long believed killed in action in North Korea were found alive and reunited with their families. A total of 436 South Koreans, aged 12 to 96, met 97 relatives from the North. However, some planned reunions were canceled; some relatives had died recently, while others were too frail to attend. The three-day event, though deeply emotional, offers little hope for future meetings. The tragedy of divided families stems from the Korean War, during which millions fled as refugees amid violence and political persecution. In the winter of 1950, an estimated 650,000 people fled North Korea after United Nations forces retreated before a surprise Chinese offensive. There is no official phone or mail service between the Koreas, but some families have established covert contact through smuggled cell phones and intermediaries across the China-North Korea border. Around 80,000 South Koreans have registered for reunions, but roughly 40,000 have died or lost hope, according to South Korea’s Ministry of Unification. Numbers in the North remain unknown. The first reunions occurred after the landmark 2000 inter-Korean summit. Since then, 17,100 individuals from 3,500 families have been reunited across 17 events. Seoul has pushed for regular reunions, but North Korea has demanded 500,000 metric tons of rice and 300,000 metric tons of fertilizer for monthly gatherings. The reunions come amid heightened tensions: North Korea denies involvement in the March sinking of the South Korean warship Cheonan, which killed 26 sailors — a claim supported by an international investigation. On the day before the reunions began, North Korean troops fired two shots at a South Korean guard post; Southern forces returned three rounds and have requested an explanation through the United Nations Military Armistice Commission. Yet, the incident did not halt the reunions.
translated_content: Seoul, Kòlèb Avèk (CNN) — Fanmi ki te separe yo nan lane 1953 te reuniti pou premye fwa samedi nan yon stasyon tirisman ki te konstwi pa Kòlèb Sidi nan Kòlèb Nò. Anndan yon restoran enmen, moun vye ki te mete kòt ak koutim nan sil kòlèb tradisyonèl yo te sèt nan tab ki te numèrote. Anpil te kriye; kèk moun te pale, te partaj foto; lòt te sèlman konsève men yo ak wè lavi yo pa te wè pou sis dékenn. Fanmi sa yo te separe yo nan guèr la Kòlèb (1950-1953). A Seoul, imaj yo te afiche sou televizyon nan yon sal pres. 'Nou te fè yon mesè funèb nan ou chak ane,' di Yi Jong-sool, ki sèn Kòlèb Sidi, pou frè li nò, Yi Jong-ryeol, 90 an. 'M pa kroie ou genyen.' Moun ki pi vye nan Kòlèb Sidi, Kim Lye-jong, 96 an, te emrase fi li nò, Woo Jong-hye, 71 an. Goh Yoon-sob, 81 an, nan Kòlèb Nò, te jwenn fi li, Koh Bae-il, 63 an, nan Kòlèb Sidi; yo te separe lè fi a te sèlman trwaz an. Yo te konsève men yo ak partaj foto. Fi a te sèlman pa pale lè pè li te pale. 'Manman nou te atann ou,' di Yi Yun, Kòlèb Sidi, pou frè li plis vye, Yi Hwa-chun, 81 an. 'Menm si li te mouri lan ane ki pase... Si li te rete yon ane depi...' Kang Kyung-won, 79 an, nan Kòlèb Nò, te sèt anfas avèk soe yon, Kang Byong-sun, nan Kòlèb Sidi. Li te netwe lèt li avèk yon mouchoir, pa kapab pale. Gen yon istwa ekstraordinè: kat solèy Kòlèb Sidi ki te kroie yo te mouri nan Kòlèb Nò te viv ak te reuniti avèk fanmi yo. 436 moun Kòlèb Sidi, ki gen ane 12 a 96, te jwenn 97 fanmi nan Kòlèb Nò. Menm jan, kèk reunitis ki te planifi pa te fèt; kèk fanmi te mouri nan dènye jou yo, oswa te tro frib la pou ale. Reunitis sa yo ki pral duré trwaz jou, se yon lètè ki gen plis lachimòs; posibilite pou fanmi sa yo rekontakti anpil fò. Tragedi fanmi separe yo rete nan guèr la Kòlèb, lè divizyon fèy la Kòlèb nan de nasyon te fèt pemanan. Anndan kòmbat yo, milyon moun Kòlèb te fèt refije — oswa te fèt fèt pafèt la, oswa te peche reperesyon politik. An hiv 1950, envesti 650,000 refije te fèt Kòlèb Nò lè Forces Nasyon Unis te retrete devan yon ofensif senpriz Chine. Pa gen telefon oswa post ki direk ant de Kòlèb, men kèk fanmi nan Kòlèb Sidi te reyisi fè kontak sekret avèk fanmi yo nan Kòlèb Nò nan dènye ane, lè frontyè Kòlèb Nò ak Chini te vin pi okipe ak telefòn ilegal yo te pene nan etat izole sa a. Anpil 80,000 moun Kòlèb Sidi te enskri avèk gouvenman yo pou jwenn yon reunitis, men 40,000 moun te mouri oswa te pèdi espwa, selon Ministè Rekonstraksyon Kòlèb Sidi. Nomb nan nò pa konnen. Premye reunitis fanmi yo te fèt aprè yon sommet historik ant de Kòlèb nan 2000. Depi sa, 17,100 moun ki reprezante 3,500 fanmi te reuniti nan 17 okazyon. Seoul te vle fè reunitis sa yo regilyè. Menm jan, nan diskisyon dènye yo, Nò te demande 500,000 metrik ton rezin ak 300,000 metrik ton enpòt pou fè reunitis sa yo mwa. Evenman sa a vini anndan yon tan konsèntrasyon. Nò pa refize tout responsabilite nan koupe bato yo Kòlèb Sidi mwa ki te tue 26 matelot. Seoul, ki baz sou yon envestigasyon entènasyonal, akize Pyongyang pou yon atak torpil. Jan vandredi, jou ki avan reunitis yo te kòmanse, troup Nò te pètè de bal yo nan yon post garde Kòlèb Sidi. Solèy Sidi te retounen tri bal, epi yo te demande yon eksplikasyon atravè Komisyon Milètè Armistis Nasyon Unis. Menm jan, evenman sa a pa te afekte reunitis yo.

article_content: In a series of disturbing incidents between 2012 and 2013, multiple individuals in Texas and New Mexico say they were subjected to deeply invasive medical examinations after being pulled over for minor traffic violations. Each time, a drug-sniffing dog named Leo alerted officers, prompting searches that went far beyond standard procedure. One woman, stopped in El Paso, Texas, says she was stripped, scanned, and subjected to manual internal examinations by medical staff — all without a warrant or her consent. Her attorney, Laura Schaur Ives of the ACLU of New Mexico, confirmed that medical records referred to the procedure as a 'bi-manual' exam, meaning two hands were used to probe her vagina and anus. No drugs were found. Two other men, Timothy Young and David Eckert, experienced nearly identical treatment months apart in Silver City, New Mexico. Both were taken to Gila Regional Medical Center, where they underwent X-rays, CT scans, and digital rectal exams under police orders. Eckert later received a bill for the colonoscopy he never agreed to. In all three cases, the victims resisted the procedures, but their objections were ignored. While Young and Eckert were targeted by local police, the woman was reportedly detained by federal Customs and Border Protection agents. Legal advocates argue these actions violate the Fourth Amendment, as no probable cause existed beyond the unreliable alert of a single dog. The incidents have sparked growing public outcry over the normalization of extreme, degrading searches in the name of drug interdiction.

Chak fwa, yon chien ki kouche dlo narkotik ki rele Leo te alèt polis, ki pousye rann yo anpil pi lwen pase pwosedi standa. Yon fanm, arête nan El Paso, Texas, te di li te enlave, skane ak soumèt a ekzan invazif pa mèdik yo — tout sa san lisan oswa konsantman li. Avoka li, Laura Schaur Ives, ak ACLU Nouvo Meksik, te konfime ke dokiman mèdik yo te dekri pwosedi sa kòm yon 'ekzan bi-manuel,' sa vle di de men yo te pran kòmèt li ak vajin li. Pa gen okenn narkotik trove. De lòt moun, Timothy Young ak David Eckert, te eksperyence menm bagay sa yo nan jounen diferan nan Silver City, Nouvo Meksik. Tout de yo te envwaye nan Gila Regional Medical Center, kote yo te fè X-ray, CT scan ak ekzan digital anal sou ordi polis. Eckert te resevwa yon faktir pou kolonoskopi li pa t konnèt. Nan tout trwè ka sa yo, vitim yo te reziste pwosedi sa yo, men objeksyon yo te ignore. Tandiske Young ak Eckert te konsène pa polis lokal, fanm lan te rapòte te detenn pa agans federèl Customs and Border Protection. Avoka yo te argumente ke aksyon sa yo violè Amanman Nèt, paske pa gen okenn kauz poubèl ki depase alèt in reliyab li nan yon sèl chien. Incident sa yo te debat anpil publik sou normalizasyon ekzan ekstrem ak degradan nan nom d’interdiksyon narkotik.
