article_content: By Harriet Arkell. Published: 03:30 EST, 17 July 2013. Updated: 08:52 EST, 17 July 2013. Royal baby fever may have gripped much of Britain—and indeed the rest of the world—but as one American interviewer discovered, not everyone is swept up in the frenzy. When CNN anchor Christiane Amanpour asked Margaret Rhodes, the Queen’s first cousin and close friend, if she was excited about the baby, her answer took the journalist by surprise. 'Not terribly,' admitted the 88-year-old, hooting with laughter. British sangfroid: The Queen’s first cousin, 88-year-old Margaret Rhodes, says she is 'not terribly' excited about the impending birth of the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge’s baby. 'Heir to the throne? History?' An incredulous Christiane Amanpour reacts to Mrs. Rhodes’ confession. 'Why on earth not?' asked the incredulous Amanpour. Mrs. Rhodes, who grew up with the Queen and was present at the Queen Mother’s deathbed in 2002, sighed: 'Well, you know, everybody has babies. And it’s lovely. But I don’t get wildly excited about it.' 'Heir to the throne?' prompted Amanpour. 'History?' Eventually, possibly to move on to more interesting topics, Mrs. Rhodes conceded: 'Yes, all right. I’m prepared to be excited.' The U.S. TV host asked Mrs. Rhodes—the youngest daughter of the 16th Lord Elphinstone and his wife, Mary Bowes-Lyon, sister of the Queen Mother—what sort of life the baby, third in line to the throne, would have. Mrs. Rhodes said she hoped it would have 'just a jolly, happy, ordinary child’s life,' something she said the royal family managed with then-Princess Elizabeth and Princess Margaret. She added: 'The king and queen in those days made an enormous effort to keep childhood sacrosanct. It was just a time for learning and enjoying. And I think they’ve succeeded awfully well.' Mrs. Rhodes, who lived at Windsor Castle and Buckingham Palace during World War II while working for MI6, staunchly defended the Queen over criticism about her response to Princess Diana’s death in 1997, choosing to stay at Balmoral rather than return to London. She said: 'I think it was an eminently sensible decision personally, because what was the point? We had two grieving children—William and Harry—whose mother had just died unexpectedly. To go to London and sit in Buckingham Palace with nothing to do except think about your mother or watch the crowds… what help was that for the boys?' Asked whether she spoke to the monarch about the aftermath, the mother of four replied: 'No. No. And I’ve never talked to her about it. There are some things one simply keeps private.' Margaret Elphinstone married writer Denys Gravenor Rhodes in 1950—Princess Margaret was bridesmaid. Mrs. Rhodes, who lives in the Garden House in Windsor Great Park, gifted to her by the Queen 32 years ago, said the Queen often visits for a drink after chapel services. 'She quite often does. She comes in after prayers for half an hour and just has a nice little drink and a chat.' She also recalled how her cousin fell in love with her 'incredibly good-looking' future husband at age 13, while he was 17: 'I think, in the way 13-year-olds do, she fell in love with a very, very handsome young man.' Mrs. Rhodes was a bridesmaid at their 1947 wedding, three years before her own. She admits that when she learned her aunt and uncle would become Queen and King, her reaction was far from dignified: 'I can remember to this day that I shamefully hopped around the dance floor, saying, 'My uncle’s now king!' It was a very shameful thing to do—but I did it.' After her husband’s death, Mrs. Rhodes became Woman of the Bedchamber to the Queen Mother—a role she held until the latter’s passing. She told Amanpour she wept watching 'The King’s Speech,' about her uncle, King George VI: 'I cried—it was so well done. It showed the difficulties he overcame. There was one moment where the actor made the king say a string of frightfully rude words…' 'I mentioned that to the Queen, and she said she’d never heard her father use bad language. Whether that’s true, I don’t know.' Row upon row of ladders mark each photographer’s spot outside the Lindo Wing of St Mary’s Hospital, Paddington, where the royal baby is due. Journalists are cursing the hot sun as they endure soaring temperatures in the press pen. Mrs. Rhodes, whose autobiography 'The Final Curtsey' details how she ensured the Queen Mother never ran out of gin, Dubonnet, champagne, or chocolate eclairs, praised the Duchess of Cambridge: 'She’s doing very, very well. I think she has a way about her that will be very appealing. And I think she won’t vie for coverage the way Diana perhaps did a little.' After two weeks waiting outside St Mary’s Hospital, journalists are running out of ways to pass the time. They secured their spots two weeks ago and now spend hours under the sun. American NBC anchor Natalie Morales, 41 and mother of two boys who competes in triathlons in her spare time, has taken to knitting pale blue booties for the baby. If she waits longer, she’ll knit a pink pair too.

Fèvèt bebe rwayal la ka pran tout Angleter, epi menm mond lan, men tankou yon jounalis amerikèn te dekouvri, pa tout moun nan fèvèt antizipasyon an. Kòm Christiane Amanpour, ankor CNN, te pozé yon lòt sa a Margaret Rhodes, kousin premye a reine ak zanmi li, si li te eksite pou bebe a, repons li te fè jounalis lan sòti. 'Pa trè,' te admèt 88-an an, te ri anpil. Sangfroid britanik: Kousin premye reine a, 88-an Margaret Rhodes, di li 'pa trè' eksite avèk naissance iminenn bebe Duk ak Dches de Cambridge. 'Eri a tron? Madam Rhodes, ki te grandi avèk reine a epi te prezan nan lit mòt reine mè a an 2002, te soupli: 'Bon, ou konnen, tout moun gen bebe. E se joli. Men m pa eksite anpil pou sa.' Kòm li te demann si li te pale avek monark la sou konsekans yo, mè nan kat timoun yo te reponn: 'Non. Non. E m pa janm pale avèk li sou sa. Gen bagay ki gen pou reste prive.' Madam Rhodes, ki rezide nan Kay Jardin nan Windsor Great Park, ki te done a li pa reine a 32 an avan, di reine a souvan vini pou yon vèt apre leviyèn. 'Li souvan fè sa. Li vini apre priyer pou yon demi-èt ak sèlman bezwen yon vèt ti ak palèt.' Li toujou raple kòm kousin li te tomè lavi a avèk mari li 'trè bèl' a l’age 13 an, lè li te 17: 'M panse, kòm 13-an yo fè, li te tomè lavi a avèk yon jenn gason trè, trè bèl.' Madam Rhodes te tèm wèt nan maje li an 1947, twa an avan maje li. Li admet ke lè li te entan ke tante ak onk li ta dwe vin reine ak roi, reaksyon li te pa tèt: 'M kapab souvenn jodi a ke m te koumanse danse nan solèy la, di, 'Mon onk se rey a!'' Sa te yon bagay trè koumanmen pou fè, men m te fè sa.' Aprè mòt mari li, Madam Rhodes te vin Femme de Chambre a reine mè a—fonksyon li te kontinye jiska mòt li. Li te di Amanpour li te plede lè li te regarde fim 'The King’s Speech,' sou onk li, Roi George VI: 'M te plede, se te fèt anpil. E m panse li te montre difikilte yo te depase. Te gen yon moman kote li te fè rey la di yon long lis mot trè malèt…' 'M te pale avèk reine a sou sa, e li te di li pa janm entan papa li itilize langaj malèt. Ki jan sa a ta vre, m pa konnen.' Lign lavi yo mark chak posisyon fotografer yo dehors Wing Lindo nan Sank Mari, Paddington, kote bebe rwayal la dwe naitre. Jounalis yo maudisèn chalè a lè yo aperèt nan températir yo elèv nan kabin pres. Madam Rhodes, ki te ekri memoir 'The Final Curtsey' kote li te detaye kòm li te sèten reine mè a pa janm manke gin, Dubonnet, champan, oswa eclairs chokolat, te aplawis Dches de Cambridge: 'Li fè travay anpil, anpil. M panse li gen yon mannyè ki ta dwe trè atraktif. E m panse li pa ta kourè pou pres ki Diana te fè yon ti jan.' Aprè de zèn anpatèman dehors Hospital Sank Mari, jounalis yo fin manke ide pou okipe timoun yo. Yo te pran posisyon yo de zèn avan, epi kounye a pa gen anyen pou fè sa yo se sèlman aperèt nan solèy la. Ankor NBC amerikèn Natalie Morales, 41 an, mè nan de timoun ki konpete nan triatlon nan lòt tan li, te kòmanse trakèt pou fè yon pètèt ble pale pou bebe a. Si li dwe aperèt pi fò, li ta kapab trakèt yon pètèt rose tou.

article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) — A number of atheist and non-religious organizations are urging that Barack Obama’s inauguration ceremony exclude all references to God and religion. President-elect Barack Obama is expected to use the Bible that Abraham Lincoln used during his own inauguration. In a lawsuit filed Tuesday in Washington, the plaintiffs demand that the phrase 'so help me God' be omitted from the end of the presidential oath of office. They also object to planned invocations and benedictions by ministers that may reference God or religion. An advance copy of the lawsuit was posted online by Michael Newdow, a California physician and attorney who previously filed unsuccessful lawsuits over religious elements in the 2001 and 2005 inaugurations. Joining Newdow in this lawsuit are groups advocating for religious freedom and atheism, including the American Humanist Association, the Freedom from Religion Foundation, and atheist organizations from Minnesota, Seattle, and Florida. The lawsuit states: 'There can be no legitimate purpose for including 'so help me God' in the oath or sponsoring prayers to God other than promoting the belief that God exists.' Newdow argues that religious references during the inauguration violate the Constitution’s Establishment Clause. Plaintiffs, identifying as atheists, say being forced to witness religious content during the ceremony makes them feel excluded and stigmatized. 'Plaintiffs are placed in the untenable position of choosing between not watching the presidential inauguration or endorsing religious views they reject,' the filing reads. Named defendants include Chief Justice John Roberts, who is expected to administer the oath; the Presidential Inauguration Committee; the Joint Congressional Committee on Inauguration Ceremonies and its chair, Senator Dianne Feinstein of California; the Armed Forces Inaugural Committee and its commander, Major General Richard Rowe Jr.; and the two scheduled clergy: Reverend Rick Warren and Reverend Joseph Lowery. The lawsuit includes a quote from Warren: 'I could not vote for an atheist because an atheist says, 'I don't need God.' Newdow explained that he did not name President-elect Obama as a defendant because, while serving in a governmental capacity, Obama also holds personal constitutional rights to express religious beliefs. 'If he chooses to ask for God’s help, I’m not going to challenge him,' Newdow said. 'I think it’s unwise, but it’s his right.' Newdow added that as a member of a racial minority, Obama should understand the perspective of atheists, who are also a minority group. He contends that religious language in public ceremonies sends a message that non-believers are less legitimate: 'The message is, we who believe in God are the righteous, the real Americans.' Newdow acknowledges his suit is unlikely to succeed but hopes it will lay groundwork for future change through appeals and public discourse.

Newdow pran pozisyon ke referans relijye yo nan seremoni inisiasyon violè klaz Establishmàn Konstitisyonèl Etazini. Nòm yo nan plen an se Jistis Kèf John Roberts, ki pral jwe juremèn nouvo prezidan; Komite Inisiasyon Prezidansyèl; Komite Kominèl Konjònt pou Seremoni Inisiasyon ak prezan li, Sènatris Dianne Feinstein nan Kaliforni; Komite Inisiasyon Arme ak komandan li, Majò Jenèral Richard Rowe Jr.; ak de ministrè yo ki pral paticipe: Revènd Rick Warren ak Revènd Joseph Lowery. Newdow te ekspike ke li pa mete Barack Obama nan plen an paske, menm si li a yon fonksyonèl gouvernman, Obama gen dwa konstitisyonèl pou eksprese kroir relijye li. 'Si li chwazi pou demann aji Bondye, m pa pral defi li,' Newdow te di. 'M panse se pa enfòm, men se dwa li.' Newdow te ajoute ke, kòm yon moun ki paticipe nan yon minòrite rasial, Obama dwe konprann perspektiv athis yo, ki tou jis minòrite. Newdow rekonèt ke plen li pa t ap reyisi, men li espere li ta kapab kreye baz pou chanjman an lavi long pase a travay apel ak diskours publik.

article_content: England Rugby has unveiled its new match kits ahead of the 2014 autumn internationals, with the home jersey making its debut when England hosts the All Blacks at Twickenham on November 8. For the first time in history, the iconic red rose emblem is centered on the chest, positioned directly above the title sponsor, O2. Two versions of the jersey are available: the premium 'Test' edition priced at £90 and the more accessible 'Pro' version at £55. While the traditional all-white home kit remains largely unchanged aside from the repositioned rose and a new chest grip designed to improve ball control, the alternate 'Scarlet' kit introduces a bold departure. It features a deep crimson shirt paired with navy blue shorts, incorporating the St George’s Cross as a nod to English heritage. This kit will be worn for the first time against Samoa on November 22. Head coach Stuart Lancaster described the jersey as a powerful symbol of pride — representing not only the players but also the generations of supporters, former internationals, and the broader English rugby community. 'It’s a special moment when players receive the shirt,' he said. 'It connects them to everything that makes English rugby meaningful.' The core values of England Rugby — Teamwork, Respect, Enjoyment, Discipline, and Sportsmanship — are subtly embroidered on the inside back of both jerseys. Canterbury ambassador and England second row Geoff Parling echoed this sentiment, calling the red rose 'magical and unique' — a mark of honor for both players and fans alike. The first test of the new kits will come against New Zealand, captained by Chris Robshaw, in the opening QBE International.

Pou premye fwa an histry, embleman roz rouj la te deplase sou mwayen chòz la, anndan sou sponsor titil la, O2. article_content: In 2009, Kajus Scuka, a Czech man with a violent past including murder and sexual violence, slipped into the UK unnoticed. Despite serving over 11 years in prison for killing his wife and assaulting other women — including with an axe — he was never flagged by British authorities. By the time police finally caught him in 2023, he had already attacked four women across Sheffield, culminating in a terrifying knifepoint rape. One victim described how he shoved her into a ditch, threatened her with a blade, and raped her — only fleeing when her dog leapt onto him. Another was assaulted while pushing her toddler in a stroller; another was offered £30 before being thrown to the ground. His DNA and the hoodie he wore during the final attack were found on his victims, yet police had to search international databases because his record didn’t appear in UK systems. Judge Peter Kelson condemned the failure: 'Even with your convictions for murder and assault, you moved as freely as any other European citizen.' The truth? The UK depends entirely on other EU nations to voluntarily report criminal histories. Czech officials never did. Meanwhile, non-EU travelers must declare past crimes to get a visa — but Scuka, like many others from within the bloc, faced zero scrutiny. His case joins others like Lithuanian child rapist Victor Akulic and Latvian axe murderer Intars Pless — all allowed entry because the system assumes trust over verification. Now, pressure is mounting for the UK to overhaul its border checks and stop treating EU criminals as invisible.

Yon viktim te dekri kòman li te pousye li nan yon diti, te amenace li avèk yon koutè, ak vwo l — se lè chen li te sòti sou tèt li epi li te fèt. ADN ak kapo li te wèt nan atak final la te jwenn sou viktim yo, men polis la te dwe chache baz donnè international paske pasé li pa te parèt nan baz britanik la. Jij Peter Kelson te kondenn defa: 'Meme avèk konviksyon ou pou moud ak vyo, ou te mache tankou n importe kote lòt syèlèpèn yo.' Vre a? article_content: PLANO, Texas — A small single-engine plane crashed and burst into flames Tuesday evening on the edge of a strip mall in Plano, Texas, killing the pilot and igniting a nearby parked car — but no one on the ground was injured, authorities said. The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed the aircraft was a Mooney M20, carrying only the pilot, when it went down around 6 p.m., just north of Air Park-Dallas Airport. On-site photos revealed the wreckage lodged in a parking spot adjacent to a nail salon and diner outside the shopping center. Although the force of the crash set the car ablaze, officials confirmed no one was inside at the time. Police verified the pilot died at the scene. The cause of the crash remains under investigation, and it is not yet clear whether the plane was attempting to take off or land at the small suburban airport, which features a single runway.

article_content: Christopher Taylor, a 21-year-old chemistry student and passionate tennis player at the University of Bath, tragically lost his life in the River Avon in the early hours of January 23. Officers responded after he was seen in the water around 4:10 a.m., attempting to reach him — but he was pulled under before they could help. Despite a swift search involving trained divers, his body was recovered several hours later. Just weeks before his death, Taylor had shared an upbeat Facebook post celebrating what he called the 'best year ever' with his girlfriend, Jessica Palmer. In it, he wrote, 'Well, that’s 2013 done and dusted... and as gay as it sounds, I’ve had the best year ever with my Jessica Palmer... I love you.' He also posted photos of them in tuxedos beside a Christmas tree and enjoying a weekend in Bristol. Taylor’s family from Southport, Lancashire, remembered him as a radiant soul who brought joy everywhere he went. 'He was a wonderful son and brother,' they said. 'His death has left us completely devastated.' His passing marks the fourth river-related fatality in Bath in recent years, following the deaths of fellow University of Bath student Kharunigan Jayanatham, Bath Spa University student James Bubear, and graphic designer Casper Flagg. In response, authorities installed an 850-yard safety fence along a stretch of the river — a measure recommended after previous tragedies. An inquest into Taylor’s death is scheduled.

'Mòt la te fè nou tout detruit.' Mòt la reprezante katmyèm mòt liy dlo nan Bath nan dènye ane yo, aprè mòt yon lòt etidyan Universite Bath, Kharunigan Jayanatham, etidyan Bath Spa University, James Bubear, ak yon grafisien, Casper Flagg. Pou reyajisye sa, autorite yo te monte yon klad 850 yard nan yon pati long rivyè a — yon mesi ki te rekomande aprè lòt traji. Yon enketis pral fèt pou mòt Taylor la.

article_content: NEW YORK — A jury has awarded Graham Chase Robinson, former personal assistant to actor Robert De Niro, a total of $1,264,284 after finding his production company, Canal Productions, guilty of gender discrimination and retaliation. Although De Niro himself was not held personally liable, the jury determined that his company fostered a hostile work environment that led Robinson to resign in April 2019. The award consists of two payments of $632,142 each. Robinson, 41, testified that she endured emotional abuse and manipulation from De Niro and his then-girlfriend, Tiffany Chen. Emails introduced in court revealed Chen expressing jealousy, writing that she believed Robinson had an 'imaginary intimacy' with De Niro and wished she were his wife. Robinson firmly denied any romantic involvement with De Niro. De Niro, 80, countered that he had elevated Robinson’s role and salary—from under $100,000 to $300,000 annually—and granted her the title of Vice President of Production and Finance, despite her responsibilities remaining largely unchanged. He accused her of misappropriating approximately $85,000 worth of airline miles and violating unwritten workplace norms. He admitted to occasionally raising his voice but denied being abusive or using profanity, stating, 'I was never abusive, ever.' During his testimony, De Niro turned to Robinson in court and shouted, 'Shame on you, Chase Robinson!'—a moment that drew strong reactions. Robinson, who has struggled with anxiety and depression since leaving her job, said she has not worked in four years despite applying for 638 positions. 'I lost my life. Lost my career. Lost my financial independence. I lost everything,' she said. De Niro’s legal team had filed a countersuit seeking $6 million in damages for breach of loyalty, but the jury rejected those claims outright. Attorneys for both sides declared victory: Robinson’s lawyer called the verdict 'thrilling,' while De Niro’s counsel emphasized that his client was fully absolved of personal liability. De Niro was not present in court when the verdict was announced.

Menm si De Niro pa te konsidere koupable pèsonèlman, juri te truve ke kompani l te kreye yon endiriman travay ki te pouse Robinson nan rezilasyon avrèl 2019. Akòrd la gen de paiman $632,142 chak. E-mail yo ki te prezante nan kòt te montre Chen ki eksprese jalousi, ki te ekri ke li te kroire Robinson te gen yon 'intimite imajinè' avek De Niro epi li te vle ete fèm li. Robinson te refize tout relasyon romantik avek De Niro. article_content: On November 15, 2022, academic workers and supporters marched and picketed at UCLA amid a statewide strike by nearly 48,000 University of California union members—making it one of the largest labor actions in U.S. higher education history. The strike, organized by the United Auto Workers (UAW), was part of a broader trend: today, roughly 100,000 of the UAW’s 383,000 members work in academia, including graduate students, postdocs, adjunct professors, and clerical staff. This expansion reflects a strategic shift for the union, once dominated by autoworkers. Founded in Detroit in 1935, the UAW originally represented auto workers but expanded its scope early on—changing its name in 1941 to include aircraft and agricultural equipment, then replacing 'aircraft' with 'aerospace' in 1962. Today, the UAW’s academic wing rivals—and in some cases exceeds—the number of workers at major automakers. For example, the UC system alone has more UAW members than Stellantis (the parent company formed in 2021 from Fiat Chrysler and PSA Group). In the fall of 2022, UC graduate student workers won a historic victory: a 46% raise over two years. Since then, unionization efforts have spread coast to coast. Graduate students at the University of Maine recently voted to join the UAW; those at the University of Alaska are currently voting. 'We think it's an exciting moment,' said Skye Kushner, a Ph.D. candidate in geoscience at UAF. Academic workers are not isolated in their activism. On the picket lines, they stand shoulder-to-shoulder with casino workers in Detroit, Blue Cross Blue Shield employees, and Mack Truck staff—all demanding higher wages, an end to tiered pay systems, and stronger job protections. 'Their fight is our fight,' said Andrea Kirby, a 21-year UAW member and Blue Cross employee. Postdoctoral researcher Andrea Joseph, who helped negotiate Mount Sinai’s first UAW contract, recalled marching with autoworkers in New York: 'It was really awesome to see how much we had in common.' Eliana Buenrostro, a Ph.D. student at UC Riverside and UAW unit chair, emphasized the financial solidarity: 'My union dues help fund a $825 million strike fund—that means my labor supports workers across the country.' Despite this growth, the UAW remains focused on rebuilding its auto base. UAW President Shawn Fain stated, 'Workers at Tesla, Toyota, Honda, and others are not the enemy—they’re the UAW members of the future.' Jim Cooper, a Jeep assembler in Toledo, Ohio, hopes that major gains from current negotiations will convince nonunion workers to organize: 'I want to see Elon watching his workforce take a vote to join a union and see how that goes for him.'

Grèn sa, ki te organizé pa L'Union des Travailleurs de l'Automobile (UAW), fèt pati yon tendans pi vòl: jodi a, aprèk 100,000 nan 383,000 mèm UAW yo travay nan edikasyon, ki gen pou yo: etidyan yo ki fèt asistan enseyman ak rechèch, postdoktora, profesè adjon, ak travayè administratif. Eksansyon sa a reflete yon chanjman strategik pou sindikat sa a, ki te domine pa travayè machin yo. Fondé nan Detroit nan 1935, UAW te reprezante travayè machin yo, men li te ekspande domèn li nan tout debòt—li te chanje non li nan 1941 pou inklè avyon ak ekipman agrikòl, epi li te remplace 'avyon' pa 'aerospatial' nan 1962. Jodi a, wèb akademik UAW a rivale—ak yon ti kote depase—nomb travayè nan gran konpayi machin yo. Pa egzanp, Systeme Kalifornia gen plis mèm UAW se tankou Stellantis (kompagni mèt ki te fòme nan 2021 nan fason Fiat Chrysler ak PSA Group). Nan dènye otòb 2022, etidyan yo ki fèt asistan nan UC te gagnen yon viktwar historik: yon haus 46% sou dènye de ane. Depi sa, efò pou sindikalizasyon te pran anpil tèt. Etidyan yo nan University of Maine te voté pou yo jwenn UAW; yo nan University of Alaska te jwenn votasyon yo. 'Nou panse se yon moman enpotan,' di Skye Kushner, yon doktè nan jiyosyans nan UAF. Travayè akademik yo pa sèl yo nan aktivite yo. Nan piken yo, yo ap gen kò ak travayè kazi nan Detroit, travayè Blue Cross Blue Shield, ak travayè Mack Truck—tout yo gen menm deman yo: salè pi wo, fini sistèm salè diferansye, ak pwoteksyon plis pou moun yo. 'Lut yo se lut nou yo,' di Andrea Kirby, yon mèm UAW 21 ane ak travayè Blue Cross. Recherchè postdoktoral Andrea Joseph, ki te ede nègosiye premye kontrat UAW nan Mount Sinai, te raple manch yo avèk travayè machin yo nan Nò Yo: 'Se te anpil fasil pou wè n anpil bagay ki te komun.' Eliana Buenrostro, yon doktènan nan UC Riverside ak presidan UAW, te mete a lavi solidarite finansyè: 'Dwòt mwen a aji pou yon fond grèn $825 milyon—sa vle di travay mwen a ap soutnenn travayè yo nan tout peyi a.' Malgre ekspansyon sa a, UAW pa t ap abandone ide pou rekonstwi sektè machin li a. Prezidan UAW Shawn Fain te deklare, 'Travayè nan Tesla, Toyota, Honda, ak lòt yo pa enemi yo—yo se mèm UAW demain.' Jim Cooper, yon asamble nan Jeep nan Toledo, Ohio, espere ke gagnen moun yo nan nègosiasyon sa yo ta kapab konvini travayè ki pa sindikalize yo: 'Mwen vle wè Elon wè sa travayè li a voté pou yo jwenn yon sindikat epi wè kòm sa pral fèt pou li.'

article_content: It’s tough for actors to shine when the script doesn’t give them much to work with—which is why many of the most memorable performances this year came from films with scripts recognized by the Writers Guild of America. On Friday, both the East and West branches of the WGA revealed their nominees for outstanding screenwriting in 2014. The list includes big names like David O. Russell for 'American Hustle,' Spike Jonze for 'Her,' and Woody Allen for 'Blue Jasmine.' But not everyone who wrote critically praised movies made the cut. Screenwriters John Ridley ('12 Years a Slave') and the duo of Steve Coogan and Jeff Pope ('Philomena') were ineligible because they didn’t write under a WGA contract. Only writers who are union members or who worked under a guild agreement can be nominated, which means some of the year’s most impactful stories were left off the ballot. The winners will be announced at twin ceremonies in New York and Los Angeles on February 1. Here are the nominees in all three categories: Original Screenplay, Adapted Screenplay, and Documentary Screenplay. From intimate dramas to explosive biopics, these scripts shaped some of cinema’s most talked-about moments this season.

Janvye 17, de branm chak ki yo se lòsòl ak lòsèl Writers Guild of America te anonsé nominasyon yo pou ekriti senaryo ki pi enpotan nan 2014. Lis la gen nòm konn yo tankou David O. Russell pou 'American Hustle,' Spike Jonze pou 'Her,' ak Woody Allen pou 'Blue Jasmine.' Men, pa tout moun ki ekri fim yo ki te resevwa kritik positif te pwochen. Ekriyen yo John Ridley ('12 Years a Slave') ak koup Steve Coogan ak Jeff Pope ('Philomena') te ineligib paske yo pa ekri sou yon kòntrat WGA. Se sèlman ekriyen ki se mèmbe sindikal oswa ki te travay sou yon akòd sindikal ki ka gen yon nominasyon, sa ki vle di kèk istwa ki pi pwofond lan te eske de lis la. Pwodiksyon yo pral anonsé nan de seremoni sou yon menm tan nan New York ak Los Angeles janvye 1. Men nouvo nominasyon yo nan tout trwa kategori: Senaryo Orijinal, Senaryo Adapte, ak Senaryo Dokimante. Depi drame intim yo tanpèt biyografi eksplòsitif, senaryo sa yo te fèt yon kantite moman ki te diskite nan sinema a sa a sezon.

article_content: A small town in rural New South Wales has been devastated by the deaths of two young residents after a Toyota Hilux, driven by a 19-year-old P-plater, flipped over and rolled into a roadside irrigation channel. Jake Isbister, 21, and a 17-year-old girl from Cootamundra were killed when the vehicle left Petersham Road in Leeton around 12:30 a.m. on Saturday. The driver and another passenger, aged 18, were injured. The group was en route to a campsite along the Murrumbidgee River when the truck rolled multiple times before coming to rest upside down in a metre-deep drainage ditch, according to The Daily Telegraph. The 18-year-old passenger, who was seated in the vehicle’s tray, was thrown clear during the crash and airlifted to Wagga Wagga Base Hospital with head injuries. He remains in stable condition but is expected to undergo surgery. The 19-year-old driver was taken to Leeton Hospital, released the following day, and later tested for alcohol and drugs. He has since been charged with two counts of dangerous driving occasioning death and one count of dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm. Tributes poured in on social media, with many expressing shock at the loss of Jake Isbister. Friends remembered him with messages like 'Forever 21' and 'R.I.P.' Leeton Mayor Paul Maytom said, 'It’s a tragic accident — to have deaths occur is absolutely devastating, especially this close to Christmas.' Emergency services, including the SnowyHydro Care Helicopter and Griffith Local Area Command officers, responded to the scene. All four individuals involved are believed to be from the Riverina region of NSW. Police are investigating whether drugs or alcohol played a role and will submit a report to the coroner. Duty officer John Wadsworth noted, 'It's always an exceptionally awful one when the people are of such a young age, so close to Christmas.' The town has recently invested in road safety upgrades along Petersham Road and surrounding areas due to prior safety concerns. The driver has been granted conditional bail and is scheduled to appear in Leeton Local Court on Friday, 6 February 2014. Police urge anyone with information to contact Crime Stoppers at 1800 333 000 or visit their website.

article_content: In a heartfelt interview with ESPN, Michael Sam, a standout defensive lineman from the University of Missouri, shared that he is gay — becoming the first known college football player to come out publicly ahead of the NFL draft. 'I’m an openly proud gay man,' he said, adding that he had already confided in his teammates months earlier and faced no backlash. Surprised to learn many in the media were already aware of his identity, Sam emphasized that his goal isn’t to make headlines — it’s to play football in the NFL. Speaking to The New York Times, he added, 'I just want to own my truth.' At 6-foot-2 and 260 pounds, Sam earned first-team All-American honors and was named the Southeastern Conference’s Defensive Player of the Year. His teammates voted him team MVP. While some analysts question his flexibility and size, suggesting he might be selected in later draft rounds, his agent, Joe Barkett, believes Sam’s openness could actually boost his appeal. 'Teams will see a man who’s honest and confident,' Barkett told CNN. 'He wants a team that accepts him fully.' The NFL responded swiftly on Twitter, praising Sam’s courage and affirming that talent and determination matter most. 'We look forward to welcoming Michael Sam in 2014,' the league stated. This moment arrives as the U.S. government moves to extend federal recognition to same-sex marriages nationwide, regardless of state laws. Though other athletes like Jason Collins and Brittney Griner have come out before, Sam stands out as the first to do so at the highest level of college football with realistic NFL prospects. GLAAD highlighted his leadership, noting that his visibility helps rewrite the narrative for young LGBTQ+ athletes everywhere. Missouri’s head coach, Gary Pinkel, called Sam 'a powerful example' of unity and respect. Even amid a difficult childhood — marked by the loss of a brother and family members incarcerated — Sam’s resilience and authenticity have inspired countless fans. In a tweet, he thanked ESPN, The New York Times, and the NFL for their support. 'I am proud to tell my story to the world,' he wrote.
translated_content: Ansèm entèvinyè pa ESPN, Michael Sam, yon lini defans ki te ekspriye nan Universite Misouri, te deklare li gay — fèt premye jwèt fòtbòl kòlèj ki te piblike konsa avan Draft NFL. 'Mwen se yon gay ki fèy ak fièt,' li di, ak ajoute ke li te deja konfide nan ekip li pandan mwa aout epi li pa te gen okenn konsekans. Li te etonè aprann ke plis mwayen komunikasyon te deja konnen identite li. Sam te mete ak poukisa li vle pa fè nouvo — se pou jwe fòtbòl nan NFL. Speaking to The New York Times, li te ajoute, 'Mwen vle domine verite mwen.' Avèk 6 pied 2 ak 260 liv, Sam te resevwa tout ane ak tout ane All-American ak te rekonèt jwèt defans pi enpotan nan Southeastern Conference. Ekip li te vot pou li jwèt ki pi enpotan. Menm jan ak analis yo ki panse ke fleksibilite ak tail li pa parfèt, epi ke li ka jwi nan dènye rounn, avoka li, Joe Barkett, panse ke ouvètir li ka fèt avantage. 'Ekip yo ta wè yon gason ki onèst ak konfyans,' Barkett te di CNN. 'Li vle yon ekip ki aksepte li kòm li ye.' NFL te reponn rapidman sou Twitter, aplodi kouraj Sam ak afime ke talan ak determinasyon se tout sa ki enpotan. 'Nou te wè pou akwelki Michael Sam an 2014,' liga te di. Kèk sa a ap pataje avèk lèt moun yo ki vle ekstend rekonosans federal pou mariyaj menm gen an tout peyi, menm nan 34 etat ki pa rekonèt yo. Menm si lòt atlet, tankou Jason Collins ak Brittney Griner, te deja piblike, Sam se premye a fè sa nan nivo pi eleve fòtbòl kòlèj ak posibilite realis NFL. GLAAD te mete a lavi lideras li, konsa ke visiblite li a aji pou reekriven kont pou jeun atlet LGBTQ+. Enstruktè fòtbòl Misouri, Gary Pinkel, te rele Sam 'yon ekzanp powè' de solidarite ak rezè. Menm avèk yon enfantè difisil — markè pa pèd frè a ak membre fami ki pran prizon — rezilans ak otantisite Sam te inspiré milyèn fan. Sou Twitter, li te merisi ESPN, The New York Times, ak NFL pou soutèn yo. 'Mwen fèy pou di istwa mwen an pou mond lan,' li te ekri.

article_content: After months without a job, legendary Dutch manager Guus Hiddink has stepped into one of football’s most unusual roles: leading Anzhi Makhachkala, a Russian club known more for its billionaire owner than its league position. Hiddink takes over from Yuri Krasnozhan, who quit before coaching a single official game—a rare move even in the volatile world of football management. At 65, Hiddink brings decades of experience: guiding the Netherlands to fourth in the 1998 World Cup, leading South Korea to the semifinals in 2002, and taking Australia to their first World Cup in over three decades in 2006. He’s also lifted trophies with PSV Eindhoven and Chelsea, and once managed Real Madrid to the Intercontinental Cup. Anzhi, based in the remote and security-sensitive region of Dagestan, doesn’t play home matches locally. Instead, players fly from Moscow for each game—an extraordinary logistical arrangement tied to safety concerns. Despite this, the club has assembled a glittering squad featuring African legend Samuel Eto’o and Brazilian icon Roberto Carlos. Owned by Russian billionaire Suleiman Kerimov, Anzhi isn’t just chasing wins. Hiddink was drawn to the club’s vision of developing grassroots football across the republic—not just building a winning team, but planting long-term roots. In interviews, he emphasized how deeply he connected with Kerimov’s ambition to use football as a tool for regional growth. Beyond coaching, Hiddink has accepted the title of vice president for football development, signaling his commitment to the broader mission. This is his first club role in six years—and possibly his most purpose-driven yet. 'I didn’t come here just for results,' he said. 'I came because I believe in this project.'
translated_content: Aprèm mwa yo san travay, entènasyonal holandè Guus Hiddink te pwojekte nan yon ròl ki pi enpotan pou fòtbòl: dirije Anzhi Makhachkala, yon klèb rus ki plis konnen pou patwòn li milyè a se kounya a. Hiddink te swiv Yuri Krasnozhan, ki te rezile avan li te dirije yon lòt match oficial—yon mo vini rare nan mon an fòtbòl. A 65 an, Hiddink ap amène yon eksperyans ki dwe moun yo: li te mennen Holand lan a katriyèm pòsition nan Kup Monde 1998, ki te mennen Kòrè di Lèd la a semifinal 2002, ak ki te mennen Ayiti a pou premyè fwa nan 32 an nan Kup Monde 2006. Li tou te rempòte trofè yo avèk PSV Eindhoven ak Chelsea, epi li te dirije Real Madrid pou Kup Intèkontinental la. Anzhi, ki sitiye nan reyion Dagestan, ki enpotan ak sekirite, pa jwe match yo a lokaly. Jwèt yo pwojen de Moscou pou chak match—yon asèn lòjistik ki rele sèlman sou ensekirite. Poutan, klèb la gen yon ekip ki fèt ak sèl nan Afrik la, Samuel Eto’o, ak legenn Brazil yo, Roberto Carlos. Patriyèt Rus Suleiman Kerimov, Anzhi pa sèlman chache gagnen. Hiddink te atrè pa vizyon klèb la pou devlope fòtbòl lokal nan repiblik la—pa sèlman kreye yon ekip ki gagne, men tou kreye yon baz pou avenir la. Anplis dirijans, Hiddink te pran tit la vès-prezidan pou devlopman fòtbòl, pou montre kominisman li a pou misyon la pi wòl. Se premyè fwa li travay pou yon klèb nan sis an, epi posibman se pi enpotan an. 'M pa vini la pou sèlman gagnen,' li te di. 'M vini la paske m kriye nan projè sa a.'

article_content: Aston Villa were thoroughly outplayed in a 4-1 pre-season loss to Dutch side FC Groningen at the Euroborg Stadium. The visitors struggled from the outset after Tjarron Chery capitalized on a rare mistake by goalkeeper Shay Given to open the scoring in the fourth minute. Just three minutes later, Chery doubled the lead with a stunning 30-yard strike that left Given helpless. Groningen continued to press forward, with Jarchinio Antonia adding a third before halftime after a well-worked move involving Danny Hoesen. Despite being three goals behind, Villa manager Paul Lambert waited until the second half to make changes. When Charles N'Zogbia finally entered the game, he immediately lifted spirits with a powerful free-kick in the 76th minute — a rare moment of quality for Villa. But the joy was short-lived: N'Zogbia then gifted possession to Groningen in stoppage time, allowing Dino Islamovic to seal the 4-1 result. Former Groningen player Leandro Bacuna, who came on as a substitute, was warmly cheered by the home crowd, recalling his four-year stint with the club. Overall, Villa’s performance lacked cohesion, creativity, and urgency — a worrying sign as they prepare for the new season.

Groningen te kontinye akrèt, ak Jarchinio Antonia te ajoute yon twazyèm avan mi-tem, aprè yon aksyon bòn ki te implike Danny Hoesen. Lè Charles N'Zogbia te ente jwenn l, li te levé mora yo avèk yon tiyèt lib ki fò nan 76èm minit — yon sèl moman ki te gen kalite pou Villa. Men, joie a te ko kout: N'Zogbia te pèdi balon an nan twa minit fò, pou fè Dino Islamovic te fèt 4-1. article_content: Jay Lovell, a fish collector from Hawaii, will not serve jail time if he complies with the terms of a plea agreement reached with prosecutors following a disturbing 2014 incident. Lovell pleaded no contest to second-degree terroristic threatening after ripping a scuba regulator from the mouth of activist Rene Umberger during a filming encounter off the coast of Hawaii’s Big Island. As part of the agreement, he received a six-month deferred sentence and must complete an anger-management assessment. If he remains crime-free for one year, the charge may be expunged from his record. Umberger, a coral reef consultant with Humane Society International, and five other divers were documenting Lovell’s legal but contentious practice of collecting tropical fish for the aquarium trade. The underwater footage shows Lovell swimming toward Umberger and forcibly removing her air supply — an act she described as terrifying and potentially fatal. Although Umberger urged the court to suspend Lovell’s fishing license during the deferment period, Judge Ronald Ibarra stated the court was bound by the plea deal’s terms. Prosecutors declined to pursue attempted murder charges, citing insufficient evidence that Lovell intended to kill. They noted he released the regulator immediately, allowing Umberger to retrieve it quickly. Lovell’s defense team argued he acted in self-defense, claiming the divers deliberately targeted and harassed him. His brother, James Lovell, and attorney Marcus Landsberg highlighted his past community contributions and insisted he did not seek confrontation. Umberger, however, has publicly stated Lovell showed no remorse. She also revealed that she and the group were filming to expose practices harmful to coral reefs, not to provoke violence. Complicating matters further, it was revealed that Umberger had been aboard a Sea Shepherd vessel that day — an organization known for direct-action tactics — and that she had previously spoken of targeting fish collectors. Lovell’s family claims the divers altered course to intercept them, escalating tensions. In a post-incident interview, Lovell told reporters, 'I didn’t go looking for it... the next time, they’ll be the ones who get arrested.' He added that his priority now is caring for his wife’s health, not fighting over fish.

Lovell te plwe pa kontèstè pou twazyèm degré menas teroris lan aprè li te tirè yon regulatè skuba nan bouk aktivist Rene Umberger pandan yon eksperyans fèm sou kòt Grann Îl Hawaii. Kòm pati akòrd la, li te resevwa yon peyin deferè 6 mwa epi li dwe fè yon evalyasyon kontwòl kolè. Si li pa fè yon krimen pou yon ane, krim la ka enkònan nan dossye li. Umberger, yon konsiltè rif koral avèk Humane Society International, ak sink lòt plongè yo te dokumente pratik legal toujou kontwèv yo kolektè pòis tropikal pou tòmèn akwaryèm. Ekipaj defans Lovell te pran pozisyon ke li te reyaksyon self-defense, di ke plongè yo te konsèntrè yo sou li ak yo te harase li. Frè li, James Lovell, ak avoka li Marcus Landsberg te mete an avant kontribisyon komunitè li epi te asire ke li pa chache konfli a. Umberger, toutefwa, te piblike ke Lovell pa montre okenn remors. Li toujou te revele ke yo te fèm pou ekspose pratik ki dòmi rifi koral, pa pou provoken violans. Kòmplike aksyon an, li te revele ke Umberger te sou yon bato Sea Shepherd an jounen an — yon organizasyon konnen pou aksyon direk — epi ke li te deja te pale de konsèntrè sou kolektè pòis. Li ajoute ke prioritè li an jounen an se pou sòti fèm yon sante fanm li, pa pou bata sou pòis.

article_content: (CNN) — Tuesday’s deadly suicide attack targeting an Afghan Shia shrine did not follow the established pattern of violence in this troubled country. Police set up their usual cordon around the site — a shrine in Kabul. Sirens broke the strange silence, but the police chief’s face twisted with fury and confusion, as if he’d witnessed something disturbingly new — even after decades of conflict. Yes, insurgents have long targeted city centers, often within meters of key institutions, aiming for maximum impact. Yet large-scale attacks like those seen in 2009 are now rare. Insurgents typically focus on strategic targets — unless their roadside bombs indiscriminately harm civilians elsewhere. And until now, Shia communities were rarely targeted. Sectarianism has historically been minimal in Afghanistan: unlike Iraq, where Sunni-Shia divisions fueled chaos after Saddam’s fall, Afghanistan has largely avoided such deep sectarian rifts. It has also escaped the brutal anti-Shia extremism seen in parts of Pakistan. The identity of the perpetrators was quickly pointed to — but unsatisfactorily. Afghanistan’s interior ministry blames the Taliban, despite a forceful denial from spokesman Zabiullah Mujahid. It’s plausible that an offshoot of Pakistan’s Lashkar-e-Janghvi, which claimed responsibility, carried out this sophisticated, targeted strike with some level of local support. If true, it raises difficult questions: How could a small, rogue extremist group linked to al-Qaeda and the Pakistani Taliban suddenly gain the capability to strike at the heart of Kabul? Are Pakistani extremists now operating openly within Afghanistan? Whether the attackers are the Haqqani network, Lashkar-e-Janghvi al-Alami, or another fragmented faction of Afghanistan’s complex insurgency — hardened by a decade of war — many Afghans point to one source: Pakistan. That’s the address Kabul assigns to the Taliban’s current base. That’s who they hold responsible for most of the nation’s suffering, even while hoping for negotiations. But we must resist rushing to assign blame — because the prospect of Pakistani extremists deliberately stoking sectarian violence in Afghanistan at this stage of the war is too horrifying to contemplate.
translated_content: (CNN) — Atak souikid ki te tue nan peyi Ay Afghanistan te pa konn fèt avèk pati ki te deja konnen nan peyi sa a. Pòlisy la te mete kòdonn li yo sou sit lan — yon shrin nan Kaboul. Sirèn yo te dekoupe silans ekstraèn an, men fès chef pòlisy la te twa kòm si li te wè kèk chose nouvo ak travay — menm apre desenn dènye konfli a. Wi, insèrjant yo te toujou atake sèntr vil la, souvan anvan mèt nan institisyon ki enpotan, pou yo fè efè. Men atak masif tankou yo te wè nan 2009, yo rari a jodi a. Insèrjant yo plis a imite atak strategik yo — lè yo pa fèt bombèn akòz sivil yo nan lòt endirèk. Epi, Shia yo pa te janm atake anvan. Sektaèrism la te toujou mwen an Ay Afghanistan: tankou Iraki, kote divizyon Sounnita-Shi’a te fèt kaos aprè tombe Saddam la, Ay Afghanistan te evite tout divizyon sektaèr avèk. Li tou evite ekstremisim Sounnita brutal ki genyen nan pòs Ay Pakistan. Identite atekan yo te vini rapidman — men pa satisfè. Ministè enteryè a te akrize Taliban yo, malgre deyèn ki te refizè l yo. Li posib ke yon sibgrup Lashkar-e-Janghvi ki te ki te pran responsabilite a, te kapab fè atak sa a sofistikè ak kèk aksè lokal. Estè ekstremis Pakistan yo te aji libman nan Ay Afghanistan jodi a? Ke se Haqqani, Lashkar-e-Janghvi al-Alami, oswa yon lòt faksyon fragmente nan insèrjans Ay Afghanistan — ki te fèt pi konplike aprè 10 ane — plis moun Ay Afghanistan te mete kòt yo sou yon sòs: Pakistan. Se sa ki adrès Kaboul yo bay Taliban yo. Se sa ki yo konsidere kòm responsab pou tout mal Ay peyi a, menm si yo espere yo ta dwe pale. Men nou dwe reziste pou mete kòt yo sou yon sòs — paske idée ekstremis Pakistan yo te vle fèn sektaèrism nan Ay Afghanistan nan etap sa a nan gwè a, se trop terib pou imajine.

article_content: On March 31, 2011, CNN Student News reported on major developments in Libya, Syria, U.S. counterterrorism efforts, and emerging advertising technologies. In Libya, U.S. and NATO forces have evolved their mission from preventing air attacks to actively targeting Gadhafi’s ground forces—including elite units like the 32nd Brigade and munitions depots. The shift includes deploying A-10 gunships for precision strikes in urban areas, reflecting a broader interpretation of the 'protect civilians' mandate that now extends into Tripoli. While initial spending exceeded $500 million, future costs are expected to drop significantly, with monthly expenses projected at $40 million. Officials are now weighing whether to arm rebel fighters, though intelligence warns some rebels may have ties to terrorist groups. In Syria, widespread protests continue, with dozens killed as citizens demand an end to a decades-old emergency law and constitutional reforms. President Bashar al-Assad acknowledged public dissatisfaction but dismissed the unrest as part of a foreign-led conspiracy, refusing to address the emergency law directly. His remarks contrast sharply with the democratic transitions seen in neighboring countries like Egypt. Meanwhile, a U.S. Senate committee reviewed post-9/11 security measures, with former 9/11 Commission members noting the nation is safer from large-scale attacks—but the threat landscape has become more complex and diverse. In a separate segment, CNN explored how modern TV advertising uses viewer data—collected via set-top boxes, credit reports, and retail loyalty cards—to deliver hyper-targeted commercials. Companies like Simulmedia and Visible World claim this increases relevance for viewers and boosts ad revenue, potentially worth billions. However, critics warn this represents a significant erosion of privacy, as viewing habits reveal intimate details about individuals’ lives.

article_content: To celebrate its 25th anniversary, lingerie brand Passionata did something different: instead of hiring a global supermodel, they invited real fans to step into the spotlight. The company launched a fun Facebook contest asking customers to share photos of themselves wearing their favorite Passionata pieces—showcasing what the brand meant to them personally. Out of countless entries, four women were chosen: 23-year-olds Josie Polington and Jessica O, 23-year-old Katie Ireland, and 19-year-old Hannah Galvin. The winners weren’t just given a title—they got a full-day experience. They spent the afternoon at the charming Watts Gallery tea shop in Guildford, Surrey, posing for photos amid tea, cakes, and laughter. The shoot had a whimsical, birthday-party vibe, complete with pink-wrapped gifts and a symbolic moment: releasing 25 pink helium balloons into the sky, one for each year of the brand’s history. Passionata has always stood for embracing femininity. Founded in the 1980s, it emerged as a response to the flat, androgynous styles dominating fashion at the time. Customers craved curves, elegance, and confidence—and Passionata delivered. By the early '90s, the brand had embraced more daring designs: lace-trimmed garters, plunging necklines, and plenty of allure. Over the years, Passionata has worked with iconic figures like photographer David LaChapelle, whose unforgettable 'Hot and Sexy Hollywood' campaign showed a sultry woman riding a pink plastic horse in satin lingerie. And since 2010, supermodel Bar Refaeli became the face of the brand. But for this milestone, the focus shifted entirely—to the women who’ve worn the lingerie every day, not just on the runway. As a thank-you, Passionata is offering a 25% discount on its entire collection, available online at Figleaves.com until June 10, 2014, and in select boutique stores across the UK. It wasn’t just a birthday party—it was a celebration of real women, real style, and real loyalty.

Marke sa a te lanse yon konkous amusant sou Facebook ki te demann kliyan yo pou yo poste foto yo nan pyjama Passionata yo, pou yo montre kòman marke sa a vle di pou yo. Nan plis 4 moun te chwazi: Josie Polington (23 an), Jessica O (23 an), Katie Ireland (23 an), ak Hannah Galvin (19 an). Pou yo, pa sèlman yo te resevwa yon tit—yo te resevwa yon jou komplet. Yo te pase lèpèy yo nan Watts Gallery tea shop nan Guildford, Surrey, yo te poz pou foto yo nan entèn yon fèt natal, avèk thé, gateau ak rire. Pwojè a te gen yon tanpèm fèt, avèk prezan ki te enpakèn pwòp ki te fèt, epi yon moman simbolik: lâche 25 balòn heliam pwòp ki te reprezante chak ane dènye marke a te eksiste. Pou remerasyon, Passionata ta donn yon remise 25% sou tout koleksyon an, disponib sou sit la Figleaves.com pou 10 Jiyè 2014, ak nan boutik selekte yo nan tout Angleter. article_content: Health officials are sounding the alarm about popular children’s toys that emit powerful lasers — including lightsabers, spinning tops, and toy guns with laser sights. While these items may seem like harmless fun, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) warns they can cause irreversible eye damage. Unlike many injuries, laser burns to the eye often don’t hurt right away, meaning vision loss can creep up silently over days or even weeks. Dan Hewett, a health expert at the FDA, explains that direct exposure to even a brief laser beam — especially from high-powered devices — can permanently harm the retina. Common culprits include handheld laser toys marketed as pretend sabers, rotating tops that shoot beams, and room-projecting lasers sold for entertainment. Because manufacturers often label them as 'toys,' parents and kids assume they’re safe. But as laser technology becomes cheaper and more powerful, the risk is growing. The FDA urges families to never point any laser device at a person, pet, or reflective surface. In fact, looking directly into a strong laser beam can be more damaging than staring at the sun. Even accidental flashes, like those aimed at drivers or athletes, can trigger dangerous distractions leading to accidents.

Menm si sa yo dwe sanse sans pè, Administrasyon Alimèn ak Dòmaj nan Etazini (FDA) avèti ke sa yo ka pòte domaj envèsib nan peyiz. Kontrèman ak plis lèzyon, lèsèn yo pa fè mal tout dekòs, sa vle di pèd presyasyon yo ka evolye silansyöman pandan jou oswa mwa. Dan Hewett, ekspè santé FDA, eksplike ke eksposisyon direk ak yon bèm lasè, menm toujou brèf, espesyalman sèl ki pwòpòsyònèlman fò, ka dòmi retin nan pèmanan. Kominèn ki pi frèkman kousè yo se jouwèt lasè tenèn an, toupis ki projekte bèm yo, ak lasèn ki itilize pou efè etenman. Meme fèn fèn, tankou sa yo ki pèdi sou divè, oswa jwètè, kapab pouse akidantan dangere yo.

article_content: On Monday, police in Tennessee arrested a family of three following a prostitution sting. The operation began when an undercover detective responded to an advertisement on a now-defunct website formerly known as Backpage.com and met with 33-year-old Christy Huxoll at the Madison Square Inn. She agreed to engage in sexual acts for $160 per half-hour. After the encounter, officers took her into custody and charged her with prostitution and unlawful use of drug paraphernalia. According to the arrest warrant, Christy’s parents, Lisa Alff and Larry Huxoll, admitted they knew their daughter was engaged in sex work. They said they provided her with a hotel room and condoms not to facilitate prostitution, but to protect her from working on the streets. After Christy was arrested, she informed authorities that someone was bringing condoms to the motel—later identified as her parents. Both parents were charged with promoting prostitution. Their bonds have been set at $10,000 each.

article_content: Amal Clooney was warned by Egyptian officials that she risked arrest for presenting a report exposing serious flaws in Egypt’s judicial system. The human rights lawyer, who married Hollywood actor George Clooney in September 2014, received the threat shortly after completing the report — a document prepared on behalf of the International Bar Association that critically assessed Egypt’s courts. The report highlighted systemic issues, including excessive control by the Ministry of Justice over judges and undue government influence over public prosecutors. It specifically called for an end to the practice of allowing officials to handpick judges for individual cases — a recommendation that was ignored. When Clooney attempted to launch the report in Cairo, authorities halted the event and demanded to know whether it criticized the army, judiciary, or government. Upon confirmation that it did, officials warned her: 'Then you’re risking arrest.' The report’s conclusions proved tragically prescient. The same judicial flaws it identified were evident in the trial of three Al Jazeera journalists — Peter Greste, Baher Mohamed, and Mohamed Fahmy — who were convicted in June 2014 by Judge Mohamed Nagy Shehata, a figure notorious for biased rulings and harsh sentences, including a mass death sentence against 188 people later that year. Clooney has represented the journalists since before the trial began. While Egyptian lawyers handle domestic legal strategy, she leads international efforts to secure the deportation of Fahmy (Canadian) and Greste (Australian) under a presidential decree enacted in July 2014, which allows foreign nationals to be repatriated. Baher Mohamed, an Egyptian citizen, remains dependent on Egypt’s own judicial system for relief. The journalists, arrested in December 2013 following the ousting of President Mohamed Morsi, have been imprisoned for over a year. Their retrial is underway, but Clooney fears the entrenched structural problems in Egypt’s courts will prevent a fair outcome.

article_content: New Delhi (CNN) — Airport security officers at New Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport detained a man from the United Arab Emirates after discovering a rare slender loris hidden in his underwear during a routine pat-down on Sunday. According to Hemendra Singh, a spokesperson for the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), the small, nocturnal primate — measuring no more than 10 inches (25 cm) in length — is native to Sri Lanka and classified as endangered under India’s Wildlife Protection Act of 1972. A second loris was later found abandoned in a nearby trash can. Both animals were transferred to wildlife authorities for care. The man and two other travelers accompanying him were handed over to customs officials. As of now, no formal charges have been filed.

Selon Hemendra Singh, yon spesyalis pou Forse Sekirite Indistriyel Sentral (CISF), primat piti a, ki se yon espèk nwa ki mache nan nwit, ki gen yon longè ki pa depase 10 col (25 cm), ki gen pou orijin Srilanka ak ki klasifiké kòm enmenaj sou Lèy Loi Pwoteje Fawnis nan Indy. Yon lòt lorisyen te jwenn nan yon poubèl ki te aji a. De anmou yo te transpòte nan otòrité fawnis pou sove yo. Moun an ak de lòt travayè ki te avèk li te remèt nan otòrité douanyo. Pou kounye a, pa gen anyen akonpann.

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) — Lindsay Lohan’s lawyer has vehemently denied allegations that the actress stole a $2,500 necklace from a Venice, California, jewelry store last month. According to police and a spokesperson for the Los Angeles County District Attorney, Lohan’s stylist turned over the unique piece just before authorities were set to execute a search warrant at her residence. 'We vehemently deny these allegations, and if charges are filed, we will fight them in court — not in the press,' said Lohan’s attorney, Shawn Chapman Holley, on Saturday. Sandi Gibbons, spokesperson for the District Attorney, clarified that no decision has been made to file felony charges. 'The case remains under review,' she said. 'When we make a decision, we will inform the public.' The necklace, described as one-of-a-kind, was valued at $2,500. LAPD detectives obtained a search warrant for Lohan’s Venice home on February 1, 2011, as part of a grand theft investigation. Lohan, 24, is currently on supervised probation following a DUI conviction. In October, the presiding judge warned her that violating probation before her next court hearing on February 25 would result in 180 days in jail. She recently completed a three-month stay at the Betty Ford Clinic, a move that convinced the judge to spare her jail time for a prior failed drug test. CNN’s Brittany Kaplan contributed to this report.

'Nou refise vireman aksezan sa yo, epi si chajman yo fèt, nou ta bat yo nan kòr, pa nan pres,' te di avoka Lindsay Lohan, Shawn Chapman Holley, samedi. Sandi Gibbons, spesyalis pou Bwato Distrèt, te klarye ke pa gen decizyon pran pou fè chajman felon. 'Kaz la ap kontinye an revyè,' li te di. 'Nou pral enfòme tout moun lè nou pran yon decizyon.' article_content: Experts are raising alarms that society and governments are dangerously unprepared for a new kind of crime: one where digital attacks lead to physical injury or death. While no one has yet been killed by a hacked device, analysts warn that the first such incident could happen soon — possibly even before the end of the year. The concept stems from the rapid expansion of the Internet of Everything (IoE), where everyday objects — from garage door openers to hospital monitors — are now connected to the internet, creating countless entry points for malicious actors. According to a Europol assessment citing research from US cybersecurity firm IID, cybercriminals are actively hunting for weaknesses in these systems. Rod Rasmussen, IID’s president, noted that a thriving black market exists for selling undiscovered software flaws, making it easier than ever for attackers to weaponize technology. Although no verified case of fatal device tampering has occurred, real harm is already happening: people have taken their own lives after being blackmailed online, and hackers have proven they can remotely trigger cash withdrawals from ATMs. One chilling example is former U.S. Vice President Dick Cheney, who had the wireless capability turned off on his implanted heart device after learning it could potentially be hacked to induce a cardiac arrest. He later recognized the scenario portrayed in the TV series Homeland as terrifyingly plausible. Similarly, renowned hacker Barnaby Jack was on the verge of demonstrating how pacemakers could be compromised when he tragically died in 2013. His work underscored a grim truth: the line between digital intrusion and physical danger is vanishing. Beyond lethal threats, experts predict a surge in digital extortion — hackers locking families out of their smart homes or vehicles until ransoms are paid. Craig Spiezle of the Online Trust Alliance warned that every new connected innovation brings with it opportunists ready to exploit it. As more devices become 'smart,' the risk grows — and so does the urgent need for stronger security standards, updated forensic methods, and global policy responses.
translated_content: Ekspè yo te fèt pou atansyon ke sosiyete ak gouvernman yo pa preparé pou yon nòm nouvo de krim: kri nan kote atak digital ka mennen a blesis oswa mò. Menm si pa gen okenn moun ki te mouri pa yon devès ki te te kome, analis yo avèn ke premye kaza sa a ka pase sou tan, posibman avan fin ane a. Konsept sa a vin de l’ekspansyon rapid Internet tout bagay (IoE), kote bagay yo kote — tankou ouvèt chèm gaj, sistèm hopital — se konsèkte ak internet, kreye plizyè entri pou aksè malikie. Ansanm ak évalwasyon Europol ki cite rechèch fèt pa firme sekirite amerikèn IID, kriminel digital yo aktifman chache fèbless yo nan sistèm sa yo. Rod Rasmussen, prezidan IID, te fèt pou atansyon ke yon mache nwa ki pwojere ekziste pou vann fèbless logisyèl ki pa konnen, fè pi fasil pou atakè yo pou yo armewon teknoloji a. Menm si pa gen okenn kaza verifye de tamperaj fatal, domaj reyèl yo deja pase: moun yo te tue yo-meme aprè yo te etranpe online, ak kriminel yo te pwouve yo kapab enstale konsènman monèt ak ATMs. Yon egzanp fèb la se ancyan Vès-Prezidant Etazini Dick Cheney, ki te fè fèm fonksyon wireless nan devès kòd kè li, aprè li te aprann li kapab etranpe pou fè yon atak kardiak. Oeuvr li te mete an evidans yon verite tris: lign ki sépare ant intrizyon digital ak danga fizik la ap disparèt. article_content: On the first day of spring, a thick fog rolled across Sydney at dawn, transforming the city’s iconic skyline into a hauntingly beautiful scene. Locals captured and shared stunning images of the Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge barely visible through the mist. While the day cleared into a crisp, sunny spring morning, the early fog left a lasting impression. At Sydney Airport, visibility dropped to 8,000 metres — classified by meteorologists as mist rather than true fog. Despite this, the airport remained open thanks to its recent upgrade from Category 1 to Category 2 instrumentation, allowing most flights to operate normally. Richmond, in Sydney’s north-west, bore the brunt of the fog. Visibility fell below 1,000 metres from around 12:50 a.m. until 8:30 a.m., making it the hardest-hit area. The Bureau of Meteorology noted that while fog is uncommon this time of year, Richmond typically sees up to six such events monthly. Meteorologist Sarah Chadwick explained that the fog formed under clear overnight skies, which allowed surface temperatures to drop to the dew point. When moist air cools to this threshold, water vapor condenses into tiny droplets, forming visible fog. Just days earlier, Melbourne faced a similar but more severe event. Visibility at Melbourne Airport plunged to 150 metres on Friday, grounding planes and forcing international flights to divert. The city’s skyline vanished beneath a dense blanket of fog for multiple mornings, prompting social media comparisons to Gotham City. Melbourne Airport spokeswoman Anna Gillett advised travelers to check airline updates but assured them the airport remained operational. Senior forecaster Terry Ryan attributed the prolonged fog to an unusual weather pattern — a slow-moving high-pressure ridge and light winds, more typical of autumn than early spring. Forecasters expect both cities to see clearer skies by midday, with Melbourne heading toward sunny weekend temperatures in the low 20s before rain arrives Monday.

Nan Aéroport Sydini, visiblite a te desann pou 8,000 mèt — meteòrolog yo te deklare se pi plis yon brouillard pase yon nebl vre. Menm jan an, aéroport la te konn fèt, paske li te te rekonstrwi nan kategori 1 pou kategori 2, sa ki pèmèt plis avyon yo te fèt san pwoblèm. Richmond, nan nòwèst Sydini, te pi viktim nebl la. article_content: Oscar Pistorius, the South African double-amputee known as the 'Blade Runner,' made history on Saturday by becoming the first Paralympian to compete in the able-bodied Olympic 400-meter event. Finishing second in his qualifying heat with a time of 45.44 seconds, he secured a spot in Sunday’s semifinals. Born in Johannesburg, Pistorius had both legs amputated below the knee at 11 months old due to a congenital bone condition. He competes using custom carbon fiber prosthetic blades — a factor that earned him his iconic nickname. His participation in the London 2012 Olympics marks a landmark moment: he is the third Paralympian ever to compete in the Olympic Games, following swimmers Natalie du Toit (2008) and table tennis player Natalia Partyka (2008, 2012). Despite failing to meet the official Olympic 'A' standard twice in international competitions, South African selectors revised their criteria last month and included him in both the individual 400m and the 4x400m relay. A four-time Paralympic gold medalist, Pistorius also earned a silver medal in the 4x400m relay at the 2011 World Championships in Daegu, South Korea. 'To represent Team South Africa at the London 2012 Games is a true honor,' he said last month. 'Years of hard work, determination, and sacrifice have finally come together.' He joins fellow South African star Caster Semenya on the track team. Semenya, the reigning 800m world champion, was subjected to a gender eligibility review by the International Association of Athletics Federations after her 2009 world title win but has since been cleared to compete.

Li fini dezyèm nan kwalifikasyon li a avèk yon tems 45.44 segond, epi li te kwalifye pou semifinal dimanch la. Li reyini ak Caster Semenya nan ekip atletizm Sòt Afrikèn an. Semenya, champiyon mondyal 800m, te soumèt a yon etid genitèl pa IAAF aprè vitwa li nan 2009, men li te toujou kwalifye pou kouri.

article_content: Mark Kizer, police chief of Bryant, Arkansas, was suspended without pay for five days after submitting a $58 restaurant receipt from Orlando, Florida, for reimbursement. The establishment, listed on the receipt as 'OC Food and Beverage,' is widely known locally as Rachel’s — a gentlemen’s club with an adjacent dining room. Kizer was in Orlando attending a professional conference on school security with colleague Lee Ledbetter. He says he dined at the restaurant based on a recommendation from his hotel concierge and insists he never entered the strip club area. He claims his server was a middle-aged man named David, as shown on the receipt, and that he saw no dancers during his meal. City officials discovered the dining venue’s association with Rachel’s, a well-known adult entertainment venue where patrons can view performers from the restaurant seating areas. Though the dining area is physically separate, the stage remains visible from many tables. Though Kizer stated he only ordered a steak and potato, and confirmed he did not witness any nudity, city attorney Chris Madison emphasized that the issue was less about what occurred and more about public perception. 'It’s a matter of appearance,' Madison said. 'It’s significant enough to warrant a personnel review.' Following the suspension, a local lawyer voluntarily reimbursed Kizer for the $58 meal and an additional $100 to cover lost wages.

article_content: Caterham F1, the only team in Formula One history never to have scored a point, has been sold to a new ownership group led by former Midland and HRT principal Colin Kolles. The consortium includes Swiss and Middle Eastern investors. The team will keep its name, headquarters in Leafield, northwest of London, and continue racing under the Caterham banner. Former Dutch Formula One driver Christijan Albers will take over as team principal, supported by Manfredi Ravetto, replacing Cyril Abiteboul. In a statement, Albers acknowledged the immense challenge of competing near the bottom of the grid, stating, 'Our target is to reach 10th place in the 2014 Constructors’ Championship.' He emphasized the team’s commitment to securing the resources needed to grow and unlock its full potential. This marks the end of a four-year involvement in F1 for Tony Fernandes, who also served as chairman of Queens Park Rangers — a club recently promoted to the English Premier League. Fernandes, founder and CEO of Asia’s first low-cost airline, AirAsia, closed his Twitter account with a reflective message: 'F1 hasn't worked, but I love Caterham Cars.' Caterham entered Formula One in 2010 and finished last in the 2013 Constructors’ Championship. As of the eighth race of the 2014 season, neither of their drivers — Japan’s Kamui Kobayashi nor Sweden’s Marcus Ericsson — has scored a single point.

article_content: A judge in Fort Hood, Texas, has postponed the pretrial hearing for Major Nidal Hasan — the Army psychiatrist accused of killing 13 people in a 2009 mass shooting — until October. Hasan, who has been confined to a wheelchair since being shot during the attack, appeared in court dressed in military fatigues and wrapped in a blanket. He answered questions briefly and calmly, even smiling slightly during a conversation with his lawyer. This was Hasan’s first court appearance related to the case. The proceeding, known as an Article 32 hearing, functions similarly to a civilian grand jury but allows both prosecution and defense to question witnesses. Security was heavy: streets were closed, bomb-sniffing dogs patrolled, and reporters underwent dual screening. Hasan’s defense team, led by retired Army colonel and seasoned attorney John Galligan, has requested a wide range of materials, including ballistic analyses of each bullet trajectory, video from the scene, and internal Army investigations commissioned by President Obama. While the Army provided 2,000 pages of documents, many key items remain unavailable. For instance, Galligan sought records detailing the exact angles of bullet paths to determine the shooter’s location — but the Army responded that no such files exist. He also requested all email correspondence between Hasan and the late extremist cleric Anwar al-Awlaki. Prosecutors agreed to release those emails. Additionally, defense attorneys are seeking classified documents, which authorities say they are currently reviewing for possible declassification. The defense also wants medical and performance records from Hasan’s time at Walter Reed, hinting at a strategy to explore his mental state before the attack. Despite the prosecution’s readiness to proceed as early as July, the judge granted the delay because Hasan’s legal team has met with him only once so far. They argue they need more time to properly prepare. Unlike civilian grand juries, Article 32 hearings are open forums where both sides actively participate — making thorough preparation essential.

Hasan, ki gen yon chèzi roulè depi li te pouse nan atak la, te parèt nan kòrt la vètman ak yon blan. Li te reponn koutman ak kalme, menm si li te souri piti piti pandan li te pale avèk avoka li. article_content: Pakistan has turned down a request by U.S. special envoy Marc Grossman to visit the country, according to a senior official. The refusal underscores growing tensions between the two nations, which are at their lowest point in years. A government source, speaking anonymously, stated that Grossman’s visit was denied 'at this time,' though no specific reason was given. Relations have been strained since a November 2011 NATO airstrike killed 24 Pakistani soldiers and the May 2011 U.S. raid that killed Osama bin Laden without notifying Pakistani authorities — an act Islamabad called a violation of its sovereignty. The U.S. State Department confirmed that Pakistan has decided to complete its ongoing review of cooperation with the U.S. and NATO before allowing Grossman’s next visit. The review, now under consideration by Pakistan’s parliament, has no set deadline. Grossman, who is scheduled to travel to Afghanistan and Qatar this week, plays a key role in U.S. efforts to broker peace in Afghanistan. His access to Pakistan is seen as vital, given Islamabad’s historical ties to militant groups and its influence over the Taliban. Ties between Washington and Islamabad have been further damaged by the 2011 killing of two Pakistanis by a CIA contractor and by internal Pakistani political strife, including unverified reports of a memo from President Asif Ali Zardari’s administration seeking U.S. assistance to curb the power of the military — a development that has worsened civil-military relations since the 1999 coup.

Yon sòs gouvènman, ki refize pèmèt identite li, te di ke demann Grossman te refize 'a jodi a,' men pa gen okenn rezon espesifik ki te donn. Relasyon yo te fènmen apre yon atak aeryen NATO ki tue 24 solèy pakistane yo nan novanm 2011 ak rade Etazyen may 2011 ki te tue Osamà Bin Laden san avize otorite pakistane — yon aks ki te deklare yon violasyon souverènete a pa Islamabad. article_content: Former LAPD officer Chris Dorner has become the subject of a controversial video game that portrays him as a vigilante fighting police. The game, titled 'Chris Dorner's Last Stand: A True American Hero,' simulates his final confrontation with law enforcement in a burning cabin near Big Bear Lake, California. The 33-year-old Dorner died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound after a two-day standoff, during which he allegedly killed three people and wounded two officers. The cabin, set ablaze by pyrotechnic tear gas canisters, was not intentionally fired upon, according to authorities. Developed by the online community 4chan, the game draws inspiration from first-person shooters like Doom. It features offensive elements, including background music that repeatedly uses a racial slur and a mechanic allowing players to restore health by collecting buckets of fried chicken. The game also includes cameos of public figures: Charlie Sheen, who publicly urged Dorner to surrender after being named in Dorner’s manifesto, and Arnold Schwarzenegger, portrayed as a cyborg enemy. In the weeks following Dorner’s death, dozens of protesters gathered outside LAPD headquarters. While they condemned his violent acts, many expressed solidarity with his allegations of systemic racism and police brutality. Some questioned whether Dorner could have been captured alive, citing concerns over due process. Authorities confirmed that the use of incendiary devices during the standoff was not meant to ignite the cabin. Dorner had already been suspected of killing three others before the final confrontation.
