article_content: Editor's note: Join Roland S. Martin for his weekly sound-off segment on CNN.com Live at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday. If you're passionate about politics, he wants to hear from you. A supporter of Senator Barack Obama, Martin is a nationally syndicated columnist and a Chicago, Illinois-based radio host. He is the author of 'Listening to the Spirit Within: 50 Perspectives on Faith' and 'Speak, Brother! A Black Man's View of America.' Please visit his website. Roland S. Martin urges candidates to stop with lofty rhetoric and simplistic solutions—and instead be specific. (CNN) — If you're a member of America's middle class during this presidential election, you're somewhat like a blue-chip football recruit: lavished with praise, attention, and adoration from fawning coaches and alumni eager to land the prized player to win the national championship. For 'Coach' John McCain and 'Coach' Barack Obama, the prize is the presidency. Like top-tier football coaches, they’ll say and do anything to win. Tax cuts? Absolutely—we don’t want you to feel any more pain. Let the rich—and the poor—bear the burden. Want more jobs? Sure, we’ll force companies that ship jobs overseas to keep them here, because we know you need those long-vanishing, high-paying manufacturing jobs that helped build this nation. Can’t afford college? Don’t worry—we’ve got tax credits, Pell grants, and plenty of other options to make it happen. Health care cuts at your job? No big deal. Coach McCain has nifty tax credits lined up to tickle your fancy. Coach Obama? He’s going for the whole enchilada: universal health care. These candidates are masters of sales pitches—they make you feel uniquely valued, as if no one else matters more to them at that moment. I must admit, the desperate pandering for middle-class votes has become so absurd it sometimes drives me crazy. First—who exactly are we talking about? Candidates and their campaigns suggest the middle class earns anywhere from $20,000 to $200,000 a year. At a recent panel I moderated for the National Black MBA Association, attendees described lower middle class, middle class, and upper middle class. One even said it’s really about a 'state of mind.' That’s right—if you love your family, go to church, and share community values, you’re middle class—even if you have $5 million in the bank. Please, let’s stop the grandstanding and vague promises. Be specific. There are four fundamental issues affecting middle-class voters: Jobs: We’ve lost 600,000 jobs under President Bush. How exactly will McCain and Obama create new ones? What in their records proves they can? McCain says 'drill, drill, drill!' Obama proposes turning old textile and steel mills into green-energy hubs powered by wind and other renewables. Housing: Congress is backing Wall Street with billions in bailouts. What will McCain and Obama do to prevent families from losing their homes? Yes, some say middle-class buyers should’ve read the fine print—but if Wall Street gets rescued, why not Main Street? Health care: This isn’t a joke—it’s a leading cause of bankruptcy in America. I know firsthand: In 2000, while covering the Democratic National Convention, my appendix ruptured. I spent five days in a Los Angeles hospital and racked up over $70,000 in bills—I had no insurance. I was a 29-year-old freelance journalist, suddenly broke. The stress pushed me behind on my mortgage and into foreclosure. Bankruptcy saved me. By God’s grace, my finances recovered—and this month, I’m making my final payment. McCain offers a $5,000 tax credit for health care—but you must pay upfront and wait for reimbursement. What if you need the money now? Obama supports universal coverage—but implementation won’t happen overnight. What happens while Washington debates and special interests dismantle the plan? Do I wait for my MRI until they finish arguing? Education: For many, education is the path to the middle class. Yet candidates keep talking about vouchers. That won’t fix the system. What we need to hear is about inequity: Wealthy school districts get funding and top teachers. Poor districts struggle with underqualified staff, outdated books, and no computers—or even heat. Bottom line: Remember those blue-chip recruits? They’re telling coaches: 'If you want me to sign, promise I’ll start. No playing time? No deal.' That’s what middle-class Americans must tell McCain, Obama, Biden, and Palin: If you won’t stand behind your promises with real action and integrity, you don’t get my vote. And if you vote based on party, gender, or race—and end up getting betrayed—you have no one to blame but yourself. Use your most powerful tool—the vote—to demand real answers to your real problems. The power is literally in your hands. The opinions expressed in this commentary are solely those of the writer.

Kandida yo se maitre nan vandaj—yo fè ou panse ou se yon sèl moun ki importan pou yo a l’moman sa a. Mwen dwe admet, pandèm pou votan medyen an vin si absèd ke sa fè m fèt. Dabò—ki moun nou pale de? Fè yo espesifik. Gen kat pwoblèm fondamantal ki afekte votan medyen yo: Emplò: Nou te pèdi 600,000 emplò sous Prezidan Bush. Kòman McCain ak Obama pral kreye emplò yo? Kay: Kongsè a bay Wall Street milyè dola pou aji. Ki sa McCain ak Obama pral fè pou evite moun yo pèdi kay yo? Oui, yon moun di moun medyen yo dwe te li kondisyon yo—men si Wall Street resevwa aji, ki pou Main Street? Santèl: Sa pa yon blag—sa se yon kauz fondamantal pou bakrout. Mwen konnen pa lòt: An 2000, pandan mwen rapòte Konvensyon Demokratik, m’apèndis mwen te defèpte. Mwen te pase 5 jou nan yon hopital Los Angeles ak pi piti 70,000 dola nan faktir—mwen pa te gen asirans. Mwen te yon jurnaliz 29 an, sèlman, brise. Pressyon sa a te pousé mwen arriere sou mòrtgage mwen ak nan proses ekspropriasyon. Bakrout te sauve m. Gras ak Bondye, finans mwen te amelyore—ak jodi a, mwen fè dènye paiman mwen. McCain propozé yon kredi tan 5,000 dola pou santèl—men ou dwe peye avan ak atann pou remboursman. Ki sa ki pase si ou bezwen kòb la tout de suite? Obama ap apwòv santèl pou tout moun—men implementasyon an pa pral fèt tout de suite. Ki sa ki pase pandan Washington ap debati ak interes espesyal yo detwi plan an? Est-ce ke m ap atann MRI mwen pandan yo fini debati? Edikasyon: Pou plis moun, edikasyon se klé pou klas medyen an. Men kandida yo toujou pale sou burs. Sa pa rezoud pwoblèm an. Sa nou bezwen ouye se inegalite nan sistèm edikatif: District yo rich resevwa fòn ak enseyann ki pi bon. District yo pòv ap dwe fè avèk enseyann ki pi mò, sans ordinate ak menm sans chofaj. Konklizyon: Souveni jwèt fòt yo? Yo di enseyan yo: 'Si ou vle mwen signe, promèt mwen ta dwe jwe. Paske m pa jwe, pa mwen signe.' Se sa ki dwe moun medyen yo di McCain, Obama, Biden ak Palin: Si ou pa prèt pou moun ou nan fèt ak integrite, ou pa pral gen mwen. Ak si ou vot pou parti, seks, oswa ras—ak ou fini pèdi, ou pa gen okenn moun pou blamé sa, se ou mèt. Itilize outil ki pi pwojè ou—vòt ou—pou mande repons reyèl pou pwoblèm reyèl ou. Pwojè a se nan men ou. Opinyon ki ekri nan kominikasyon sa a se sèlman anpil auteur.

article_content: Once again, 'The Avengers' ruled the box office, outperforming three new releases in its third weekend with a formidable $55.1 million — a strong hold given its massive earnings. By Sunday, the Marvel blockbuster had amassed an estimated $457.1 million domestically, hitting the $450 million mark in just 17 days — shattering the previous record held by 'The Dark Knight,' which took 27 days. Globally, 'The Avengers' also surpassed 'Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest' to become Disney’s highest-grossing film ever, both at home and abroad. It now ranks fourth on the all-time worldwide chart, trailing only 'Avatar,' 'Titanic,' and 'Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows — Part 2.' Meanwhile, 'Battleship' sank on arrival with a disappointing $25.3 million opening — the weakest domestic launch ever for a film with a $200 million or higher budget. Universal spent $209 million on the PG-13 action flick, and its opening lagged behind this year’s other major flop, 'John Carter,' which debuted with $30.2 million. Actor Taylor Kitsch, known for 'Friday Night Lights,' now stars in two of the year’s biggest box-office failures. While 'Battleship' earned $226.8 million overseas — helping offset losses — its U.S. performance remains a major setback. Audience feedback was lukewarm: CinemaScore gave it a 'B,' but it struggled to attract younger viewers — 55% were 30 or older, and men made up 57% of ticket buyers. Universal hopes the Memorial Day weekend will boost its second week. 'The Dictator' landed in third place with $17.4 million in its opening weekend (a five-day total of $24.5 million after a Wednesday debut). Though this marked a dip from Sacha Baron Cohen’s earlier hits — 'Borat' ($26.5M) and 'Bruno' ($30.6M) — the film showed better momentum, rising 16% from Friday to Saturday, unlike 'Bruno,' which plummeted 39%. Produced for $65 million, 'The Dictator' drew a young, male crowd: 65% male, 56% under 25. Overseas, it earned $30.3 million across 29 markets, topping the charts in the UK, Germany, and Australia. However, its CinemaScore of 'C' raises concerns about staying power. 'What to Expect When You're Expecting' opened poorly with just $10.5 million. The $40 million romantic comedy, featuring Cameron Diaz, Jennifer Lopez, Elizabeth Banks, Chris Rock, and Dennis Quaid, appealed mostly to women — 70% of its audience — and older viewers — 64% over 25. CinemaScore awarded it a 'B-,' reflecting tepid audience enthusiasm. Other releases saw mixed results: 'Dark Shadows' tumbled 57% to $12.8 million, bringing its domestic total to $50.9 million and global haul to $81.3 million. In limited release, 'Crooked Arrows' surprised with $280,000 from 55 theaters, while 'The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel' continued its strong run, earning $3.3 million from 178 locations — a 22% increase despite no added screens. Conversely, the British comedy 'Hysteria' debuted weakly with just $40,800 from five theaters.

Dimanch, fim Marvel sa a te genyen envesti 457.1 milyon dola nan domesik, te atenn 450 milyon dola an seyèt jounen sèlman — ki te kase rekòd ki te pètèt pa 'The Dark Knight,' ki te bezwen 27 jounen. 'What to Expect When You're Expecting' te ouvri mal avèk sèlman 10.5 milyon dola. CinemaScore te donnen 'B-' pou li, ki reflete entewes ti ti. Autre fim yo te gen rezilta mèl: 'Dark Shadows' te tonbe 57% pou 12.8 milyon dola, ki amène total domesik li a pou 50.9 milyon dola ak total mondial pou 81.3 milyon dola. Nans distribisyon limité, 'Crooked Arrows' te surpriz avèk 280,000 dola nan 55 sinema, menm 'The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel' te kontinye son bon performans, te genyen 3.3 milyon dola nan 178 endri — yon pwogres 22% menm si pa te ajoute sinema. article_content: In a groundbreaking medical milestone, a woman in the United States became the first to receive a near-total face transplant — a 22-hour operation conducted in December at the Cleveland Clinic. Led by Dr. Maria Siemionow, the surgical team reconstructed her face using tissue from a deceased donor, restoring abilities she had lost after severe trauma: she can now breathe through her nose, taste food, drink from a cup, and even smell coffee — simple pleasures most people never think twice about. Before the surgery, she had no nose, upper jaw, or right eye, and struggled with daily tasks and social stigma — strangers often shouted insults on the street. Now, despite still avoiding public attention, she finds comfort in touching her face and feeling a nose where there was once none. Her surgeon stresses that rebuilding function mattered more than perfect looks: 'No one’s focused on beauty right now,' Siemionow said. The transplant included skin, muscles, nerves, arteries, veins, eyelids, and even the hard palate — all essential for basic human interaction. While the procedure has been done before in France and China, this marks the first time such a complex reconstruction succeeded in the U.S. The Chinese recipient, Li Guoxing, passed away in July under unclear circumstances. Because transplant recipients must take immune-suppressing drugs for life, cancer patients are currently ineligible. But researchers are exploring ways to reduce or eliminate this lifelong burden. Meanwhile, scientists are diving deeper into the genetics behind facial development, uncovering how mutations in genes like TCOF1 cause conditions such as Treacher Collins syndrome — a rare disorder affecting roughly 1 in 50,000 births. Understanding these genes may not only help treat deformities but also explain why human faces vary so much across populations. As Dr. Ethylin Jabs noted at the AAAS meeting, we’re entering an era where facial conditions might be treated medically — not just surgically. For this patient, the transplant wasn’t just about anatomy; it was about reclaiming dignity, connection, and the quiet joy of being seen as human again.
translated_content: Mounmèn moun ki te fèt nan Etazini, yon fanm te resevwa yon transplanti pòtè konsidere kòm 'preske total' — yon operasyon ki te dwe 22 lè a, fèt desanm lan nan Klinik Cleveland. Anndan ekip ki te dirije pa Doktè Maria Siemionow, yo te rekonsitwi pòtè a avèk tisik ki te vini nan yon donè kadafer, pou yo retounen kapasite yo te pèdi aprè yon traumatism grav: li kapab aje ak nez la, goute manje a, bòd kafé a, epi menm santi kafé a — bagay senp ki genyen moun yo pa pènse yo. Avan operasyon an, li te gen okenn nez, mandibul oswa èy la dwe, epi li te gen pwoblèm pou fè aktivite yo jodi a epi te eksperyence stigman sosyal — moun ki te krize yo sou roud la. Apre sa, malgre li pa vle wè moun yo, li findi konfòtabl nan tounen sou pòtè a epi santi yon nez la oukòs ki te genyen. Chirurgien an mete aksan sou restituisyon fonksyon yo plis pase estetik: 'Moun pa renmen konsidere belè a jodi a,' di Siemionow. Transplanti a te envolvi peyi, mous, nèf, artè, vein, poulè, epi menm palat dur la — tout sa yo esansiel pou interaksyon entènman yo. Menm si operasyon sa a te fèt deja nan Frans ak Chine, sa se premye fwa ke yon rekonsitision komplè sa a te reyisi nan Etazini. Resepsyan Chine a, Li Guoxing, te mouri julya a nan kondisyon ki pa klè. Poukisa rezipyan yo dwe pran medikaman ki bloke imunitè pou tout lavi, moun ki gen kansè pa kapab resevwa transplanti sa yo. Menm tan an, sitwasyon sa a te eseye pou moun yo reduk oswa elime sa a konsèvman. Anmwen, syantifik yo ap etidye pi fò nan jenetik pa genèz pòtè a, pou yo konprann kòman moutasyon nan jen TCOF1 ka kousi kondisyon tankou sindrom Treacher Collins — yon kondisyon ki afekte 1 pou 50,000 nesans. Konprann jen sa yo kapab ede nou pou traite deforme yo, menm tou pou konprann poukisa pòtè moun yo diferan anndan popilasyon yo. Kòm Doktè Ethylin Jabs te di nan konferans AAAS, nou ap antre nan yon erè ou lè ki kapab traite kondisyon pòtè a medikman — pa sèlman chirurgicalman. Pou fanm sa a, transplanti a pa sèlman te pou anatomi; li te pou reklamè dignite, koneksyon, epi jouisman senp nan itilite yo konsidere moun.

article_content: Barcelona utility player Javier Mascherano has come to the defense of teammate Lionel Messi, arguing that criticism of the superstar forward has been excessive. The 27-year-old believes Messi has set the bar so high through his remarkably consistent performances over the years, leading to unrealistic expectations. He told Tot Sant Cugat: 'Criticism of Messi, on several occasions, has been excessive. We are accustomed to unimaginable things—only he can do them—and when he doesn’t score, it doesn’t mean he isn’t good. It’s practically impossible to see him play badly.' 'Everything Barcelona has achieved in recent years has been thanks to players like Messi, Andrés Iniesta, and Xavi,' he added. 'They’ve made this team one of the best in history. Messi has given a lot to Barcelona, and Barcelona has given a lot to Messi too.' Messi has already scored six goals for the Catalan club this season, including a brace against Granada last weekend, pushing his total goal tally for the club past 400. Messi and his teammates aim to bounce back from their midweek Champions League defeat against PSG when they face Rayo Vallecano on Saturday night.

article_content: Once a sacred ritual, the family dinner has become a quiet affair — not because of conflict, but because of distraction. New findings from the Museum of London reveal that while British households still gather around the table, the depth of conversation has sharply declined. Instead of debating politics or global events, families are more likely to chat about the summer heatwave, Andy Murray’s Wimbledon triumph, or the arrival of Prince George. These uplifting, locally resonant moments dominate dinner chatter, pushing complex issues like the economy or healthcare to the sidelines. Only one in five families report regularly discussing politics, and nearly half say they struggle to connect meaningfully with each other. The average meal lasts just 22 minutes of actual talking — with nearly half of all dinners eaten while watching TV. Parents cite exhaustion, packed schedules, and the ever-present glow of smartphones and tablets as barriers to real connection. Sharon Ament, Director of the Museum of London, notes that while light topics offer easy common ground, they also mask a deeper trend: families are losing the habit of listening to each other. With one in four parents feeling out of touch with their children’s lives, the dinner table, once a hub of storytelling, is becoming a silent stage.

Rezilta nouvo yo nan Mwizèm London montre ke moun britanik yo toujou renmen ranpli tab la, men deepèr konvèrsasyon yo te kourbe. Plutot pase debate sou politik ak evenman mondyal, fami yo plis pataje aktyèlman chalè an, viktwi Andy Murray nan Wimbledon, oswa naissan Prens Jòj. Momen pozitif sa yo, ki rezonab lokalman, domine konvèrsasyon yo sou tab la, pou mete enpozan tankou ekonomi ak sante nan aryè-plan. Se sèlman yon kinsen fami ki di yo diskute regilyèman sou politik, ak preske mitan yo di yo gen pwoblèm pou fè yon koneksyon meyè. Dinnè a pase sèlman 22 minit nan konvèrsasyon akti — ak preske mitan tout dinnè yo mange devan televizyon an. Paran yo cite fatig, orè yo fò, ak lumanèt kontinyèl telefòn ak tablèt yo kòm baryèr pou koneksyon reyèl. Sharon Ament, Direktè Mwizèm London, fèn ke menm si tem sa yo fasil pou jeneralize, yo toujou kache yon tendans pi fò: fami yo pèd abitid lan pou ekoute lòt yo. Avèk yon kwen moun ki di yo pa konnen sa ki pase nan livè yo, tab dinnè a, ki te yon sente istwa yo, vin yon etaj silans.

article_content: Wealthy travelers are lining up to be among the first to fly in the lap of ultimate luxury aboard Etihad Airways’ new £12,500 suite on the world’s largest passenger jet. The Gulf carrier announced that The Residence—an ‘apartment in the sky’ featuring three rooms, a Savoy Academy-trained personal butler, and an in-flight chef capable of crafting custom menus—has sold out for the initial ten flights between Abu Dhabi and London Heathrow. Built by B/E Aerospace in the UK, this ultra-luxurious, Wi-Fi-enabled cabin is the crown jewel of Etihad’s first Airbus A380, which has a total capacity of just under 500 passengers. The Residence, measuring 125 square feet, is the first of its kind and was designed by leading interior designers and hospitality experts with passenger comfort and privacy in mind. The living room features a Poltrona Frau leather sofa with a retractable ottoman controlled by touchscreen, two dining tables, a chilled drinks cabinet, and a 32-inch flat-screen TV. When it’s time to rest, guests retreat to a bedroom adorned with delicate fabrics and furnished with a natural-fiber mattress, Egyptian cotton sheets, and a selection of pillows. The £12,500 fare covers a one-way trip for two people, including a private chauffeur for airport transfers, private check-in, and access to an exclusive lounge. Bookings for The Residence have far exceeded the typical 50% reservation rate for first-class seats, according to Etihad CEO James Hogan, who told an industry conference in Dubai: 'We’ve been quite happy with the take-up. There’s a market there.' Etihad’s superjumbo Airbus A380s will also operate on routes to Sydney and New York in 2015, expanding the suite’s availability. For travelers seeking a more affordable option, Etihad offers First Apartments—private cabins with Poltrona Frau upholstery, a wide armchair that converts into an 81-inch bed, a 24-inch TV, vanity cabinet, mini-bar, and wardrobe. Each First Apartment allows passengers to join a companion for meals or meetings, and dividers between units can be lowered to connect adjacent suites. The business class cabin offers comfortable studios with seats that convert into fully-flat beds. Peter Baumgartner, Etihad’s chief commercial officer, said: 'The Residence will set Etihad Airways apart from the rest of the industry and allow us to provide the complete range of world-class products and services to cater for the individual tastes of every VIP traveler. This is the culmination of five years of intensive effort and research into how Etihad Airways can provide an unparalleled VIP experience. Without doubt, we are ushering in a new era of luxury travel in commercial aviation.'

Karyè gòf sa a te anonse ke The Residence—yon 'apatman an nèt' ki gen twa chamb, yon sèvè pèsonèl ki te fòme pa Savoy Academy ak yon koch ki kapab prepare meni espesyal yo—te sòti pou dek fliyè premye yo ant Abou Dabi ak London Heathrow. Rezervasyon pou The Residence te depase tanpòt 50% ki te tipik pou sièj premyè klas, selon prezidan Etihad James Hogan ki te di konferans an nan Dubaï: 'Nou te trè kontan avèk takip la. Yo gen yon mache la.' Avyon Airbus A380 konsènne Etihad yo pral tou fè vwayaj yo nan Sydney ak New York an 2015, pou ekspande disponibilite suite a. Pasejè ki nan klas biznis yo vole nan studio konfòtab ki gen yon sièj ki konvèti an yon lit plat total. Peter Baumgartner, ofisè komèrsyal chèf Etihad, te di: 'The Residence pral fè Etihad Airways diferans avèk tout lòt endistri a ak nou pral kapab ofri tout gam chak prodwi ak sèvis mondèl pou repondi goûta chak pasejè VIP. article_content: Paul Smith is ready to turn the tables on Arthur Abraham this weekend in Berlin, where the two will meet again in a highly anticipated super-middleweight rematch. Last September, Smith walked away disappointed after the judges handed Abraham a unanimous victory — despite what Smith believed was a closely contested battle. The scorecards favored Abraham by wide margins, a result that left Smith questioning the decision but not his own ability. Training under Joe Gallagher in Berlin, Smith says he’s not just hoping to win this time — he knows he will. 'I thought I could beat him before,' he said. 'Now, I know I can.' He’s spent months sharpening his technique, improving his fitness, and studying every aspect of Abraham’s style. 'He’ll be in better shape this time, and I’ve trained for that. But so have I — better than ever.' Smith views their first encounter as a proving ground. Even though he didn’t get the win, he walked away convinced he belonged among the world’s elite. 'I proved to myself I can fight with the best. Now, I’m here to take what’s mine.' With no reliance on judges’ favor this time, Smith is focused on delivering a performance that leaves no room for doubt.

Septanm dènye a, Smith te konsidere l tris pandan jij yo te pèmèt Abraham pou gagnen ak yon dekizyon mounmòt — malgre ke Smith te kroire li te gen yon batay ki te trè fèt. Kòd skò yo te fèvòr Abraham avèk yon marge lòt, yon rezilta ki te lèman Smith sou jij yo, men pa sou kapasite li. Aprenti avèk Joe Gallagher nan Berlin, Smith di li pa sèlman espere gagnen sa fèn lan — li konnen li va gagnen. 'M te croi m kapab bat li avan,' li te di. 'Mantenant, m konnen m kapab.' Li te pase mwa yo ap fèt teknik li, amelyore fitnes li, ak etidye tout aspè stil Abraham. 'Li pral pi fèt sa fèn lan, epi m te prepare pou sa. Men m tou, m pi fèt pase jan m te a.' Smith wè kònta premye a kòm yon esèy pou montre kapasite li. Menm si li pa te gagnen, li te lwen konvi ke li ta dwe nan nivo mondyal. 'M te prouve mwen kapab bata avèk pi bon yo. Mantenant, m la pou pran sa ki mwen ta dwe a.' Apre pa sipoze sou fèvòr jij yo sa fèn lan, Smith se fokis sou yon prestasyon ki pa lajèn kòm sa.

article_content: Two U.S. embassy officials were wounded in a shooting on Tuesday at Antonella 2012, a club located in the basement of a mall in northeast Caracas, Venezuela. According to Miroslava Gómez, a police spokeswoman, the incident occurred at the establishment, which mall security confirmed is a strip club. Signs posted at the entrance declared it a 'weapon-free zone' and prohibited entry to unaccompanied women, couples, and anyone under 30. Images of dancers around poles adorned the interior walls. Dr. Carlos Pacheco, a physician at a Caracas hospital, confirmed that one official sustained gunshot wounds to the abdomen and leg, while the other was shot in the abdomen. Both injuries were non-life-threatening. The officials are affiliated with the embassy’s defense liaison office, according to two unnamed U.S. officials familiar with the case. The U.S. State Department acknowledged the incident but declined to disclose the identities of the injured or confirm the venue’s nature. Spokesperson Patrick Ventrell referred to it only as 'some sort of social spot' and stated he had 'no information on the site whatsoever' when directly asked if it was a strip club. The department confirmed it was coordinating with Venezuelan authorities and that embassy security and medical staff had visited the hospital and contacted the officials’ families. No arrests have been reported.

Selon Miroslava Gómez, yon spesyalis pòlis, incident la te pase nan endiristri sa a, ki sekirite mal la konfime se yon kliyb striptiz. Panj yo ki afiche sou entree a te deklare li 'zon san arm' epi refize entree pou fèm nan pa akòmpagne, koupl, ak tout moun ki gen moin de 30 an. article_content: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld Luis Suarez’s four-month ban from competitive football following his bite on Italy’s Giorgio Chiellini during the 2014 World Cup. However, CAS has significantly narrowed the scope of the ban, allowing the Barcelona forward to train with his new team, attend matches, and participate in promotional and administrative duties. Suarez will be officially unveiled at Barcelona’s Nou Camp on Monday and is set to train with the squad starting Friday. He is eligible to play in the Joan Gamper Trophy friendly against Mexican side Leon on Monday, provided he is fit. The original FIFA-imposed sanction — which prohibited all football-related activity — has been revised by CAS, which determined that banning training and public appearances was disproportionate. The ban now applies only to official matches. Suarez remains suspended from all competitive matches for Barcelona until October 26, when they face Real Madrid at the Bernabéu. He is also barred from playing in Uruguay’s next eight official international fixtures. This is Suarez’s third major disciplinary incident involving biting, following previous offenses at Ajax in 2010 and Liverpool in 2013. He has also faced sanctions for racially abusive behavior toward Patrice Evra in 2011. Despite the controversy, Barcelona completed its £75 million signing of Suarez in July, and the club has maintained support for the player. He has been maintaining fitness independently during his suspension. CAS stated the revised sanction ensures the punishment fits the offense while avoiding undue harm to Suarez’s professional development beyond the suspension period. Full hearing details will be released at a later date.

CAS te di ke sètenn modifiye a pèmèt pou peyi a gen yon sanzasyon ki konvenn avèk ofans lan, san fèt domaj pou devlopman profesional Suarez aprè sètenn lan. Detay komplet anpliwa pral piblie pi ta.

article_content: Nvidia has informed its Chinese clients that the release of its H20 artificial intelligence chip — the most capable of three models tailored for the Chinese market under new U.S. export limits — will be postponed until early next year, according to two people with knowledge of the situation. Originally expected to debut around mid-November, the chip’s launch is now anticipated between February and March 2024, due to technical difficulties encountered by server makers trying to integrate it into their systems. While the L20 variant is still on track for its planned release, details about the third chip, the L2, remain undisclosed. Nvidia, which was barred from exporting its top-tier A800 and H800 GPUs to China after Washington tightened restrictions in late 2022, is relying on these modified chips to retain its foothold in the world’s second-largest AI hardware market. Meanwhile, domestic players like Huawei are stepping in: Baidu, one of China’s leading tech giants, reportedly placed a major order for Huawei’s AI processors earlier this year — even before the export controls were officially announced — signaling a strategic pivot away from reliance on American suppliers. These shifts underscore how geopolitical regulations are reshaping global AI supply chains, giving homegrown Chinese firms a significant advantage.

Orijinalman antend pou lansman an lavi novanm, lansman pirogrèm la pral probabelman gen pou avèk fevriye ak mas 2024, kòm rezilta de pwoblèm teknik ki konnenn fabrikè servea yo nan integrasyon li. Menm lè l, vayant L20 a pa gen okenn reta epi pral lansmen sou orijinal li, men detay sou twazyèm pirogrèm, L2, pa konnen. Nvidia, ki te enfòme pa etazini yo pa kapab ekspte pirogrèm fò A800 ak H800 yo nan Chini aprè restriksyon yo te fèt lan dènye novanm 2022, ap chache pou retenn posisyon li nan mache AI ki pi fò de monde a. Nan frans, jeneral kominote lokal tankou Huawei ap monte: Baidu, yon sèl nan grand kompani teknoloji Chini yo, te fè yon komand fòm pou pirogrèm AI Huawei an anvan mandamant yo te anonsye — sa ki evidans yon pivot strategik ki vle moun yo pa pi fò nan fournisseur Etazini yo. Changman sa yo montre kòm politik geopolitik yo ap rekonstwi kadeyè akseptasyon AI mondyal la, ak avantage pou entèpriz lokal Chini yo.

article_content: Van Cliburn, the acclaimed classical pianist who received a New York ticker-tape parade after winning the prestigious International Tchaikovsky Competition in Moscow in 1958, died Wednesday after a battle with bone cancer, his publicist said. "He died peacefully at his home in Fort Worth, Texas, surrounded by loved ones," said spokeswoman Mary Lou Falcone. Cliburn, 78, won the competition just months after the Soviet Union launched Sputnik I — the world’s first artificial satellite — shocking the United States. His triumph came at a low point in Cold War morale and became a powerful symbol of American resilience and artistic excellence. When his illness was revealed last August, Falcone noted, "His spirits are high." "Van Cliburn was an international legend for over five decades — a great humanitarian and a brilliant musician whose light will continue to shine through his extraordinary legacy," she said Wednesday. "He will be missed by all who knew and admired him, and by countless others who never met him." He was widely credited with helping to ease cultural tensions between the United States and the Soviet Union. Cliburn toured the USSR multiple times during the height of the Cold War. Considered one of the greatest pianists of the 20th century, Cliburn performed for every U.S. president since Harry Truman, according to his official biography. At the end of his 1958 ticker-tape parade, the 23-year-old addressed the crowd at New York City Hall: "I appreciate more than you will ever know that you are honoring me, but the thing that thrills me the most is that you are honoring classical music. Because I’m only one of many. I’m only a witness and a messenger. I believe deeply in the beauty, structure, and invisible architecture of music — its importance for all generations, for the young people who will come after us. It shapes their minds, refines their attitudes, and instills lasting values. That’s why I am so grateful you’ve honored me in this spirit." CNN’s Douglas Hyde contributed to this report.

Van Cliburn, pianis klasis ki te resevwa yon parèd kòs tike nan New York aprè li gagnen Konkou Inètènasyonal Tchaikovsky nan Moskow an 1958, te mouri merkredi aprè yon bataj kont kansè os, li te di sèvis publik li. "Li te mouri paèzman nan kay li nan Fort Worth, Texas, entouré de timoun yo," te di spokeswman Mary Lou Falcone. Cliburn, 78 an, te gagnen konkou sa a lè kout moun ki te lansman Sputnik I — satelit artifiyèl premye nan mond lan — ki te etonè Etazini. Viktwar li te vin yon simbol pou rezilans ak ekselans artistik ameriken nan yon moman kri fòt nan Guèf Frid. Kanmèm li te revele malad li a aout deren, Falcone te anonse, "Espri yo te enpòtan." "Van Cliburn te yon legenn inètènasyonèl pandan plis pase sink antèn — yon gran umanitè ak yon mizisyen jeni koulyè li ta konn lavi a atravè legasi li ekstraòdinè,"
ti di li merkredi. "Li ta manke tout moun ki te konnen ak admire li, ak tout moun ki pa te konnen li." Li te anndan plis konsidere kòm yon figi ki te ede a detend tanson kiltirèl ant Etazini ak Union Sovièt. Cliburn te fèt travèl nan URSS plizyè fwa nan peyòd pi fòt guèf frid la. Konsidere yon nan pi bon pianis syèk 20 a, Cliburn te pleye pou chak prezidan Etazini depi Harry Truman, daprè biyografi ofisyèl li a. A kòt fin parèd kòs tike an 1958, moun ki te 23 an yo te pale devan foule nan City Hall New York: "Mwen rekonèt pi fò pase ou ta konn moun yo ki honoré m, men bagay ki fè m senpi plis se ou honoré mizik klasis. Li ap fòme esprit yo, refine atitud yo, ak implan valè yo. Se pou sa m si remerisye ou te honoré m nan esprit sa a." Douglas Hyde nan CNN te kontribiye a rapò sa a.

article_content: Lawyers for actors Kevin Costner and Stephen Baldwin began jury selection this week in a federal court in New Orleans, where a lawsuit over stock sales tied to oil spill cleanup technology is being heard. Baldwin and New Orleans businessman Spyridon Contogouris claim they were misled into selling their shares in a company developing oil-water separation equipment—just days before BP announced a $52 million order for 32 of its machines in June 2010. They argue that had they known about BP’s imminent deal, they wouldn’t have sold: Baldwin’s 10% stake, sold for $500,000, may have been worth nearly $3.8 million, and Contogouris’s 28%, sold for $1.4 million, could have been valued at over $10.6 million. Costner and his business partner Patrick Smith, however, maintain that Baldwin and Contogouris sold their shares voluntarily, seeking to exit a deteriorating partnership and pursue other opportunities. The defense notes that BP’s potential involvement was widely reported in the media, and Costner had publicly discussed the technology during congressional testimony just two days before the sale. Court documents state that Costner was reportedly stunned and furious upon learning of the sale, as it meant the plaintiffs cashed out before the company generated any revenue. Both actors are listed as key witnesses and are required to attend every day of the trial.

Baldwin ak nannan biznis Nò Orléans Spyridon Contogouris prétend ke yo te piyek yo nan vandèt aks yo nan yon kompani ki developpe tekonoloji sekresyon oliv-ea, kèk jou avan BP te anonsye yon komandman $52 milyon pou 32 machin yo nan jen 2010. Défens la montre ke involvman BP te konn nan medya, ak Costner te te diskute tekonoloji a nan teyemèn kongres lan de jou avan vandèt-la. Dokiman kòt la montre ke Costner te sot ekspresé yon sòti sòti ak fèn ak aprann ke yo te vandèt, paske sa te pèmèt plenitif yo kase yo avan kompani a te genyen anyen. De aktè yo sou lis témoen ki dwe tèmònen, ak yo dwe prensen chak jou nan proses la.

article_content: Sandwich chain Jimmy John's disclosed a potential cybersecurity breach affecting 216 of its corporate and franchised locations. The breach, first identified on July 30, occurred when an intruder gained access to login credentials belonging to a third-party vendor. Using these credentials, the attacker remotely accessed point-of-sale systems across affected stores between June 16 and September 5. According to the company, the compromised data includes card numbers, and in some instances, cardholder names, expiration dates, and CVVs — but only for transactions made by swiping physical cards in-store. Payments made manually or online were not affected. More than 12 of the impacted locations are in the Chicago area, based on a list released by Jimmy John's. However, no specific store has been confirmed as compromised. The breach has since been contained, and customers can safely use their cards at all locations. Jimmy John's, headquartered in Champaign, Illinois, has engaged forensic cybersecurity experts to support its investigation. This incident follows a string of high-profile retail breaches, including those at Target, Home Depot, Michaels Stores, and Neiman Marcus. Last week, Home Depot reported that up to 56 million payment cards may have been compromised in its own attack — a scale larger than the Target breach.

Apre sa, atakè a te akse pwograme pwen vandaj sou lokasyon yo afekte ant 16 jen ak 5 septanm. Jimmy John's, ki gen siyèt la nan Champaign, Illinois, te engaje ekspèt siyètik pou aji ak envestigasyon yo. Eveneman sa a siv yon seri brenn siyètik enpotan nan sektor retail, tankou Target, Home Depot, Michaels Stores, ak Neiman Marcus. Lètè vini, Home Depot te annonse ke 56 milyon kard paiman an te posibman vole nan atak li — yon ekskalasyon ki pi enpotan pase brenn Target.

article_content: By Tim Shipman, Deputy Political Editor. No one can accuse Communities Secretary Eric Pickles of not taking his job seriously. While most ministers focus on shaping national policy, Mr. Pickles took direct action when he spotted a group of travelers heading toward his constituency. He followed them in his car and confronted them after they parked on a cricket pitch. Pickles — who has introduced multiple measures to prevent unauthorized encampments on greenfield land — first noticed their convoy exiting a motorway as he drove home. He watched as 40 travelers with 15 caravans moved onto the cricket pitch around 10 p.m. last Thursday. He pulled over, asked them what they were doing, and, unsatisfied with their responses, contacted the police and local council. One Conservative source said the incident led to jokes in the House of Commons, where Pickles has been nicknamed 'P.I. Pickles.' The source added: 'People in Whitehall know you don’t mess with Eric. This is a great example of local action.' Following police involvement, the travelers were served a Section 61 eviction notice and ordered to leave the field in Mountnessing, Essex. Failure to comply could have resulted in unlimited fines under new regulations introduced by Pickles. However, in what appears to be retaliation, some travelers returned the next day and deliberately damaged the cricket square, forcing the Mountnessing Cricket Club to cancel its weekend match. Witnesses reported the travelers drove repeatedly across the pitch, performing handbrake turns to ruin the grass. The club’s groundskeeper said: 'It was clear they were trying to plow up the pitch and cause maximum damage. We were lucky there hadn’t been rain — the surface was hard. If it had rained, the field would have been destroyed.' Someone had attempted to carve initials near the crease but abandoned the effort because the ground was too firm. Last night, Pickles told the Daily Mail: 'I’m glad they’ve left, but this appalling behavior shows we’re dealing with a small minority who have no respect for the law. This government is cracking down on unauthorized traveler sites because the public wants fair play and proper enforcement of planning rules. After seeing the damage, I’ve never felt it more important to protect our green belt and the communities around it.' Karl Afteni, chairman of Mountnessing Parish Council, confirmed £600 in damage and said the club will close for a month while £1,500 is spent on enhanced security. 'Nothing can stop a determined effort with machinery and power tools — but we must make unlawful access harder,' he said. Under the Coalition government, planning guidance now classifies any traveler encampment — temporary or permanent — in the green belt as 'inappropriate development.' Local councils have been instructed to strictly limit new traveler sites in open countryside.

Pickles te fè aksyon direk lè li te wè yon gwoup travayè yo te ale vini sou konstitwans li. Li te suivi yo nan machin li epi te konfronte yo aprè yo te mete yo sou yon kous kricket. Pandan koalisyon an, direktiv planifikasyon an te fèt pou klasifikasyon tout kampman travayè — tempòrèl oswa pèrmanent — nan zòn vèt kòm 'devlopman inapropriye.' article_content: Pop star James Blunt has publicly clashed with Labour MP Chris Bryant after Bryant suggested that British culture is overly dominated by celebrities from elite private schools—naming Blunt and actor Eddie Redmayne as examples. Blunt, who attended the prestigious Harrow School, responded sharply, arguing that his background didn’t open doors—it actually blocked them. In a candid open letter shared on social media, Blunt explained that his family couldn’t afford to connect him to the music industry. He bought his first guitar with money earned from packing sandwiches during holidays, learned four chords from a friend, and was repeatedly told by industry insiders that his upper-class accent made him unmarketable—even one label asked him to adopt a different voice, jokingly suggesting he try speaking Russian. Despite graduating from university and serving as an army officer, Blunt says everyone around him thought pursuing music was a ridiculous dream. He eventually found success in the U.S., where his background wasn’t held against him, and now accuses Bryant of fueling resentment instead of opportunity. Bryant, who himself attended Cheltenham College and Oxford, replied that he admires Blunt’s work and isn’t attacking his talent—but argues that financial hardship makes artistic ambition exponentially harder for those without privilege. The exchange has ignited a national conversation about whether success in the arts stems from innate talent and grit—or from inherited connections—and whether criticizing privilege is fair when even the critics benefited from it.
translated_content: Jame Blunt, yon chante akòmèd, te fèt avèk deputè Lòbè Chris Bryant aprè Bryant te di ke kilti britanik la te tro pwopòsyone pa istèl ki te alèn epi lèkòl privè—kite Blunt ak aktè Eddie Redmayne tankou ezyèm. Blunt, ki te alèn epi lèkòl prestijyoz Harrow, te reponn vireman, di li ke sa ki te fèt li pa te ouvri pòt yo—li te bloke yo. Nan yon let ouvè ki te partajé sou rezo sosyal, Blunt te eksplike ke fami li pa te kapab fè li konnen moun nan endistri mizik la. Li te achte yon gitar la avèk lajan li te regagne pandan travay lajèn li te fèt (pako sandwij), li te aprann katre kòd avèk yon zanmi, ak te di repete pa moun nan endistri a ke akant li 'posh' li te imarketab—menm yon sèl etikèt te demann li si li kapab chanje akant li, ak jokis di li pou li eseye pale Rous. Malgre ke li te fini universite ak te sèvi tankou ofisye an armè, Blunt di ke tout moun ki entou li te pènse ke vle fè mizik se yon ide fòl. Li te reyeni siksè nan Etazini, kote li te pa jere kontrè, ak li maintenan akize Bryant de fèt envy ak pa ouvri oportunite. Bryant, ki toujou te alèn epi lèkòl Cheltenham ak Oxford, te reponn ke li admire travay Blunt ak li pa atake talan li—menm li di ke difikilte ekonomik fè yon aspè mizikèl pi fòk pou moun ki pa gen resous. Ekschaj la te debwaze yon konversasyon nasyonal sou si siksè nan art la vini nan talan ak gwo kouraj la—oswa nan koneksyon enfèritè—ak si kritik privilej la fèk lèmoun ki kritike yo tou jwenn avantage yo.

article_content: In a clever, if questionable, move, a Brazilian tech firm named Gradiente has launched a budget smartphone called the 'iphone Neo One' — deliberately echoing Apple’s iconic name while running entirely on Android. Though the name plays on Apple’s brand power, the device bears little resemblance to the iPhone beyond the lowercase 'p'. With a modest 700MHz processor and a 3.7-inch screen running Android 2.3 Gingerbread, it’s a far cry from Apple’s flagship devices in performance or design. The phone features dual SIM support, a 5-megapixel rear camera and a basic 0.3-megapixel front camera — no flash included — but in sunny Brazil, that may not matter much. Priced at just 599 Brazilian reais (roughly £180), it’s being sold in ten interest-free installments, making it accessible to price-sensitive buyers. While Apple famously sued Samsung over design similarities, it remains to be seen whether they’ll target Gradiente for this more subtle naming tactic. For Android users in Brazil, the phone offers a low-cost entry point into the ecosystem — and with Google apps like Maps, Gmail, and YouTube already available, the user experience isn’t entirely alien. Outside Brazil, however, there are no plans to distribute the device.
translated_content: Nan kòm yon manèv kòkèt, men ki gen yon ti konsèn, yon kompani tekonolojik Brazilyen ki rele Gradiente te lanse yon telefòn abitèl ki rele 'iphone Neo One' — ki fè yon kopi de nomenklati Apple tout enpatik, men li itilize Android. Menm si non sa a fè yon kopi de imaj Apple, aparèy sa a pa rezeme pa gen anyen ak iPhone Apple yo, se sèlman lèt 'p' ki genyen miniskil. Apre 700MHz, epi ekràn 3.7-inch ki itilize Android 2.3 Gingerbread, li pi piti ke iPhone Apple yo nan prestashon ak konsepsyon. Telefòn sa a gen de sim, yon kamera aryè 5 megapiksèl ak yon kamera avan 0.3 megapiksèl — pa gen flash, men nan Brazil ki gen dlo solèy la, sa pa enpotan. Prix li se 599 reais Brazilyen (apwoksime 180£), epi li disponib nan 10 paie san intewèt, sa ki fè li ase abordab pou moun ki gen limis ekonomik yo. Même si Apple te fèt yon liti kont Samsung pou kopi konsepsyon yo, pa klè si yo pral pèse Gradiente pou kopi non sa. Pou moun ki itilize Android an Brazil, telefòn sa a pèmèt yo dwek antre nan ekosistèm la ak yon pri piti, ak aplikasyon Google tankou Maps, Gmail, ak YouTube ki disponib, eksperyans itilizatè a pa totalman etranje. Anndan Brazil, pa gen okenn plan pou distribye aparèy sa a.

article_content: World No. 1 Rafael Nadal has been placed in Group A at the ATP World Tour Finals in London, where he will face Novak Djokovic, Tomas Berdych, and Andy Roddick in the group stage. Group B features World No. 2 Roger Federer of Switzerland, alongside Sweden’s Robin Soderling, Britain’s Andy Murray, and Spain’s David Ferrer. The tournament kicks off Sunday with Murray taking on Soderling at 1400 GMT, followed by Federer versus Ferrer at 2000 GMT. On Monday, Djokovic meets Berdych at 1400 GMT, and Nadal battles American Roddick in the evening session. In Monday’s updated rankings, Soderling surged to No. 4 after capturing the Paris Masters title on Sunday. Meanwhile, Murray fell to No. 5 but remains buoyant about competing on home soil. Murray shared on his website: 'It’s an incredible atmosphere — a huge arena and one of the biggest events in tennis, just behind the Grand Slams. I’m really looking forward to it. My last few weeks haven’t been perfect, though I did win my first doubles title with my brother, which was special. Playing in front of a home crowd always gives me an extra boost. Winning here would be a huge psychological win — I’ll give it everything.' Federer, coming off a surprising semifinal loss to France’s Gael Monfils in Paris, is focused on London. Despite the setback, he remains confident, citing his strong physical condition and mental freshness. He told the ATP Tour’s official website: 'I feel good. I’m playing well. I believe I have a real chance to win in London. Physically, I’m healthy — finishing Paris without injury was a relief. Mentally, I’m refreshed. Victories matter, but being fit matters more. I’ll recover quickly from that loss. It wasn’t a bad match — I’m pleased with my performance. Of course, winning would’ve kept me in contention. Now, I shift focus to London and prepare fully.' Federer holds an impressive record at the season-ending event: 29 wins and just seven losses since his debut in 2002.

Gwoup B gen Roger Federer, ki se numèro 2 mondyal, ki se Suis, ansanm avèk Robin Soderling nan Sved, Andy Murray nan Angleter ak David Ferrer nan Espay. Tounen an komanse Dimanch la avèk Murray ki jwe Soderling a 1400 GMT, epi Federer ki jwe Ferrer a 2000 GMT. Lendi a, Djokovic ta jwe Berdych a 1400 GMT, epi Nadal ta jwe American Roddick nan swèt la. Klasman yo te piblie Lundi a, Soderling te monte nan pozisyon 4 aprè li gagné Paris Masters Dimanch la, menm si Murray te desann nan pozisyon 5, li ap espere avantage akèl li ka inspiré li nan London. Dènye semèn yo pa te anpil kòm m vle, men mwen te gagné premye tit mwen nan doblè avèk frè m, sa te koze, men jwe devan foule akèl toujou bon. Pèdi la ta yon bòn avantaž psikolojik, mwen ta bay tout mwen.' Federer, ki te pèdi yon defèt surpran nan demifinal Paris la kontra Gael Monfils, se fokisé sou London. Fizikman, mwen sante — fini Paris san lesyon te yon soulajman. Mentalman, mwen rete fraich. Gagnen se enportan, men sante se plis enportan. Mwen ta rekoverye rapid aprè pèd lan. Sa pa te yon mèt mal — mwen kontan avèk prestashon mwen. Bien sûr, si mwen te gagné, mwen ta gen chans gagné tounen an. Kounye a, mwen ap prepar pou London.' Federer gen yon konsèn impresif nan kousman sezon final: 29 gagn ak sevèn pèd nan pwochen 2002.

article_content: Prince Charles has come under fire for paying what critics call an unusually low tax rate on the £19 million income he received from the Duchy of Cornwall in 2012–2013. Labour MP Austin Mitchell accused the Prince of benefiting from a centuries-old legal structure by treating the Duchy as a private estate rather than a corporation — a designation that exempts it from corporation tax. While Charles does pay income tax — £4.4 million, or 23.6% of his gross income — Mitchell noted this is significantly lower than the 38% average paid by the poorest 25% of UK households. The Prince’s representatives argue that his official duties as heir to the throne qualify as legitimate business expenses, which are subtracted from his income before taxation. William Nye, his principal private secretary, explained that this tax treatment has been in place since 1993 and is fully authorized by the UK government. 'He pays income tax on what remains after covering his public responsibilities,' Nye said, emphasizing that this method mirrors how private entrepreneurs deduct necessary business costs. Meanwhile, in a separate development, Duchess Camilla hinted during a visit to a Cornish children’s hospice that the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge’s first child might arrive by the end of the week, reigniting media speculation. Kensington Palace declined to confirm the due date, though sources had previously indicated it was expected around mid-July.

Menm si Charles paye taks sib — 4.4 milyon £, oswa 23.6% sou reveni li total la — Mitchell te pwopoze sa a fèt anpil pi piti ke 38% ki gen pou vini nan 25% pi piti moun yo nan Angleterre. Reprizantan Prins la, William Nye, sekretè pèsonèl li, te ekspike ke sistèm sa a te anplwaye depi 1993 epi li egzakteman autorize pa gouvenman Angleterre. 'Li paye taks sib sou sa ki rive aprè li fin pase depans yo pou misyon publik yo,' Nye te di, mete aksan sou fason sa a rezime fason moun privi yo dedekte depans biznis yo nesesè. Anmèm, nan yon devlopman ki pa konekte, Dchesse Camilla te fèt yon alizman pandan yon vizit nan yon moun enfan Kornwal la pou fè konnen ke premye timoun Prins William ak Dchesse Kate a ka arive avèk fiyèn nan se a fèn semèn an, ki te reanime spikylasyon medya a. Biro pèsonèl William ak Kate nan Kensington Palace te refize konfime dat la, men sòs yo te indike ke dat la te estime nan mi jiyè.

article_content: I've spent years living and working on Tyneside, and I truly get why Newcastle United fans are so upset. Back in the day, I was a young football reporter earning barely enough to get by — by day, chasing stories, and by night, pouring drinks as a barman at the Tuxedo Royale, a quirky nightclub on a boat docked under the Tyne Bridge. The place had a spinning dance floor, flashy staff, and endless conversations about the Toon well into the morning. I often wonder why I ever moved away. After Saturday’s crushing 4-0 loss to Southampton, fans demanded Alan Pardew’s dismissal again — but he’s still in charge. The pressure keeps mounting weekly, yet owner Mike Ashley appeared unfazed, even cheerful, after the defeat. It’s hard to reconcile that with the pain fans feel. Back then, legends like Micky Quinn roamed the halls of the Tuxedo Royale. I even served Paul Gascoigne and his crew one night — if I’d known then what I know now, I’d have turned them away for their own sake. But for most people in that room, Newcastle United wasn’t just a team — it was their identity. Win or lose, that’s all they talked about. Sure, trophies were scarce, but fans found pride in Shearer’s grit, Ginola’s flair, Quinn’s goals, and Keegan’s fire. Today? There’s nothing to celebrate. The anger at Pardew is real, but fans are also screaming for answers from Ashley — answers he’s shown no interest in giving. The club misses players who embody local pride, like Shearer did. The golden era of Ginola in black and white feels like a distant memory. Pardew did have moments — remember that incredible run of seven wins in nine games last season? Until Cabaye was sold and never replaced. Now, his credibility is at rock bottom. Managers change, but owners stay. And that’s why it’s always baffled me: why haven’t Newcastle fans pooled their resources and bought the club? Over 50,000 attend every home game. Thousands more — former residents, ex-pats, loyal supporters scattered across the UK and beyond — still bleed black and white. They have the numbers. They have the heart. Some even have the means. Imagine a fan-led trust — backed by wealthy supporters, legendary Geordies lending their names, and real power returned to those who care most. This isn’t fantasy. It’s possible. And frankly, after decades of disappointment, it’s long overdue. The city deserves better. The fans deserve control. I’ll be at St James’ Park this Saturday — a ground I hold dear, where I learned my trade. It’s emotional. So here’s my question to the Toon Army: if you hate Ashley and Pardew so much… why aren’t you buying the club yourself?

Anvan, mwen te yon rapòte fòtbòl ki pa genyen anpil — jounen la, mwen te chache istwa, ak nwit la, mwen te sèvi dlo kòm yon barmen nan Tuxedo Royale, yon naktik ki te sou yon bato anndan pòt Tyne Bridge. Endèk la te gen yon solèy ki tournen, plis fòm yo ki te pwotè, epi konvèsasyon anndan tout tan sou Toon. Mwen toujou mande mwen poukisa mwen te ale. Aprè defèt 4-0 yo te fèt sou Southampton, fan yo te demande Pardew yo te vire — men li toujou la. Pressyon an monte chak sezan, men mwenn Mike Ashley te parèt pa enpòtan, menm apre defèt sa a. Se difisil pou konprann sa avèk doule fan yo resèv. Anvan, legan konsa tankou Micky Quinn te al nan salòn Tuxedo Royale. Mwen menm te sèvi Paul Gascoigne ak zanmi yo yon nwit — si mwen te konnen sa mwen konnen anjodi a, mwen ta refizé yo pou bonè yo. Men pou plis moun nan salòn sa a, Newcastle United pa sèlman yon ekip — li te identite yo. Gagnen, pèdi, oubyen egalite, sa yo te vle pale de. Vre, trofè yo te rare, men fan yo te jwenn fièté nan kras Shearer, malis Ginola, gol Quinn, ak pasyon Keegan. Ajourdhui? Pa gen anyen pou fè fèt. Kolèr yo nan Pardew se vre, men fan yo toujou chache repons nan Mike Ashley — repons ki pa janm pèmèt yo. Kloub la manke jwèt ki montre fièté pou kloub ak vil la, tankou Shearer te fèt. Epoq doré Ginola nan nwa ak blan, li sanble lontan. Pardew te gen moman — souveni sa chain 7 gagnen nan 9 jwèt lan? Tan ke Cabaye te vende epi pa remplace. Ajourdhui, kredibilite li nan solèy. Enseman yo chanje, men mwenn yo te toujou la. E se poukisa mwen toujou panse: poukisa fan Newcastle pa fèt yon trist pou achte kloub la? Plis pase 50,000 moun pran jwèt a chak sezan. Milyèn lòt — ansi yo ki te leve, eksilé, fan loyèl ki rete anndan Royaume Uni ak lòt kote — toujou fèt nwa ak blan. Yo gen nomb yo. Yo gen kòd yo. Kèk nan yo gen mwayen yo. Imajine yon trist fan — apye sou fan rich, legan Geordie ki bay non yo, ak pouvwa ki retounen nan moun ki prèt pou yo. Sa pa fiksyon. Sa posib. Epi, aprè desèn de disan an, sa fèt lontan. Vil la mériti pi bon. Fan yo mériti kontwo a. Mwen pral nan St James’ Park sezan sa — yon stadyèm ki gen yon endri pou mwen, kote mwen te aprann metyè mwen. Se emosyonèl. Alòske mwen te konn mande fan Toon Army: si ou detest Mike Ashley ak Alan Pardew anpil… poukisa ou pa achte kloub la pou ou menm?

article_content: La Paz, Bolivia — Incumbent President Evo Morales has declared victory in Bolivia’s presidential election, citing a national exit poll that places him ahead with 61% of the vote. Although official results have not yet been released, analysts widely expect his third consecutive term, which would extend his leadership until 2020. Speaking to a jubilant crowd in La Paz, Morales thanked the Bolivian people and pledged to transform the nation into South America’s energy hub. He framed his win as a democratic victory for all those resisting capitalism and imperialism, dedicating it to the legacies of Fidel Castro and Hugo Chávez. As Bolivia’s first indigenous president, Morales rose to power in 2006 on a platform centered on uplifting the poor. His tenure has coincided with strong economic growth — including a 6.5% GDP increase in 2013 — though some citizens report feeling little improvement in their daily lives. Critics accuse Morales of centralizing power, particularly after a 2013 court ruling allowed him to run again, interpreting his previous term under Bolivia’s new constitution as his ‘first.’ His campaign slogan, 'With Evo, we’re doing well,' resonated with voters seeking continuity. Morales has drawn sharp criticism from U.S. officials, who view his policies as hostile. In 2008, he expelled the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration; in 2013, he ordered the departure of the U.S. Agency for International Development, accusing it of interference. He once claimed U.S. authorities might plant drugs on his plane to frame him for trafficking. Amid speculation last year that fugitive NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden might be aboard Morales’ plane, several European nations denied it landing rights. Snowden was not on board, but Morales had publicly offered him asylum. International observers, including former Guatemalan President Alvaro Colom, confirmed the election proceeded peacefully with no major irregularities. Voters cited economic stability and security as top concerns. Despite quiet streets due to election-day traffic restrictions, turnout appeared high and informed. Morales’ third term will end in 2020; he cannot seek re-election beyond that under current constitutional rules.

Menm si rezilta ofisyèl pa te publiye, analis yo te estime ke li ta kapab genyen tèm konsiktyf twazyèm li, ki ta voye li nan fonksyon l jiska 2020. Anrejou nan yon foule jojou nan La Paz, Morales te remerasyon popilasyon Bolivyen an ak li te pwomet pou fè peyi a vin kapital enerji Amerik Sou, epi li te prezante viktwa li kòm yon viktwa demokratik pou tout moun ki reziste kapitalis ak imperyalis, ak dedikasyon pou legati Fidel Castro ak Hugo Chávez. Kapitan premyè prezidan indijen Bolivi, Morales te monte pou pouvwa an 2006 sou yon platfòm ki te sentralize aksyon pou amelyore kondisyon moun pòv yo. Tèm li te koresponn ak otorite ekonomik fòt — yon gwosman PIB 6.5% an 2013 — men kèk moun ki di yo pa reswèt anyen nan jounen a jounen yo. Kritik yo akize Morales pou kontròl fòt pouvwa, pito apre yon kour 2013 ki te pèmèt li ranpli ankò, ki te interpreté tèm avan li sou konstitisyon nouvo a kòm 'premyè' li. Slogan kampan li, 'Avek Evo, nou ap al bon', te rezo nan elektè yo ki vle kontinuite. Morales te gen kritik fòt nan men ofisyèl Etazini, ki konsidere politik li kòm antipatik. An 2008, li te eksprime DEA Etazini; an 2013, li te dekri USAID, ak akize yo dènye. Li te deklare ke ofisyèl Etazini ka mete koka sou avyon li pou fè li kouspèk travay narkotik. An teyor ak vèsyon ke fèt NSA Edward Snowden ta kapab sou avyon Morales an 2013, plizyè nasyon Ewopeyen te refize li atèj la pou refwou. Snowden pa te sou avyon an, men Morales te ofri li azil publikman. Obyèv intènasional, tankou anvan prezidan Gwatémalèn Alvaro Colom, te konfime ke eleksyon an te pase san anyen enfòmasyon. Elektè yo te cite stabilité ekonomik ak sekirite kòm konsepn moun yo. Malgre rilman rive nan ròt yo poulèt, tèm eleksyon an te fò. Tèm twazyèm Morales ta fini an 2020; li pa kapab ranpli ankò aprè sa sou baze konstitisyonèl aktèl.

article_content: In Qadem Khel, Ghazni province, Afghanistan, the day begins with logistics: 85 halal Meals Ready to Eat (MREs) are counted out for a joint U.S.-Afghan operation. At FOB '4 Corners,' soldiers of the 172nd Infantry prepare for their mission, catching glimpses of home — a televised baseball game from Fenway Park, the national anthem sung by 11-year-old Rose Newton, an email confirming a mortgage approval. For many, this may be one of their last missions before the U.S. drawdown accelerates. Tonight, they plan an air assault into Qadem Khel, a village where the Taliban effectively governs. Intelligence suggests two high-value targets may be nearby — one identified by a photo showing him with and without thick, unkempt hair. Helicopters arrive under cover of darkness. With night-vision gear and precise coordination from their Afghan counterparts, U.S. troops board and descend onto a vast desert expanse. At dawn, they advance on foot, following the NATO directive: 'Afghan-led.' The Afghan soldiers — mostly from northern and northeastern provinces — lead the operation. To locals, they are outsiders, no less foreign than the Americans. Their pace is unhurried. In broad daylight, dozens of them stroll into town, entering homes without resistance. Doors that won’t open are simply left alone — even when a pocket knife fails to pry them open. When two boys are caught riding banned motorbikes, an Afghan soldier considers shooting the fuel tank but opts against it. Instead, the tires are deflated, and one boy receives a few firm slaps to the head — instant, informal justice, Afghan-style. Locals watch, unalarmed, almost amused. For them, this is the first contact with any government authority in over half a year. Captain Chris Barlow, with just eight weeks left in his tour, says villagers report the Taliban warn them over mosque loudspeakers before planting bombs — a chillingly organized form of local law. As the team searches a house where weapons were previously found, gunfire erupts. An A-10 Warthog roars overhead, but when it becomes clear women and children are nearby, the Americans call off the assault. At dusk, they retreat across open fields to the landing zone. With the whir of Chinook blades and a swirl of dust, they depart — possibly for the last time.

Nan FOB '4 Corners,' solèy yo nan 172nd Infantry ap prepar pou operasyon yo, ap jwenn ti koupe d'vyenn — yon match de baseball ki te transmis depi Fenway Park, l'anmenn nasyonal la chante pa Rose Newton, 11 an, yon imèl ki konfime yon mòtgaj. Pou plis, sa a ka fèt yon sèl fwa avan retreman U.S. a aksele. Nwit a, yo plan yon atak aèl nan Kadem Khel, yon vila kote Talibàn yo te domine. Enformasyon an sipoze ke de kòmèk valè pi wo yo ka nan zòn sa a — yon foto ki montre li avèk ak sans touvèl ki long. Helikoptè yo arive sou kouvet nwa. Ak otorizasyon visyon nwa ak koordinasyon presiz nan kote Afgan yo, troup U.S. yo monte ak desann sou yon ekstensyon vaj. Lè lèn, yo avanse a pied, an sivin direktiv NATO: 'Afgan-led.' Solèy Afgan yo — ki pral plis nan nò ak nò-est — ap mennen operasyon an. Pou popilasyon lokal yo, yo se etranje, pa moin fòk pito U.S. yo. Pase yo pa rapid. Lèn, desen moun yo al nan vil la, antre dan kay yo san rezistans. Kay ki pa ouvri yo simpleman kite yo — menm si yon koutèl pa kapab ouvri yo. Kouman de timoun yo te kapti ak moto ban yo. Yon solèy Afgan te panse tiri sou tanke gason yo, men li te refize. Plutot, yo defle tire yo, epi yon timoun ki pi shyè te resevwa kèk klap sou tèt li — jistis istantan, stile Afgan. Popilasyon lokal yo regarde, pa alarme, preske amize. Pou yo, sa a se premye kontak avèk anyen ki ressemble pouvwa gouvenman an depi sis mwa. Kapiten Chris Barlow, ki gen 8 jou pa travay li, di popilasyon yo di yo ke Talibàn yo avètis yo atravè loudspeaker moske yo avan yo mete bom yo — yon fòm jistis lokal ki fèy. Pendan ekip la chache yon kay kote arm yo te detekte anvan, yon tir envole. Yon A-10 Warthog fèt pasè, men lè li klè ke timoun ak fanm yo nan zòn sa a, U.S. yo abandone ide atak la. Lè nwa, yo retire atravè champ ouvri yo pou zòn atèjman. Avèk brèm de Chinook ak yon nube pouvyè, yo disparèt — posiblement pou dènye fwa.

article_content: They are often dismissed as pesky birds that spread disease — but to one couple, homing pigeons were their livelihood. Maria and Alberta Morales have seen their primary source of income vanish after 1,000 of their 2,200 pigeons were stolen. Thieves broke into their Marion County farm near Orlando, stealing hundreds of valuable homing pigeons and slaughtering an additional 100 baby birds, resulting in losses of nearly $20,000. The couple, who started their pigeon farm in 2012, believed it would fund their retirement. The birds, valued at around $18 each, were used for racing and recreational purposes, and could breed multiple times annually — making their true loss closer to $40,000 when accounting for future breeding potential. Maria Morales told the Orlando Sentinel: 'There is a huge demand for them. We have live-animal auctions in Marion County. Every time you go to an auction, if you have pigeons, you know for sure you'll sell out.' The owners believe the thieves knew exactly how valuable the birds were — yet cannot explain why they killed 100 young pigeons. Authorities suspect the intruders drove through an open field belonging to a neighbor, leading directly to the back of the coop.

Vòlè yo te vole plisè a pibèn valè yo nan yon ferm nan Marion County, non loin Orlando, ak tue 100 pitit pibèn depi, fè yon pèd nèt aproksimativman $20,000. Koup lan, ki te kreye ferm pibèn yo an 2012, te panse li ta kapab finansye retraite yo. Pibèn yo, ki vale envi $18 chak, te itilize pou kous ak pou lozi. Yo kapab repwodwi plizyè fwa an ane — sa ki fè pèd total yo pèdi envi $40,000 si on tenvi pou repwodiksyon yo. Maria Morales te di Orlando Sentinel: 'Yon demann enmen pou yo. Polis yo sospèke vòlè yo te al travèse yon chemen ouvri ki patenn yo, ki mennen direkteman nan dèyè kòb la.

article_content: BAGHDAD, Iraq — Two suicide bombers killed 60 people and wounded at least 125 near the Imam Musa al-Kadhim shrine in Baghdad’s Kadhimiya neighborhood on Friday, according to Iraqi security and medical officials. Many of the victims were Iranian pilgrims visiting one of Shiism’s holiest sites. The attackers, both women, struck along roads leading to the shrine on a day of Muslim prayer. In a separate attack, a car bomber detonated explosives at a dealership in Jawlawla, Diyala province, killing at least seven people and injuring 29. The town has been a flashpoint in tensions between Iraq’s central government and the Kurdistan Regional Government. The bombings came just days after Iraq experienced its deadliest day of violence this year — 87 killed — with many of those victims also Iranian pilgrims. Friday’s attacks marked the third assault on Kadhimiya this month. Iraqi Prime Minister Nuri al-Maliki ordered an immediate investigation. Gen. Raymond Odierno, the top U.S. commander in Iraq, told CNN that Iraqis would not be intimidated and would continue moving forward despite the violence. He attributed the spike in attacks to al Qaeda and its affiliates, emphasizing that they are targeting innocent civilians — including women, children, and pilgrims. Iran responded swiftly. Iranian officials announced a temporary ban on pilgrimages to Iraq through the Khosrawi border crossing. Reza Moussavi of Iran’s Cultural Heritage Ministry and MP Javad Jahangirzadh suggested the attacks were politically motivated, designed to undermine Iraq’s government and damage improving Iran-Iraq relations. Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad expressed deep sorrow for the loss of Iranian citizens, calling the violence a consequence of occupation and terrorism. Meanwhile, U.S. officials are grappling with how the renewed violence might affect the planned withdrawal of American troops, with General Odierno expressing uncertainty about whether Mosul — a known al Qaeda stronghold — will be included in the scheduled pullout from urban areas by June 30. All U.S. combat troops are due to leave Iraq by December 31, 2011. Earlier on Friday, a female suicide bomber attacked as national police were distributing Red Crescent aid to displaced families in Baghdad’s Karrada district.

article_content: A 10-week-old American Staffordshire terrier named Cleo was saved from fatal antifreeze poisoning after being administered nearly a bottle and a half of vodka as an emergency medical treatment. Cleo ingested ethylene glycol — a toxic component of radiator fluid — after licking it off spare car parts in a garage. Within 30 minutes, she became unsteady, refused food, and faced imminent risk of kidney failure. Her owner, 27-year-old Stacey Zammit from Melbourne’s Truganina suburb, rushed her to a veterinary clinic where Dr. Yenny Indrawirawan recognized the urgency. With no specific antidote available, the vet used vodka — a recently received Christmas gift — to halt the metabolic conversion of ethylene glycol into lethal toxins. Cleo was fed vodka via a nasal tube every six hours for 48 hours, consuming approximately 1.5 bottles total. The treatment successfully prevented renal failure. Though she exhibited signs of acute alcohol intoxication — including bloodshot eyes and extreme unsteadiness — Cleo recovered fully. Her owner noted she slept extensively and ate well during recovery, now appearing happy and energetic. Dr. Indrawirawan confirmed the method, while rare, is scientifically grounded: ethanol competes with ethylene glycol for liver enzymes, preventing toxic metabolite formation. Without intervention, Cleo would have likely died within 72 hours.

Cleo te manje etilen glikol — yon konpozan toksik nan lwin dèlètman — aprè li te lese sou pati ki pa itilize yo nan yon garaj. Anndan 30 minit, li te vin fèt, refize manje, epi te anmenace de defizyans renal. Moun ki gen li, Stacey Zammit, 27 an, ki viv nan Truganina, yon sibòr nan Melbourne, te amene li rapidman nan yon klinik veterenè, kote Doktè Yenny Indrawirawan te rekonèt sitiyasyon la aktyèl. Paske pa gen okenn antido pou konsève, doktè a te itilize vòdka — yon prent ki te resevwa pandan Nwel — pou bloke transformasyon metabilik etilen glikol an toksin fatal. Cleo te pwochen vòdka atravè yon sonde nazo tout 6 è a, pandan 48 nèt, epi li te konsume nèt 1.5 botèl. Traiteman an te reyisiri pou prevni defizyans renal. Menm si li te montre sinptòm intoksikasyon alkolik aktyèl — tankou lèy yo roud epi nèt fèt — Cleo te retounen anndan. Moun ki gen li te obseve li te dòmi anpil epi te manje anpil pandan rekonvalesans, epi li menm genyen anpil jodi a. Doktè Indrawirawan te konfime metòd la, menm si li rare, se yon metòd ki gen baz syantifik: etanol ap konpeti avèk etilen glikol pou enzim liver yo, pou evite fòmasyon metabolit toksik. San intevansyon, Cleo ta kapab mouri anndan 72 è a.

article_content: In a landmark move, Alibaba Group and Yahoo have finalized a $7.1 billion agreement allowing Alibaba to buy back half of Yahoo’s 40% ownership stake in the Chinese tech giant. This cash infusion comes at a crucial time for Yahoo, whose market value has plummeted by 65% since its 2006 high and has been rocked by leadership scandals—including the controversial resignation of former CEO Scott Thompson, the third CEO in just three years. Yahoo acquired its original stake in Alibaba back in 2005 for $1 billion, a move now widely seen as the most profitable investment in its history. Yet the partnership has been anything but smooth: years of strategic clashes, including Yahoo’s public support for Google during its 2010 dispute with Chinese authorities, have strained ties. In September, Alibaba’s founder Jack Ma hinted at a potential buyout, and now, that possibility has become reality. 'This transaction opens a new chapter in our relationship with Yahoo,' Ma stated in a joint announcement. For Yahoo, the deal offers long-awaited clarity about one of its core assets. Interim CEO Ross Levinsohn emphasized that the agreement underscores the enduring importance of Alibaba to Yahoo’s overall value. Under the terms, Yahoo will receive $6.3 billion in cash and up to $800 million in newly issued Alibaba preferred shares. Yahoo’s CFO, Timothy R. Morse, noted that the funds will be distributed to shareholders soon, while also laying the groundwork for future value creation through additional monetization opportunities.
translated_content: Anmèn konsèy la, Alibaba Group ak Yahoo te fè yon akòrd $7.1 milyè pou Alibaba rachete moitie pati Yahoo nan 40% ki yo te pwopriyete nan entènèt chine a. Enfòmasyon sa a ap pèmèt Yahoo yo te resevwa kòd sèlman, paske valè l te chide 65% depi 2006 ak te tounen viktim yon skandale lèdiral—kote ancyan presidan Scott Thompson te rezide, tankou triyèm presidan nan twa ane sa. Yahoo te achte pati l an Alibaba an 2005 pou $1 milyè, yon investiseman ki te genyen tout tan. Men, relasyon yo te toujou pa fasil: anndan ane yo te gen konfli strategik, tankou Yahoo ki te pòte soutien Google lè konfli l avèk autorite chine yo an 2010. An septanm, fondateur Alibaba Jack Ma te anonse ke li te posib ke li ta vle achte pati Yahoo, ak menm kounye a, posibilite sa a te fèt. 'Aksyon sa a ouvri yon nòt nouvo nan relasyon nou avèk Yahoo,' Ma te di nan yon komiken komun. Pou Yahoo, aksyon sa a pèmèt yo gen klarete sou yon asèt enpotan yo. Presidan provizwa Ross Levinsohn te fèt anplis ke akòrd sa a mete an evidans importans relasyon Alibaba pou valè Yahoo. Anndan kondisyon akòrd la, Yahoo pral resevwa $6.3 milyè an espesè ak lèpi $800 milyè an akts prefere nouvo Alibaba. CFO Yahoo, Timothy R. Morse, te deklare ke fond sa yo pral distribye a aksyonè yo an tèm pi fèt, tout while lanmèm yo fè yon baz pou valè ki pral grandi ak monétizasyon ki pral vini.

article_content: James Hood, one of the first Black students to enroll at the University of Alabama in 1963, has died at age 70. A resident of Gadsden, Alabama, Hood defied racial segregation alongside Vivian Malone when they attempted to register at Foster Auditorium — a moment immortalized by Gov. George Wallace’s infamous 'stand in the schoolhouse door.' Though Wallace initially blocked their entry, federal intervention led by Deputy U.S. Attorney General Nicholas Katzenbach compelled the governor to step aside. Hood and Malone successfully registered that same day. After leaving the university after a few months, Hood earned a bachelor’s degree from Wayne State University and a master’s from Michigan State. He spent 26 years working at Madison Area Technical College in Wisconsin, retiring in 2002 as chairman of public safety services overseeing police and fire training. Decades later, in 1997, Hood returned to the University of Alabama to earn his doctorate — a full-circle moment that underscored his enduring commitment to education. University President Judy Bonner honored him as a man of 'courage and conviction,' noting his lasting impact on campus. Hood was the last surviving figure from the 1963 standoff; Wallace died in 1998, Malone in 2005, and Katzenbach in 2012. Historian Culpepper Clark described the event as an 'iconic moment' in the Civil Rights Movement, symbolically challenging segregation and helping pave the way for the Voting Rights Act. Community leaders, including Rev. Preston Nix and UA’s Samory Pruitt, reflected on how Hood’s bravery opened doors for generations of Black students. 'Because of what he did, people like me were afforded the opportunity to go to the University of Alabama,' Pruitt said. Hood passed away on Thursday. Adams-Buggs Funeral Home in Gadsden is handling arrangements. His legacy endures not in grand speeches, but in quiet persistence — a life lived to make education accessible to all.

article_content: David Viens, a chef on trial for murder in Los Angeles, told investigators he disposed of his wife’s body by boiling it for four days—leaving only her skull. The chilling admission was captured in a recorded hospital interview played during his trial, where he described placing her body in a 55-gallon drum of boiling water, weighing it down, and mixing the remains with kitchen waste before discarding it. He claimed the skull was stored at his mother’s home, but searches there and at his restaurant, Thyme Contemporary Cafe, turned up nothing. Viens made these statements in March 2011 while recovering in a hospital after jumping 80 feet off a cliff in Rancho Palos Verdes when police came to question him about his wife’s 2009 disappearance. He now attends court in a wheelchair due to his injuries. His daughter, Jacqueline, testified that Viens once confided in her about killing Dawn after she nagged him and refused to let him sleep. She said he tied her up, taped her mouth, and the next morning, she was dead. He allegedly told her the body would never be found. Though she recalled helping him pack Dawn’s clothes, she also said she’d never seen them fight—and that they appeared deeply in love. The defense questioned Jacqueline’s reliability, noting she had used marijuana and alcohol the night of the alleged conversation. Meanwhile, police noted inconsistencies: Dawn left behind her phone, wallet, and personal items, and Viens’ girlfriend soon moved into her home. Viens initially claimed Dawn ran away to the mountains after a dispute over rehab, but authorities found his story unconvincing. Evidence of blood in Viens’ apartment led police to classify the case as homicide. Officers pursued Viens and his girlfriend near the Point Vicente Interpretive Center, where he fled, struggled with Galvan, then deliberately jumped off a cliff to evade questioning. Detectives called the act 'somewhat telling.' Despite the fall, Viens survived—but barely—after spending time in a medically induced coma.

Admisyon an fèy yo te enkri nan yon enntèvityè enkri ki te lide nan proses la, ki te dekri l te mete korpi a nan yon tambou 55 gallon dlo bouyante, mete pèz sou li, epi melange rest yo avèk rezidi kokenn lan avèk poulèt yo.
