article_content: This time of year is traditionally one of the busiest, as Christmas draws nearer and parents feel mounting pressure to find the perfect gift for their children. According to a PayPal study conducted by Galaxy Research, Australians now spend an average of 46 hours—nearly two full days—preparing for the holidays, compared to just eight hours actually celebrating them. eBay has released its top 10 predictions for the best-selling toys this Christmas, with Disney’s Frozen-themed items leading the pack. Popular Frozen products include ice-skating dolls, costumes, and royal sister dolls, all priced from $49. Other top contenders include cartoon-inspired toys like Despicable Me, Lego, Transformers, and Peppa Pig, ranging from $10 to $50. The FurReal Friends GoGo My Walkin’ Pup ($100), ride-on cars ($300), and the LeapFrog Leap Pad 3 ($150) round out the top five. Additional high-demand items include Nerf weapons ($20), the Kidizoom Smart Watch ($90), My Friend Cayla dolls ($100), and the Uptown Espresso Kitchen interactive playset ($150). The study, which surveyed 1,009 Australians aged 18 to 64 in late October, also revealed that smartphones are not helping shoppers save time—instead, they’re becoming distractions. Seventy-one percent of respondents use their phones primarily to check Facebook, while nearly half (49%) play games during free moments. Frozen, the 2013 Disney film featuring the global hit 'Let It Go,' remains the highest-grossing animated movie of all time, with $1.3 billion in worldwide ticket sales, reinforcing its dominance in holiday toy trends.

article_content: Starting January 1, dairy farmers in Victoria, Australia, must either render raw milk undrinkable or pasteurize it under new health regulations. This move follows the tragic death of a three-year-old child who reportedly consumed milk labeled as 'bath milk' — a product legally sold for cosmetic use only. The Victorian government, responding to growing public concern, has imposed fines of up to $17,700 and possible license revocation for violations. Health officials warn that unpasteurized milk, even when marketed as non-food, poses deadly risks: it has been linked to severe illnesses including HUS and cryptosporidiosis, particularly in young children. Despite being banned for human consumption for over 70 years, raw milk continues to be sold in stores next to pasteurized milk, often in nearly identical containers. This similarity confuses buyers, some of whom mistakenly drink it believing it’s safe. Mountain View Farm, the producer involved, voluntarily recalled its products after the child’s death and pledged to improve warning labels. While the farm insists it clearly marks the milk as 'not for consumption,' regulators argue that current labeling isn’t sufficient. Experts like Dr. Rosemary Lester stress that even tiny amounts of harmful bacteria in raw milk can cause life-threatening illness, especially for children, the elderly, and those with weakened immune systems. The ACCC and Consumer Affairs Victoria are now investigating whether the product’s marketing crosses legal boundaries by misleading consumers. Meanwhile, a cultural trend promoting 'natural' foods has fueled renewed interest in raw milk, despite overwhelming scientific consensus that pasteurization is essential for safety.

Gouvènman Victoria, ki reyaji sou inquietid piblik la grandi, te impoze amande pou pi wo $17,700 ak posibilite revokasyon lisen pou violation yo. Sante a avèse ke lait krud, menm lè li etikete kòm pa pou konsumasyon, kapab prezon riske mortel: li te konekte ak maladi grav yo tankou HUS ak kriptosporidiozis, souvan nan timoun yo. Malgre ke li defenni pou konsumasyon anmoun 70 ane, lait krud pa ka vann nan boutik yo a lòt bò lait pasteurize, souvan nan kontanè ki rezime yo. article_content: A Spanish judge has officially cleared Sir Sean Connery of criminal involvement in a fraud probe tied to the sale of his former Marbella villa, Casa Malibu — but not without scathing criticism. Judge Alfredo Mondeja ruled that while Connery bears no legal blame, his conduct throughout the investigation was unnecessarily delayed and demonstrated a troubling disregard for judicial procedures. Connery submitted an affidavit from the Bahamas explicitly rejecting the authority of the Spanish court and refusing to comply with an international request for testimony — a move the judge called legally uninformed and obstructive. The delay in submitting the affidavit — over two years after the initial international request — forced the court to extend the probe. The investigation now focuses solely on Connery’s wife, Micheline Roquebrune, who remains under suspicion for alleged fraud, tax offenses, and illegal construction linked to the 1999 sale of the property. At least 20 other individuals, including former Marbella officials and lawyers, have already been scheduled for trial. Judge Mondeja noted that the delays were not the court’s fault, but the result of the couple’s failure to engage with the legal process. He suggested their inaction may have been intended to protect Roquebrune — inadvertently damaging Connery’s standing. Roquebrune, who has publicly denied any wrongdoing, calling the allegations 'nonsense,' has ten days to appeal the decision to continue proceedings against her. She has not yet been formally charged.

Connery te envoye yon afidavit nan Bahamay ki refize eksplisitman autorite kòt espagnyòl la ak refize repons ak yon demand internasyonal pou témoinaj — yon movman jij la te dekri kòm pa konnen dwa ak obstruktif. Retard nan envwaye afidavit la — plis pase de a nan pwojèt inisyal la — te oblige kòt la pou extenden enkèt la. Enkèt la maintenan fokis sou fèm Connery, Micheline Roquebrune, ki toujou sou soupçon pou fraid, ofans fiskal ak konstwi ilegal ki konèk ak vand la nan 1999. article_content: A mother has defended her choice to undergo a controversial fertility treatment that helped her conceive her now-teenage daughter. Sharon Saarinen became pregnant through a process called cytoplasmic transfer, which involves injecting donor cytoplasm—including mitochondrial DNA—into her own egg to improve its viability. The procedure has since been banned in the United States and is now under investigation for potential long-term health effects on children born from it. 'I think it was the only thing that helped me,' Mrs. Saarinen told The Independent. 'If there were risks, it didn’t matter. I wanted a child too much at that point.' She added, 'It was definitely the right thing to do.' Her daughter, Alana, is now a healthy teenager thriving in high school. 'The right thing to do': Alana Saarinen (right) was conceived through cytoplasmic transfer. She sits at home with her mother Sharon, who says she does not regret the decision. However, concerns persist that the treatment may compromise children’s health, as it results in offspring inheriting mitochondrial DNA from three individuals: the mother, the father, and the donor. The Institute for Reproductive Medicine and Science at Saint Barnabas Medical Center in New Jersey is now examining whether any long-term health consequences emerged from the technique, which was used on approximately 30 women before being halted. About 17 of those cases originated at Saint Barnabas. Why now? More than a decade after the procedure ended, the clinic is conducting its first formal review of the children’s health outcomes. Only two of the children born from the treatment have been publicly identified: Alana Saarinen and Emma Ott, who was born in 1997 as the world’s first child conceived via this three-parent method. Both are now healthy teenagers. According to The Independent, neither Alana nor Emma has undergone comprehensive long-term health screenings related to the technique. At the time, scientists hoped cytoplasmic transfer would improve IVF success rates for women whose eggs had poor developmental potential. Instead, it inadvertently introduced donor mitochondrial DNA—which is maternally inherited—into the embryo, creating a genetic mix of three parents. In Emma’s case, researchers found no lasting trace of the donor’s mitochondrial DNA. However, some of the roughly 30 children conceived globally using similar methods retained small amounts of donor DNA. Before the technique could become widespread, the U.S. halted its use due to insufficient safety data. A request for comment from the Institute for Reproductive Medicine and Science was not immediately returned. Reports of this follow-up investigation coincide with the United Kingdom’s consideration of legalizing newer, more refined mitochondrial replacement therapies—not to enhance fertility, but to prevent mothers from passing on severe mitochondrial diseases such as muscular dystrophy, epilepsy, heart conditions, and intellectual disabilities. About one in 200 children in the UK is born with a mitochondrial disorder. Modern mitochondrial replacement techniques involve transferring only the nuclear DNA from the mother’s egg into a donor egg with healthy mitochondria, then fertilizing it with the father’s sperm. Critics, including some religious and ethical groups, oppose these procedures, arguing they involve the destruction of embryos. British tabloids famously labeled the early versions ‘three-parent babies,’ a term scientists reject as misleading, since the donor contributes less than 0.2% of the child’s total DNA.
translated_content: Mèt la te defenn chwa li pou fè yon traiteman fètilizasyon kontwèv ki te pèmèt li konsevwi fi jèn li akòrèt. Sharon Saarinen te encepe pa yon proses ki rele transyè kiploplazmik, ki enplike enjeksyon sitoplazm ki gen mitokondri yo nan ouvèt li pou amelyore sante ouvèt la. Menm traiteman sa a te defènitivman interdi nan Etazini epi li te kounye a sou enfesyon pou riske posib sante gwo moun yo. 'Mwen pens ke se sèl bagay ki te pèmèt mwen,' Mme. Saarinen te di The Independent. 'Si yo te gen risk, sa pa te mete. Mwen te vle yon timoun tro pi lwen nan moman sa a.' Li te ajoute, 'Li te definitivman bagay ki te pi bon pou fèt.' Fi li, Alana, kounye a yon timoun jèn sant ki ap travay byen nan lise. 'Bagay ki te pi bon pou fèt:' Alana Saarinen (dwe a) te konsevi atravè transyè kiploplazmik. Li sèt nan kay li ak mèt li Sharon, ki di li pa regrete paske a. Menm si, yo te panse ke traiteman sa a ka afekte sante timoun yo, paske li rezilte nan yon timoun ki resevwa ADN mitokondriyal nan twa peyis: mèt, pè, ak donatè. Institi pou Medisin epi Sijens Fètilizasyon nan Saint Barnabas Medical Center nan New Jersey kounye a ap etidye si gen anyen ki te pwodui yon efet long tem sou timoun yo ki te nèt atravè teknik sa a, ki te itilize sou envi 30 fanm avan li te bloke. Enviròn 17 nan sa yo te sòti nan Saint Barnabas. Poukisa kounye a? Plis pase dekenn apre proses sa a te fèmen, klênik la te kounye a fè premye enfesyon formel sou sante timoun yo. Se sèl de timoun ki te nèt atravè teknik sa a ki te identifie publikman: Alana Saarinen ak Emma Ott, ki te nèt an 1997 kòm premye timoun nan mond lan ki te konsevi atravè teknik tri-pè a. De yo kounye a se timoun jèn sant ki san fèn. Anfòmasyon The Independent, pa gen okenn test long tem pou Alana oubyen Emma ki te fèt pou konnen si yo gen anyen ki rela ak teknik sa a. Nan moman sa a, syantifik yo te espere ke transyè kiploplazmik ta kapab amelyore sans konsepsyon pou fanm kote IVF tradisyonèl pa te fèt. Menm jan an, li te entròdwi ADN mitokondriyal donatè—ki gen pou fè avèk mèt—nan zonk fèt, ki te kreye yon kombinason jenetik tri-pè. Nan kaza Emma, syantifik yo te jwenn pa gen anyen ki te rejwenn nan ADN mitokondriyal donatè a. Menm jan an, kèk nan enviròn 30 timoun ki te nèt mondyalman atravè metòd sa a te konsève yon ti kantite ADN donatè. Avan teknik sa a ka vin pi wid, Etazini te bloke itilizasyon li paske pa te gen dòmèn sekirite sifiyan. Yon kous te fèt pou Institi pou Medisin epi Sijens Fètilizasyon pa te retounen tout deyò. Rapò sou enfesyon sa a koincide avèk etid pou legalizasyon metòd modern yo nan Royaume Uni—pa pou amelyore fètilizasyon, men pou prevni mèt yo pa transmete maladi mitokondriyal grav yo tankou distrofi musikil, epilepsi, pwoblèm kòd, ak defisyan sivil. Enviròn yon sou 200 timoun nan Royaume Uni te nèt ak yon maladi mitokondriyal chak ane. Metòd modern mitokondriyal yo enplike transfè sèlman ADN nukleyè nan ouvèt mèt la nan yon ouvèt donatè ki gen mitokondri sante yo, men ki te vide nan tout ADN lòt yo, answit fèt avèk sperm pè a. Kritik yo, ki gen yon kantite goup relijye ak etik, te opoze prosedir sa yo, yo di yo enplike detwiyisyon ouvèt oubyen zonk fèt. Prens britanik yo te pran prosedir sa a lè li te anonsi an 2008 epi yo te rele li kreyasyon yon timoun tri-pè—a te nòm syantifik yo rejete kòm mizè, paske donatè a kontribi piti kantite ADN yo—moin pase 0.2% nan total ADN timoun an.

article_content: A stuffy, overcrowded cell — perhaps two or three men sharing a single bunk. Lockdown for most of the day. Is this what awaits South Africa’s Oscar Pistorius after his conviction for culpable homicide in the death of his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp? Legal experts say it is impossible to predict the sentence Judge Thokozile Masipa may impose. Yet many are watching to see whether the Olympic champion’s dramatic fall from grace ends with time behind bars. If sentenced to prison, life would likely be extremely difficult for South Africa’s most famous disabled athlete. A double amputee, Pistorius relies on prosthetic limbs to move. Rights campaigners warn that South African prisons — notorious for overcrowding, gang violence, and unsanitary conditions — are challenging even for the healthiest inmates. Nooshin Erfani-Ghadimi, project coordinator at the Johannesburg-based Wits Justice Project, believes Pistorius will likely receive better treatment than the average prisoner — as he has throughout the judicial process. He may even get a cell to himself. Still, she told CNN, 'I don’t think anyone with a disability can currently be provided for in a way that guarantees proper medical care or appropriate physical infrastructure.' While some South African prisons are marginally better than others, none compare to the $560,000 home in the luxury Silverwoods Estate near Pretoria, where Pistorius fatally shot Steenkamp in 2013. The Department of Correctional Services has policies for accommodating disabled inmates, Erfani-Ghadimi noted. 'But policy and practice are often poles apart,' she said. 'Disabled prisoners endure the same inhumane conditions as able-bodied ones.' Spokesperson Koos Gerber previously stated that detention facilities 'can accommodate people with any disabilities.' Yet access to prisons remains restricted, making independent verification difficult. Speculation suggests Pistorius could be sent to Pretoria Central Prison — a facility with a poor reputation. In 2022, six inmates testified in Pretoria High Court that they shared overcrowded, poorly ventilated cells with dirty mattresses, no bedding, and faced threats of sexual violence from gangs. Many were locked in for 18 hours daily. Overcrowding strains sanitation, ventilation, and medical services. According to the Wits Justice Project, cells designed for 32 inmates often hold 88. Three men may share a single bunk, and communal cells are doubled or tripled beyond capacity. Tuberculosis — labeled the leading cause of death in South African prisons — spreads rapidly in damp, crowded conditions. Nurses are overwhelmed; inconsistent treatment leads to drug-resistant strains. Disruptions to antiretroviral therapy endanger HIV-positive detainees. Erfani-Ghadimi cited cases of diabetics going into insulin shock after being denied medication upon arrest. Correctional Services Minister Sibusiso Ndebele acknowledged overcrowding as a global issue, noting that South Africa’s prison population has declined over the past decade. As of April this year, there were approximately 157,400 inmates — nearly 28% held on remand — in a country of 54 million. Pistorius’s legal journey has drawn international scrutiny. While uncomfortable for authorities, this attention appears to have benefited him: granted bail with relaxed conditions, his trial began less than a year after Steenkamp’s death — a rarity in a system where indigent suspects wait years for court dates. Erfani-Ghadimi called this process 'an anomaly' — marked by speed and abundant expert resources. 'In most cases, both victims and accused face a high risk of miscarriage of justice,' she wrote in The Conversation. Yet fame may become a double-edged sword in prison. 'He hasn’t been able to bribe his way out,' she said. 'But he has accessed privileges others cannot.' The case of Ronnie Fakude, a paraplegic man held on remand for 28 months before being released on bail with an electronic monitor, illustrates the brutality faced by disabled inmates. Fakude described sharing a cell meant for 32 with 88 men. He slept alone on a bottom bunk — a rare privilege. With no wheelchair, he dragged himself across the floor. Ten inmates had TB; four or five were HIV-positive. One man with multidrug-resistant TB slept directly above him. Erfani-Ghadimi argues Fakude should never have been detained — and that the same logic should apply to Pistorius.
translated_content: Yon klas sòl, soupli, ak pi fòs — pèpèt de oswa twa gason ki paticipe yon lit sèl. Konsinman pou plis pase tout jou a. Est-ce ke sa ki pati pou Oskar Pistorius lè li konvike pou homisid koupable nan mòt Reeva Steenkamp? Eksèt la di ke se imposib pou predi senstans ki ta dwe ban li jij Thokozile Masipa. Men, anpil moun ap vwoye pou wè si chwaz Pistorius ki te fèt nan tèt li a fini avèk timoun lèt. Si li konvike, viv nan prizon ta dwe trè difisil pou atlet ki pi konn nan Afrik sa a. Yon ampute doubl, Pistorius bezwen protez pou mache. Aktivist yo di ke prizon yo an Afrik sa a — ki konnen pou soupli, violans gang ak kondisyon sanitè mal — yo difisil menm pou moun ki pi sante. Nooshin Erfani-Ghadimi, kordinatris projè Wits Justice Project ki sou Johannesburg, panse ke Pistorius ta resevwa trè pi bon traiteman pase yon prizonye klasik — tankou li te resevwa tout tan proses jidisyè a. Li ka menm gen yon klas pou li sèl. Menm jan, li te di CNN, 'M pa panse ke yon moun ki gen yon defisians fizik yo kapab resevwa yon trèman ki garantit trèman medikal korek oswa infrastrakti fizik korek an jodi a.' Menm si yon piti kantite prizon yo an Afrik sa a pi bon pase lòt yo, pa gen okenn ki konsiderabman pi bon pase kay la ki valè $560,000 nan distrikt Silverwoods, apre Pretoria, kote Pistorius te pouse Reeva Steenkamp an 2013. Ministèr Konrisyon Sèvis la gen politik pou akomode moun ki gen defisians fizik, Erfani-Ghadimi te di. 'Men politik ak praktik yo souvan kontrè. Malerezman, moun ki gen defisians yo viv menm kondisyon inuman yo ke moun ki pa gen defisian yo.' Pòt-parol Koos Gerber te di CNN ke fasilité detansyon yo 'kapab akomode moun ki gen tout tip defisian.' Men, pa gen akès ki fasil pou rechèchè aktyèl yo, sa ki fè vèrifikasyon endepandan difisil. Konsèn, Pistorius ka al nan Prizon Pretoria Central — yon fasilité ki gen yon reyèl reputasyon mal. An 2022, sis prizonye te té témoine nan Kòt Pretoria ke yo te paticipe yon klas soupli, ki pa gen vantiyasyon, matras sal, pa gen linn, ak menas seksèl gòd. Anpil yo te konsinman 18 or koupe. Soupli a afekte sanitè, vantiyasyon ak trèman medikal. Selon Wits Justice Project, klas ki te destine pou 32 moun yo souvan gen 88. Twa moun kapab paticipe yon lit, ak klas kominal yo gen plis pase twa fwa kapasite yo. Tuberkiloz — ki te konsidere kousman ki pi fòt nan prizon yo an Afrik sa a — li pafe rapidman nan klas sòl ak soupli. Enfermyè yo soukòp. Trèman ki pa konstan fè rezistans medikaman an pafe. Diskontinyite nan program antiretroviral yo mete moun ki gen VIH an danje. Erfani-Ghadimi te cite kaza moun ki gen diabetik ki te fèt enkònshèn inslin lè yo te arete ak pa te resevwa medikaman yo. Ministè Konrisyon Sèvis Sibusiso Ndebele te rekonèt ke soupli a se yon defi mondyal, ak ki popilasyon prizon an Afrik sa a te diminye pandan dènye dizanèn. An avril, te gen enviròn 157,400 prizonye — nèt 28% yo te detenn avan tri — nan yon peyi ki gen 54 milyon moun. Pwosesis jidisyè Pistorius te fèt anpil atansyon mondyal. Menm si sa te anpli pou autorite yo, sa te benefisye li: li te ase kòm ba, kondisyon relaks, epi tri li te kòmanse anmwen anndan yon ane pita mòt Reeva Steenkamp — yon rarite nan yon sistèm kote moun ki pa gen lekòl te atann anndan ane pou kòmènse tri yo. Erfani-Ghadimi te dekri sa kòm 'yon anomali' — markè pa vitès ak resous ekspèt ki anpil. 'Nan plis kaza, vitim ak akuzé yo gen yon risik fòt pou jistis ki pa fèt,' li te ekri sou The Conversation. Men, fama li ka vin yon espesè dèbòt lè li pral nan prizon. 'Li pa kapab achte libète a,' li te di. 'Men li te kapab resevwa avantaj ki pa disponib pou lòt moun.' Kaza Ronnie Fakude, yon paraplegik ki te detenn avan tri pou 28 mwa avan li te lèt avèk yon balòm elektronik, montre brutalite moun ki gen defisians yo viv. Fakude te dekri ke li te paticipe yon klas ki te destine pou 32 moun ak 88. Li te mache sèl sou yon lit ki nan tout ba — yon privilèj rare. Pa gen chèzi, li te tirè piye yo devan li. Dix moun te gen tuberkiloz; kat oswa senk te gen VIH. Yon moun ki gen tuberkiloz rezistan miltipli te mache sou li. Erfani-Ghadimi panse ke Fakude ta dwe pa jami detenn — epi menm lojik la ta dwe aplike pou Pistorius.

article_content: CNN) — Playing an anxiety-ridden mobster made him famous, but it was the beloved, talented man that stars and politicians came together to honor on Thursday. A funeral service was held for James Gandolfini at the Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine in New York City, where friends, family, fans, and co-stars gathered to mourn the 51-year-old actor, who died of a heart attack in Italy on June 20. The Sopranos creator David Chase was scheduled to speak at the service, along with Gandolfini’s widow, Deborah Lin Gandolfini, and two family friends. Gandolfini rose to fame portraying mob boss Tony Soprano on Chase’s hit HBO series. See James Gandolfini’s 1989 screen debut. Cast members from The Sopranos, including Lorraine Bracco and Tony Sirico, embraced one another as they arrived. Spectators lined the streets, watching a wide range of celebrities enter the church—from actor Alec Baldwin to New Jersey Governor Chris Christie. In addition to personal tributes, the 90-minute service included traditional hymns and contemporary musical selections, according to HBO. The Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine was chosen for its capacity to accommodate the large number of attendees, an HBO representative said. Despite reports that HBO planned to film the funeral, a spokesperson clarified: 'HBO is not recording it. It is being recorded for personal archival use.' The service followed a private wake held Wednesday at a funeral home in Park Ridge, New Jersey, the New York Daily News reported. Invitation-only, the gathering drew tearful family and friends grappling with their loss. 'It's a nightmare for the whole family,' said Bob Price, married to one of Gandolfini’s cousins. 'It's a horrible, horrible thing. Everybody is just devastated.' That evening, Broadway dimmed its lights in memory of the actor, who earned a Tony Award nomination in 2009 for his performance in God of Carnage.

A sèvis funèbri te fèt pou James Gandolfini nan Katedral St. Jean l’Evanjisè nan Vilye New York, kote fami, fan, ak kòlèg yo te vini pou yo plede pèd lan, aktè a ki te mouri dènye 20 juin nan Itali, nan 51 an. Kreyatè The Sopranos, David Chase, te panse pale nan sèvis la, jodi a ak vèf la, Deborah Lin Gandolfini, ak de zanmi fami a. Gandolfini te fèt konn pou l fè wòl Tony Soprano nan serè HBO a. Vwè debi 1989 a nan sinema a. Aktè The Sopranos tankou Lorraine Bracco ak Tony Sirico te emrase yo lè yo arive. Moun ki te la yo te wè yon gran kantite kélébrité rentrè nan egliz la—tankou aktè Alec Baldwin ak govenè New Jersey Chris Christie. Anplis de tèmoinaj fami ak zanmi yo, sèvis 90 minit la te gen chante tradisyonèl ak mizik kontanporè, selon HBO. Katedral St. Jean l’Evanjisè te chwazi paske li gen asèz de plas pou tout moun ki te vini, yon reprezantan HBO te di. Malgre rapòt yo te di ke HBO te panse enrejistre sèvis la, yon spesyalis te klare: 'HBO pa enrejistre sèvis la. Enrejistremen an se pou ariv chache pèsonèl.' Sèvis la te pralèv yon veje pèvèl ki te fèt mekredi nan yon kabin funèbri nan Park Ridge, New Jersey, New York Daily News te rapòte. Evènman sa a te rezève pou moun ki te konnen yo, epi tout moun te plede pèd lan. 'Se yon nwat pou tout fami a,' di Bob Price, mari yon kousin Gandolfini a. 'Se yon bagay terib, terib. Tout moun la tout dèyè.' Mekredi swa, Broadway te fèm lè yo pou yo memore aktè a, ki te resevwa yon nominasyon Tony nan 2009 pou l’èkspresyon nan peyis God of Carnage.

article_content: Tripoli, Libya (CNN) — A slate of Cabinet ministers for Libya’s emerging government was finalized on Sunday, according to two spokesmen for the National Transitional Council. The names of the appointees are expected to be announced soon, the spokesmen said, declining to be identified. The NTC, which led the military and political movement to overthrow longtime ruler Moammar Gadhafi, relocated its capital from Benghazi to Tripoli last month after anti-Gadhafi forces captured the city. It is now recognized as Libya’s legitimate government by numerous nations and international organizations, including the United Nations and the African Union. While fighting continues against Gadhafi loyalists in a few areas, NTC representatives have begun representing the country internationally and managing domestic affairs — though until now, it lacked formally appointed ministers to oversee specific government functions. One of the remaining conflict zones, along with Bani Walid and Sabha, is Sirte. Last week, the NTC announced that its forces had surrounded the central coastal city and approximately 5,000 pro-Gadhafi loyalists inside. On Saturday, NTC Chairman Mustafa Abdul Jalil gave civilians 48 hours to evacuate before launching a full-scale offensive. Earlier this weekend, ICRC spokeswoman Souad Masoudi reported that around 10,000 people had fled Sirte. The ICRC described humanitarian conditions inside the besieged city as dire, noting severe shortages of medical supplies. On Sunday, after previous attempts to reach Sirte by boat were halted due to 'the security situation,' a Red Cross team entered the city by land from the west. They met with local officials who reported critical shortages of drinking water, hygiene products, and food — including for infants. The team visited Ibn Sina Hospital, where operation leader Hichem Khadraoui described conditions for medical staff as 'extremely difficult.' The team delivered surgical supplies — including body bags and dressing kits — sufficient to treat about 200 wounded individuals, as well as 400 liters (approximately 106 gallons) of fuel for the hospital’s generator. 'The hospital is experiencing a massive influx of patients, medical supplies are nearly exhausted, and there is an urgent need for oxygen,' Khadraoui said. 'To make matters worse, the water reservoir is damaged.'

Konsey Transisyonel Nasyonal, ki te dirije moviman milityè ak poltik pou chache enpi Moammar Gadhafi, te deplase kapital li nan Benghazi pou Tripoli mwa lan dènye, aprè fòs ki te kontra Gadhafi te kapte vil la. Yon sèl endri ki toujou yon zòn batay, anplis Bani Walid ak Sabha, se Sirte. Lètèn, NTC te anonse ke fòs yo te entoure vil koastal sentral sa a ak enviròn 5,000 lòyalist Gadhafi ki nan ladan. Samedi, prezidan NTC Mustafa Abdul Jalil te pèmèt sivil yo 48 èt pou evacue avan li lanse yon ofensiv total. Anvan, sovraspokesman ICRC Souad Masoudi te di ke enviròn 10,000 moun te fèt nan Sirte. ICRC te desri kondisyon umanitè a nan vil enkèt la kòm direk, ak defisyon grav ak sòs medikal. 'Hopital la gen yon ente anpil moun, sòs medikal yo ap fini, epi gen yon beswen urgè pou oksijèn,' di Khadraoui. 'Pou ajoute, rezervwa dlo a detwòye.'

article_content: Five-year-old Callum Slater, a student at Longmoor Community Primary School in Liverpool, was separated from his classmates during lunch after his mother, Lesley, submitted his weekly £9 dinner payment after the school’s unofficial cutoff time. Although the school’s newsletter only stated payments must be made on Friday, it never specified a time — leading to confusion. Lesley delivered the money at 3:30 p.m., but was told it was 'too late' — even though it was still Friday. As a result, Callum was asked to eat lunch outside the headteacher’s office. His grandmother, Sheila, claimed he was given only a plain bread roll and water, which deeply upset the child, who repeatedly asked, 'What have I done?' However, the school maintains that Callum received the same meal as other students that day — a tuna baguette, juice, and dessert — but was served separately to shield him from potential embarrassment, as is standard practice for children with unpaid meals. The following day, despite his account having a credit balance from a prior missed meal, Callum was given packed lunches for the rest of the week until the next payment window opened. The family, heartbroken by how their son was treated, is now exploring other schools. The school has since acknowledged a miscommunication, apologized to the family, and pledged to clarify payment deadlines more clearly in future communications.
translated_content: Kalem Slater, yon timoun ki etidye nan Longmoor Community Primary School nan Walton, Liverpool, te oblije manje lòt kote pandan déje nwa a aprè mè l, Lesley, te peye 9£ pou repas semèn an apre kote skol te gen yon limit pa ofisyèl. Menm jan ak nouvèl la nan skol, li te di se vendredi yo dwe peye, men pa te precise kèk tan. Lesley te ban lajan an a 3h30 apremidi, men yo te di li 'trop fèy' — menm si se toujou vendredi. Konsa, Kalem te konmande li manje lòt kote devan bati dirèktè. Granmè l, Sheila, te deklare li te ban li yon boulèk brèn ak yon vè kou, sa ki te fè timoun an tris, ki te repeye 'Ki sa m fèt?' Menm jan, skol te deklare ke Kalem te resevwa menm repas lan ak tout lòt timoun sa jou-lan — yon baguèt tonbe, jis ak desèt — men li te sèvi lòt kote pou li evite enbàsman, tankou se pratik stanndard pou timoun ki pa peye. Lè swivan, malgre ke kont li te gen yon solde pa yon repas ki te manke, Kalem te resevwa repas pakkè pou tout semèn an tan ke mè l ta kapab peye lòt kote semèn swivan. Fanmi a, tris pa mannyèr yo te traite fèy yo, te konsidere kousi lòt skol. Skol la te rekonèt yon malèntanndi, te deswè fèy yo, ak te engaje pou klè fè yon lòt kote ki te rezime pwoblèm la.

But this shouldn’t happen to any kid. #SchoolPolicyFail #KidsDeserveBetter #LunchGate

article_content: A heartbreaking tragedy unfolded in Chippenham, Wiltshire, when one-year-old Leo Clark drowned in just seven inches of bathwater after his mother stepped away for less than a minute. On the evening of July 16, 2011, Natasha Clark was giving her two sons, Leo and his older brother Jamie, their nightly bath. She filled the tub with 18.5 centimeters of water—a standard amount—and sat nearby to call their father, Darren Scrivens. While she briefly stepped into the kitchen to retrieve something, Leo slipped underwater, lying on his back and unresponsive. When she returned, she immediately pulled him out and began CPR. Unable to reach emergency services directly, she called her mother, who dialed 999. Paramedics arrived quickly and airlifted Leo to the Royal United Hospital in Bath, but despite their efforts, he was pronounced dead at 9:42 p.m. An inquest held at Trowbridge Coroner’s Court concluded that the death was entirely accidental. Coroner Dr. David Singleton emphasized that Leo’s previous breathing problems, though documented, played no role in the drowning. Police confirmed no signs of neglect or wrongdoing; Natasha was described as distraught and cooperative throughout. The case underscores how swiftly and silently infant drownings can occur—even in shallow water during routine activities.
translated_content: Yon trajezi doulouros te pase nan Chippenham, Wiltshire, lè yon ti gason ki gen anpil 1 an, Leo Clark, te mouri nan yon banyè avèk sèlman 7 col nan dlo a, aprè mèt li te ale pou menm yon minit. Soir la 16 jiyè 2011, Natasha Clark te ban de pitit li, Leo ak frè li pi enpli, Jamie, banyè yo. Li te mete 18.5 santimèt dlo nan banyè a—yon kantite ki norma—ak te sèt la pou rele pè pè yo, Darren Scrivens. Lè li te ale pou al chache yon bagay nan kay la, Leo te chide nan dlo a, sou do a, ak pa gen okenn respire. Lè li te retounen, li te pran li tout vit ak te kòmanse CPR. Pa kapab rele 999, li te rele mèt li, ki te rele 999. Medikaman yo te vini rapidman ak te transpòte Leo nan Hopital Royal United nan Bath, men malgre tout efò yo, li te deklare mouri a 9:42 p.m. Enkèt ki te fèt nan Kòt Trowbridge te konklè ke mòt la te totalman anpech. Kòtè David Singleton te fènmen ke pwoblèm respire yo antèryèr yo, menm si yo te dokumente, pa te gen okenn lòt ak mòt la. Pwolès la te konfime pa gen okenn nimewo nijile oswa neglijans; Natasha te deklare konsèy ak detrist. Kas sa a mete an evidans kòman mòt nan pitit yo ka pase rapidman ak silansie—meme nan dlo ki pa enpli lè yo fè yon aktivite norma.

article_content: WASHINGTON — The anticipated meeting between President Joe Biden and Chinese leader Xi Jinping is on track for next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in San Francisco. However, the White House is not expecting the face-to-face encounter to result in major changes to U.S.-China relations, according to a person familiar with the planning. The White House announced late last month that the United States and China had reached an agreement in principle for Biden and Xi to meet in person during the summit — the first direct engagement between the two leaders in what has been a tense year for the world’s two largest economies. As Biden prepares to arrive in San Francisco next week, the exact timing and other logistical details have not yet been formally announced. The U.S. believes the two sides may make modest announcements following the meeting, but fundamental differences in the relationship will remain unchanged, according to the person, who was not authorized to speak publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity. Jude Blanchette, chair of China Studies at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, said Biden and Xi are aiming 'to intentionally keep that bar low.' 'What’s happening here is an attempt to have a deep conversation where the two sides directly share their concerns — but more importantly, the meeting unlocks, especially within the Chinese system, space for further constructive engagement,' Blanchette said. Both sides have worked to lay the groundwork for the San Francisco meeting. U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen is scheduled to meet Thursday and Friday with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in San Francisco, ahead of the official start of the APEC summit on Saturday. This meeting follows Biden’s one-hour phone call with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi at the White House last month, during which Wang also held talks with U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken and National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan. Xi similarly met with Blinken in June when the secretary visited Beijing for discussions with Wang. Yellen last met her counterpart He during a July visit to Beijing, where she urged Chinese officials to cooperate on climate change and other global challenges, warning against allowing trade disputes and other irritants to derail bilateral ties. Biden and Xi last met nearly a year ago on the sidelines of the Group of 20 summit in Bali, Indonesia — a nearly three-hour discussion in which Biden directly criticized China’s 'coercive and increasingly aggressive actions' toward Taiwan, and raised concerns about Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and other issues. Since the Bali meeting, the relationship has grown more complicated due to U.S. export controls on advanced technologies, Biden’s decision to shoot down a Chinese surveillance balloon after it crossed the continental United States, and Taiwanese President Tsai Ing-wen’s stopover in the U.S. earlier this year. Beijing views any official U.S. contact with Taiwan as encouragement for the island’s de facto independence — a step U.S. leaders say they do not support. Under the 'One China' policy, the United States recognizes Beijing as the government of China and does not maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan, but considers Taipei an important partner in the Indo-Pacific region.
translated_content: WASHINGTON — Mèt antwit ant Prezidan Joe Biden ak dirijan Chine Xi Jinping ta nan pwojè pou lavi nèt la, nan kote moun yo ap gen yon mèt sou latè sommet APEC nan San Francisco, men Bli Kòs pa tande ke sa a mèt la pral rezilte nan chanjman maje nan relasyon Etazini-Chin, selon yon moun ki konnen planifikasyon an. Bli Kòs te anonsye lòt mwa a ke Etazini ak Chine te fè yon akòrd nan prensip pou Biden ak Xi pale ansanm nan kote a — premye kontak direk ant dirijan yo pandan ane ki te plen de tensyon nan antre de ekonomi ki pi enpotan nan mond lan. Kouma Biden pral arive nan San Francisco nèt la, dat la eksakt ak lòt detay logistike pa tèt fèt anko. Etazini panse ke de peyi yo ka fè yon ti anons modèst aprè mèt la, men diferans fondamantal yo pral rete menm, selon moun sa a, ki pa t asepté pou pale publikman epi te pale sou kondisyon anonymité a. Jude Blanchette, presidan Etid Chine nan Sènt pou Etid Stratèjik ak Internasyonal nan Washington, di ke Biden ak Xi ap chache 'pou mete bar la anba intansyonèlman.' 'Sa ki ap fèt la se yon entèn syon pou fè yon konvèrsasyon profè non se kote de peyi yo pataje anpil inquietid yo, men pi enpotan an, mèt sa a ouvri espas, espesyalman nan sistèm chine a, pou engajman ki pi konstriktif anko,' Blanchette di. De peyi yo te travay pou preparé mèt San Francisco a. Sekretè Trezi Etazini Janet Yellen pral mèt jeudi ak vendredi avèk Vès-Premye Minis Chine He Lifeng nan San Francisco, anvan demaraj ofisyèl sommet APEC a samedi. Mèt sa a vin aprè Biden te fè yon kònferans telefòn anndan yon èt avèk Minis Etranje Chine Wang Yi nan Bli Kòs lòt mwa a, kote Wang te tou fè mèt avèk Sekretè d'Etat Etazini Antony Blinken ak Konseyèr sekirite nasyonal Bli Kòs Jake Sullivan. Xi te tou mèt Blinken jen a, kote sekretè a te ale nan Pekin pou diskisyon avèk Wang. Yellen te mèt kontrapartiy li He lè li te ale nan Pekin jiyè a, kote li te apelè ofisye chine yo pou kolektivman travay sou chanjman klimatik ak lòt defi global yo, ak avèti yo pa laisser diferans komèsyal ak lòt enplikasyon yo fèt relasyon yo. Biden ak Xi te mèt preske yon ane anvan, nan latè sommet G20 nan Bali, Indonezi — yon diskisyon ki te dure preske twa èt kote Biden te kritike direkman 'aksyon koèsif ak de plis agresif' Chine yo fè sou Taivan, epi te diskute invazyon Rus la sou Ukrain ak lòt lavi yo. Depi mèt Bali a, relasyon an te vin pi komplike a cause kontwòl ekspòt Etazini sou teknoloji avanse, decizyon Biden pou abat yon balon veye chine ki te travèse kontinen Etazini a, ak eske pa Tsai Ing-wen, prezidan Taivan, ki te fè yon kout nan Etazini anvan ane a. Pekin wè tout kontak ofisyèl Etazini avèk Taivan kòm yon enkourajman pou konsakre inndepandans de fèt Taivan an — yon etap ki pa anndan pozisyon dirijan Etazini yo. Pou politik 'Yon Chine,' Etazini rekonèt Pekin kòm gouvènman Chine a, epi pa gen relasyon diplomatik avèk Taivan, men li konsidere Taipei kòm yon partnè imòtan nan reyion Indo-Pasifik la.

article_content: On December 27, 2012, Marie Easter, 43, lost control of her Ford Focus on a wet section of the A47 near Wisbech, Cambridgeshire, killing two young sisters—Jessica Portor, 7, and Tamzin Portor, 10—who were visiting their father for the holidays. Both girls suffered fatal head injuries and were pronounced dead at Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Investigators determined that two of the car’s tires had illegally low tread depth, and all four were underinflated—factors that experts concluded significantly increased the risk of losing control. Easter, who had formed a close bond with the girls and treated them like her own children, initially claimed she swerved to avoid another vehicle, but multiple eyewitnesses reported seeing no other car nearby. She later pleaded guilty to two counts of causing death by careless driving. Though she and the girls’ father, Allan Portor, and his 12-year-old son Liam survived with minor injuries, the emotional impact was devastating. At Norwich Crown Court, Judge Mark Lucraft recognized her deep remorse, describing her as a 'broken woman' whose life would be forever haunted by the tragedy. He imposed a 15-month prison sentence, suspended for two years, and banned her from driving for four years—even though she stated she no longer wanted to drive. The girls’ parents remembered Tamzin as endlessly joyful, musical, and compassionate, and Jessica as a vibrant spirit who lit up every room with her dancing, singing, and love of chocolate. Norfolk Police emphasized that while tire condition played a part, it was Easter’s substandard driving that directly caused the fatal crash. 'A festive visit turned into a tragedy because of preventable negligence,' said a spokesperson.
translated_content: Dé 27 desanm 2012, Marie Easter, 43 an, te pèdi kontwòl veyikil li sou yon zòn mouye nan A47 toujou apre Wisbech, Cambridgeshire, epi te tue de sœ yo—Jessica Portor, 7 an, ak Tamzin Portor, 10 an—ki te vini rende vizit papa yo pou Nwel. De ti gason sa yo te pòte lèz mòt yo ak te deklare mòt nan Hopital Queen Elizabeth nan King’s Lynn. Envestigatè yo te konstati ke de pney yo te gen dèpòt ki te ilegal ak tout kat yo te tènpli anba presyon—faktè ki te konsidere konsiderabman te ajoute riske pèdikontwòl. Easter, ki te fèmen yon kòmèn ki te fòt avèk ti gason sa yo ak te traite yo konsa kòm timoun yo prop, te deklare dènye fwa li te vire pou evite yon lòt veyikil, men plizyè témoins te di pa gen okenn lòt veyikil lè sa a. Li te admèt de kòt de tèt ak pèt de konsèy poul. Menm si li ak papa ti gason sa yo, Allan Portor, ak fi 12 an yo, Liam, te sòti avèk lèz mòt ki te fèb, domaj emosyonèl la te trè lour. Nan Kòt Norwich, Jij Mark Lucraft te rikonnèt remòs la fòt, ki te dekri li kòm 'youn moun ki te brèk', ki pral tènpli tout lavi li avèk travaj sa a. Li te imposen yon peyis 15 mwa, suspendi pou 2 an, ak interdi li pwochen pou 4 an—meme si li te di li pa vle pwochen anko. Tèt ti gason sa yo te dekri Tamzin kòm yon moun ki te toutan joui, mizikal, ak kompasif, ak Jessica kòm yon esprit vivan ki te pouse tout sal la avèk danse, chante, ak lèt chokola yo. Polis Norfolk te mete an avant ke menm si kondisyon pney yo te jwe yon ròl, se konsèy poul Easter ki te pouse direkman nan mòt sœ yo. 'Yon vizit Nwel te vin yon trajedi poul nèg pa pèmèt,' te di yon spesyalis.

article_content: Convicted rapist Ched Evans could face an additional 14 months out of professional football if he continues pursuing efforts to overturn his conviction. After serving two and a half years of a five-year sentence for the 2011 rape of a 19-year-old woman in Rhyl, North West Wales, Evans was released on license. Since then, he has been unable to secure a contract with any professional football club. His best chance of returning to the sport lies in having his conviction quashed by the Court of Appeal — a process that could take more than a year. During this time, he will have gone four full years without playing professionally. Because he remains under license, Evans is prohibited from leaving the UK for extended periods, forcing him to postpone his planned wedding and honeymoon with fiancée Natasha Massey. Following his release, Evans launched a website funded by his fiancée’s father to advocate for his innocence and submitted an application to the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) to review his case. Several clubs, including Sheffield United and Oldham Athletic, declined to sign him after sponsors and public figures expressed opposition. Prominent figures such as Jessica Ennis-Hill and Charlie Webster withdrew their associations with Sheffield United over the prospect of his return. These decisions sparked a wave of online abuse targeting women associated with the debate. Chloe Finnigan, daughter of TV presenters Richard Madeley and Judy Finnigan, received rape threats after her parents publicly supported Evans’s potential return. Jessica Ennis-Hill also faced similar threats after voicing her stance. PFA chief executive Gordon Taylor stated it would now be 'very difficult' for any club to sign Evans while his conviction stands. Evans has maintained his innocence throughout. In a recent statement, he offered a carefully worded apology for the 'impact' of the night in Rhyl on the victim — a move criticized by many as lacking genuine remorse. Some commentators, including Rod Liddle, have raised questions about the strength of the original conviction, suggesting there may be grounds for appeal. However, the CCRC typically takes around 38 weeks to make a decision, with appeals sometimes taking up to six months to resolve.
translated_content: Ched Evans, konsèkse pou vwole, kapab dwe atend 14 mwa depi li kontinye chache anlèman kònviksyon li. Aprè te pran de an ak demi nan yon peyi kinkan vye de 5 an pou vwole yon fanm 19 an nan Rhyl, Pwòp Nòt Ouest, Evans te libere avèk lisans. Depi sa, li pa ka jwenn yon kontrat ak yon klèb pwofesyonèl de fòtbol. Chans li pi bon pou retounen sou teren se si kònviksyon li anlèman pa Kòt Apel — proses ki kapab dwe pase plis pase yon ane. Pandan sa, li ta dwe pase kat an sans jwe pwofesyonèl. Koska li toujou sou lisans, Evans pa kapab kite Angleteri pou periode long, ki fè li mete mariaj ak fiancée li Natasha Massey sou pouspwen. Aprè li te libere, Evans te kreye yon sit web finansye pa pè fiancée li pou defenni inosans li ak te soumèt yon aplikasyon pou Komisyon Revizyon Kas Kriminel (CRKC) pou revize kas li. Kèk klèb, tankou Sheffield United ak Oldham Athletic, te refize signe li aprè sponsor ak figi publik te eksprime opozisyon yo. Figi enpotan tankou Jessica Ennis-Hill ak Charlie Webster te retire asosyasyon yo avèk Sheffield United sou posibilite retounen li. Decizyon sa yo te provoke yon ond piblik ki vize fanm ki gen lavi avèk deba sa a. Jessica Ennis-Hill te gen menm mena yo aprè li te deklare pozisyon li. PFA prezidan Gordon Taylor te di li kapab 'tres difisil' pou yon klèb signe Evans tanpri kònviksyon li pa anlèman. Evans te kontinye di li inosan. Nan yon deklarasyon reyis, li te fè yon aploji sove pou 'efè' nwi a nan Rhyl sou vitim lan — yon mouvman k ap kritike pa plis moun kòm pa gen remorsi vre. Kèk kominatè, tankou Rod Liddle, te poze kesyon sou forès kònviksyon orijinal la, sipoze ke gen posibilite apel. Menm jan, CRKC gen anviwon 38 semèn pou fè yon desizyon, ak apel yo kapab pran jiska sis mwa pou rezoud.

article_content: On June 4, 1969, Mexican Airways Flight 704 crashed into the mountains near Monterrey, claiming the lives of 79 people — among them, Rafael Osuna Herrera, Mexico’s greatest tennis player and a national hero. At the peak of his career, Osuna had just led Mexico to a historic Davis Cup victory over Australia, capping a decade of dominance on the international stage. A Grand Slam singles champion, former World No. 1, and revolutionary doubles specialist, he remains one of the most gifted yet overlooked figures in tennis history. Playing in the pre-television era, Osuna’s brilliance was captured only in grainy black-and-white footage — yet even today, his speed and creativity stand out. While modern stars like Rafael Nadal wear down opponents with relentless baseline rallies, Osuna ended points with lightning-fast volleys, often rushing the net after his serve. Legendary broadcaster Bud Collins called him 'the quickest of his era,' recalling Osuna’s stunning 1963 U.S. Open final win over Frank Froehling. His nephew, Rafael Belmar, revealed that Osuna’s reflexes were honed as a junior table tennis player — and even martial arts legend Chuck Norris once said Osuna was one of only two men he knew who could catch a fly with two fingers. A student at the University of Southern California, Osuna was coached by George Toley, who noted that Osuna’s technique was technically flawed — but his natural athleticism made it irrelevant. 'He could move like a GOD!' Toley wrote. Osuna’s first major triumph came in 1960 at Wimbledon, winning doubles with his USC roommate Dennis Ralston — the first unseeded pair ever to do so. He later formed a legendary partnership with fellow Mexican Antonio Palafox, pioneering the now-common 'I-formation' in doubles, where the server’s partner crouches near the center line to intercept returns. In 1963, Osuna stunned the tennis world by defeating serve-and-volley powerhouse Froehling at the U.S. Open — not by attacking the net, but by standing deep behind the baseline and hitting impossible lobs. He became the first — and still only — Mexican to win a Grand Slam singles title. Despite being offered $120,000 by pro tour promoter Jack Kramer in 1962, Osuna refused to turn professional. Instead, he joined Philip Morris, remained an amateur, and kept competing in Wimbledon and other elite tournaments. He owned homes in Beverly Hills, Mexico City, and Caracas — wealth never drove him. In 1964, he and Palafox won their third Grand Slam doubles title at Wimbledon and became the first Mexicans to appear on the tournament’s official program. That same year, he graduated from USC with a business degree. In 1968, during Mexico’s Olympic Games, Osuna won exhibition gold in both singles and doubles — medals the family still treasures, since tennis wasn’t an official Olympic sport until 1988. His final great act came in 1969, when he single-handedly defeated Australia 3-2 in a Davis Cup zonal final, clinching the match with a dramatic win over top Australian Bill Bowrey — using unorthodox tactics to deny his opponent at the net. Just days later, Osuna died in the plane crash. Mexico lost its greatest tennis champion, and the sport lost a visionary. Today, a statue stands in his honor, and Mexico’s main tennis stadium bears his name. He was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 1979. Yet, as Mexico struggles to produce world-class players today, Osuna’s name fades into obscurity. 'Maybe Mexico isn’t good at celebrating our heroes,' says his nephew. 'He’s become a footnote.' But as Spanish legend Manuel Santana once said: 'The man surpasses his achievements.'

Alòske li te nan pike kariyè li, Osuna te viyen Meksik pou yon viktwar historik sou Australye nan Davis Cup, fini yon dekenn de dominasyon sou etap inyènal. Yon chanpyon Grand Slam, anvan nimewo 1 mondial, ak yon spesyalis revolisyonè nan dwa, li rete yon nan plis geniyè ak plis oublie figi nan tenis. Li te jwe nan èpok pre-televizyon, brillans li te kapte sèlman nan fòm bwè-nèg gran — menm jan moun ki pa konnen tenis, vitès ak kreativite li fèt diferan. Tandiske jwèt modèn tankou Rafael Nadal fatige advesè yo avèk rallys long nan linè fond, Osuna te fini pwen yo avèk volè vif, souvan al nan rezo aprè sèv li. Kominikatè lejendè Bud Collins te rele li 'pi vif de èpok li,' epi li te souvene viktwar osèn Osuna nan final U.S. Open 1963 kontra Frank Froehling. Neve li, Rafael Belmar, te revele ke refleks Osuna te evolwe nan jwèt tab la, ak menm karekteristik Chuck Norris te di li te yon nan sèl de moun ki kapab pran yon mouch avèk de pous. 'Li te kapab move tankou ZIO!' Toley te ekri. Premye viktwar mòdèn Osuna te vin nan 1960 nan Wimbledon, li te gagnen dwa avèk kòlèg li nan USC, Dennis Ralston — premye pè ki pa sèn epi te gagnen. Li te fòme yon patnèship lejendè avèk kompatriyot li Antonio Palafox, ki te inovè yon fòmasyon ki toujou itilize jodi a 'I-formation', kote partnè sèv a kouche nan linè sentral pou evite repons. Nan 1963, Osuna te etonn monde tenis ak viktwar li sou Froehling nan U.S. Open — pa al nan rezo, men l te stade lòt nan linè fond epi fè lòb imposib. Li te devni premye — ak sèl — Meksiken ki gagne yon tit Grand Slam sèl. Malgre ke li te pwopozè $120,000 pa Jack Kramer, pwomòtè tour profesyonèl nan 1962, Osuna te refize fè profesyonèl. Plutot li te al nan Philip Morris, te rete amatè, epi te kontinye jwe nan Wimbledon ak lòt koumanfòm elèv. Li te gen kay yo nan Beverly Hills, Meksiko City, ak Caracas — lavi pa te pouse li. Nan 1964, li ak Palafox te gagnen twazyèm tit Grand Slam dwa yo nan Wimbledon, epi yo te devni premye Meksiken yo ki te parèt sou program ofisyèl tourno a. Annè sa a, li te diplome nan USC avèk yon degre enpòtan. Nan 1968, pandan Jwèt Olimpik Meksik, Osuna te gagnen meday dòr eksibisyon nan sèl ak dwa — meday ki tèt fami a konsève, paske tenis pa te yon moun olimpik ofisyèl tan 1988. Dernyè aksyon li te vin nan 1969, lè li te sèlman defèti Australye 3-2 nan final zonal Davis Cup, vin viktwar dramatik sou Bill Bowrey, itilize taktik inovatè pou refize advesè a nan rezo. Jouk apre kèk jou, Osuna te mouri nan akidenn avyon an. Meksik te pèdi pi bon jwèt tenis li, ak sport lan te pèdi yon visyonè. Jodi a, yon staty akòt nan onor li, ak stadyam pèn tenis Meksik gen non li. Li te kore nan Hall of Fame Tenis International nan 1979. Menm tan ke Meksik ap chache gen jwèt mondial, non Osuna ap disparet nan obsirisite. 'Pètèt Meksik pa bon pou konsève ero yo,' di neve li. 'Li te vin yon nota.' Menm tan ke legenn espagnòl Manuel Santana te di yon fwa: 'L’moun lan depase rezilta li.'

article_content: Though Bob Dylan insisted, 'This here ain't no protest song,' his 1963 classic 'Blowin' in the Wind' became one of the most iconic political anthems in history. Even when artists deny intent, audiences imbue music with meaning—and Dylan’s song resonated deeply with the civil rights movement. Dylan stood atop a long tradition of folk protest, stretching from 14th-century England's 'Cutty Wren' to 1940s labor champions Woody Guthrie and Pete Seeger. When Dylan electrified his sound, protest music didn’t vanish—it migrated. Rock n’ roll absorbed its spirit: Hendrix’s searing 'Star-Spangled Banner' at Woodstock in 1969, CSNY’s 'Ohio' after the Kent State shootings in 1970, James Brown’s defiant 'Say It Loud' in 1968, and Marvin Gaye’s soulful 'What’s Going On' in 1971 all carried political weight. Hip-hop carried the torch in the 1980s with Public Enemy’s unflinching critiques of systemic racism, while UK punk bands like The Clash channeled anger into anthems against racial division. By the 21st century, the solo guitarist with a message seemed outdated. Mainstream pop stars like Pink tried with 'Dear Mr. President'—but even that song was strategically released only in Europe and Australia, raising questions about performative activism. Yet protest didn’t disappear—it transformed. Artists like Bono and Bob Geldof moved beyond songs, leveraging global platforms like Live 8 (2005) and Live Earth (2007) to pressure world leaders on poverty and climate change. Geldof openly dismissed protest songs as 'a laughable farce,' arguing real change comes from influencing policy, not lyrics. Though critics called Live 8 self-congratulatory, it succeeded: global media attention pressured G8 leaders into pledging $50 billion in aid and canceling debt for poor nations—even if, as the DATA report later confirmed, follow-through on aid and trade reforms faltered. Today, musicians aren’t outsiders shouting from the margins. They’re insiders using wealth, influence, and corporate networks to lobby from within. Whether through concerts, lobbying, or advocacy, music’s political voice remains powerful—but its form has changed.

Meme lè mizisyen yo refize entansyon yo, audiyan yo ap imbri mezik la ak sennifikasyon—ak son Dylan te rezonan anpil avèk mouvman kiviltè. Dylan te sou yon tradisyon long ki pase de 'Cutty Wren' Anglè 14yèm syèk la pou mizisyen travay 1940 yo konsa Woody Guthrie ak Pete Seeger. Lè Dylan te elektrifye son mizik li, mizik pou proteste pa te disparèt—li te migrate. Rock n’ roll te absorbe spiri li: Hendrix te jwe 'Star-Spangled Banner' sou tan Woodstock 1969, CSNY te ekri 'Ohio' aprè masak Kent State 1970, James Brown te jwe 'Say It Loud' 1968, ak Marvin Gaye te fè 'What’s Going On' 1971 tout sa yo te gen pouvo politik. Hip-hop te pran tòch la nan 1980 yo avèk kritik Public Enemy sou rasistm sistèmik, tandiske bann punk Angleter yo konsa The Clash te chanje kolèr yo kont diskòd rasyal. Lè 21yèm syèk te vini, mizisyen solè ak gitar pa te plis tankou yon mode. Mizisyen pop moun ki te eseye avèk 'Dear Mr. President'—menm chante sa te sèlman distribye an Ewope ak Ayiti, sa te leve kesyon sou aktivis pèfòrmans. Men protest pa te disparèt—li te transforme. Mizisyen konsa Bono ak Bob Geldof te al pi lwen pase chante yo, yo te itilize platform global konsa Live 8 (2005) ak Live Earth (2007) pou presye dirijan mondyal sou povrete ak chanjman klomatik. Pou yon konsern, pou lobi, oswa pou aktivis, vo politik mizik la toujou pwòp—men form li te chanje.

article_content: Before the sun fully rises over Williamsport, Pennsylvania, the sharp crack of a baseball bat echoes through the quiet morning air. This small town hosts the Little League Baseball World Series every August, drawing tens of thousands of fans who come to watch young athletes from around the globe chase the ultimate prize in youth baseball. But long before the crowds show up, a group of 11-year-olds from Lugazi, Uganda, is already swinging away in the practice cages—downhill, near the empty stadium, where no one else is watching. Their journey to this moment wasn’t easy. Uganda isn’t known for baseball—it’s a nation ruled by football. Yet, Coach Henry Odong, one of the country’s earliest baseball players and an employee at the local Mehta Group sugar factory, has spent years teaching the game to kids who have little more than passion and grit. Last year, another Ugandan team won the regional qualifier in Poland but was blocked from entering the U.S. due to visa complications tied to paperwork errors. This year, Lugazi stepped up. With help from the U.S. Embassy and Little League officials, they cleared every hurdle—and became the first African team ever to compete in Williamsport. For many of these boys, baseball is more than sport. Shortstop Tonny Okello plays to forget the weight of home, where his mother is fighting breast cancer. 'I think about her when I’m out there,' he says. 'She hides how hard it is. I want to be strong for her.' None of the players’ families could afford to travel with them, yet when Lugazi was introduced at the opening ceremony, they received the loudest cheers of the entire event. They didn’t win their opening games against Panama—the experienced Latin American champions—but they didn’t back down. Their first batter, Justine Makisimu, crushed a hit on the very first pitch. Later, they defeated the U.S. team from Oregon in a consolation match, giving Africa its first-ever victory in Little League World Series history. Eleven-year-old Ronald Olaa, playing third base, summed it up perfectly: 'I like history. And we’ve made it.'

Vila ki ti sa a te akseptè Championship Baseball Little League chak aout, ki ap tounen moun moun nan nan konsèn pou wè jwenn yo kote yo ap chache koupe final nan jeunès la. Men, avan konsèn yo arive, yon gwoup timoun 11 an ki pa nan Lugazi, Ugan, deja ap frappe bal la nan kaj la—anba, apre stadion vide a, kote pa gen moun ki wè yo. Pato a yo pa te fasil. Ugan pa konn pou baseball—li se yon peyi kote fotbal dominè. Men, antrenè Henry Odong, yon nan premye jwenn baseball nan peyi a ak yon emplwaye nan fabrik mòs Mehta, te kousi jwenn yo pou timoun ki pa gen plis pase pasyon ak kras. An 2022, yon lòt timoun Ugan te genyen kvalifikasyon an nan Pôl, men yo te refizé entre Etazini a pa konsèkans papye yo. An 2023, Lugazi te pran plas yo. Ak aji U.S. Embassy ak Little League, yo te detèmine tout obstak yo—ak fèt premye timoun Afrikèn ki te jwe nan Williamsport. Pou plis timoun sa yo, baseball pa sèlman yon jwèt. Timoun ki ap jwe kòm shortstop Tonny Okello, ap jwe pou bliye lèlèt yo a, kote manman li ap bataj kont kancer sey. 'Mwen panse sou li lè mwen la,' li di. 'Li pa montre kòman li difisil. Mwen vle ete fò pou li.' Pa gen yon sèl fami ki te kapab pafe voyaj la, men lè Lugazi te prezante nan seremoni ouvètir la, yo te resevwa kri yo pi fò nan tout evenman an. Yo te pèdi match yo dènye kontra Panama—champion Latè Ameriken ki te fèt 7 fwa nan historik la—men yo pa te kòmbe. Premier batè yo, Justine Makisimu, te fèt yon bon kou nan premye bal la. Aprè, yo te gagnen match konpensasyon kontra ekip U.S. nan Oregon, ak fèt premye gagn nan historik Afrikèn nan Championship Little League. Ronald Olaa, 11 an, ki ap jwe trozyèm baz, te rezime sa a perfèkteman: 'Mwen renmen istwa. Epi nou fèt istwa.'

Check. Kids playing to forget hardship, chasing dreams bigger than their fields. #UgandaMadeHistory #LittleLeagueHeroes #BaseballBeyondBorders

article_content: Real Madrid have firmly denied rumors that striker Alvaro Morata will join Juventus on loan this summer. Spanish media reported that the 21-year-old had agreed to personal terms for a potential move to Turin. However, Real Madrid president Florentino Perez told Spanish radio station Cadena Ser: 'I am friends with the Juventus executives and president Andrea Agnelli. But I have not spoken to them about Morata—and honestly, the possibility he goes to Turin is zero.' Morata, who has one year left on his contract, is reportedly eager to seek more playing time away from the Bernabéu. Arsenal have been strongly linked with a move for the Spain U21 international, while Bundesliga side Wolfsburg are also interested. In the 2013/14 season, Morata made just three league starts but scored eight goals in 23 appearances across all competitions. 'I will meet with the player and we will try to find the best solution for him and for the club,' Perez added.

article_content: Scientists have sequenced the oldest complete human genome, derived from the remains of an anatomically modern male who lived in Western Siberia approximately 45,000 years ago. His fossilized thighbone was discovered in 2008 near the village of Ust’-Ishim, on the banks of the River Irtysh, by an ivory hunter searching for mammoth tusks. Radiocarbon dating confirms the bone is about 45,000 years old, making it the oldest directly dated modern human remains found outside Africa and the Middle East. Anthropologist Bence Viola noted that the bone’s morphology indicates it belongs to an early modern human — an individual closely related to the direct ancestors of people alive today. Dr. Janet Kelso of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology extracted DNA from the femur and led genomic analysis alongside colleagues under the direction of Svante Pääbo. Analysis revealed that this individual carried approximately 2% Neanderthal ancestry — comparable to levels seen in present-day East Asians and Europeans. By examining the length of Neanderthal DNA segments in his genome, researchers determined that interbreeding occurred between 7,000 and 13,000 years before his lifetime — placing the event between 50,000 and 60,000 years ago. This refined timeline aligns with the known expansion of modern humans into Eurasia and significantly narrows previous estimates, which ranged from 37,000 to 86,000 years ago. Genetic comparisons show the Ust’-Ishim man was equally related to ancient Europeans and modern East Asians, suggesting his population diverged from the ancestors of modern West and East Eurasians either just before or at the time of their split. Chemical isotopes in the bone suggest his diet included berries, nuts, vegetables, meat, and fish. Researchers propose he may have belonged to an early wave of human migrants into Europe and Central Asia whose lineage did not survive in modern populations. Svante Pääbo stated, 'It is very satisfying that we now have a high-quality genome not only from Neanderthals and Denisovans, but also from a very early modern human.'
translated_content: Siyansis yo te sekwanse jenom komin plek la pi vye a, ki te pran nan rezis anmèn modern ki te viv nan Sibèri occidental anvan 45,000 an. Os fèm li te detekte an 2008 tou pre vila Ust’-Ishim, sou rivyè Irtysh, pa yon chache ivoir ki te chache tèt mamon. Datage karbon 14 konfirme os la se anvan 45,000 an, epi li se os modern pi vye ki te detekte a l’èkstèriè ak Afrik ak Moyen-Orient. Antropoloj Bence Viola te anonse ke morfoloji os la montre li se yon anmèn modern préko — yon endivid ki gen yon liyon direk avèk anmèn ki viv jodi a. Doktè Janet Kelso nan Institut Max Planck pou Antropoloji Evolitiv te pran ADN nan fèm li epi te dirije analiz jenomik la ak kolèg yo sous direksyon Svante Pääbo. Analiz la te revele ke endivid lan te gen aproksimativman 2% ADN Neandertal — kòm sa ki gen anmèn modèn ki viv nan Asya oriental ak Evrop. Enpòtan analiz longè segman ADN Neandertal yo nan jenom li, rezisatè yo te konprann ke koupè a te fèt anvan 7,000 a 13,000 an avan li te mouri — ki plase evenman an ant 50,000 ak 60,000 an. Tim lin ajou sa a konfòme ak ekspansion anmèn modern nan Euryazi epi pèti yon gran fenèt estime pètèt ant 37,000 ak 86,000 an. Kòmparason jenetik montre ke nèg Ust’-Ishim te egaleman liye avèk anmèn Evropéyen anpil ak anmèn Asya oriental modèn, sa ki suggere ke popilasyon li te separè avèk ansestr yo Evropéyen ak Asyatiyen oubyen anvan oswa nan menm tan kote yo te separè. Isotòp kimik nan os la suggere ke diet li te konpozè de bèt, noz, legim, viand ak pois. Rechèchè yo pwopoze ke li te kapab pati yon vòl préko migran nan Evrop ak Asya sentral ki pa te lajenn anyen nan popilasyon modèn. Svante Pääbo te di, 'Li trè satisfè pou nou gen yon jenom kalite elève pa sèlman nan Neandertal ak Denisovèn, men tou nan yon anmèn modern trè préko.'

article_content: (CNN) — Add REO Speedwagon to the growing list of musical acts canceling performances at SeaWorld due to public outcry fueled by the documentary 'Blackfish.' 'Due to concerns regarding our February 16 appearance at SeaWorld, we have chosen to cancel the performance,' the rock band stated on its Facebook page Friday. A promoter could easily organize a concert series featuring the artists who have withdrawn from SeaWorld in recent weeks—including Trisha Yearwood, Willie Nelson, Cheap Trick, Heart, and Barenaked Ladies. These artists pulled out of SeaWorld’s 'Bands, BBQ and Brew' concert series amid mounting pressure from fans who launched online petitions, shared messages on Twitter, and posted on Facebook pages urging them not to perform at the Orlando theme park. The surge in protest followed the October premiere of CNN’s documentary 'Blackfish,' which recounts the 2010 death of a SeaWorld trainer killed by an orca and raises serious questions about the safety and ethics of keeping killer whales in captivity. 'In light of recent concerns, Trisha has decided to remove the February 22 date from her upcoming tour plans,' Yearwood’s representative told CNN Thursday. SeaWorld confirmed REO Speedwagon’s cancellation Friday and referred to prior statements on the withdrawals. 'We expect that other artists will be targeted in this campaign,' SeaWorld spokesman Nick Gollattscheck told CNN on Wednesday and Thursday, beginning with Cheap Trick’s withdrawal. The park’s six-week concert schedule—originally featuring Martina McBride, 38 Special, Justin Moore, and Scotty McCreery—has been removed from SeaWorld’s website. It now simply promises 'incredible concerts with top artists in classic rock and country music.' SeaWorld is actively seeking replacement acts, according to Gollattscheck. 'We’ll announce the full lineup of bands when all artists have been confirmed. We’ll repost the schedule on our site then.' The Canadian rock band Barenaked Ladies were the first to cancel, responding to a petition on Change.org. 'This is a complicated issue, and we don’t claim to understand all of it, but we don’t feel comfortable proceeding with the gig at this time,' the band said on Facebook. 'I don’t agree with the way they treat their animals,' Willie Nelson said on December 6 when announcing his cancellation. 'It wasn’t that hard a deal for me.' Heart’s sisters Nancy and Ann Wilson did not elaborate when announcing their decision last week, though they acknowledged it was 'due to the controversial documentary film.' 'We’re disappointed a small group of misinformed individuals was able to deny fans what would have been great concerts at SeaWorld,' Gollattscheck said. SeaWorld maintains that artists should learn the facts firsthand. 'The bands and artists have a standing invitation to visit any of our parks to see for themselves—or speak to any of our animal experts—to understand how we care for animals and how little truth there is to the allegations made by animal extremist groups opposed to the zoological display of marine mammals,' he added. SeaWorld asserts that 'Blackfish' overlooks its conservation initiatives and scientific research.

article_content: Alan Evans, 35, is accused of killing his wife, Louise, 32, after she discovered he was having an affair with Amanda Chadwick, a 30-year-old married teaching assistant at their children’s school. Worcester Crown Court heard that Evans attempted to make Louise’s death appear as a tragic accident by placing a skipping rope and a vacuum cleaner beside her body. Chadwick testified that their affair began when they met to let their children play together or walk dogs, but later became physical, with secret meetings at hotels and sexual encounters in each other’s marital beds when their spouses were away. Over 1,000 text messages between Evans and Chadwick were read to the jury, revealing intimate details and coordinated efforts to deceive Louise and Chadwick’s husband, Simon. Just one month before Louise’s death, Chadwick said the couple had discussed running away together and starting a family, despite knowing Louise struggled to conceive. Chadwick stated that Evans mocked Louise’s infertility, calling it insensitive — even if directed at himself, he wouldn’t have joked about it. She admitted to sending fabricated text messages to both Louise and Simon to mislead them, including one claiming she was trying to save her marriage. Despite the affair, Chadwick said she grew close to Louise, spending time with her at the movies and visiting each other’s homes. Prosecutor Jonas Hankin QC highlighted that Louise confronted Evans after discovering the messages, leading to a furious phone call at work. Evans denies one count of murder. The trial, expected to last another five weeks, continues.
