article_content: In our Behind the Scenes series, CNN correspondents share their experiences covering news and analyze the stories behind the events. Tito Mukhopadhyay uses poetry to communicate with his mother, Soma. The autistic teenager is a published author. (CNN) — Tito Mukhopadhyay shuffles to the front door of his home in Austin, Texas, returning from school — something that would have been unthinkable just a few years ago. His mother, 45-year-old Soma Mukhopadhyay, is considered a pioneer in a breakthrough approach for some autistic children often stigmatized as 'mentally retarded.' Soma never accepted that label for her 19-year-old son. After hearing Tito’s story, you’ll never view an autistic child the same way. 'How was your day?' Soma asks. Before Tito can answer, he compulsively moves around the house — placing the TV remote in its proper spot, arranging the salt and pepper shakers just so. Then he sits at his specially designed keyboard to type his response: 'It was like a floating kangaroo that kept itself invisible.' Tito’s cryptic phrasing stems from his neurological condition, yet his unique way of expressing himself has become a powerful gift — one that has brought him recognition within a deeply misunderstood community. Though Tito is nearly nonverbal, he comes alive when he picks up a pencil or taps on his keyboard. He is a poet and the author of several books and essays in which he eloquently describes what it means to be autistic. He explains why he avoids eye contact, what it feels like to be fixated on a ceiling fan, and how his brain struggles to process sound, touch, and sight simultaneously. Experts confirm Tito’s observations about autism. One doctor described it as a failure of neural integration. While no consensus exists on its exact cause, most researchers believe autism arises from a combination of genetic predisposition and environmental triggers. The developmental disorder affects how the brain processes information and how individuals interact with the world. Some speculate links to childhood vaccines, pesticides, or medications taken during pregnancy — but experts agree there is no single cause. Autism symptoms vary widely — from mild to severe, with some individuals requiring lifelong support. Many people with autism absorb information easily, but their brains struggle to organize it into coherent thought or language. Tito has offered experts rare insight into this inner experience. His poetry includes lines like: 'I am he. And I am me. I am he behind that mirror. I am me watching the he.' One of his favorite books is Plato’s 'Republic.' The world might never have known about Tito’s talent without his mother, Soma, originally from India. Doctors there told her Tito was mentally retarded and beyond help. She left her career in chemistry to teach him herself. Eventually, a U.S.-based organization brought Soma and Tito — then 10 years old — to the United States to study him, as he defied the stereotypical profile of autism. Soma’s teaching method is called the Rapid Prompting Method (RPM). I observed her working with other children at the HALO Center — Helping Autism through Learning and Outreach — in Austin, Texas, where she teaches while Tito attends school. RPM begins by having children point to words on paper. Once they master that, they use a stencil. If motor skills improve, they progress to typing on a customized keyboard. RPM appears effective for many children at HALO, which maintains a yearlong waiting list for its four-day therapy sessions. Progress often takes years. However, RPM has not been validated through long-term scientific studies, and Soma faces criticism. Some call her methods overly demanding and unproven. Unlike many therapies, she never offers praise, high-fives, or treats — a stark contrast to conventional reward-based approaches. 'I don’t see the child as autistic. I don’t see the label at all,' Soma says, speaking rapidly in her melodic Indian accent. 'I see the child as a person. Just as I would speak to any person, I speak to a child — because the world doesn’t speak to them slowly.' Dr. Michael Merzenich, a neuroscientist at the University of California, was among the first experts to take notice of Soma’s work. He believes RPM works. 'There is no doubt these children are using their minds to generate their own words and express their own ideas,' he says. Unlike discredited facilitated communication methods, Soma does not physically guide the children’s hands. 'Imagine what it would be like,' he adds, 'to understand everything said to you — to think clearly — yet be unable to communicate your thoughts.' Merzenich doesn’t claim RPM helps every autistic child, but he’s certain it can benefit thousands. On this day in Austin, I watched several children in therapy. Some struggled intensely. The sessions were stressful, yet small breakthroughs occurred — answers came correctly, often after long pauses. Soma conducts about ten therapy sessions daily. 'You must be exhausted,' I said. 'I can’t be,' she replied sharply, smiling. 'I have to go home and teach Tito.' At home, I asked Tito if he’s happier now that he can communicate. He wrote a lengthy response on a clipboard: 'I can’t say whether I am happy or not, because happiness is a state of my mind. So sometimes I think I’m happy. Other times, it’s hollowness.' It’s a profoundly human observation — one many of us recognize at some point in our lives. Soma smiled and didn’t miss a beat. 'Keep writing,' she urged. 'Keep going.'
translated_content: Nan seris 'Behind the Scenes' nou, korespondan CNN yo partaj eksperyans yo nan rapòtaj nouvo yo ak analiz istwa ki dèyè evenman yo. Tito Mukhopadhyay itilize poezie pou komonike avèk manman li, Soma. Je nèg otistik sa a se yon auteur publie. (CNN) — Tito Mukhopadhyay al nan pòt la nan kay li nan Austin, Texas, ki retounen nan ekol — bagay ki te imposib il y a kèk ane avan. Manman li, Soma Mukhopadhyay, 45 an, se yon pionyè nan yon metòd revolisyonè pou kèk timoun otistik ki souvent etikete kòm 'menèl retardè.' Soma pa janm aksepte etiket sa a pou fi 19 an li. Aprè ou entan istwa Tito, ou pa pral plis wè yon timoun otistik menm jan. 'Kouman jounen ou te ye?' Soma di. Avan Tito ka reponn, li deplase avèk osefman nan kay la — mete telekominand la nan endri li, rangi sèl ak piper la nan bon endri yo. Pita li sèt nan klavyè spesyal li pou tape repons li: 'Jounen an te tankou yon kangourou ki flote ki te konsève li anvisib.' Repons kriptik Tito a vin de konplike nèvwojik li, men mod li espresyon li se yon don ki te fè li konn nan yon kominite ki mal konprann. Menm si Tito pa preske pa pale, li redevi viv lè li pren yon stylo oswa tapé sou klavyè li. Li se yon poèt ak auteur de plizyè liv ak esè ki dekri avèk elokans sa ki gen pou wè avèk otizm. Li eksplike pouki li evite kontak vye, ki jan sa a pouw fèt lè ou kapab fiksè sou yon ventilatè sou tèt ou, ak kòman nèv li gen pwoblèm pou pran son, tan, ak imaj an mème tan. Eksèp yo konfime observasyon Tito a sou otizm. Yon medekan te dekri li kòm yon echèk integrasyon nèvwojik. Pa gen konvensyon sou kòmansman li, men plis rèsèchè yo kroie otizm gen pou wè avèk yon kombinason de predisposisyon jenetik ak faktè enviwonnmanèl. Diskòd devlopman sa a afekte kòman nèv la pran enfòmasyon ak kòman timoun an interaki avèk monn an. Kèk moun panse l pa gen pou wè avèk vaksin timoun, pesticid oswa medikaman pou mè nan gravidès — men eksèp yo tout konvini ke pa gen yon sèl kòmansman. Sinptom otizm varie anpil — nan yon fòm leger pou yon fòm sevyè, avèk kèk moun ki bezwen soutèn pou tout la vies yo. Plis moun otistik kapab absorbe enfòmasyon an byen, men nèv yo gen pwoblèm pou organizi li an panyèl koheran oswa langaj. Tito te bay eksèp yo yon ensèn rare sou sa ki gen pou wè avèk sa. Poezi li gen lign sa yo: 'Mwen se li. Et mwen se mwen. Mwen se li dèyè miroir lan. Mwen se mwen ki vwaye li.' Yon nan liv prefere li se 'Republic' de Platon. Monn te ka pa janm konnen talan Tito a san manman li, Soma, ki te nan Inde. Medekan la te di li Tito te menèl retardè ak depi anndan. Li abandone karir li an kimik pou l ensèn li. Fèk yon organisasyon Etazini te amene Soma ak Tito — ki te 10 an — nan Etazini pou etidye li, paske li defiye stereotip timoun otistik. Metòd ensèn Soma a rele Rapid Prompting Method (RPM). Mwen te wè l travay avèk lòt timoun nan HALO Center — Helping Autism through Learning and Outreach — nan Austin, Texas, kote l ensèn tandan Tito ale ekol. RPM an kòmanse avèk mande timoun yo pou yo montre mo yo sou fey papye. Lè yo maîtrise sa a, yo itilize stensil la. Si sik mòtè yo amelyore, timoun yo ap tapé sou yon klavyè kousime. RPM pa gen pou wè avèk timoun yo nan HALO, ki gen yon lis atenn anpil ane. Avanseman an dwe pran ane. Menm si RPM pa te teste nan etid syantifik long te, Soma gen kritik. Kèk moun di metòd li a tro fò ak pa prouvè. Tankou plis terapi, li pa janm bay aplodi, kòl oswa reyèl — yon kontrast net ak metòd reyèl konvansyonèl. 'Mwen pa wè timoun kòm otistik. Mwen pa wè etiket lan pafè,' Soma di, pale vif avèk akant Indyen melodi li. 'Mwen wè timoun kòm yon moun. Tankou mwen ta pale avèk yon moun lòt, mwen ta pale avèk yon timoun, paske monn pa pale avèk yo anmanèt.' Doktè Michael Merzenich, neyrosyantist nan Universite Kaliforni, te yon nan premye eksèp ki te remare travay Soma a. Li kroie RPM ta travay. 'Pa gen okenn deoub, timoun yo itilize nèv yo pou genere mot yo ak espresyon ide yo,' li di. Tankou metòd komunikasyon fasilitè ki te dekredite, Soma pa deplase mòt timoun yo. 'Imajine ki jan sa ta dwe ye,' li ajoute, 'pou konprann tout sa ki di ou — pou pense klè — men pa kapab komonike ide ou.' Merzenich pa prétan RPM ta travay pou tout timoun otistik, men li konvini li ka benefisye milyèn. Ajourod’hui nan Austin, mwen te wè plizyè timoun nan terapi yo. Kèk nan yo te strate anpil. Sesyon yo te stresan, men piti piti avanseman yo te pataje — repons yo te kòrèk, souvan aprè long pous. Soma fè de 10 sesyon terapi jounalisman. 'Ou dwe fatige,' mwen di li. 'Mwen pa ka,' li reponn vèt, souri. 'Mwen dwe retounen kay la pou ensèn Tito.' Nan kay la, mwen te demande Tito si li pi fèt lè li kapab komonike. Li tape yon repons long sou yon klapèt: 'Mwen pa kapab di si mwen fèt oswa pa fèt, paske fèt se yon etat nèv mwen an. Donk, kèk fwa mwen panse mwen fèt. Autre fwa, se vide.' C’est yon observasyon profondman humain — yon ki konprann plis moun nan kòm nou yo a kèk fwa nan vies yo. Soma souri epi pa fè yon pous. 'Kontinye ekrir,' li eksije. 'Kontinye.'

article_content: According to GLAAD’s 17th annual 'Where We Are on TV' report, the 2012-13 television season features the highest number of LGBT characters ever on scripted broadcast networks. Cable networks also saw an increase. Of the 701 regular characters across 97 prime-time shows, 31—4.4%—identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, or transgender, up from 2.9% in 2011. ABC leads all networks with 10 LGBT characters among its 194 regulars (5.2%), including the acclaimed gay couple on 'Modern Family.' FOX follows closely with six LGBT characters (5.1%) out of 118, while CBS made the most significant leap—from just 0.7% to 2.8%, with four LGBT characters among 142 regulars. Its new comedy 'Partners' highlights a gay character in a committed relationship, signaling a deliberate push toward diversity. On cable, representation rose to 35 LGBT characters from 29 last season. HBO’s 'True Blood' remains the most inclusive show with six LGBT roles, while Showtime leads all cable networks with 12. Other platforms like FX, MTV, Syfy, and TeenNick also contributed to the growth. Despite progress, male LGBT characters still dominate broadcast TV at 55.5%, compared to 44.5% for females. Racially, African-American representation climbed to 12% from 9.9%, but Hispanic representation dropped from 5.6% to 4.1%. GLAAD President Herndon Graddick stressed the importance of authentic, nuanced storytelling: 'As more Americans embrace their LGBT loved ones, viewers expect to see themselves reflected on screen.'

Sou 701 karaktè regyèl sou 97 emisyon primtim, 31—4.4%—se LGBT, yon kroisans pa 2.9% an 2011. ABC epi pwochen avèk 10 karaktè LGBT sou 194 regyèl (5.2%), ki gen koupl gòn yo sou 'Modern Family.' FOX aprè a avèk sis karaktè LGBT (5.1%) sou 118, men CBS te fè pi gwo pwogres—de 0.7% pou 2.8%, avèk kat karaktè LGBT sou 142. Komedi nouvo li, 'Partners,' mete an avant yon gòn nan yon relasyon komitman, ki montre yon engajman konsyèy pou diversite. Sou kabl, reprizantasyon monte a 35 karaktè LGBT, alèkile 29 anvan. 'True Blood' d’HBO rele pi inklivyan ak sis karaktè LGBT, men Showtime epi pwochen avèk 12. Autre platfòm tankou FX, MTV, Syfy, ak TeenNick tou kontribye a kroisans sa a. Malgre progres la, karaktè LGBT moun moun dominé televizyon difizyon an a 55.5%, kontrè 44.5% pou fanm. Rasyalman, reprizantasyon Afrikèn-Amerikèn monte a 12% depi 9.9%, men reprizantasyon Hispànik ta chite de 5.6% pou 4.1%. Prezidan GLAAD, Herndon Graddick, te mete a lavi importans kontèks ak istwa nwen pou LGBT: 'Kouman plis Ameriken aksepte fami, zanmi, koleg ak peyi yo LGBT, tèlman audiyan yo antann emisyon yo favori yo, yo atenn pou wouj yo moun yo konnen an jounen a.'

article_content: After one of the most shocking defeats in their history, Spain’s national team is facing a turning point. Coach Vicente del Bosque is quietly evaluating possible changes to his starting XI ahead of their crucial Group B clash against Chile at the Maracanã Stadium. The 5-1 thrashing by the Netherlands wasn’t just a loss—it exposed deep cracks in a team long seen as invincible. Del Bosque isn’t pointing fingers. In fact, he’s resisting the urge to make reactive swaps. ‘We’re not here to blame,’ he said. ‘This tournament moves fast, and we need smart solutions—not panic.’ While fans and pundits are calling for goalkeeping changes after Iker Casillas’ disastrous outing, the captain still holds his place. Del Bosque praised Casillas’ composure in the locker room post-match, noting how he rallied teammates despite personal failure. Criticism has centered on Spain’s reliance on aging stars from their 2010 title-winning squad—especially Piqué, Alonso, and Alba—who’ve struggled to replicate their peak form. But Del Bosque stands firm: ‘Sixteen of our 23 players are world champions. They’ve delivered in qualifiers, the Champions League, and La Liga. We believe in them.’ He adds that seven fresh faces have also earned their spots, signaling a gradual evolution rather than a full overhaul. Spain’s path forward is narrow: beat Chile or risk elimination. Their last meeting in 2010 ended in a 2-1 win, but this time, the context is drastically different. Once feared for their tiki-taka mastery, Spain now looks vulnerable, unprepared for high-pressure opponents like Chile. ‘We’re used to winning,’ Del Bosque admitted. ‘Now we have to learn how to suffer—and still fight.’ The message to the squad is clear: accept the pain, learn from it, and rise. With no room for error, Spain’s next game isn’t just about points—it’s about identity.

article_content: It could have been a scene from a violent video game — but it happened in real life. Just minutes after Grand Theft Auto V launched at midnight, a 23-year-old man was attacked and robbed in Colindale, North London. He had spent hours waiting in line at an Asda supermarket to buy the game and was walking home when a group of teenagers assaulted him. The attackers, estimated to be five or six youths, chased him down a deserted street, stabbing him twice in the back with a kitchen knife and striking him on the head with a brick. They stole the game and his mobile phone, leaving him unconscious on the pavement. The victim, whose identity has not been disclosed, is now recovering in hospital in stable condition. Police believe the attackers targeted him after noticing the large crowd of fans gathered outside the store. The incident occurred on Princes Avenue around 1:20 a.m. on the day of the game’s release. The attack has sparked renewed debate over the impact of violent video games on society. Alison Sherratt, president of the Association of Teachers and Lecturers, warned that children are increasingly mimicking game behavior — citing incidents of kids reenacting in-school violence after watching titles like Grand Theft Auto. Labour MP Keith Vaz condemned the game’s graphic content, urging the industry to better warn consumers and parents to monitor access. Meanwhile, Scotland Yard confirmed the attack was robbery-related and appealed for witnesses. The case has also revived discussions about possible links between violent video games and real-world atrocities, including the shootings by Aaron Alexis, Anders Breivik, and Adam Lanza — all known players of violent games. While no direct causal proof exists, experts continue to call for deeper research into potential correlations.

Li te pase plizyè lèn nan fil pou achte jwèt la nan yon magasin Asda epi li te renmen souvwa lè yon goup timoun yo te atake li. Menm si pa gen preuv direk, espès yo kontinye mande pou etid pi profond sou posib korelasyon yo.

article_content: On the second day of the first Test in Ahmedabad, Sri Lanka fought back strongly after being asked to follow on. Opener Tillakaratne Dilshan starred with a brilliant century, scoring 112 runs and anchoring key partnerships with fellow opener Tharanga Paranavitana (35) and captain Kumar Sangakkara (31). Together, they helped Sri Lanka dominate much of the day, reaching 275 for three by close, still trailing India by 151 runs. Dilshan and Paranavitana put on 74 for the first wicket at a brisk pace, putting pressure back on India. Ishant Sharma eventually broke the stand when Paranavitana edged a delivery outside off stump to wicketkeeper MS Dhoni, who took a sharp catch. After a promising start with the new ball, Zaheer Khan delivered a decisive spell in the final session, dismissing both Dilshan and Sangakkara in successive overs. Dilshan was caught at gully attempting a pulled shot, while Sangakkara top-edged a short ball to Sachin Tendulkar at fine leg. With Sri Lanka reeling at 194 for three, Mahela Jayawardene (36 not out) and Thilan Samaraweera (5 not out) steadied the ship. Samaraweera, who had amassed 1,083 runs in eight Tests during the 2012 calendar year, unleashed a flurry of boundaries off Ravichandran Ashwin, sparking a steady recovery. The unbroken fourth-wicket partnership added 81 runs by stumps, offering Sri Lanka hope for the next day. On Day 1, Sri Lanka’s spinners dismantled India’s lower order. Muttiah Muralitharan claimed three wickets — including Harbhajan Singh and Ishant Sharma — while Chanaka Welegedara removed Rahul Dravid for 177 in the morning session. Dravid’s dismissal came via an inside edge attempting a drive. Harbhajan and Zaheer added 25 runs for the eighth wicket before Sri Lanka’s spinners wrapped up the tail, with Herath trapping Zaheer lbw and Muralitharan finishing off the innings.

article_content: In an unusual twist, the UK’s Treasury building — usually associated with sober budget meetings and spreadsheet-filled desks — became the backdrop for a wild party scene in Fast & Furious 6. The circular courtyard, typically used as a parking spot for civil servants and tax officials, was temporarily turned into a neon-lit underground club, complete with speeding supercars and dancers in short skirts. The film, starring Vin Diesel as Dominic Toretto, features a key sequence where his character arrives in London to reunite his crew, unaware that the glamorous event unfolding before him is actually taking place inside one of Britain’s most iconic government buildings. The location, officially known as Government Offices Great George Street (GOGGS), has housed the Treasury since 1940 and sits just across from St James’ Park and near Parliament. While the public rarely sees the interior, it’s now forever linked to Hollywood action thanks to Universal Pictures, which rented the space over a weekend. Though exact fees were not disclosed, industry sources suggest payments ranged between £2,000 and £5,000 per day — a welcome boost for a department grappling with record public debt of £1.2 trillion. The decision to allow filming wasn’t made by the Treasury itself, but by the private contractor managing the building under a long-term Private Finance Initiative agreement. This mirrors past uses of government properties for film, like the Department for Energy and Climate Change’s rooftop in Skyfall, or the Scotland Office’s minor earnings from the same Bond movie. With borrowing still high and public funds tight, officials seem open to monetizing underused assets — even if it means letting Vin Diesel drift through the heart of British finance.

article_content: Roger Weber, a Republican candidate for the Minnesota House of Representatives, is facing a civil lawsuit after cutting his neighbor’s garage in half with a power saw. Weber claims the structure encroached onto his property, a dispute rooted in a decades-old land division from his father’s 1978 estate plan. The property in question—located in Nashwauk, Minnesota—was originally part of a 40-acre estate owned by Robert Weber, who died in 2012. In 1978, he deeded 39 acres to his son Roger and retained one acre, including a house and the garage. Upon Robert’s death, the remaining parcel passed to his daughter, Ann Anderson, who sold it to Mark Besemann in April 2013. Besemann, unaware of the boundary dispute, arrived to find the garage severed cleanly in two. He alleges that Weber had previously warned he would destroy any structures crossing the property line. Besemann has filed a lawsuit seeking $20,000 in repair costs and $20,000 in punitive damages. Weber insists the act was a legitimate response to trespassing and maintains the conflict is a private matter unrelated to his political campaign. However, media reports have linked the incident to his candidacy, raising public scrutiny. Additional allegations suggest the home’s septic system was deliberately damaged, rendering the property unrentable. The case, originally scheduled for hearing in Itasca County District Court, has been postponed until December 15. Weber has since installed a fence marked with 'No Trespassing' signs along the disputed boundary.

article_content: Beauty may be in the eye of the beholder — but when the Duchess of Cambridge’s first official portrait was unveiled, art critics were nearly unanimous in their harsh reactions. Robin Simon, editor of the British Art Journal, called it 'ghastly, rotten, an out-and-out disaster.' David Lee, formerly of Art Review, offered faint praise: 'Its only saving grace is that it’s not by Rolf Harris.' Yet the Duchess herself, attending the unveiling at the National Portrait Gallery, warmly commended artist Paul Emsley: 'It’s just amazing. Absolutely brilliant.' Prince William echoed her sentiment: 'It’s beautiful, absolutely beautiful.' Most criticisms centered on the portrait’s aged appearance. Despite being only 31, Kate was widely perceived to look 15 years older. Critics pointed to heavy shadows under her eyes, a squared jawline, and a coppery tint to her brunette hair — details that clashed with her public image of youthful radiance. One observer remarked on her 'grey, smoker’s skin'; another noted her lips appeared set in a grimace, not the intended enigmatic smile. The sapphire and diamond earrings she wears were once owned by Princess Diana, gifted by Prince Charles upon their marriage. These same jewels, famously worn by Diana on the July 1994 Vogue cover, were later passed to Kate after her 2011 wedding — a poignant link between generations. Emsley, known for hyper-realistic portraits and past accolades like the 1997 BP Portrait Award, worked from photographs taken during sittings in May and June 2012 — before Kate’s pregnancy. He designed the Windsor blue pussy-bow blouse in the painting, as she wore different outfits across sessions. He admitted altering the color of her eyes slightly to harmonize with the background and blouse, aiming to capture her 'natural self' rather than her official persona. The gallery’s director, Sandy Nairne, called the portrait 'captivating,' but many visitors bypassed it entirely for the nearby video artwork of a sleeping David Beckham by Sam Taylor-Wood. Still, Kate — who holds a degree in the history of art — personally selected Emsley from a shortlist of four artists, underscoring her deep engagement with the project. The 2.5-meter-tall oil painting, donated by art philanthropist Sir Hugh Legatt, reportedly cost over £20,000. Though controversial, it remains a significant cultural artifact — not just for its artistic merit, but for the complex interplay of legacy, perception, and public expectation surrounding Britain’s modern royals.

Men Dches la, ki te prezan nan revelasyon la nan National Portrait Gallery, te konsèy ak Emsley: 'Li se incroyable. Absoilimàn briljan.' article_content: Condoleezza Rice has once again shattered a barrier—this time by becoming one of the first two women ever admitted to Augusta National Golf Club, an institution that barred women for its entire 80-year history. In a statement, Rice expressed deep honor at joining the prestigious club, praising its legacy in the sport of golf. Her admission comes after years of public pressure from women’s advocacy groups and growing scrutiny from political leaders. President Obama, while affirming the club’s autonomy, made clear his personal view: women belong there. Mitt Romney echoed that sentiment during his campaign. Rice’s journey reflects more than prestige; it’s a story of resilience. Born in segregated Birmingham, Alabama, she rose through academia and diplomacy, serving as National Security Advisor and Secretary of State under President George W. Bush. A Stanford professor since 1981, she’s also a published author, concert pianist, and devoted football fan who once joked about wanting to become NFL commissioner. She’s a member of other historically exclusive clubs, like Shoal Creek, which began admitting Black members in 1990. Augusta itself welcomed its first Black member, Ron Townsend, that same year. Though Rice recently ruled out a presidential run, her life story continues to inspire across political lines. At a 2023 commencement speech, she recalled how her parents in Birmingham instilled in her the belief that—even if she couldn’t sit at a Woolworth’s lunch counter—she could still aspire to lead the nation. Now, she sits among the first women to call Augusta National home.

Nan yon deklarasyon, Rice te eksprime yon gran onè pou li te resevwa klasman an, ak aplodi li pou lespri li nan jwenn la. Konsa te vini aprè anpil ane de presyon publik ak presyon politik. article_content: Former Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, 76, has announced his engagement to Francesca Pascale, a 27-year-old television personality and former local politician — a 49-year age gap. Though still legally married to his second wife, Veronica Lario, Berlusconi says Pascale has brought him emotional comfort during a difficult time. He described her during a lengthy interview on his own TV network, Canale 5, as not only physically attractive but deeply principled and emotionally close to him — even calling her a dear friend of his daughter Marina. The couple has been spotted frequently together in Milan, attending AC Milan matches and dining casually at city restaurants. Pascale, who previously served as a city councilor in Naples under Berlusconi’s People of Freedom Party, has long been a vocal supporter, even singing a catchy campaign tune with the line: 'If you pull your knickers down, the ratings go up.' The announcement comes amid Berlusconi’s ongoing criminal trial, where he faces charges related to alleged sexual activity with Karima El Mahroug, then 17, at his private parties known as 'bunga bunga.' Berlusconi insists the events were merely elegant dinners held during a period of deep personal grief — after his mother and sister passed away and shortly after separating from Lario. He claims he felt isolated and sought companionship, not illicit encounters. Italian law considers paying a person under 18 for sex as prostitution with a minor, punishable by up to three years in prison. Berlusconi denies any wrongdoing, accusing prosecutors of launching a politically driven campaign to destroy him. He argues the trial is a tool of defamation meant to undermine his political comeback — a bid he says is necessary to prevent the left from returning to power. Despite his confidence, opinion polls suggest his party trails far behind, sitting at roughly 20% support. Critics have condemned the engagement as a glaring conflict of interest, especially given his control over national media outlets. Online reactions have been sharply critical, with many calling the relationship inappropriate and emblematic of elite entitlement.

Menm si li toujou mari legalman avèk dezyèm fanm li, Veronica Lario, Berlusconi di Pascale te pòte l konfò anndan yon moman difisil. Koupl lan te wè yo frèkman ansanm nan Milan, alèn match AC Milan epi manje souyèn nan vil la. Pascale, ki te te konsèyè vil Nanp, sou pati Berlusconi, te toujou yon apwòvè vòkal, menm chante yon chansòn kampany ki gen lìn: 'Si ou tira sou lyèn ou, notifikasyon yo monte.' Anons sa a vini nan kontèks tribinal ki pwochenn an, oubyen li ta konvike pou aktivite seksèl alejè ak Karima El Mahroug, ki te 17 an, nan fèt 'bunga bunga' li. Berlusconi refise tout fòm de kòmpòtman kriminel, akize prokire yo dènye yon kampany politik pou detwi li. Li deklare tribinal sa a se yon outil de defamasyon ki vle fèmen kominikasyon li — yon projè ki, li di, esansiel pou evite gouvènman gwo gwo a retounen. article_content: When in Rome, it's tempting to try the city's world-famous gelato. But some British tourists were left with a nasty aftertaste — a £54 bill. After complaining about being charged £13.50 each for their takeaway cones, an Italian politician has called for a crackdown on such excessive pricing. Outraged holidaymakers Roger Bannister, 58, his brother Steven Bannister, 68, and their wives Wendy Bannister, 61, and Joyce Bannister, 69, all from Stourbridge in the West Midlands, received the startling bill on Sunday, the last day of their six-day trip. They stopped at the Antica Roma ice cream parlour near the famous Spanish Steps in central Rome. Though they requested three scoops each and avoided extra toppings to control costs, they were shocked by the total. Roger Bannister said, 'How can they charge £50 for four ice cream cones? The cones had three flavors and a few wafers, but if we wanted whipped cream, it was another €3 per person. We knew prices were high if you sat down, but we took our ice cream to go — how much would it have cost if we’d stayed?' He added, 'Up until then, we’d had a brilliant trip, but this left a bad taste in the mouth — quite literally. To be honest, the gelato wasn’t even that good. We’d had better ones earlier in the holiday. I felt ripped off, but what could I do?' Local councillor Matteo Costantini responded, 'They were justifiably outraged. This shouldn't be allowed. Such practices damage Rome’s reputation and deter visitors.' He personally offered to refund the money, but the family asked him to donate it to charity instead. The shop gave a cold response: a staff member, who declined to give her name, said, 'Prices are clearly displayed. They got exactly what they ordered — four gelatos.' She noted the most expensive cone is €25 (£21) and that each customer received approximately €16 worth — nearly a kilogram of gelato. 'We get this all the time,' she added. 'The prices are in black and white. If they don't like them, they can go elsewhere.' Carlo Rienzi, president of Italy’s Codacons consumer group, has formally requested an immediate investigation into what he called 'fraudulent pricing.' Have you been overcharged on holiday? Share your story at editorial@dailymailonline.co.uk. The shop is located near the Spanish Steps, one of Rome’s most popular tourist spots.

Roger Bannister, 58, frè li Steven Bannister, 68, ak fman yo Wendy ak Joyce Bannister, 61 ak 69, tou de sòti nan Stourbridge, Angleter, te resevwa yon faktyèl ki te fèt yo nan dimanch, dènye jou yo te nan Ròm. article_content: Cindy Ann Yuille, a 54-year-old hospice nurse and beloved member of her community, was killed Tuesday in a mass shooting at Clackamas Town Center Mall in Happy Valley, Oregon — a suburb of Portland. Known for her compassion and selflessness, she spent 16 years caring for patients and families through Kaiser Permanente’s hospice program. A native of California, Cindy enjoyed hiking and cross-country skiing, and is survived by her husband, Robert, her 23-year-old daughter, and her 13-year-old stepson. Friends noted she wasn’t typically a ‘mall person,’ but had gone out that evening for a simple errand. Steve M. Forsyth, 45, of West Linn, Oregon, was also fatally shot during the attack. A devoted father of two and passionate entrepreneur, Steve turned a family hobby into a thriving business producing custom wooden coasters and trivets. Described by loved ones as energetic, humorous, and deeply generous, he was known for uplifting others and putting their needs before his own. His business partner, Clayton Oswald, called his death incomprehensible, saying Steve was simply trying to make a living and share joy when he was taken. Fifteen-year-old Kristina Shevchenko, a passenger in a van near Macy’s, was critically wounded by gunfire. She suffered bullet fragments in her lung and liver and requires additional surgeries, but doctors remain optimistic about her full recovery. She was awake and speaking to her family as of Wednesday. Kristina’s family expressed gratitude to first responders and extended heartfelt condolences to the families of the other victims. They revealed she had previously survived a serious car crash in August — a reminder of her resilience. The suspect, identified by authorities as Jacob Tyler Roberts, opened fire without warning. The community, including Kaiser Permanente and local media, has rallied around the victims’ families, offering counseling, prayers, and public tributes. No motive has been publicly confirmed.

Yon fèm Californie, Cindy te renmen monte ak ski kros-koura, epi li te lave avèk mari li, Robert, fi li 23 an, ak fiyèt li 13 an. Manman yo te di li pa t yon moun ki te renmen ale nan magazin, men li te al mardi swen pou yon ti bagay. Steve M. Forsyth, 45 an, de West Linn, Oregòn, te vann tou pandan atak la. Pèp la, papa de de timoun, ak yon entreprenèr ki te entènse, Steve te fèt yon lozi fami nan yon biznis ki fè kòt, kòt, ak trivet enkri. Moun ki te konnen li te dekri li kòm enerjik, amiz, ak generòs. Men, medik la te espere li ka gueri totalman. Li te reve ak pale avèk fami li mardi. Famili Kristina te remerasye respondan d’emèjans ak te envite kondolans yo pou fami lòt vitim yo. Yo te anonse ke Kristina te sòti nan yon aksidan voitir moun an 8 aout — yon preuve rezilyans li. Sospè a, identifiye pa autorite yo kòm Jacob Tyler Roberts, te pèdi boul san avètisman. Kominote a, ki gen Kaiser Permanente ak medya lokal, te ralanti pou fami vitim yo, avèk konsèy, pèyè, ak tribit. Paske pa gen mòtif ki te confirmè.

article_content: Netflix just announced a surge of nearly 9 million new subscribers this quarter, pushing its global total to 247.2 million as of September 30. But not everyone is celebrating—some existing customers will see their monthly bills rise starting this Wednesday. In the U.S., the no-ads basic plan (no longer available to new subscribers) is jumping from $9.99 to $11.99, and the premium tier, which allows downloads on six devices and Ultra HD streaming, is now $22.99. Meanwhile, the popular ad-supported plan stays firmly at $6.99, as does the standard plan at $15.49. Similar adjustments are rolling out in the UK and France. Netflix pointed to its hit shows—like 'One Piece,' 'The Witcher,' 'Love at First Sight,' and 'Suits'—as key drivers of engagement. The company also highlighted how its $6.99 ad plan has become a major growth engine, noting it costs less than a typical movie ticket. In its shareholder letter, Netflix acknowledged the recent resolution of the WGA strike but confirmed talks with SAG-AFTRA are still underway, expressing hope for a swift settlement so production can resume. Interestingly, this price hike comes despite earlier rumors suggesting Netflix would delay increases until after the SAG strike ended.

Men pa tout moun ki fèt kontan—kèk abone ki deja gen aktyèlman yo pral wè pib li yo monte a parti a merkredi sa. Etazini, plan baz san advètisman (pa plis availab pou nouvo abone) monte de $9.99 pou $11.99, ak plan premium ki pèmèt telechajman sou sis aparèy ak stream Ultra HD, li toujou $22.99. Menm tan sa a, plan avèk advètisman ki popilè a pa chanje, li toujou $6.99, menm jan avèk plan stanndard a ki nan $15.49. Mem kòmansman an ap pase an Angleter ak Frans. Netflix te mete an avant ses seri ki fèt byen—tankou 'One Piece,' 'The Witcher,' 'Love at First Sight,' ak 'Suits'—komme faktè pwomòtèn konpòtman. Kompagni a tou mete an avant fakta ke plan advètisman $6.99 li te vin yon mwayen pwomòtèn moun anpil, epi li di li pi piti pase pri yon tikè sinema. An leta li a pou aktyè, Netflix te rekonèt rezolysyon strik WGA menm tan li konfime ke négosyasyon avèk SAG-AFTRA toujou enkò, epi li espere yon rezolysyon vèlòs pou tout moun ka retounen travay fè fim ak televizyon yo k ap plèz. Intéresanman, monte pri sa a vini malgre ròm ki te di ke Netflix ta dwe retard monte pri a tan ke strik SAG ta fini.

article_content: Forget the days of lumpy mashed potatoes, grey mince, and mushy carrots. At Loreto High School, lunchtime has been completely reinvented. Thanks to two award-winning chefs — Adam Leavy, a MasterChef UK semi-finalist, and Sukhdev Singh, formerly of the acclaimed Manchester restaurant Abode — students now enjoy fresh, flavorful meals like smoked mackerel with beetroot and kale salad, Thai-style fishcakes with pak choi, and even lemon and rosemary chocolate truffles for dessert. All for just £2.35 a day — including pudding. The chefs were hired after students voiced their dissatisfaction with the old menu. They competed in a rigorous audition, preparing two-course meals under pressure — much like on MasterChef — and impressed Headmaster Peter Tite so much that he hired them on the spot. Initially, many students were hesitant. 'They don’t always trust what’s on the plate,' says Leavy, who now prepares up to 500 meals daily. 'But most of the time, they end up loving it.' Taster sessions are held weekly to introduce new dishes — last week’s kale trial became an instant hit. Today, kale chips and ciabatta are student favorites. The impact extends beyond the school gates. Parents report their children now refuse ordinary meals at home — insisting on extra virgin olive oil on salads or turning up their noses at beans on toast. Canteen revenue has risen by 21%, and lunch participation has jumped from 60% to 72%. Staff now line up to eat alongside students. Looking ahead, the school plans to replace plastic trays and chairs with table settings and install ‘special of the day’ signs at the entrance — transforming the cafeteria into a true dining experience. For Leavy, this role also offers personal fulfillment: with his first child due in November, he’s found a better work-life balance than he ever had in fine dining.

article_content: On November 15, 2012, Army Sergeant Joshua Michael, 34, lost his life saving his wife, Daylyn, during a tragic accident in Midland, Texas. A Union Pacific freight train struck the Veterans Day parade float he was riding on, killing Michael and three others. In the final moments before impact, Michael pushed Daylyn off the flatbed truck, ensuring her survival at the cost of his own life. A decorated veteran and Purple Heart recipient, Michael served two deployments to Iraq with the 101st Airborne Division. He was medically retired after suffering multiple traumatic brain injuries from an IED explosion. Despite his injuries, he remained proud of his service, once writing, 'I wouldn't change anything that happened. I am a better man, husband, and father because of my service.' His funeral on November 24, 2012, in Amarillo, Texas, drew hundreds of mourners. American flags lined the streets outside the chapel and cemetery, and a formal military salute honored his sacrifice. Born and raised in Hereford, Texas, Michael graduated from Hereford High School in 1996 and married Daylyn in 1997 after meeting at Amarillo College. The nonprofit America Supports You Texas is holding a prayer vigil on Sunday at the Texas Panhandle War Memorial in Amarillo, where Mayor Paul Harpole will speak. 'It’s important to honor Sgt. Michael and his family here in Amarillo because Hereford is part of our local family,' said Larry Lewis, acting president of the organization. 'Whenever we lose a service member, we feel a need to honor that family and reach out and support them.' Michael is survived by his wife Daylyn, daughter Maci, and son Ryan.

article_content: Red Bull team principal Christian Horner credits former driver Sebastian Vettel for inspiring the team’s camouflage car livery during testing this week. The black-and-white design is visually disruptive, making it difficult for rivals to analyze the car’s aerodynamics. Horner revealed the concept originated from Vettel’s helmet design during the 2014 Italian Grand Prix weekend. Although Vettel has since moved to Ferrari, Horner said, 'Seb’s helmet was quite fun, so we thought it would be interesting to extend that concept to the whole car.' 'Dietrich Mateschitz loved it when he saw it,' Horner added. 'It epitomizes Red Bull—we like to do things a bit differently.' The unusual livery has drawn strong reactions, with many fans hoping it will be used throughout the season. Horner confirmed it won’t appear in the opening race but teased, 'The fans won’t be disappointed—the livery will be even stronger.' During testing at the Circuito de Jerez in Spain, new Red Bull driver Daniil Kvyat damaged the team’s sole front wing during an early installation lap. The 20-year-old Russian, promoted from Toro Rosso to replace Vettel, drove several laps without a front wing before pitting for repairs. Horner explained: 'Unfortunately, Daniil very lightly touched the tyre wall with the front wing, causing damage. It’s the only front-wing assembly we have in Jerez right now—which is fairly typical at this stage of the year when spare parts are limited.' 'More components are arriving later today, this evening, and over the next two days. We’ll definitely have a new front wing by tomorrow morning.'

Menm si Vettel te ale Ferrari, Horner te di, 'Kasa Seb te plis amizan, nou te pence ke se enteresan pou etend konsept sa a sou tout machin an.' 'Dietrich Mateschitz te aime l lè li te wè l,' Horner te ajoute. 'Sa montre Red Bull—nou aime fè bagay yo yon ti jan diferan.' Koulè an eksepisyèl la te gen reaksyon fò, anpil fan yo espere li ta pral itilize tout sezon an. Horner te konfime li pa pral itilize pou kou premye a, men li te pèmèt, 'Fan yo pa pral despoti—koulè a pral pi fò ankò.' Nou pral gen yon nouvo aile avan demen maten an.'

article_content: In Alaska, where seaplanes are a routine mode of transport, it pays to look before you land — not just before you leap. Last week in the remote village of Angoon, resident Thomas Hamm captured a startling moment on video: a seaplane nearly colliding with a humpback whale during landing. The footage, which began as an ordinary scene in a community accessible only by boat or air, took an unexpected turn. As the plane descended, Hamm noticed the pilot suddenly increase throttle. 'I didn’t know why,' he told CNN. 'I thought, something must be wrong.' What he didn’t see was the whale swimming just beneath the surface. Moments before impact, the pilot pulled up sharply, clearing the mammal by mere feet. Seconds later, the plane landed safely. When Hamm showed the pilot the video, the pilot admitted he hadn’t seen the whale. Instead, he reacted to people on the shore waving and shouting. Just as the plane ascended, the whale breached — its blowhole erupting directly over the cockpit, drenching the windshield in seawater. A truly unforgettable landing.

Videyo a, ki te kòm yon sitiyasyon lènman nan yon kominote ki se yon sèlman accesib avèk bato oswa avyon, te pran yon tounen net. Pandan avyon an te desann, Hamm te remare pilòt la te pouse akseleratè a. 'M pa konnen pouki,' li te di CNN. 'M te pense, gen kèk bagay ki fèt.' Moun sa a pa te wè balèn lan ki swim tou pre sifas la. Moman avan kolizyon an, pilòt la te leve avyon an vreman, ki te fè li woule balèn lan ak yon ti distans. De sekond aprè, avyon an te atè sans pwoblèm. Lè Hamm te montre videyo a pilòt la, pilòt la te avou li pa te wè balèn lan. Li reyaji sou tout moun ki te montre ak kriye sou rivyè a. Lè avyon an te monte, balèn lan te fè yon brech — bouche a te koule direkman sou kabin lan, koupe tout vitri a ak sel dlo. Yon atè ki pa ka oublie.

article_content: A tip led to the Wednesday arrest in Louisiana of Michael Francis Mara, 52, a suspected serial bank robber nicknamed the 'Granddad Bandit,' federal authorities said. Mara was taken into custody at his home in Baton Rouge, according to FBI Special Agent Sheila Thorne. When agents arrived to execute an arrest warrant, Mara initially retreated inside the residence. After six hours, he emerged and was peacefully arrested. The FBI says Mara is linked to at least 25 bank robberies across 13 states — from Virginia to Texas to Kansas — since 2008. He earned the nickname 'Granddad Bandit' because he appeared elderly and non-threatening, often balding, overweight, and wearing glasses. Despite his mild demeanor, authorities stress he is dangerous: he frequently pointed to his waistband, suggesting he was armed, though it remains unclear whether he carried a firearm. Earlier this month, the FBI’s field office in Norfolk, Virginia, received a tip that included photographs of Mara. These were matched against surveillance images from multiple robberies. U.S. Attorney’s Office officials confirmed investigators found consistent identifiers — including a distinctive hat, eyeglasses, and wristwatch — linking Mara to the crimes. Mara has been charged with one count of bank robbery and is currently in custody. If convicted, he could face up to 20 years in prison. According to the FBI, Mara worked for a vehicle transportation company and traveled frequently between states for work. In recent weeks, the FBI launched a nationwide billboard campaign featuring surveillance photos of the robber in hopes of public identification. Authorities credit this effort, along with widespread media coverage, as instrumental in his capture. An FBI affidavit released Wednesday detailed Mara’s modus operandi: he calmly enters banks, often waiting patiently in line before approaching a teller with a handwritten demand note specifying the amount of money desired. He wears no disguise, makes no threats beyond gesturing toward his waist, and leaves quietly after receiving cash — rarely drawing attention to the crime.

Mara te arête nan kay li nan Baton Rouge, selon Agent Spesyal FBI Sheila Thorne. Kounye a agent yo te rive pou ekzekite yon mandat d'arête, Mara te rete nan kay la. Apre sis ôre, li te sòti epi te arête. FBI di ke Mara se entènse a lèdmanm 25 vòl de banik nan 13 etat — depi Virjini a Teksas ak Kansas — depi 2008. Li te jwenn non 'Granddad Bandit' paske li te genyen yon aspè vye ak pa menasè, souvan kalv, obèz, ak wèyè. article_content: The emotional weight in Andy Murray’s voice and the sorrow in his eyes reveal just how deeply he feels about the end of his coaching partnership with Ivan Lendl. The Wimbledon champion described himself as 'gutted' after deciding to part ways, fearing their collaboration had become 'half-baked'. In his first public statement on the split, Murray recounted how a planned dinner on Saturday to discuss their future instead became their final meeting. 'That night was tough,' he said. 'He was a big part of my life. We talked for an hour about everything else — then we talked about moving forward.' The 26-year-old British No. 1 likened beginning a player-coach relationship to starting a new romance: intense effort at first, followed by complacency as familiarity grows. Now, he says, ending it has been equally painful. Under Lendl’s guidance since December 31, 2011, Murray achieved historic milestones: Olympic gold in London 2012 and his first Grand Slam title at the 2012 US Open. Murray credits Lendl with helping him 'get over the line' — a transformation he calls undeniable. Originally, Lendl agreed to work 25 weeks per year in Year 1, reducing to 20 in Year 2. Murray felt this reduced commitment in 2014 would compromise his progress. 'It wasn’t going to be of benefit to anyone doing the job half-baked,' Murray explained. 'That’s Ivan’s nature — he does things properly.' Despite the split, Lendl will still be in Murray’s player box during his match against Australia’s Matthew Ebden at the Sony Open — his first tournament since their farewell dinner. Murray admitted his recent form has been inconsistent, partly due to lingering effects of his September 2013 back surgery and a difficult week at Indian Wells. Yet he remains hopeful: 'I’ve been in worse situations before. I know I’ll turn this around.' Looking ahead, Murray aims to hire a new coach before the French Open in late May. He seeks someone with Grand Slam experience who’s willing to commit long-term — though he acknowledges such candidates are rare. 'I don’t want to rush it. This has to be for the medium to long term.' Meanwhile, Novak Djokovic faces similar challenges, as Boris Becker undergoes further hip surgery and remains absent from his team.

An premye enfòmasyon li te bay sou separe a, Murray te rekonte kòm yon dinè planné samedi pou diskute avenir yo te vin dènye dinè yo te fè. 'Sa a so a te difisil,' li te di. 'Li te yon pati enpotan nan mwen. Nou te pale pou yon èt nan tout bagay lòt, pita nou te pale sou avni a.' Britanik #1 ki gen 26 an, te konpare kòmansman relasyon jwèt-kouche a ak kòmansman yon relasyon amoure: ou fè tout pou imprese poulè a nan premye mwa yo, men ou tènman yon ti jan nan tan ki pase. Pendant, Novak Djokovic gen menm pwoblèm yo, paske Boris Becker fè yon operasyon laviyè a epi pa genyen kouche a.

article_content: Drag racer Christine Steffens is lucky to be alive after her car erupted in flames during a high-speed run at the Perth Motorplex on Saturday night. Despite the catastrophic explosion—which occurred at nearly 400 kilometers per hour—she still won the race series. Steffens, an accountant from Gatton in southeast Queensland, was competing against Mark Sheehan in the three-race Nitro Thunder match race series. She led early in her green 'Croc' Nitro funny car, but soon encountered trouble. The vehicle burst into flames mid-track, reportedly due to a supercharger backfire at full throttle. According to ABC News, this triggered a fireball that sent shrapnel into a front tire, causing the car to veer into the safety barrier. Steffens escaped unharmed through the car’s roof hatch before the vehicle came to rest. Fire and rescue crews quickly arrived to extinguish the flames. Remarkably, her car still recorded an impressive 5.42-second elapsed time over the quarter-mile, securing her a 2–1 series victory over Sheehan. Steffens is the only woman in Australia to compete in a nitro funny car—a vehicle capable of reaching speeds up to 500 km/h. With 18 years of experience in drag racing, she drives the iconic green 'Croc' car alongside her husband, Ricky.

article_content: Chris Jordan delivered a match-winning performance on Wednesday, helping England recover from their humiliating defeat on Sunday with a commanding victory over Sri Lanka at Old Trafford. The 24-year-old pace bowler took five wickets for just 29 runs, bowling Sri Lanka out for a mere 67 runs. Alastair Cook and Ian Bell then chased down the target in only 73 balls, sealing the win with ease. This emphatic reply came just three days after England were dismissed for 99 in Durham — their worst-ever home one-day international loss. Jordan admitted the team was deeply affected: 'It wasn’t just that we were beaten, but the way we lost. Those days can happen during a transition phase, but we were determined to put things right — and I’m glad we did.' Jordan’s spell included the crucial wickets of Kumar Sangakkara and Lasith Malinga, sparking Sri Lanka’s collapse. His raw emotion on each dismissal reflected how much the victory meant to him. Alastair Cook, who led England to their 33rd ODI win as captain, surpassed Michael Vaughan to become England’s most successful 50-over skipper. 'The lads came out firing today,' Cook said. 'They were desperate to prove a point — and we did. Sunday was strange, but we kept our nerve and hit back.' He added high praise for Jordan: 'Every time he takes a wicket, you can see how much it means to him.'

article_content: In November 2013, the UK government quietly shelved a controversial plan to require certain foreign visitors to pay a £3,000 deposit before entering the country—a move meant to discourage visa overstays. The idea, initially floated by the Conservative Party as part of its election platform, was later claimed by Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg as his own during a March speech. But when the Home Office prepared to test the policy, Clegg and his Liberal Democrat colleagues blocked it, arguing the version on the table was too broad and unfairly targeted people from specific nations like Nigeria, Ghana, India, and Sri Lanka. Prime Minister David Cameron publicly criticized Clegg for what he called a reversal, telling an audience at the CBI conference: 'This was your idea—but we’re not doing it anymore.' His comment drew laughter, underscoring the growing rift within the coalition. Meanwhile, Home Secretary Theresa May dismissed Liberal Democrat objections as hypocritical, pointing out that the party had previously praised the government’s success in lowering migration numbers. Business Secretary Vince Cable had offered a different interpretation: that the bond could serve as a tool to grant visas to applicants previously denied entry, turning financial risk into opportunity. But May mocked the notion, saying it essentially meant 'paying for more immigrants.' Labour’s Keith Vaz condemned the entire concept as racially biased and unjust, noting that it punished lawful travelers seeking work or study, not those exploiting the system. Liberal Democrat insiders insisted the policy as drafted was never acceptable to them, nor supported by other government departments. They emphasized they had raised concerns from the beginning. A Home Office spokesperson confirmed the decision to abandon the pilot, citing lack of consensus. With the Conservatives aiming to reduce net migration below 100,000 before the next election, the bond’s collapse left behind a trail of political finger-pointing—each side blaming the other for the confusion.

article_content: New York (CNN) — Nick Brooks, the 24-year-old son of Oscar-winning composer Joseph Brooks, was indicted Thursday in connection with the strangulation death of his girlfriend, Sylvie Cachay, 33. Her body was discovered last week in a bathtub at the exclusive Soho House hotel in Manhattan. Details of the indictment remain sealed until Brooks’ next court appearance on January 4, according to Manhattan District Attorney spokeswoman Joan Vollero. Police report that Cachay’s body showed signs of severe trauma: bruising on the neck, bite marks, internal hemorrhaging, scalp injuries, and cuts to her lips and mouth. She was found fully clothed. Brooks, who was arraigned on charges of attempted murder and strangulation, pleaded not guilty. His attorney, Jeffrey C. Hoffman, stated that Brooks believes someone else may have been present in the room at the time of the incident. According to authorities, the only other person confirmed in the room was a hotel employee who delivered ice and stayed for approximately one minute. Brooks escorted the employee in and remained alone afterward. Investigators based their case on interviews with staff and surveillance footage from the hotel. In a statement released through Cachay’s publicist, her brother, Patrick Orlando-Cachay, said their parents are ‘devastated’ and unable to speak coherently amid their grief. ‘Nobody should have to make arrangements to bury a child,’ he said. The medical examiner’s office confirmed the cause of death aligns with neck compression but awaits final results from toxicology and tissue tests, expected in several weeks. Publicist Kate Godici remembered Cachay as ‘one of those rare individuals who truly sparkled when she spoke.’ ‘She will be deeply and painfully missed, yet celebrated, honored, and never forgotten.’

Brooks, ki te amen anvan jij la pou akizasyon de mòt la ak atèm de mòt la, te deklare pa koupable. Avoka li, Jeffrey C. Hoffman, te di ke Brooks kroie ke yon lòt moun ka te la nan piyèt la pandan evenman an. Konsèn nan autorite yo, se yon sèl lòt moun ki konfime te nan piyèt la: yon emplwaye hotel ki te amene glas la epi te rete yon minit envi. Nan yon déklarasyon ki te piblie atravè piblisiste Sylvie Cachay, frè li, Patrick Orlando-Cachay, te di ke peyè yo ‘sont devasté’ epi pa kapab pale klè akòz deuil yo. ‘Pa gen moun ki dwe fè preperatif pou enterèn yon timoun,’ li te di. article_content: What is the essence of Native American identity? Photographer Matika Wilbur set out to answer this question by traveling more than 60,000 miles across the United States to photograph members of every federally recognized Indigenous tribe. Using Kickstarter to fund her journey, she lived simply — often sleeping on floors — to capture authentic moments in everyday life. The result is Project 562, a powerful collection of portraits and personal stories from 161 distinct Indigenous nations. Wilbur, a graduate of the Rocky Mountain School of Photography and a member of the Tulalip and Swinomish tribes, aimed not to portray Indigenous people as relics of the past, but as vibrant, contemporary communities thriving in the 21st century. Her subjects include Sky and Talon Duncan, world-champion hoop dancers from the Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation; Chief Bill James of the Lummi Nation; Stephen Yellowtail, an industrial engineering student from the Crow Nation; and many others — health professionals, farmers, lawyers, activists, and elders preserving sacred sites. Wilbur intentionally highlights strength, dignity, and continuity. 'I seek the positivity of Indian country,' she says. 'We have heroes — they’re walking among us.' These include fishers navigating sacred waters, attorneys defending tribal sovereignty, and grandparents protecting ancestral lands. One striking image shows an Indigenous woman standing before a field of wind turbines — a symbol of modern energy intersecting with traditional land stewardship. Another captures a Pechanga cultural leader beside a 2,000-year-old oak tree, reflecting deep historical roots amid current struggles over water rights and violence against Native women. Unlike Edward S. Curtis’s early 1900s project, which framed Native Americans as a 'dying race,' Wilbur’s work celebrates survival, adaptation, and renewal. Her mission: to shift public perception, combat racism, and inspire awareness of Indigenous cultures. Project 562 has exceeded expectations: it raised three times its original Kickstarter goal and earned a publishing deal with the University of Washington Press. Wilbur plans to continue documenting tribes for another two years, believing that 'the level of success... has been a direct result of people’s commitment to change the way the world sees Native America.'
translated_content: Ki se esans identite Ameriken Natif? Fotografer Matika Wilbur te chache reponn kesyon sa a enèt travèse Etazini pou fotografe moun ki ap viv nan tout tribi endijenn rekonèt. Li te itilize Kickstarter pou finanse voyaj li, epi li te viv senp — souvan dòmi sou sol la — pou kapte moman otentik nan jounen a. Rezilta a se Projè 562, yon koleksyon pwofond de portret ak istwa pèsonèl nan 161 nasyon endijenn distenk. Wilbur, yon diplômé ekòl fotografi Rocky Mountain ak moun tribi Tulalip ak Swinomish, te vle pa prezante moun endijenn tankou relik pati, men tankou kominote kontanporeyèn vivan ki ap tiri nan 21yèm syèk la. Sousjèt li yo gen Sky ak Talon Duncan, danse ak boul klas mondial yo nan tribi Mandan, Hidatsa, ak Arikara; Chef Bill James nan tribi Lummi; Stephen Yellowtail, yon etidyan jeniery indistriyèl nan tribi Crow; epi anpil lòt — profesyonèl santè, peyizan, avoka, aktivis, ak granpè a ki proteje sit santi. Wilbur te vle mete an evidans fòs, dignite, ak kontinite. 'Mwen chache pozitivite de peyi Indyen,' li di. 'Nou gen héro — yo a kouran anndan nou.' Sa yo gen pèchè ki navige ansanm ak lòt ak lòt ak dlo santi, avoka ki defenn sovènete tribi, ak granpè ki proteje teren ansestrèl. Yon imaj frappan montre yon fman endijenn ki debòte devan yon chenn turbine vèn — yon simbol enerji kontanporeyèn ki entèsekte avèk tradisyon konprann teren. Yon lòt imaj montre yon lider kiltirel Pechanga ki genyen yon chèn chenn 2000 ane, reflete radyal historik yo nan konfli aktèl sou dwèt dlo ak violans kont moun endijenn. Kontrè ak projè Edward S. Curtis nan 1900, ki te prezante Ameriken Natif tankou yon 'ras ennem,' travay Wilbur a fè yon kantik pou rezistans, adaptasyon, ak renouvelman. Misyon li: chanje pepsyon publik, konbat rasisme, ak inspiré konprann kilti endijenn. Projè 562 te depase espwer yo: li te ramase twa fwa plis lajan ke li te vle, epi li te resevwa yon kontrat edisyon avèk Pres Universite Washington. Wilbur ta vle kontinye dokumente tribi pou de lèn anplis, kroie ke 'nivo siksè a... se rezilta direk de kominman moun yo pou chanje mannyè moun monde a wè Ameriken Natif.'

article_content: Finale Emilia, Italy (CNN) — Thousands of survivors huddled in tents or in their cars under rainy skies early Monday, following a weekend earthquake that killed seven people across northern Italy. Aftershocks rattled the country’s industrial heartland throughout Sunday evening after the magnitude-6.0 quake struck around 4 a.m. (10 p.m. Saturday ET). Franco Gabrielli, head of Italy’s Civil Protection Department, said 11,000 people had been displaced, with the government providing shelter for 3,000 in tents or hotels. In Finale Emilia, about 35 km (21 miles) north of Bologna, 75 people were sleeping in their cars in a public park. One of them, Filomenna Gatti, planned to squeeze into a Fiat Punto with her husband and three children under six. 'I close my eyes and I see stones falling and I feel the ground shaking—even when it’s still,' Gatti said as she walked her dog. 'I don’t want to be in any building.' Italian Prime Minister Mario Monti announced Sunday he would leave the NATO summit in Chicago early, vowing, 'All that is necessary will be done as soon as possible' to aid survivors. The quake was centered about 4 kilometers (2.4 miles) outside Camposanto, northwest of Bologna, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. In addition to the seven fatalities, 50 people were injured, Gabrielli said. The affected region is part of Italy’s industrial heartland. Two victims died when a ceramics factory collapsed in Sant’Agostino di Ferrara, roughly 30 km from the epicenter, said civil protection spokesperson Elisabetta Maffani. Workers continued digging through rubble in Sant’Agostino, hoping to find survivors. A magnitude-4.8 aftershock brought down part of the town’s city hall Sunday evening, while the church bell also collapsed. 'We have just lost our history. Four generations of my family lived here—and now it’s gone,' said 72-year-old Luciano Frendo, walking through Finale Emilia. 'Our history has collapsed.' The civil protection agency anticipates more injury reports as rescuers reach remote mountain villages. Heavy rain, expected to continue into Tuesday, has hampered rescue operations and aerial searches. Other deaths included one person killed when a work shed collapsed in nearby Ponte Rodoni di Bondeno; a woman in Bologna died of a heart attack during evacuation; a Moroccan national perished when his factory collapsed; and a sixth victim was found under rubble in Sant’Agostino, Maffani said. The body of a seventh victim was recovered from beneath a collapsed house, according to Alessio Bellodi of the Bologna civil protection unit. The same region was hit by a 5.3-magnitude quake in January. In 2009, a 6.3-magnitude earthquake near L’Aquila—over 400 km to the south—killed more than 300 people and caused massive destruction. CNN’s Joseph Netto and journalist Livia Borghese contributed to this report.

Aftershocks te fèt tout swa dimanch answit aprè terèmòt magnitid 6.0 ki te frap peyis la a 4 a.m. (10 p.m. samedi ET). Franco Gabrielli, dirijan Départman Sivil Proteksyon Italiyen, te di 11,000 moun te deplase, ak gouvènman an ki te mete 3,000 nan tanp oswa hotel. Nan Finale Emilia, ki se envi 35 km (21 mily) nòd Bologna, 75 moun te kouche nan machin yo nan yon parèk publik. Yon nan yo, Filomenna Gatti, te vle mete tout timoun yo ki gen moine siks ans, ak mari li, nan yon Fiat Punto. 'M ap fèmen peyèt mwen e m wè pye ki chache tonbe e m ressenti teren ki vire—meme lè li pa fèt,' Gatti te di lè l te marche chyen li. 'M pa vle rete nan yon bati.' Premye Minis Italiyen Mario Monti te anonsé dimanch li ta retounen nan sommet NATO nan Chicago, ak yon jènman: 'Tout sa ki nesesè a pral fèt anvan posib.' Zòn ki te frapé se yon zòn endistriyèl Italiyen. De moun te mouri lè yon fabrik sèramik te tombe nan Sant’Agostino di Ferrara, envi 30 km nan nòwèst èpisyent, Elisabetta Maffani, espesyalis proteksyon sivil te di. Travayè yo te kontinye vire nan detwit pou yo chache sòti viv nan Sant’Agostino. Yon aftershock magnitid 4.8 te fèt tombe yon paryèl nan mairie a dimanch answit, menm klochèt egliz lan te tombe. 'Nou pèdi tout istwa nou. Fèm katri jenerasyon mwen te rete la—epi l’ap moun toujou.' Luciano Frendo, 72 an, te di lè l te marche nan Finale Emilia. 'Istwa nou te tombe.' Départman proteksyon sivil an antand ke pi fòm rapòt blesir yo pral vin lè secouris yo rive nan vila mòn yo. Plui lour te antand pou kontinye jiska mardi, epi li te obstrwe operasyon sekouzi ak rechèch aeryèn. Autre mouri yo: yon moun ki te mouri lè yon kabann travay te tombe nan Ponte Rodoni di Bondeno; yon fanm ki te mouri nan Bologna nan yon atak kè pandan evakuasyon; yon nasyonal Marokèn ki te mouri lè fabrik li te tombe; ak yon sisyèm viktim ki te jwenn nan detwit nan Sant’Agostino, Maffani te di. Kò yon sètyèm viktim te jwenn sou yon kay ki te tombe, selon Alessio Bellodi nan unité proteksyon sivil Bologna. Menm zòn sa te frapé pa yon terèmòt magnitid 5.3 nan janvye. An 2009, yon terèmòt magnitid 6.3 nan L’Aquila, envi 400 km sou, te tue plis pase 300 moun epi te kreye domaj masif.

article_content: Among countless images of Princess Diana, one stands out—not for its glamour, but for its quiet heartbreak. In the photo, she sits alone at the edge of a diving board on Mohamed al-Fayed’s private yacht, wearing a simple turquoise swimsuit, surrounded only by open sea. Taken by a paparazzo just days before her tragic death, the image feels hauntingly prophetic, captured during a time when the press was relentless after photos of her with Dodi Fayed surfaced. Though she was constantly in the public eye, this moment reveals a woman profoundly alone. Over the years, this single frame has echoed through culture: from the 2013 film starring Naomi Watts, to Off-White’s 2018 runway collection, and now, in SZA’s album artwork for SOS. The singer admitted she was drawn to the photo because it perfectly captured the feeling of being utterly isolated—even in a crowd. Even Netflix’s The Crown paid tribute, recreating the scene with Elizabeth Debicki, her posture echoing Diana’s protective hunch, her back turned, her solitude unmistakable. While other photos show Diana’s discomfort in royal settings—like her stiff engagement portrait or her solitary trip to the Taj Mahal—this diving board image lingers because it doesn’t need words. It says everything: a woman who gave so much to the world, yet never found peace within it.

Nan foto sa a, li sèt nan kòt yon plongeòr sou yon bato pèsonèl Mohamed al-Fayed, ak yon ti bainman tirkiz, tout entoure pa dlo ouvri. Prensipalman pran pa yon paparazi, kèk jou avan mòt travajik li, foto sa a gen yon chans fè l konsidere yon presag. Même si li te toujou nan vye publik, moman sa a revele yon fman ki te fèl anndan. Anpil tan, foto sa a te reyeni nan kilti: nan fim 2013 ki te jwe pa Naomi Watts, nan koleksyon Off-White 2018, epi anpil tan an, nan kover albom SZA pou SOS. Chanse a te di li te atrè pa foto sa a paske li kapab ekspriye yon senstyon d'izolman total—menm nan yon foule. Menm Netflix The Crown te fè yon omaj, rekre yo avèk Elizabeth Debicki, posti li reflete posti Diana, dos li tounen, solitid li evidan. Menm si anpil foto lòt montre konfòm nan lavi rwayal li—tankou foto fiançay li fèk oswa visit li sèl nan Taj Mahal—foto plongeòr sa a rete paske li pa bezwen mo. Li di tout bagay: yon fman ki te donne anpil pou mond lan, men ki pa janm travèse pa pa l.

article_content: Police are investigating claims that the late actor Leonard Rossiter was present during alleged sexual assaults on the set of the 1968 BBC drama, 'The Year of the Sex Olympics'. Officers from Operation Yewtree — the unit established following the Jimmy Savile revelations — are examining allegations that Rossiter and other BBC staff committed abuses during filming at the London Television Centre. Rossiter, best known for roles in 'Rising Damp' and 'The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin', died in 1984. A 66-year-old former extra, who was 18 at the time of filming, says he was assaulted twice by multiple men, with Rossiter watching and appearing to enjoy the ordeal. He described the set as a 'cesspit of depravity'. The man also reported witnessing a female colleague in distress after her own alleged assault, saying she cried out, 'It’s like a f***ing orgy in there — I didn’t come here to get f***ed.' Both victims reportedly reported the incidents to senior BBC staff, but were warned: 'If you pursue this, you will never work for the BBC again.' Filming was halted early that day due to the woman’s emotional state. The drama, which satirized a future ruled by reality television and pornography, was controversial upon broadcast — but claims of on-set abuse only emerged decades later. The Metropolitan Police declined to provide updates on the investigation, and the BBC stated: 'Any allegations of criminality are a matter for the police, and the BBC is not able to comment.'

article_content: Britain’s nuclear power stations may be vulnerable to drone-based attacks, according to warnings from a London-based nuclear expert. John Large, who investigated a series of unauthorized drone flights over more than a dozen nuclear sites in France, says the risks are equally serious across the Channel. The UK operates 16 nuclear reactors, which supply 18% of the nation’s electricity — yet current security measures, he argues, are ill-equipped to counter emerging threats like drones equipped with explosives or surveillance gear. Large presented his findings to the French parliament, warning that existing nuclear plants would likely fail under simulated drone sabotage scenarios — potentially leading to a major radioactive release. His assessment has been reviewed by UK officials and shared with the Office for Nuclear Regulation (ONR), though the government has not requested a full copy of his report. Large urges authorities to reconsider this stance. In France, at least 15 unauthorized drone overflights have been recorded since October, peaking with five incidents on a single day. Three individuals were briefly detained near the Belleville-sur-Loire reactor after flying remote-controlled devices within 200 meters of the facility, but were later released when it was determined they were hobbyists mistaken about restricted zones. While EDF, France’s state-owned utility, insists that plant operations were unaffected, concerns persist. French law strictly forbids drone use near nuclear sites, military installations, and airports — yet enforcement remains inconsistent. Meanwhile, in the UK, recreational drone ownership is booming. Around 2,000 units are sold monthly, with some costing as little as £35. Electronics retailer Maplin reports drones as one of its top-selling items this holiday season. These devices, often equipped with cameras, are increasingly used for commercial purposes — but also pose risks to aviation safety. Recent near-misses have raised alarms: a drone nearly collided with a passenger jet at Heathrow, another flew within 80 feet of a plane approaching Southend Airport, and crew members at Gatwick reported seeing unidentified aerial objects. In April, a drone operator was fined over £4,000 after crashing his device in a restricted zone near a BAE Systems shipyard building nuclear submarines. The British Airline Pilots Association (Balpa) is calling for urgent reforms, demanding that drones be subject to the same safety standards as manned aircraft — including mandatory pilot training and geofencing technology. Intelligence experts warn that unregulated drone use could become a major threat by 2035. Although Greenpeace has previously staged protests at French nuclear sites to highlight security weaknesses, it denies any link to the recent drone incidents. The Fukushima disaster in 2011 prompted France to upgrade nuclear defenses, but drone threats represent a new, rapidly evolving challenge that regulators have yet to fully address.

John Large, ki te envestige yon seri vwayaj droyon anlè plis pase douz stasyon nuclear an Frans, di ke menm riske yo gen pou fèt sou lòt bò Channel. Angleterre gen 16 reaktè nuclear ki pwodui 18% elektirite nasyonal yo — men moun yo pa prete pou kontròl menas ki vin ak droyon ki kapab karayi eksplozif oswa aparèy espionaj. Large te prezante rezilta li a devan parlamàn Frans, avèk avertisman ke stasyon nuclear yo kapab pa reyisi nan skenar yo simile ak atèk droyon — ki kapab kondui a yon lâchman radioaktiv moun. Analiz li a te revize pa ofisyèl britanik ak transmis a Office for Nuclear Regulation (ONR), men gouvènman an pa demann yon kopi komplè rapò a. Large reqi pou yo reyenvesti pozisyon yo. Twa moun te arete pito stasyon Belleville-sur-Loire aprè yo te flite aparèy kontwòl distant anlè 200 mèt nan site a, men yo te libere aprè li te revele ke yo te afisyonèn avyon model ki te fèt yon erè. Menm si EDF, entèpri elektrik etatèl Frans, di ke operasyon yo pa te afekte, inquietid yo kontinye. Lo Frans defini anndan yon zòn interdi pou droyon nan site nuclear, baz militè, ak aeroport — men aplikasyon lo a pa toujou efikas. An Angleterre, vandaj droyon rekreatif yo monte rapidman. Environ 2000 aparèy yo vann chak mwa, ak kèk sa yo ki koûte sèlman 35£. Retèl elektronik Maplin di ke droyon yo se yon nan pi bòn vandaj yo pandan sezon endirik la. Aparèy sa yo, ki gen kamera souvan, yo devenen depi de rezim komèsyal — men yo toujou gen menas pou sekirite aviasyon. Avril lan, yon moun ki te flite yon aparèy kontwòl distant te kondamne a plis pase 4000£ aprè li te krase aparèy a nan yon zòn interdi pito yon atelie BAE Systems kote submari nuclear yo te konstri. Asosyasyon Pilòt Avyon Britanik (Balpa) ap reqi pou reyisyon urgàn, pou droyon yo jwenn menm standa sèkiritè yo kòm avyon tradisyonèl — avèk formasyon obligatwa pou pilòt ak teknoloji geofens. Espesyalis enformasyon yo avize ke uzaj droyon san règlementasyon ka vin yon menas moun pandan 2035. Menm si Greenpeace te fè yon sèl pwojèk nan site nuclear Frans pou mete an evidans defisit sekirite, yo refize tout lòt ligan ak vwayaj droyon yo. Katastrof Fukushima an 2011 te pouse Frans pou amelyore defans nuclear yo, men menas droyon yo reprezante yon nouvo defi ki evolye rapidman ki pa te entegre ansanm pa regilatè yo.

article_content: California prosecutors have decided not to press criminal charges against Deputy Andrew Wood, who killed prominent attorney and former Napster executive Milton Olin Jr. in December 2013. Olin, 65, was cycling along Mulholland Highway in Calabasas when Wood’s patrol car veered into the bike lane, striking him. At the time, Wood was responding to a work-related message on his in-car computer system—a use explicitly permitted under California law for law enforcement on duty. Prosecutors concluded that since Wood was acting within the scope of his responsibilities, no criminal violation occurred under Vehicle Code Section 23123.5. Despite this legal determination, Olin’s family has pursued civil action, filing a wrongful death lawsuit against the Sheriff’s Department and accusing Wood of negligence. They’ve also launched an online petition on Change.org that has gathered more than 67,000 signatures calling for criminal accountability. Olin, a seasoned lawyer with 38 years of experience and a former COO of Napster, was known for his work in intellectual property and business law. He is survived by his wife, Louise, and two sons, Chris and Geoff. In the wake of his death, his family has begun establishing the Milt Olin Foundation, aiming to improve cycling safety and reduce preventable fatalities on the road.

Olin, 65 an, te roulè sou Mulholland Highway nan Calabasas lè kars patwol yo te vire nan lane syklist la, li frapè. Lè sa a, Wood te reponn yon mesaj travay sou sistèm informatik la, yon pratik espesifikman pèmèt pa ley Kalyfòniyen pou polis yo ki travay. Pwosikèt yo te konklwe ke, paske Wood te aktive nan kòr de devoir li, pa gen okenn violasyon kriminel ki te fèt sou Seksiyon 23123.5 Kòd Veyikil la. Apre mòt li, fami li te kòmanse kreye Fondasyon Milt Olin, ki vle amelyore sekirite syklist ak redui mòt ki kapab evite yo sou route yo.
