article_content: Eighteen-year-old Australian cycling sensation Macey Stewart is recovering after a terrifying hit-and-run incident during a solo training ride in east Devonport, Tasmania. Around 2 p.m. on Thursday, she was struck from behind by a car while cycling home — the force of the collision sending her flying and detaching the vehicle’s side mirror. The driver paused briefly to collect the broken mirror, then sped away without checking on her welfare. In a heartfelt Instagram update, Stewart described the ordeal as her first — and hopefully last — encounter with 'green whistle' (nitrous oxide), jokingly referencing the euphoric sensation some associate with near-death experiences. 'I’m incredibly lucky to be alive,' she wrote, noting how she barely avoided being hit by an oncoming truck as she scrambled off the road. Despite the shock, she suffered only minor scrapes and bruises, with no broken bones. The world champion, who recently claimed gold in the junior individual time trial at the UCI World Championships in Spain, vowed to return to her bike within days. 'I’m sore, but I’m not quitting — I love cycling too much,' she told The Advocate. Her message to fellow riders? 'Be careful out there. Some people on the road are just crazy.' Tasmania Police confirmed they’ve identified a dark-colored sedan linked to the crash and are conducting forensic analysis. They’re also appealing for information from the truck driver who swerved to avoid Stewart after the impact. Authorities stress that leaving the scene of an accident involving injury is a serious offense.

article_content: A new study reveals that two million young people aged 17 to 21 in the UK have no intention of voting in next year’s general election. Many feel disillusioned, believing politicians prioritize big business, pensioners, homeowners, and even celebrities over their own concerns about jobs, education, and housing. Among those who do plan to vote, Labour leads with 40% support, followed by the Conservatives at 25%, UKIP at 12%, the Green Party at 9%, and the Liberal Democrats at just 5%—a sharp decline attributed to the party’s reversal on tuition fees. Surprisingly, non-politicians are viewed as more capable of leading the country than many elected officials. Labour leader Ed Miliband is chosen by 17% of young voters as the best person to run the country, followed by David Cameron and Boris Johnson, both at 15%. Comedian Russell Brand and businessman Alan Sugar tie at 12%, while Top Gear host Jeremy Clarkson receives 11%. In contrast, UKIP leader Nigel Farage garners only 9%, and former Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg ties with TV chef Jamie Oliver at just 6%. Sunder Katwala, director of British Future, emphasized that while young people feel ignored, abstaining from voting is unlikely to make politicians listen. He warned that if the election is as close as predicted, just half of the two million disengaged voters could determine the outcome. The study, conducted by YouGov for the think tank British Future, highlights a critical gap between youth priorities and political engagement—and urges both sides to act.

article_content: Last December, 13-year-old Hailee Lambeth took her own life after months of relentless bullying at Thurman White Middle School in Henderson, Nevada. Her parents, Jason and Jennifer Lambeth, now say her death might have been prevented if school officials had alerted them to the abuse she was enduring. Just hours before her death, Hailee had texted her parents with excitement—she’d been named Student of the Month in math. She was found dead at home from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, discovered by her younger brother, Jacob. In her final note, Hailee pleaded for her school to know she had taken her life, hoping it would make others think twice before targeting students like her. She named two classmates—referred to in court documents as 'C.H.' and 'J.J.'—who subjected her to daily humiliation. According to witnesses, C.H. repeatedly called her 'fat' and 'ugly,' shoved her during lunch, and even left a note in her locker demanding she 'drink bleach and die.' He also left a chilling voicemail in September, asking, 'Where are you Hailee? I hope you died,' referencing her recent epilepsy diagnosis. At least two separate reports of bullying were submitted to the school district: one by a peer who saw C.H. harass Hailee at lunch around Thanksgiving, and another from a PE teacher who witnessed J.J. making Hailee cry nearly every day. Neither report was formally shared with her parents, despite Nevada law requiring written notification in such cases. District policy also mandates that all bullying reports be investigated within ten days. C.H. had already been suspended twice for bullying other students, yet no action was taken to protect Hailee. The Lambeths filed a wrongful death lawsuit against the Clark County School District, arguing that had they been informed, they could have intervened—seeking counseling, transferring schools, or taking other protective steps. The district has declined to comment on the ongoing legal case. Their grief is compounded by the belief that their daughter’s suffering went unseen, unheard, and unaddressed—even though others tried to speak up.

Pèt yo, Jason ak Jennifer Lambeth, di ke mòt la te kapab evite si administratè ekol yo te avize yo sou abizman yo te rezive. Piti piti avan mòt la, Hailee te envoye yon mesaj pou pèt yo ki te kontan—li te dekare Student of the Month nan klas matematik li. Li te jwenn mouri nan kay la ak yon kou pyon ki te fèt pa li menm, epi se frè li pi piti a, Jacob, ki te jwenn li. Nan let ki te dènye a, Hailee te pleye pou ekol yo konnen ke li te pwopriye l mèt, espere ke sa ta kapab fè yon lòt timoun panse de fwa avan yo bòtè yon lòt. Li te anonse de klasè yo—sipoze tankou 'C.H.' ak 'J.J.' nan dokiman kour—ki te fèt yo te bòtè li chak jou. Dapre témoins, C.H. te repete 'moun moun' ak 'laj', te pouse li nan déjeuner, ak menm fèt yon let nan loke li ki te mande li 'bouè blèch ak mouri.' Li te toujou envoye yon mesaj vwayèl nan septanm, ki te mande, 'Ou kote ou Hailee? M espere ou mouri,' ki te referans pou diagnozis epilipsi li. Aucun rapò sa yo te transmis ak pèt yo, menm si lòd Nevada mande yon notifikasyon ekrit nan kèlkonk kote abizman rapòte. Politik distrikt mande tou ke tout rapòt abizman yo envestige an 10 jou. C.H. te deja suspendi de fwa pou abizman lòt timoun, menm pa gen okenn aksyon ki te pran pou proteje Hailee. Pèt Lambeth te deklare yon aksyon pou mòt anmèt kont Distrikt Ekol Clark County, di ke si yo te konnen, yo ta kapab aksyonne—chwazi yon konselè, transpòte ekol, oswa fè lòt aksyon pou proteje. article_content: At Ain Shams University, biologist Hebat Abdel Hadi is turning a pest problem into a poultry solution. Faced with rising feed costs and declining profits among major chicken producers like Pilgrim’s Pride and Tyson, she’s exploring an unexpected alternative: the discarded shells and carcasses of invasive Nile crayfish. These crustaceans, which have overrun Egypt’s Nile River and damaged fishing nets, might hold the key to cheaper, nutrient-rich chicken feed. In her PhD research, Abdel Hadi compared chickens fed traditional fish meal with those fed ground-up crayfish waste. The results were striking — chickens on the crayfish diet developed stronger bones, richer-colored meat, better taste, and laid more eggs with higher protein content. Nutritionally, the hard outer shells are packed with calcium and essential minerals, making them ideal for supporting rapid poultry growth. Yet experts remain cautious. Martin Humphries of a UK-based poultry feed firm acknowledges the theoretical benefits but warns that balancing nutrition for fast-growing chickens involves complex genetics and energy requirements — not just mineral supplements. Meanwhile, Dr. Madgy Khalil, another researcher at Ain Shams, confirms the crayfish population has exploded without natural predators. But scaling this idea beyond the lab? Andrew Kendall from BOCM Pauls, the UK’s biggest feed producer, doubts it. 'There simply aren’t enough crayfish to sustain large-scale production,' he says. Still, he adds, it could work well for small, localized farms looking to turn a local nuisance into a resource.

Devan kout manje yo ki monte ak pèt yo ki genyen nan kompani poul enportan tankou Pilgrim’s Pride ak Tyson, li ap eseye yon alternativ ki pa konn: kòs ak kòs krabèt invazif yo nan Nij. Krabèt sa yo, ki te pran tout rivyè Nij ak detwòye resevwa pèchè yo, kapab pote yon solisyon pou poul ki pi abòdab ak rich nan nutrisyon. Nan rekèch PhD li, Abdel Hadi te komanse pou kominikasyon poul ki te manje mèl pèch pa poul ki te manje kòs krabèt moun yo rejete. Rezilta yo te frapante — poul ki te manje kòs krabèt yo te fèt os pwochen, karne ki pi fò, pi bon gòt, ak lavi ki pi plis ak plis pwotèn. Noutrisyonèman, kòs yo ki pi dur yo pwovwa kalisyèm ak minèral yo, ki fè yo ideyal pou soutni poul ki grand vèl. Men, eksèp yo te konsènman. Martin Humphries, yon direktè vann manje poul nan Angleter, aksepte avantaj teorik yo men li avètiz ke balans nutrisyon pou poul ki grand vèl yo gen yon sèl lojik genetik ak enèji — paske se pa sèlman minèral yo. Pandan, Dr. Madgy Khalil, yon lòt rechèchis nan Ayiti Shams, konfime popilasyon krabèt yo te monte san anyen ki ap mache yo. Men, tounen idèe sa a an yon inisiativ laj? Andrew Kendall, espesyalis nan BOCM Pauls, pi gro kompani manje poul Angleter, pa konfyan. 'Pa gen assez krabèt pou sèvi yon pwodiksyon masif,' li di. Men, li ajoute, sa kapab moun yon piti makèt lokal ki vle tounen yon nòm lokal nan yon resous.

article_content: Manchester City defender Eliaquim Mangala has acknowledged that Chelsea striker Diego Costa frequently attempts to rattle opponents by provoking reactions — whether through physical contact or psychological tactics. But Mangala insists that whether or not Costa plays in Saturday’s crucial Premier League clash at Stamford Bridge won’t change City’s approach. Costa is set to appear before the FA on Friday to contest a charge of violent conduct after allegedly stamping on Liverpool’s Emre Can during their midweek EFL Cup semi-final. If found guilty, he could miss three matches, including the high-stakes game against City. The incident was one of several heated moments involving Costa, who also tangled with Martin Skrtel and Steven Gerrard in a fiery encounter. Mangala, however, believes the best response to Costa’s antics is complete indifference. 'It doesn’t matter to me if he plays or not,' he said. 'What matters is that we focus on our own game. Whether it’s Costa, Drogba, or Rémy up front, we still need to beat them.' According to Mangala, Costa thrives on mental warfare, trying to throw defenders off their rhythm. 'He wants you to lose your cool. But if you don’t react, he loses his power. That’s the key.' With City trailing Chelsea by five points in the league table, Mangala stressed the importance of securing a win at Stamford Bridge. 'This isn’t just another game — it’s a turning point for our title hopes.' He expects Chelsea to sit back and strike on the break, but says City won’t alter their attacking identity. 'We’ve got the talent to control the game. They’re solid defensively, but so are we — and we’ll play our way.'

Menm jan, Mangala te asire ke si Costa jwe oswa pa jwe nan klasik Premier League samedi nan Stamford Bridge, sa pa chanje aprovach City. Costa pral pwochen FA vandredi pou kontestè akuzasyon de konduite vyolen an aprè li te alègèman piste sou Emre Can, mwayen fèd Liverpool, nan demi-finale EFL Cup ki te pase. Si li trove koupable, li ka manke twa match, ki enkli match ki genyen City. Incidan sa a se yon nan plizyè moman tansyon ki te pase avèk Costa, ki te gen yon bagay ak Martin Skrtel ak Steven Gerrard nan yon match ki te fèt chalè. Mangala, menm tan an, panse ke reyons pi bon pou aksyon Costa se total indiferans. 'M pa konsidere si li jwe oswa pa jwe,' li te di. 'Sa ki enpòtan se nou dwe konnentre sou jwenn nou. Ke se Costa, Drogba oswa Rémy ki jwe devan, nou toujou dwe bat yo.' Pou Mangala, Costa vin nan gwo batay psikolojik, eseye fè defènse yo dekoncentre. 'Li vle ou pèdi wòl ou. Men si ou pa reyaji, li pèdi pouvwa li. Se sa ki klé.' Apre City ki arye Chelsea pa 5 pwen nan tab la, Mangala te mete aksan sou enpòtans pwochenn match nan Stamford Bridge. 'Se pa yon match tankou lòt yo — se yon moman kritik pou espwa tit la.' Li antèn ke Chelsea va rete arye ak frappe sou kounye a, men li di City pa pral chanje identite atak yo. 'Nou gen talan pou kontwole jwenn an. Yo solid de fason defans, men nou tou, e nou pral jwe nòmal nou.'

article_content: By Anna Edwards. PUBLISHED: 12:56 EST, 27 December 2013. | UPDATED: 15:49 EST, 27 December 2013. A retired company director who waited more than six hours for an ambulance died later that day in hospital. On the day Rodney Butcher became seriously ill, the East Midlands Ambulance Service (EMAS) was struggling to cope — paramedics had to respond to multiple calls before he was finally seen. The 76-year-old, who had diabetes, Parkinson’s disease, and Alzheimer’s, developed a severe urinary tract infection. His GP requested an ambulance to transport him to Royal Derby Hospital within four hours. When the ambulance did not arrive on time, staff at his nursing home called 999 twice. However, these repeated calls inadvertently canceled his original request, causing further delays. Mr. Butcher arrived at Royal Derby Hospital more than two hours late and was taken directly to accident and emergency, where he later died. Although the inquest concluded the delay did not contribute to his death, EMAS reviewed its policy on handling duplicate calls for the same incident. Mr. Butcher was receiving respite care at the Old Lodge Nursing Home in Etwall in November 2012. His condition worsened over three days, prompting his GP, Dr. Michael Vickers, to request an ambulance at 2:50 p.m. on the day of the incident. Dr. Vickers later said he should have requested an ambulance within two hours — though the inquest noted that even a two-hour window would have been challenging due to flooding and poor weather. At 7:34 p.m. and again at 8:11 p.m., nursing home staff called 999, reporting Mr. Butcher had become very pale. EMAS service delivery manager Alison Crowe confirmed the original request was overwritten by the new ones. An ambulance finally arrived at 9:27 p.m. and reached the hospital at 10:28 p.m. Assistant Coroner Paul McCandless recorded a narrative conclusion stating it was 'more likely than not' Mr. Butcher would have died even with timely arrival. The medical cause of death was diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by the infection. After the inquest, EMAS apologized to Mr. Butcher’s family and stated it had updated its procedures. The family thanked the service for taking responsibility.

article_content: A teenager thought to be the smallest in Britain has been hailed as 'inspirational and beautiful' by TV viewers. Georgia Rankin, 15, is just 2ft 8in (80 centimeters) tall. She was born with a rare form of skeletal dysplasia — commonly known as dwarfism — which caused her bones to fuse permanently during toddlerhood. Despite enduring constant pain, Georgia is determined to live like any other teenager: attending school, going to her prom, and shopping with friends. After appearing on ITV’s 'This Morning,' viewers flooded Twitter with admiration for her positive spirit. Carol Firman wrote: 'Georgia is an inspiration on how to live life to the full despite pain and physical difficulties. I’d want her as my friend!' Liv Haddow tweeted: 'Inspirational Georgia Rankin on TV this morning #yougogirl.' Lew said: 'Literally crying — Georgia is so inspirational.' DoubleKill Chrissie added: 'That sweet Georgia on This Morning with a bone condition — she’s lovely. It’s often people with disabilities who are the most positive.' Host Philip Schofield described Georgia as 'a delight to be around, with a sunny character.' Georgia’s parents, Andrea and Simon, were initially told she wouldn’t survive past her early teens. But after more than a decade of medical care, doctors now believe she can live a normal life. She shared: 'The hardest thing growing up was not being able to do things for myself. I couldn’t reach things — not even get a glass of water.' Georgia found a jewel-studded dress made for a three-year-old for her prom. The pain she experiences causes poor sleep, leaving her often 'half-asleep' at school. Her most recent surgery in October lasted five hours, during which surgeons reshaped the jagged tops of her thigh bones to reduce pain. She spent two weeks in hospital and six weeks undergoing intensive hydrotherapy and physiotherapy. Despite this, she still struggles with severe pain in her left hip. Georgia, whose feet are size seven, has already been outgrown by her four-year-old brother Brody — yet she remains upbeat. Her friends in Warrington call her 'Lil G' and are helping her raise £18,000 for a specially adapted 'Snap Dragon' wheelchair. The wheelchair would allow her to reach cupboards, operate switches, and move independently, as she currently cannot bear weight or lift objects like a kettle. Her current NHS wheelchair is too large and lacks essential features. The family hopes to use the funds to help Georgia fulfill her dream of traveling to Florida to swim with dolphins. On their campaign website, they wrote: 'Georgia will always remain at 80cm in height — but we believe great things come in small packages! Our Lil G has to live independently in a big world, where everything is a challenge. Despite all of this, nothing stops her smiling!' Georgia says: 'I just forget I am small. I see myself as the same as everyone else.'

Li te nes avèk yon fòm rar de displazi skeletèl — konn anndan kòm dvafis — ki fèt os li yo fèt permanent lè li te yon ti enfan. Men aprè plis pase dekenn an kounye a, medikaman yo kropan konsidere ke li ka viv yon lavi normèl. Li te di: 'Kos ki pi difisil nan pwogres la se pa kapab fè yon bagay pou mwen menm. M pa kapab atenn bagay yo, menm pou m pran yon vèt dlo.' Georgia te trove yon roba kouti ak jetè pou yon timoun 3 an pou fèt li. Doulè ki kontinyèl li fèt li pa ka dòmi byen, konsa li souvan 'dòmi mitan' soukòl. Operasyon ki pi rese a nan Oktòb la te dure 5ò, kote chirurgiyen yo te fèt tout oso kòt kousè yo pou yo fèt plis ronde ak pou redui doulè ki kontinyèl Georgia te ressenti. Li te rete 2 semèn nan hopital ak 6 semèn travay intensif idroterapi ak fizioterapi. Menm jan an, li toujou enkonfòm avèk doulè fort nan kousè gòch li. Georgia, ki piti pye 7, te deja depase pa frè 4 an li Brody — men li refize dwe yon lòt bagay sa pa pozitif. Zanmi li nan Warrington rele li 'Lil G' epi yo aseme pou li leve 18,000£ pou yon chèzi 'Snap Dragon' ki adaptè pou kò li piti. Chèzi sa a ta dwe pèmèt li atenn kabin ak intèrwit, ak move libète, paske l kounya pa kapab mete peyiz li, menm pouse yon bouyèl. Fanmi a vle itilize lajan sa pou pèmèt Georgia realize son vòlonté pou ale Floride pou bann danmòn. Sou sit kampani a, yo ekri: 'Georgia ta toujou rete 80cm nan longè a — men nou kropan konsidere ke bagay ki pi bon yo vin nan piti pakèt! Nòt Lil G dwe eseye viv anndan yon monn ki gwo, kote tout bagay se yon defi. Malgre tout sa, pa gen anyen ki arrete souri li!' Georgia di: 'M oublie m piti. M wè m kòm menm bagay ak tout moun lòt yo.'

article_content: On October 18, Singapore Airlines Flight SQ424, an A380 traveling from Singapore to Mumbai, encountered sudden turbulence at 15,000 feet, resulting in injuries to 22 people — eight passengers and 14 crew members. The aircraft landed safely at Mumbai’s Terminal 2 at approximately 10 p.m. All injured individuals were promptly transported to two private hospitals in the city. According to Singapore Airlines, the seat belt sign was illuminated at the time of the incident. Six passengers and all 14 crew members were treated and discharged; two passengers remained under observation for further medical care. The airline confirmed that the aircraft carried 408 passengers and 25 crew members and issued a statement: 'Flight SQ424 experienced sudden turbulence during descent on October 18. Injuries were addressed by medical personnel upon arrival.' The Mumbai Airport Authority also verified the medical response, noting its team assisted injured passengers and crew at Terminal 2. Following a thorough inspection by engineers, the aircraft was cleared to resume operations. This incident recalls a similar event in May 2013, when a Singapore Airlines flight to London suffered turbulence during meal service, injuring 11 passengers and causing widespread disruption in the cabin.

article_content: In a courtroom twist straight out of a thriller, a Colorado-based Army soldier is claiming his identical twin brother — not him — committed a series of horrific sexual assaults on young girls. Aaron Gregory Lucas, 32, faces 27 serious charges related to crimes in Colorado, Alabama, and Texas, but his legal team argues that because he and Brian Lucas share the exact same DNA, forensic evidence linking Aaron to the scenes could actually belong to his brother. Authorities have confirmed that DNA collected from crime scenes in all three states matches Lucas’s profile, but his attorneys point to witness reports from Alabama describing a vehicle tied to Brian, not Aaron. They also suggest a third individual — a man previously arrested for indecent exposure who resembles the suspect and drove a similar car — might be responsible for some attacks. A judge recently approved the defense’s right to name both Brian and the third man as possible perpetrators, allowing the jury to consider reasonable doubt. Though Brian has never been charged and reportedly visited Colorado only once in the past ten years — never entering El Paso County — the defense insists the genetic match alone doesn’t prove guilt. Legal experts warn such twin defenses are rare and risky; success hinges on which brother can provide the stronger alibi. Meanwhile, Aaron Lucas, a decorated soldier stationed at Fort Carson, remains jailed as prosecutors push to combine all six cases into one trial. The defense wants them separated. With the trial slated for January, the case is poised to become a landmark test of how courts handle forensic evidence when identical twins are involved.

article_content: Geneva, Switzerland (CNN) — Western diplomats and Iran appear to be nearing a breakthrough agreement that could slow the nation’s suspected progress toward a nuclear weapon while easing some sanctions that have strained its economy. Top diplomats from the United States, France, Britain, and Germany rushed to Geneva on Friday to finalize the deal, which emerged unexpectedly after years of stalled negotiations and Western suspicions of Iran’s evasive tactics with international inspectors. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov may join the talks on Saturday, according to Russia’s state-run Ria Novosti news service. China’s foreign minister is also en route to Geneva, per Press TV. The planned arrival of these officials on Saturday suggests no agreement was reached Friday night — contrary to earlier predictions by Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif. Saturday’s negotiations will include a meeting between US Secretary of State John Kerry, EU foreign policy chief Catherine Ashton, and Zarif. "The negotiations have reached a critical, highly sensitive stage and require decisions at the highest levels," said Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. Under the emerging framework, Iran would halt uranium enrichment to 20% purity — a key step toward weapon-grade material — dismantle its existing stockpile of such material, and refrain from using advanced IR-2 centrifuges or activating the Arak plutonium reactor. In return, the P5+1 would unfreeze some Iranian assets held abroad and consider easing sanctions on gold, precious metals, and petrochemicals. US officials say the goal is to extend Iran’s breakout time — the period needed to produce enough fissile material for a bomb — while offering limited, reversible sanctions relief. US President Barack Obama emphasized that core sanctions would remain in place, allowing rapid re-imposition if Iran violates the terms. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticized the potential deal as "the deal of the century for Iran" and "very dangerous for peace," arguing Iran gains relief without dismantling any centrifuges. British Prime Minister David Cameron, however, said discussions with French President François Hollande revealed an opportunity for "real progress." The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) announced its director will travel to Tehran on Monday to meet Iranian officials and conduct parallel technical talks. Despite progress, Kerry and French Foreign Minister Laurent Fabius acknowledged significant gaps remain. Iran insists its right to enrich uranium is non-negotiable, though Zarif stated, "We can deal with various issues. Various issues are on the table." The negotiations follow a thaw in Iran-West relations under President Hassan Rouhani, though Iran continues to deny any military intent behind its nuclear program. The IAEA estimates Iran possesses 185 kilograms of uranium enriched to 20% purity — enough, experts say, to be further refined for a nuclear weapon, though not yet sufficient for a full warhead. Sanctions imposed by the UN since 2006 and the US since 2000 remain in effect, demanding Iran prove its program is exclusively peaceful.

Otifis Etazini di objektif la se pou extend tan ki dwe pou Irèn fè yon arme nukleyè — periòd ki dwe pou fè yon kantite fissil — tout nan menm tan ki bay souleman limite ak revesib. Premye Minisè Angleter David Cameron, menm jan an, te di diskisyon avèk Prezidan Frans François Hollande te montre yon oportunite pou "avanse reyèl." Agency Nukleyè Entènasyonal (IAEA) te anonse direktè li a pral al Téhran lundi pou pale avek dirijan Irèn ak fè yon mèt teknik paralèl. article_content: Switching on breakfast television last week, I was startled to see Vogue editor Alexandra Shulman discussing a 'school initiative' she is involved in. At first, I assumed that instead of jet-setting to fashion shows in discounted or free designer clothing, Ms. Shulman would be visiting comprehensive schools across the country. But no — Vogue is simply distributing a video and lesson plan for Year Nine teachers (students aged 13–14) to help them deconstruct the illusions behind the magazine’s glossy pages. Or, more accurately, to market its products in a campaign perfectly timed with the latest international fashion weeks. Let me reveal what Vogue’s curriculum actually includes. Shulman’s lesson plan instructs teachers to tell students that 'only a very small percentage of the population have the natural build and appearance of a model.' It outlines each step of a fashion photoshoot and lists, without critical context, the 'diverse' individuals Vogue has photographed — including Adele — while omitting that the magazine only showed her airbrushed head, hiding the rest of her body. It is, frankly, laughable. This is not Vogue admitting it must evolve or respect its readers more. Instead, it asks young women to change how they react to images designed to sell products — reactions that are often visceral, emotional, and unconscious. Shulman claims the magazine’s pictures 'aspire and entertain,' but she’s being disingenuous. They are designed to sell. If readers stopped believing the fantasy — that wearing a certain dress will make them look like a model, attract a boyfriend, and find happiness — Vogue would go out of business. Simple as that. I don’t accept Shulman’s claim that fashion imagery is harmless fantasy, separate from real life. Fashion is seductive and persuasive. It chips away, bit by bit, at self-esteem. Not every young woman’s — if you’re surrounded by a loving family, supportive friends, and vigilant teachers, you may shield yourself, like a high-quality Burberry mac. But for Shulman to say, 'the problem, if there is one, arises when people judge themselves against models in magazines and feel they fall short,' is astonishing. From personal experience, knowing the truth — that models have vein marks and acne, that images are digitally altered, that heads are grafted onto other bodies (as the short film reveals, it takes 20 professionals to produce one photo) — doesn’t help. It cannot undo the damage done deep within the brain, in the reptilian cortex, which 'does not respond to talking therapies,' as Professor Janet Treasure of Guy’s Hospital explains. The rational mind may understand Kate Moss doesn’t look like her June cover — but the subconscious still whispers: you don’t measure up. I was taught to hate my body by an industry I loved — but that never loved me back. It’s heartbreaking to see this cycle repeat with younger generations, who still believe the lies Shulman repeats in her new film: 'It’s just fantasy. You’re not supposed to want to look like them — they’re just an escape, not an aspiration.' Yes, we need education on this topic — but not from the gatekeepers, the very people who profit from keeping us blind to their artifice. Meanwhile, legendary designer Diane von Furstenberg is celebrating 40 years of the wrap dress next year with a new spring 2014 capsule collection. (Actually, the wrap dress debuted in 1972 — designers aren’t always great at math.) Inspired by feminism, it was lightweight, wrinkle-resistant silk jersey, perfect for the working woman: easy to pack, quick to wear. As DvF told Vogue in 1976: 'Simplicity and sexiness — that’s what people want, at a price that’s not outrageous.' When I visited her shop, it was small and quiet, with polite staff and a few customers whose faces looked tightly pulled. Today, the wrap dress — once styled with tan skin, cowboy boots, and Jerry Hall’s hair — is worn by 'everywoman,' often looking frumpy unless paired with killer heels. Options range from £300 to £500, with leopard and snake prints dominating. I admire DvF’s consistency: her body-con dresses and lace shifts don’t work as well. Only one criticism: the shoes are pedestrian, barely better than LK Bennett. LIZ’S VERDICT: 9/10.

Mwen te pense ke, plis pase pou al nan fason syèl la pou fèt fason nouvo avèk vêteman designer ki te redui oswa sèlman pou yo bay, Madam Shulman ta pral ale nan tout eko lekòl komprèhensif nan peyi a. Menm pa — tout sa Vogue fè se pousi yon videyo ak yon plan leson pou mèt yo nan nivo neyèn (13-14 an) pou yo itilize pou dekonstri reyalite ki pèmèt fèt paj yo glasman. Oswa pi fidelman, pou vann prodwi yo nan yon kampan ki te pa t ap pati a kounye a pou fason syèl la internasyonal la. Mwen pral revele ki sa ki genyen nan plan leson Vogue a. Plan leson Shulman mande mèt yo pou di eleve yo ke 'sèlman yon ti poulaj nan popilasyon an gen konstitis ak aparans ki gen pou fè ak mode a.' Li detaye chak etap nan yon syèl fason, epi li liste, san kritik, moun ki 'divès' ki te fotografiye pa Vogue, tankou Adele — san pèmèt ou konnen ke magazin an te pa montre okenn lòt pati kò a l’apre yo te retouche tèt li! Se fasil, absèd. Sa ki rive se pa Vogue ki admet li dwe evolye, oswa respekte lide li pi fò. Plutot, li mande timoun fi yo chanje reaksyon yo sou imaj yo ki te fèt pou vann pwodui — reaksyon ki souvan senkèt, emosyonèl, epi sans konprensyon. Shulman di imaj yo nan magazin an 'apire ak amize,' men li fè yon fòs. Yo fèt pou vann. Si lisè yo te konsa pa kriye fantsi a — ke si yo mete yon roba jeneral, yo ta kapab vin tankou yon mode, epi jwenn yon kòmansman, epi jwenn bonheur — Vogue ta pral fèmen. Trè senp. Mwen pa aksepte afirmasyon Shulman an ke imaj fason an se fantsi sans domaj, separé de reyalite a. Fason an se sediktiv epi konvinsan. Li koupe, koupe, koupe, sou estime moun yo. Pa tout timoun fi — si ou gen yon kouti protèktiv ak fami ki aime, ak zanmi ki bon, ak mèt ki veye, ou kapab reziste imaj yo, tankou yon mac Burberry ki bon. Men pou Shulman di, 'pwoblèm la, si gen yon pwoblèm, se lè moun yo jije yo menm sou baze imaj yo wè nan revi yo epi yo santi yo pa gen asèt,' se konsa ekstèn. Mwen te eksperyansyen an, konnen reyalite a — ke mode yo gen ven yo, ak akne, ke imaj yo te retouche, ke tèt yo te mete sou kò ki pa menm (videyo a montre ke 20 pèsonn yo bezwen pou fè yon foto), pa aji. Li pa kapab retounen domaj ki te fèt nan pi profond kòt kò a, kòt reptilien ki nan kran kran ou, ki 'pa reponn ak terapi oral,' (mèsi Janet Treasure, profesè psikiyatri nan Hopital Guy’s). Kòt rasional kò a, ki konprann ke Kate Moss pa vreman gen menm aparans ki nan kouvèt jen an, pa kapab domine subkonskye a ki di ou pa gen asèt. Mwen te aprann pou deteste kò m pa yon endistri mwen renmen — men pa t renmen mwen reyèlman. Se tris pou wè istwa mwen reapele, anpil, pa timoun ki vini aprè m, ki kroie menm fòs ki Shulman reprezante nan videyo sa a: 'Ou, se fantsi, ou pa dwe vle vin tankou sa yo, se sèlman yon evazyon, pa yon asipasyon.' Wi, nou bezwen edikasyon sou sa a — men pa pa moun ki gardè port, moun ki gen tout bagay pou pèdi si ou ouvri jwenn yo sou artifi sila yo. Mwenm, konsa, Diane von Furstenberg, ki te fèt 40 an anndan ane a, avèk yon koleksyon kapa pou printem 2014. (Enpotan, roba enfle a te pèdi an 1972 — moun ki fè fason pa toujou bon nan kalkil yo.) Li te inspiré pa moviman feminis: lèt, fèt avèk sèl silk jersey ki pa fèt, li te parfèt pou moun ki travay: fasil pou pake, fasil pou mete oswa enlevé. 'Simplisite ak sekse, se sa moun vle,' DvF te di Vogue an 1976. Koum mwen te al, boutik la ti, pa gen moun, ak vandè yo ki poli epi entènse, epi kèk klant ki fèt fèt. Menm kounye a, roba enfle a — ki te mete sou tan, bot kowboy, ak timoun Jerry Hall — te pran pou tout moun, epi li ka fèt si ou pa akseptè avèk soulye ki fèt. Gen anpil varyasyon yo, ki koute nan 300£ pou 500£, men ki pi konprann se imaj panyèl oswa kòb. Mwen renmen fason konsa DvF rete fidel ak idè a: roba ki kòt kò a ak shift yo pa fèt byen. Epi, bien sûr, ou kapab achte varyasyon roba enfle a nan tout kote, depi nan Issa pou Asos. DvF pa pèdi sèlman yon pwen pou soulye yo ki pa gen anyen espesyal, pa pi bon pase LK Bennett. LIZ’ VERDIT: 9/10.

article_content: UK manufacturing could save up to £7 billion annually as the government moves to freeze carbon taxes, offering major relief to energy-heavy industries. Chancellor George Osborne announced that the carbon price floor — a levy on emissions — will remain at £18.08 per tonne through 2026, halting planned increases to £30. This decision is expected to cut costs for factories producing steel, paper, and other goods, with medium-sized firms potentially saving £50,000 a year. Tony Pedder, head of Sheffield Forgemasters, said his plant may shut down 30 times this year due to soaring energy bills caused by green taxes. He welcomed the move, calling it a step toward leveling the playing field against overseas competitors. The government will also extend compensation to affected businesses until 2020 and introduce a new system to refund companies for renewable energy surcharges they’re forced to pay. Meanwhile, households might see a small drop of about £15 on their annual energy bills. But the policy isn’t all good news: drivers of electric and low-emission vehicles, once exempt, will now face growing taxes. For example, a Nissan Leaf bought before 2015 will incur a £1,350 annual charge by 2019 — up from zero. Classic cars like the Reliant Robin are also getting a break: starting April 1, any vehicle over 40 years old will be exempt from road tax, expanding the list beyond pre-1973 models to include the Austin Allegro and MGB V. Critics, including economist Lord Nicholas Stern, argue the policy undermines long-term green investment by creating uncertainty. 'Fiddling with climate policy raises the cost of capital,' he warned. Still, industry groups like the EEF and steel union Community praised the move as overdue support for British manufacturing — especially in the North, Scotland, and Wales, where 80% of energy-intensive firms are located. On the flip side, company car taxes will rise 2% yearly through 2019, hitting drivers of petrol and diesel vehicles harder — but offering slight discounts for ultra-low emission alternatives.

article_content: From the ninth floor of an office building in San Francisco, Verizon Wireless executives gazed out at the sweeping view of the East Bay. Behind them, baristas crafted free cappuccinos for guests visiting the newly renovated space in SoMa — the heart of the city’s tech scene. This is the Verizon Application Innovation Center, launched last month, offering software developers — both large and small — complimentary access to development phones, wireless testing equipment, shielded rooms, and endless coffee. Executives say the center is part of a broader strategy to reshape Verizon’s image among app developers, who have long criticized carriers for restrictive data caps and blocked high-bandwidth applications. Similar moves are underway across the industry: Vodafone, which holds a stake in Verizon Wireless, opened its own innovation hub in Silicon Valley this month. AT&T recently unveiled its Foundry Development Center in Palo Alto, complete with wheeled furniture designed for spontaneous collaboration. Over 100 projects are currently active there, many in partnership with external companies. 'We wanted to be right in the middle of Silicon Valley — the epicenter of innovation,' said Jon Summers, an AT&T technology executive. AT&T is also collaborating with top venture firms like Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia Capital to identify promising startups. Developers can drop by unannounced and receive direct technical support from AT&T engineers, Ericsson staff, and occasional visitors from Microsoft and Juniper Networks. Verizon’s San Francisco team includes 25 engineers; the company previously launched similar centers in Waltham, Massachusetts, and AT&T has opened additional ones in Plano, Texas, and Ra’anana, Israel. Executives acknowledge that while these centers foster goodwill, they don’t expect developers to sign exclusivity deals. 'No one has a monopoly on good ideas,' said Verizon CEO Dan Mead. Analysts like Michael King of Gartner argue that carriers risk becoming mere 'dumb pipes' — simple data conduits — unless they add real value. Yet developers remain cautious: Facebook’s Andrew Bosworth notes telecoms still operate in 'closed loops,' restricting access to core services like SMS. While carriers are trying to appear supportive, many developers believe true innovation requires open ecosystems — not just free lattes and fancy offices. Still, early feedback suggests a shift in perception. According to Verizon’s Kyle Malady, some developers who once saw Verizon as 'the big, bad carrier' now describe it as 'so open.' As Verizon CTO David Small put it: 'The potential for innovation is bigger than Verizon.'

article_content: New data reveals that the average British person spends just over four hours each day watching television — the third-longest viewing time in the world, trailing only the United States and Italy. According to Ofcom, UK viewers tuned in for 242 minutes daily in the latest survey, up 17 minutes from 2010, when the average was three hours and 45 minutes. While Americans clock nearly five hours and Italians watch just over four hours and ten minutes, Britain remains firmly in the global spotlight for its TV habits. James Thickett, Ofcom’s head of research, notes that the UK has long been passionate about television, but today’s viewers are doing it differently. Thanks to smart TVs, high-definition screens, and streaming platforms like BBC iPlayer, Channel 4’s 4OD, and Sky Go, families are gathering again in the living room — not because they’ve abandoned technology, but because they’re using it to connect. Smartphones play a surprising role too: 60% of Brits own one, and two-thirds of 16-to-34-year-olds do. Rather than isolating themselves, many are watching the same show as their family while texting friends or posting reactions online. The shift away from multiple TVs in every room has led households to invest in one larger, better-quality screen in the main living area. And crucially, the UK leads the world in online TV access: nearly a quarter of viewers stream content weekly, far outpacing the U.S., where only 17% do the same.

article_content: Hundreds of jobs were under threat at three of BAE Systems’ UK shipyards last night, as unions prepared to meet defence officials to discuss potential layoffs of more than 1,000 workers. BAE Systems is expected to announce cuts as early as tomorrow. The future of the shipyards has been uncertain for months, following concerns that no new contracts would follow completion of two aircraft carriers. Jobs at the Govan, Scotstoun, and Portsmouth sites could be affected. However, a potential lifeline exists in the form of a contract to build the Type 26 Global Combat Ship for the Royal Navy — though BAE has not yet confirmed which site will undertake the work. The Govan and Scotstoun yards in Scotland hold particular political significance ahead of next year’s referendum on Scottish independence. A BAE spokesperson stated: 'We continue to work closely with the Ministry of Defence to explore all possible options to sustain the UK’s capability to deliver complex warships. We remain committed to keeping employees and unions informed as this process evolves.' Scotland’s Finance Secretary, John Swinney, said: 'We have been in ongoing dialogue with BAE Systems regarding the future of the Clyde shipyards. We are awaiting the outcome of their talks with the MoD and are closely monitoring the situation.' Hugh Scullion, General Secretary of the Confederation of Shipbuilding and Engineering Unions, added: 'We’ve secured talks with senior BAE executives next week to review the business case behind the upcoming announcement. This is not a time for speculation or political posturing — it’s about the future of an entire industry. Workers are delivering vital national defence assets and deserve clear answers.' A GMB union representative noted: 'Full-time union officials and shop stewards will meet BAE next week to examine the detailed plan for organizing work after the carrier program ends.' BAE launched a strategic review of its defence operations 18 months ago. Labour’s Shadow Defence Secretary, Vernon Coaker MP, warned: 'There will be deep anxiety among highly skilled workers, their families, and their communities. This decision has major implications for the future of UK shipbuilding and national defence.'

article_content: On Tuesday night, Fernando Alonso captained a team of Formula One drivers in a charity football match against a 'Star XI' at Stade Louis II in Monaco. The annual event, 'Star Team for Children,' was founded by Prince Albert II two decades ago to support youth causes. The Star XI featured high-profile athletes including tennis champion Novak Djokovic, former footballers Freddie Ljungberg and David Ginola. Djokovic opened the scoring, and his team went on to win 3-2. In a surprising turn, Claudio Ranieri — who was dismissed as manager of AS Monaco earlier that same day — still appeared on the sidelines to coach the F1 drivers, displaying grace under pressure. Williams driver Felipe Massa shared photos from the event on Instagram, while Toro Rosso’s Daniel Kvyat also participated ahead of the upcoming Monaco Grand Prix. Leonardo Jardim is now considered the leading candidate to replace Ranieri as Monaco’s head coach. The match, held every May, brings together global sports stars for a good cause. More information can be found at www.starteamforthechildren.org.

Ekip Star XI te gen atlet enpòtan tankou tenisè Novak Djokovic, anviwòmèn anpil Freddie Ljungberg ak David Ginola. Djokovic te ouvri score a, epi ekip li te gagnen 3-2. article_content: The U.S. Department of Justice offered major news organizations a chance to attend an off-the-record briefing and Q&A session with Attorney General Eric Holder regarding the agency’s intrusive surveillance of reporters. However, there was one condition: the entire session had to be off the record—meaning reporters could not publish anything about it. Most major media outlets, including the Associated Press and Fox News—the two whose phone records and emails were secretly seized during DOJ investigations into national security leaks—announced they would boycott the meeting. Brad Woodhouse, communications director for the Democratic National Committee, criticized the media’s refusal, tweeting that President Barack Obama had asked Holder to review how leak investigations were conducted—and that some in the media ‘refuse to meet with him,’ thereby ‘kind of forfeiting your right to gripe.’ His remarks sparked immediate backlash from journalists across the political spectrum. Critics called the statement tone-deaf and hypocritical, especially given the DOJ’s recent surveillance actions. Dylan Byers of Politico—one of the few outlets agreeing to attend—was mocked by colleagues, while others like BuzzFeed’s Andrew Kaczynski pointedly linked the request for secrecy to the DOJ’s own secretive tactics. The Washington Post’s decision to attend drew skepticism, but Executive Editor Marty Baron defended it, stating that journalists often participate in off-the-record meetings to advocate for their interests and that he trusted his team to report on the discussion vigorously. White House Deputy Press Secretary Josh Earnest defended the offer on Air Force One, insisting the administration was genuinely seeking media input. But reporters questioned the logic of holding a secret meeting about press freedom. Commentators like Ron Fournier of National Journal and editorial writer Don Surber of The Daily Mail (Charleston, WV) emphasized that journalists set the terms for off-the-record conversations—not the government. Surber quipped that ‘forfeits your right’ was now the administration’s motto. Conservative humorist Sean Medlock, writing as ‘Jim Treacher’ for The Daily Caller, mocked the bipartisan outrage against Woodhouse, noting, ‘You must be doing all kinds of things right.’ Andy Levy of Fox News’ Red Eye summed up many views: ‘It’s hard to believe Americans are cynical about politics with people like you around.’ The New York Times and other outlets that declined the invitation were praised for standing firm on press principles, while the White House’s stance appeared increasingly disconnected from the reality of its own actions.

Men, gen yon kondisyon: tout renyon an dwe 'hors de l'enregistrement'—sa vle di rapòte yo pa ka ekri okenn bagay sou li. Plispi medya ki te invité yo te anonse yo ta boikote renyon an, konsa l'Associated Press ak Fox News—de moun ki te pran enformasyon telefòn ak e-mail yo sekrèman lè enfèstigasyon DOJ sou fèt sekirite nasyonal. Brad Woodhouse, direktè kominikasyon pou Komite Nasyonal Demokrat, te fache. Li te twete jeudi ke Prezidan Barack Obama te demann Holder 'pou revizyòn kòman enfèstigasyon fèt,' men plispi medya refize pale avèk li. Sa, Woodhouse te di, 'sa vle di ou pa gen droit pou kriye.' Kouman travay la te monte, ki te vini nan tou de kote politik: dwa ak gòch. Brad Woodhouse, espesyalis kominikasyon pou Americans United for Change ki maintenan travay pou Komite Nasyonal Demokrat, pa fèt anyen pou medya jeudi. Woodhouse te debite konfli a pa tèlman Associated Press, Fox News, New York Times, Huffington Post ak lòt medya ki refize ala renyon 'hors de l'enregistrement' avèk Eric Holder, avoka jeneral ki te nan entèn. Don Surber, redaktè editorial pou The Daily Mail—pa edisyon imprimè nou yo nan London, men yon journal daily nan Charleston, Virjini Kanbèn—te sòti yon repons twete ke 'sa vle di ou pa gen droit pou kriye' se 'mot d'ordre de aministrasyon sa a.' 'O, epi Brad Woodhouse,' Surber te twete apre, 'droit ou yo vin de God. Ou pa ka forfeit yo.' Rapòte medya Politico Dylan Byers te pi senp. 'Jésus, Brad,' li te twete. Gregg Keller, direktè ekzekitif pou American Conservative Union, te pren plèzi wè Politico ki sipoze akròch avèk Pati Demokrat. Repons twete li te yon gwo rire: 'HAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA.' Organizasyon Byers a se nan lis ti moun ki te di yo ta ala avèk avoka jeneral sou kondisyon li. Lòt yo tankou ABC News, Washington Post, The Wall Street Journal, ak LA Times ak Chicago Tribune ki partaje yon chefdibwè Washington an komun. Dylan Byers, ki rapòte sou medya, se nan relasyon premye non avèk komunikatè demokrat pi enpotan men li pa renmen sa li te envni. Andrew Kaczynski, rapòte BuzzFeed Politik, te reponn, ki referans pou sekrèt seize enfòmasyon telefòn ak e-mail yo nan AP ak Fox News. 'TV's Andy Levy,' tankou li te prezentè chak jou nan emisyon Fox News 'Red Eye,' te fè yon koup nan dirèksyon Woodhouse. CNN, CBS News, Reuters, McClatchy, New York Times ak Huffington Post te jwenn ak Fox News ak Associated Press nan refiz ala. Adecyon Washington Post pou pale avèk Holder te leve sourcèl nan kapital nasyonal, men direktè ekzekitif Post Marty Baron te defenn decizyon li a sou blog medya li a. 'Mwen prefere tout renyon an dwe sou l'enregistrement,' Baron te di. 'Men, rapòte yo fèt toujou renyon hors de l'enregistrement, si yo prefere kondisyon sa yo oswa pa, epi kontinye rapòte sou evènman yo. 'Mwen al renyon sa a pou reprezante interè mwen yo kòm rapòte ak pou mete enplasyon mwen yo. Mwen toujou panse ke rapòte mwen yo ap rapòte sa a tankou tout lòt bagay yo.' Ron Fournier, direktè editorial nan National Journal ak yon vo respekte nan DC beltway, te pran inquietid avèk kòman Woodhouse te sugere govènman dwe balanse proteksyon Premier Amendman pres ak sekirite nasyonal. Eske Woodhouse rey? Rapòte yo pale avèk souris pou 'hors de l'enregistrement' konvèsasyon tout tan... Se sa ki fè diferans: Rapòte yo konsènman kondisyon yo. Souris yo pa ka fòse rapòte yo pou pale—sa ki pa dwe konnen yon spesyalis politik eksperyans. Andrew Kaczynski, rapòte BuzzFeed Politik ki se yon maîtresse konprann video arkiv politik, te konekte demann DOJ pou renyon sekrè avèk enfòmasyon sekrèt yo sou AP ak Fox News. Si Holder ak ekip li vle reyaksyon nan rapòte yo, li te twete, 'Mwen pènse yo kapab trove kòman yo santi yo pa e-mail ak enfòmasyon telefòn sekrèt.' Blogger kas The Daily Caller, Sean Medlock—yon komedyan konservatè ki ekri avèk yon nom pseido 'Jim Treacher'—te rapidman mete sel nan pla Woodhouse. 'Remake kòman moun yo tou de kote aks yo montre ki enpotan sa a?' li ekri. 'Ou dwe fè tout bagay yo dwe.' Partisan konservatè yo te komplimante rapòte yo nan medya ki gen tendans gòch tankou Politico ak BuzzFeed. Surber se redaktè editorial pou 'lòt' The Daily Mail, journal nan Charleston, Virjini Kanbèn. Josh Earnest, sous-sekrètè pres pou kominikasyon Bòs Blan, te reponn kèk pyèt nan Air Force One jeudi, epi tem ki te vini sou renyon Holder ki te fèt pou medya. 'Ou kapab konprann ke yon renyon sou inquietid rapòte yo sou Premier Amendman ki 'hors de l'enregistrement' se yon hypokrizi sou lavi,' te demann yon rapòte, selon transkripsyon Bòs Blan. 'Non,' Earnest te reponn. 'Mwen pa vèman wè sa... Mwen pa panse gen okenn dòub pou seriosite avoka jeneral lan ki pwochen sa li te identifiye ak sa prezidan te identifiye kòm yon priorite veritab. Epi nou sèlman interese nan enput, opinyon, konsèy, ekspètiz lider medya prominent.' 'Eske Prezidan an sou inquietid ke Holder se konsa sou presyon a kounye a ke li ka afekte kapasite li pou fè travay li?' te presé rapòte Earnest? 'Pa janm,' te reponn li. Kolumnis New York Post ak editeur Commentary Magazine John Podhoretz te kritike gramatik twet Woodhouse, antòm lòt bagay. Projè Politik SIDA te pran inquietid avèk Woodhouse epi tèt kapèl New York Times pou yon nan premye yo ki montre 'kèk kouraj' nan refiz administrasyon an. Men rapòte yo menm—ki twete, nan okenn kote—te wè Bòs Blan tankou hypokrit ak Woodhouse tankou fòl. 'Wow,' te twete Andy Levy, personalite Fox News, kòmak ak emisyon Red Eye. 'Sèlman difisil pou kreye Ameriken yo enkredil sou politik avèk moun tankou ou a jwenn.' Direktè editorial National Journal Ron Fournier, anvan chefdibwè Associated Press nan Washington, te mete sarkazm li a deyò epi te engage Woodhouse serièman. 'Balans ant sekirite/libète mérite pi bon ke ton sa a,' li ekri. 'Gen plis ton tou de kote, Woodhouse, te ekri nan twet li sèlman. 'Eske rapòte yo pa di yo pa janm pale avèk subjèt 'hors de l'enregistrement'? Aji jodi a tout tan.' 'Sou kondisyon nou,' Fournier te reponn. 'Pa govènman an.' 'Jim Treacher,' blogger kasa The Daily Caller, te remèt bato a bato a kòm yon tsonnèn bipartizan epi te pouse Woodhouse lè li te anba. article_content: Havana, Cuba (CNN) — Cuban President Raúl Castro has granted Pope Benedict XVI’s request to make Good Friday a public holiday — at least for this year, according to Cuban state media. During his visit to Cuba this week, the Pope asked Castro to recognize the day Christians commemorate the crucifixion of Jesus Christ, a Vatican spokesman said. The government announced that workers would have the day off on April 6, marking the first official observance of Good Friday since the 1959 Cuban Revolution. Previously, Christmas was the only other religious holiday officially recognized in Cuba, a status granted in 1997 following a request by Pope John Paul II ahead of his visit. Cuban state media reported that Castro informed the Pope on Wednesday that Good Friday would be observed this year. Whether the holiday will become permanent remains under consideration. In a private meeting, Benedict also requested permission for the Catholic Church to open schools and broadcast religious programming, according to Vatican spokesman Federico Lombardi during a press conference in Havana. As of now, the Cuban government has not publicly responded to these additional requests.
translated_content: Havanna, Kiba (CNN) — Prezidan Raúl Castro te pèmèt Papa Benèdikt XVI pou fè Vèndredi Sèn yon jounè fèt — duvan an, selon medya etatik Kiba. Pandan visit li a Kiba sa a, Papa te demann Raúl Castro pou rekonèt jou ki kòmèmòre krisifikasyon Jezu Krist, tankou yon spesyalis Vatikan te di. Gouvènman an te anonse ke travayè yo pral gen yon jou lib le 6 avril, marken premye fwa Kibèn te fèt ofisyèlman Vèndredi Sèn pandan revolisyon Kibèn 1959. Anvan sa, Nwèl te sèlman lòt fèt religyè ki te rekonèt nan Kiba, statis sa te pèmèt nan 1997 aprè demann Papa Jean-Paul II avan visit li a. Medya etatik Kiba te rapòte ke Raúl te di Papa lenwedri ke Vèndredi Sèn pral fèt ane sa a. Si fèt sa a pral devenn ofisyèl pèrmanan, li pa vini ankor. Pandan yon rezond privè, Benèdikt tou te demann pèmèt Egliz Katolik la pou ouvri ekòl ak diffizyon pwogram religyè, tankou spesyalis Vatikan Federico Lombardi te di pandan yon konfèrens pres a Havanna. Pou kounye a, gouvènman Kibèn pa reponn ofisyèlman sou demann sa yo.

article_content: Nakoula Basseley Nakoula, the man connected to the inflammatory short film 'Innocence of Muslims,' was denied bail by a California judge after being arrested for violating his probation. Judge Suzanne Segal ruled that Nakoula had engaged in a persistent pattern of deception, misleading both his probation officers and the court. During the hearing, he gave conflicting responses when asked his name—first saying 'Mark Basseley Yousseff,' then 'Mark Basseley'—despite court records indicating he has used at least 17 aliases over the years. He is most widely known as Nakoula, though he once publicly claimed to be 'Sam Bacile,' a fictional identity portraying him as an Israeli-American real estate developer funded by Jewish donors—a claim later disproven by Israeli officials. His defense attorney, Steve Seiden, requested a $10,000 bond, asserting that Nakoula had remained compliant with probation requirements since his 2010 conviction for bank fraud and had never attempted to flee. Seiden also warned that incarcerating Nakoula in the Metropolitan Detention Center in Los Angeles could endanger his life due to the high population of Muslim inmates and the global outrage sparked by the film. However, Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert Dugdale argued that Nakoula had repeatedly broken probation rules, including using fake names to secure a passport and during the film’s production. He also noted Nakoula had failed to pay nearly $800,000 in court-ordered restitution despite having the financial resources to fund the film, raising serious concerns about his potential to flee. Judge Segal cited Nakoula’s unstable living and employment history, his violation of probation restrictions banning internet access and alias use, and his history of deceit as key reasons for denying bail. Though prosecutors assured the court Nakoula would be placed in protective custody if detained, the judge emphasized that his credibility had been permanently compromised. She scheduled a future hearing to determine his true legal identity and set a date for probation revocation proceedings. Moments after the hearing, Nakoula was transported under heavy guard by U.S. Marshals to the detention center. The film, originally posted on YouTube and later amplified by Egyptian media, ignited deadly protests across the Middle East and North Africa—including attacks on U.S. embassies in Egypt, Yemen, Tunisia, Morocco, Sudan, Iran, Iraq, Israel, and the Palestinian territories. Chechnya subsequently banned the film, declaring it extremist and a threat to regional stability. Meanwhile, Nakoula remained secluded in his home in Cerritos, California. Former crew members revealed they were misled: one recalled him as 'Sam Bassil,' another noted the name 'Abenob Nakoula Bassely' on SAG paperwork. Public records confirmed that Abenob B. Nakoula lived at the same address as Nakoula Basseley Nakoula, underscoring a deliberate effort to obscure his identity.
translated_content: Nakoula Basseley Nakoula, moun ki te konekte ak fim kout 'Innocence of Muslims,' te refize bay kòd pa yon jij Kalifòniyen aprè li te areste pou violasyon probasyon li. Jij Suzanne Segal te deklare ke Nakoula te fè yon patern persistan de deyisyon, dekètman jeneral yo ak ofisye probasyon li. Pendant asezan an, li te reponn konfizion an lè li te demann non li—dabò di 'Mark Basseley Yousseff,' pita 'Mark Basseley'—malgre dòkiman kòt ki montre li te itilize toujou piti piti 17 aliyaz yo. Li pi konn ak non Nakoula, men li te pataje yon identite fe yo tankou 'Sam Bacile,' yon identite fe ki te prezante li tankou yon devlopè immobyèl Israelyen-Ameriken finansye pa donatè Zho, yon klam ki te prouvè pa ofisyèl Israelyen. Avoka defans li, Steve Seiden, te demann yon kòd $10,000, te anndan ke Nakoula te kontinye respekte kondisyon probasyon li depi kònviksyon li nan 2010 pou fraid ak li pa janm eseye fèt. Seiden tou te alarme ke enprisonman Nakoula nan Metropolitan Detention Center nan Los Angeles ka mete l an danje a cause de popilasyon fòm yo nan moun Muslim ak koler global ki te soulevé pa fim an. Menm tan an, avoka fèderèl Robert Dugdale te argumente ke Nakoula te vyolette kondisyon probasyon an plizyè fwa, tankou itilizasyon nòm fe pou jwenn yon paspò ak pandan prodiksyon fim an. Li tou te pwospe ke Nakoula pa t peye $800,000 yo sou remboursman kòt la malgre li te gen resous finansyè pou finanse fim an, sa ki leve inquietid sou posibilite l fèt. Jij Segal te cite historik rezidan ak travay instabil Nakoula, violasyon kondisyon probasyon ki interdi akse ak internet ak itilizasyon aliyaz, ak historik deyisyon li kòm fason pou refize kòd la. Malgre ke prosekisyon te asire jij ke Nakoula ta pral mete nan kouti protèksyon si li te enprisonne, jij te aksente ke kredibilite li te detwò. Li te anndan yon asezan fèt pou determinen non lègèl li ak dat pou asezan revokasyon probasyon an. Momantan aprè asezan an, Nakoula te transporte sou garde lourde pa U.S. Marshals pou enprisonman an. Fim an, ki te posté sou YouTube epi ki te anplifye pa medya Egipsyen, te soulevé protest fatale akròs Medyèn Oryantal ak Afrik Kòrèn—tankou atak sou misyon diplomatik Ameriken nan Egips, Yeman, Tnis, Marok, Soudan, Iran, Irak, Israël ak teritoir Pandalestin. Chechen te proskri fim an, deklare l ekstremis ak yon menas pou stabilite rejyon an. Menm tan an, Nakoula te rete kache nan kay li nan Cerritos, Kalifòni. Membè ekipaj ki te travay avèk li te revele yo te dekètman: yon te konnen l tankou 'Sam Bassil,' lòt te sonje non 'Abenob Nakoula Bassely' sou dokument SAG. Rechèch dòkiman publik te konfirme ke Abenob B. Nakoula te rezide nan menm adrese ak Nakoula Basseley Nakoula, ki montre yon efò deliberé pou kache identite li.

article_content: Carly Fleischmann spent much of her childhood unable to speak or move with precision, trapped inside a body that refused to express her vibrant mind. Diagnosed with severe autism at age two, she was a mystery—even to her own family. Who was she? What did she think? Could she ever find her voice? All that changed one day during therapy. Feeling unwell and unable to speak, Carly reached for the keyboard and typed: 'Help teeth hurt.' That simple phrase became the key to unlocking her world. When the first iPad launched in the U.S., just after her 15th birthday, her family rushed from Toronto to buy one. For Carly, it wasn’t just a gadget—it was freedom. Previous communication devices like the Lightwriter and DynaVox felt clinical and stigmatizing. 'They made me look disabled,' she told her parents. 'I’m not disabled—I’m a kid with autism.' With the iPad and the ProLoQuo2Go app, Carly gained a voice. She cracked jokes about her brother’s smell, shared her love of pop culture, and even argued with classmates—all without saying a word aloud. The app, though costly at nearly $200, gave her control, speed, and dignity. Now with two iPads and a laptop, Carly uses technology to attend school, connect with friends via phone calls (using ProLoQuo2Go, a dialer attachment, and a speakerphone), and post online. Her father, Arthur, says she dreams of going to UCLA and earning a degree—maybe even a doctorate like her hero, Temple Grandin. Celebrities like Ellen DeGeneres and Senator John Kerry have taken notice. At a recent panel, Carly declared: 'Technology is the key to unlocking autism.' For her, it’s not about curing her—it’s about giving her the tools to be heard, seen, and understood on her own terms.
translated_content: Karli Fleischmann te pase plis pòt enfan li an kounye a pa kapab pale oswa move avèk presizyon, emprisonnè nan yon kò ki refize ekspriime lide vi yo. Diagnozike avèk otizm grav a de an, li te yon misteri—menm pou fanmi li. Ki moun li ye? Ki sa li panse? Eske li ka jwenn vo li yon jou? Tout sa te chanje yon jou pendant terapi. Li te santi li mal ak pa kapab pale, Karli te alèt klavye a epi te tape: 'Aid mwen dant mwen fèt.' Fras sa a te vin kle pou ouvri monn li. Kouman premye iPad la te lansman an Etazini, aprè 15an li, fanmi li te alèt nan Toronto pou achte yon. Pou Karli, li pa sèlman yon aparèy—li te libète. Aparèy kominikasyon anvan yo tankou Lightwriter ak DynaVox te santi klìnik ak stigmatisan. 'Yo fè mwen sanse mwen se yon moun disablis,' li te di papa ak manman li. 'Mwen pa se yon moun disablis—mwen se yon timoun ki gen otizm.' Apre iPad la ak aplikasyon ProLoQuo2Go, Karli te jwenn yon vo. Li te fè kominikasyon sou odèr frè li, te pataje afèsyon li pou kilti pop, epi menm kontra ki klas li—tout sa sans pale yon mot. Aplikasyon an, menm si li chè a peyè aproksimativman $200, li te pèmèt li kontwole, rapidite, ak dignite. Apre de iPad ak yon laptop, Karli itilize teknoloji pou al soukòl, konekte avèk zanmi yo atravè apel telefòn (ki itilize ProLoQuo2Go, yon adhesif dial, ak yon telefon anndan), epi mete tout sa sou rezo sosyal. Papa li, Arthur, di li ta vle al nan UCLA epi pran yon diplôm—peut-etre yon doktora konsa li idòl, Temple Grandin. Kèk sitiyatè tankou Ellen DeGeneres ak Sénatè John Kerry te remakè. Nan yon panel reyent, Karli te deklare: 'Teknoloji se kle pou ouvri otizm.' Pou li, sa pa yon kòs pou gueri li—li se pou pèmèt li jwenn outil pou li pale, wè, ak konprann sou kondisyon li.

article_content: In November 2011, three American college students—Derrick Sweeney, Gregory Porter, and Luke Gates—were detained in Cairo after being accused of hurling Molotov cocktails at security forces during violent clashes in Tahrir Square. All three were participating in a semester-long program at the American University in Cairo to strengthen their Arabic skills. While Egyptian authorities claim the students were caught red-handed with homemade firebombs and no identification, their families insist they were simply caught in the chaos of a pro-democracy uprising. Sweeney, a 19-year-old from Missouri, had previously volunteered for President Obama’s 2008 campaign before interning for Republican Congressman Blaine Luetkemeyer earlier that year. His parents describe him as a principled advocate for justice who avoids violence, recalling how he stepped away from protests after witnessing fatal police crackdowns. Luke Gates, the oldest of the trio, shared raw, emotional updates on Twitter, expressing both idealism and despair, including a now-deleted tweet asking if he could renounce his U.S. citizenship online. Gregory Porter, from Pennsylvania, was similarly described by peers as quiet and thoughtful. Video footage from the scene shows the students standing near plastic bottles filled with liquid, but does not conclusively prove they lit or threw them. U.S. universities and the State Department are working closely with Egyptian officials to secure their release, emphasizing that the students were never intended to be participants in violent acts. Their families maintain that the students were inspired by global calls for democracy—not destruction—and were likely swept up in the fervor of the moment.

Tout twa yo te aprann lang arab la nan American University n Kairo. Menm si autorite egipsyen yo pran yo te kapab fèt avèk bòmb konsèy ak pa gen pasepòt, fami yo deklare yo te tout simplement piye nan krasis revolision demokratik la. Sweeney, yon timoun 19 an, ki sòti nan Misouri, te genyen pou kampay Barack Obama nan 2008 avan li te travay pou kongresis repiblikèn Blaine Luetkemeyer ane sa a. Pè ak mè yo dekri li kòm yon advoka presis pou jistis ki refiz vyoans, yo te rapòte kòm li te kite manifestasyon aprè yo te wè krasis polis ki te tue dezan. Luke Gates, pi vye nan trwa yo, te pòte mizik otoral sou Twitter, ki te montre ideyalis ak desesp, yon tweet ki te efase ki te mande si li ka renonsye citoyennete Amerikèn li sou Twitter. Gregory Porter, ki sòti nan Pensilvani, te dekri pa pèsonèl yo kòm yon moun rezève ak senp. Fami yo deklare ke timoun yo te inspiré pa kri pou demokrasi mondyal—pa vyoans—ak te probabman pran nan entousiasm moman an.

article_content: By Leon Watson for MailOnline. It's cheap as chips — the fish and chip shop on the market for just £9,000. Brunshaw Fish and Chips in Burnley, Lancashire, is one of the most affordable businesses of its kind in Britain. The National Federation of Fish Friers calls it an 'absolute bargain,' suggesting it could fetch nearly twice the price — at least £16,000. The owners, siblings Abigail Francioli, 30, and Ben Francioli, 28, decided to sell quickly after the death of their father, Louis, 65, who passed away last month following an 18-month battle with cancer. Their mother, Michaela, 59, supported the business while working full-time and caring for her husband. Originally listed at £16,500 as a going concern, the family lowered the price to £9,000 to facilitate a swift sale. The sale includes all kitchen and dining equipment, a salad bar, and seating for a full-service restaurant. Abigail, who also runs a nursery in Radcliffe, Greater Manchester, said: 'We built this shop from the ground up — transforming an outdated chip shop into a thriving business that increased profits by 400%, generating between £500 and £800 weekly. We loved running it as a family. Dad handled the accounts, Mum helped after work, and Ben and I ran the shop. I’m heartbroken to let it go, but we simply can’t afford the time anymore. We’d love for it to stay a fish and chip shop.' Andrew Crook, treasurer of the National Federation of Fish Friers, added: 'Burnley has changed demographically — fewer residents are traditional fish and chip customers. But this is still an absolute bargain and could be a brilliant start-up for anyone willing to invest the time to revive it.'

Anfòm 16,500 £ kòm yon biznis ki ap fonksyone, fami a te bese pri a pou 9,000 £ pou fasilite yon vand rapid. Vand la pran tout ekipman kichè ak salè, yon bar salade, ak sit pou yon restoran komplè. Men sa a toujou yon bòn afè epi kapab yon bon debi pou kounya ki vle investi tan pou reanime li.'

article_content: By Suzannah Hills. PUBLISHED: 11:07 EST, 12 February 2013. | UPDATED: 14:56 EST, 12 February 2013. An astonishing collection of 30 unique dollhouses from around the world is being auctioned by 89-year-old pensioner Nora Boll, who has spent her life assembling them. Nora Boll was just two years old in 1925 when her mother bought her first dollhouse — a second-hand, joiner-made piece dating to around 1910. That humble start sparked a lifelong passion. Over the decades, Mrs. Boll collected miniature furniture and décor from Japan, Switzerland, Yugoslavia, fairs, junk shops, and gypsy markets during her travels. Among the treasures: tiny chandeliers, silk curtains made from parachute fabric, miniature toilet rolls, and even a toilet brush. One standout piece is a three-tiered dollhouse entirely furnished with Swiss Lundy pieces. Another favorite is a large house purchased from Featonby’s, featuring 1940s-era furniture and parachute-silk curtains, accessible from both front and back. Her collection was interrupted when her mother died at the start of World War II; the family’s belongings were dispersed. Fortunately, her brother preserved the original dollhouse and a box of furniture, which he returned to her after the war. After retiring as a physiotherapist, Mrs. Boll resumed collecting — carefully acquiring each item over time, never able to afford much at once, but always treating every piece with care. The entire collection — including hundreds of miniature furnishings — will be sold in two separate auctions at Anderson & Garland’s Newcastle salerooms. The first auction takes place tomorrow; the second follows in two weeks. Auctioneer John Anderson notes that dollhouse collecting remains a vibrant, niche hobby. 'There’s something of a cult around miniature interiors,' he says. 'People who can’t afford a Grand Designs home can still create one — in miniature.' Some items have sold for more than their life-size counterparts. Alex Kingsley of Anderson & Garland adds, 'This is one of the largest and most globally diverse collections we’ve ever handled — from Japan to Yugoslavia. It’s bizarre, beautiful, and utterly unique.' Mrs. Boll hopes her collection finds a home with fellow enthusiasts or a museum — somewhere it will be cherished as deeply as she cherished collecting it.
translated_content: Pa Suzannah Hills. PUBLIYE: 11:07 EST, 12 fevriye 2013. | JOUNEN: 14:56 EST, 12 fevriye 2013. Yon koleksyon ekstraordinèn ki gen 30 kay poupèt ki diferan yo, ki vini de tout moun an mond lan, ap etre vandu pa yon reyreti 89 an, Nora Boll, ki te pase tout lavi li a kolekte yo. Nora Boll te sèlman de an yo lè mèt li te achte premye kay poupèt li an 1925 — yon pekèt d’okasyon, fèt pa yon karayè ki daté aprè 1910. Sa te demare yon pasyon pou tout lavi li. Pendan dekenn yo, Mme. Boll te kolekte mebli ak dekorasyon piti piti yo nan Japòn, Suis, Yougoslav, fèt, ti ti boutik ak marche gitans pandan viyaj li yo. An antre kous: lanterne piti piti, drapo silke fèt avèk tish pòt, rolyon piti piti, epi menm yon bwos toilèt. Yon pekèt ki sòti anndan se yon kay poupèt twa nivo ki tout fèt avèk mebli Swiss Lundy. Yon lòt pekèt ki pi fèy li se yon gwo kay ki te achte nan Featonby’s, ki gen mebli anndan ane 1940 ak drapo fèt avèk tish pòt, ki ouvri anvan ak arye. Koleksyon li te arrete lè mèt li te mouri nan debi Dezyèm Guèr Mondyal; bagay fami li te dispèse. Malgre sa, frè li te konserve kay poupèt la ak yon kafè mebli, ki te retounen an lavi li aprè guèr la. Aprè reyret la, Mme. Boll te rekomanse kolekte a — achte chak pekèt pa piti piti, pa janm kapab achte anpil a menm tan, men toujou trimete chak bagay avèk timoun ak respe. Tout koleksyon an — tankou sèn nan mebli piti piti yo — ap etre vandu nan de vandès diferan nan saleroom Anderson & Garland nan Newcastle. 'Gen yon kilti ki entouren kay poupèt piti piti,' li di. 'Moun ki pa kapab achte yon maison Grand Designs ka toujou fèt yonn nan piti piti.' article_content: SpaceX has announced that Starlink’s Direct to Cell service will begin rolling out in 2024, offering text messaging via satellite to users in remote areas. Voice and data capabilities are planned for 2025, with full integration of IoT devices using LTE standards expected next year. According to SpaceX’s official website, the service will work with existing LTE-enabled smartphones—no new hardware, software, or apps required. The goal is to eliminate communication dead zones and provide peace of mind when users need connectivity most. To launch the service, SpaceX must first receive approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). The company submitted its request in December 2023, proposing to use approximately 2,000 of its Gen 2 satellites. As stated by SpaceX senior regulatory engineer Kyle Wesson, full global coverage between +58° and -58° latitude is projected by mid-2024, with 80 to 100 satellites dedicated to serving the contiguous United States, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, and select remote corridors in Alaska. This initiative builds on a partnership announced in August 2022 between SpaceX and T-Mobile. At a live event that month, both companies confirmed their collaboration to bring cellular service to underserved regions. T-Mobile CEO Mike Sievert described the alliance as a transformative effort to redefine connectivity, calling it 'an industry-shaking innovation' that challenges traditional telecom models. Other players are entering the space: Apple introduced an Emergency SOS feature via satellite in 2022 for iPhone 14 and later models, enabling users to send location data and brief messages during crises. Meanwhile, AT&T-backed AST Space Mobile successfully completed its first 5G satellite call on September 8, 2023. Originally slated for a 2023 rollout, AST Space Mobile’s consumer service has been delayed into 2024 due to supply chain constraints.
translated_content: SpaceX te anonsye ke serivis Direct to Cell Starlink ta kòmanse pou mete an mache an 2024, pou pèmèt enmèt tèks atravè satelit pou itilizatè yo nan zòn elijib. Kapasite vwa ak donnè yo ta plan pou 2025, ak integrasyon total devès IoT ki itilize norme LTE ta espere an nèt ane. Selon sit web oficial SpaceX, serivis saa ta travay avèk telefòn LTE egzisantan—pa gen beswen nouvo aparèy, logisiel, oswa aplikasyon. Pou kòmanse serivis saa, SpaceX dwe resevwa aprobasyon depi Federal Communications Commission (FCC). Kompani a te soumèt demann li an Desem 2023, propozan itilizasyon enviròn 2,000 satelit Gen 2 li yo. Kòm Kyle Wesson, jeniyè règlatè SpaceX te di, kouvètij global ant +58° ak -58° latitid ta projete pou mitan 2024, ak 80 a 100 satelit rezève pou sèvi kontinèt Etazini, Hawaii, Porto Riko, ak kèk kòridòr elijib nan Alaska. Initiativ saa ta baz sou yon alians anonsye an Aout 2022 ant SpaceX ak T-Mobile. An lè evenman live sa a, de kompani yo te konfime kolaborasyon yo pou pèmèt senkèl la nan zòn ki pa sèvi. Pèfèk T-Mobile Mike Sievert te dekri alians saa kòm yon efò transformatif pou redefini koneksyon an, rele li 'yon inovasyon ki fè yon chanjman nan endistri a' ki defi yon modèl tradisyonèl telekom. Autre aktè yo enterèn nan espas sa a: Apple te introdwi yon fonksyon Emergency SOS atravè satelit an 2022 pou iPhone 14 ak modèl ki pi reyent, pou pèmèt itilizatè yo envwaye lokasyon yo ak mesaj kout nan tan kriz. Menm tan an, AST Space Mobile, ki finansye pa AT&T, te reyalize premye apèl 5G atravè satelit li an 8 Setanm 2023. Orijinalman planifik pou mache an 2023, serivis konsumatè AST Space Mobile te reta arive an 2024 poulèt pwoblèm katèn aprovizyon.
