article_content: Supermodel Gisele Bundchen has used her blog to advocate for natural childbirth. The 32-year-old, who is expecting her second child with NFL star Tom Brady, published a new blog post supporting a woman’s right to a drug-free labor. The post, written by midwife Mayra Calvette—who previously spoke on behalf of the 5-foot-11-inch model—titled 'Gentle Birth: This Is The Way!', highlights a woman’s decision to give birth at home under the care of doulas, midwives, and obstetric nurses. The blog post, published on Blog.giselebundchen.com, was inspired by a recent ban issued by the Regional Council of Medicine of Rio de Janeiro, which prohibited obstetricians from assisting in home births and restricted the use of doulas and midwives during hospital deliveries. Calvette, who was present during Bundchen’s delivery of her first child, Benjamin Rein Brady, in December 2009, wrote: 'These resolutions disregard the most current scientific evidence, the recommendations of the WHO and the Ministry of Health. Furthermore, they fail to respect the right to freedom of choice for women, families, and healthcare professionals.' Calvette, an advocate for the home birth movement, draws on her research from the 'Birth Around the World Project,' which included visits to England, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Sweden, and New Zealand. She observed that the most socially developed countries tend to provide humane, woman-centered maternity care. 'Pregnant women have the right to choose their companions during childbirth, to remain in the same room for labor, birth, and postpartum, and to decline any procedure affecting them or their baby,' she wrote. Bundchen herself wrote on her blog in January: 'When Mayra told me her idea about the project, I thought it was a beautiful concept and knew it would be powerful to share her journey on my blog. I experienced the natural process of birth, and it was one of the most life-changing and deeply special moments of my life.' Miranda Kerr also sparked public attention last month after telling Harper’s Bazaar UK that she declined epidural anesthesia when giving birth to her son Flynn in 2011. The 29-year-old Victoria’s Secret model said she chose natural birth after watching videos showing newborns instinctively seeking the breast without medication. Her decision ignited debate online, including skepticism from some mothers, such as one comment on TheStir.com: 'Being a supermodel doesn’t make you an expert.'
translated_content: Supermodèl Gisele Bundchen te itilize blog la pou avoka pou akouchman nati. Modèl 32 an sa a, ki ap attenden dezyèm timoun li ak NFL star Tom Brady, te pwoblime yon nòt nouvo sou blog la ki soutenn droit fanm yo pou fè yon akouchman sans medikaman. Nòt sa a, ekri pa yon mwayenn Mayra Calvette—ki te pwoche modèl 5 pied 11 col la nan pwojè avan, titile 'Accouchman Doux: Se Menm Sa a!', montre decizyon yon fanm pou akouché nan kay la avèk aji, mwayenn ak infimyè obstetrik. Nòt sa a, ki te piblie sou Blog.giselebundchen.com, te inspiré pa yon interdiksyon reyis la pa Konsey Rejonal Medisin Rio de Janeiro, ki te defèn akilite obstetrisyen yo nan akouchman nan kay la ak limiti itilizasyon aji ak mwayenn nan akouchman nan hopital. Calvette, ki te prezan lè akouchman premye timoun li, Benjamin Rein Brady, desanm 2009, ekri: 'Rezolisyon sa yo pa respekte evidans syantifik ki pi reyis yo, rekòmandasyon OMS ak Ministè Santé. Anplis, yo pa respekte droit a libète chwa pou fanm, fami ak profesyonèl santé yo.' Calvette, yon advokat pou moviman akouchman nan kay la, sipoze sou rechèch li nan 'Pwojè Accouchman An Toute Monn,' ki te enkliz travèl la nan Angleter, Almay, Nederlan, Awstri, Sved, ak Nvel Zeland. Li te remare ke peyi ki pi sosyalman devlope yo te plis sanse konsèv yon sovwa ak akouchman ki sentre fèm. 'Fanm enceyante gen droit pou chwazi konpani yo nan tan akouchman, deme nan menm piyès lan pou travay, akouchman ak post-partòm, ak refize tout prosedi ki afekte yo oswa timoun yo,' li ekri. Bundchen menm te ekri sou blog li janvye: 'Kounye a Mayra te konte m sou ide li sou pwojè sa a, m te pense se yon idèe bèl ak m te konnen se ta kapab pwovokatif pou partaje jounen li sou blog mwen. M te gen oportunite pou viv proses nati akouchman an, epi se te yon nan eksperyans ki pi chanje vèy ak pi espesyal mwen te viv.' Miranda Kerr te fèt vètè lan mwa pase lè li te di Harper’s Bazaar UK li te refize anesthési epidural lè li te akouché fils li, Flynn, an 2011. Modèl 29 an Victoria’s Secret sa a te di li te chwazi akouchman nati lè li te wè videyo ki montre nenfèt yo al direkteman pou sezi tèt mè yo san medikaman. Dekizyon li te debatè lèn an, yon mè nan yon kòmantè sou TheStir.com: 'Etre yon supermodèl pa fè ou yon ekspè.'

article_content: On the evening of May 25, 2012, a masked gunman wearing a balaclava entered the Cotton Tree pub in Manchester’s Droylsden district during a 60th birthday celebration and opened fire near a pool table, killing 23-year-old Mark Short. Three other men—aged 25, 26, and 29—sustained non-life-threatening gunshot wounds to the legs and lower back and were hospitalized. Around 20 to 30 people were present at the private gathering. Greater Manchester Police believe the attack was targeted, not random, and confirmed that all individuals involved were known to law enforcement. The suspect escaped in a Ford Focus, later found abandoned and on fire in Hattersley. Chief Superintendent Nick Adderley and Assistant Chief Constable Garry Shewan stressed that the motive is still under investigation but urged anyone with information—no matter how small—to contact authorities anonymously via 101 or Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111. Nearby resident John Aldridge, owner of a barber shop next door for 29 years, temporarily shut down his business during the forensic investigation. An 84-year-old neighbor said he planned to relocate due to safety concerns. Heartfelt floral tributes left at the scene included messages like 'Rest in peace, Mark' and 'May you have a bed in heaven.' Police have increased patrols and are actively seeking public help.

Twa lòt moun—25, 26, ak 29 an—te resevwa boulèt nan jèn ak kòb yo, epi yo te envite nan hopital; lès yo te serye, men pa te vivan. Ant 20 ak 30 moun te la nan fèt privè a. Pwolès Manchester Grand te konfime ke atak lan te targeted, pa random, ak tout viktim yo te konn yo pa pwolès. Moun ki te fèt li te fèt nan yon Ford Focus ki te jwenn an flamm nan Hattersley. Kèf Sipèrintandan Nick Adderley ak Assistan Kèf Shewan te deklare ke motif lan pa konnen anko, men yo te pran pou yon moun ki gen anyen pou di—menm si sa ta piti piti—apelen 101 oswa Crimestoppers nan 0800 555 111. John Aldridge, ki ran yon barbiyè ki gen 29 an nan peyis la, te fèm magazin li pou jou a pandan enspeksyon yo te fèt. Yon vye moun 84 an te di li ta pote deplase l pou safeti a. Pwodui fèt yo te lave sou zòn la, tankou 'Rest in peace, Mark' ak 'May you have a bed in heaven.' Pwolès la te anpliye patwol yo ak chache aksyon publik.

article_content: Dozens of protesters were injured on Sunday when Yemeni security forces opened fire and deployed tear gas during mass anti-government demonstrations, according to witnesses and medical teams. In Sanaa’s Change Square, 11 protesters sustained gunshot wounds, two of whom were in critical condition. 'We were being shot at directly,' said protester Abdullah Kulaibi. 'They weren’t trying to disperse us—they were trying to kill us.' Yemeni officials denied allegations of targeting peaceful demonstrators, stating that at least 20 arrests made that day were followed by releases within hours. An anonymous security official noted that some detainees were freed early due to medical needs after inhaling tear gas. Medical worker Osama Qurashi confirmed that severely affected individuals were transported to nearby hospitals, while others received care at a makeshift clinic set up in Change Square. Meanwhile, in Dhammar province, over 45 protesters were injured by tear gas and baton attacks, per eyewitnesses and local medical staff. Protests have intensified for weeks, with tens of thousands flooding Sanaa’s streets—many of them women. 'Every day the numbers grow. Today, there were more women than men,' said activist Ameera Abdul Jabbar, attributing the surge to Saleh’s recent attacks on female demonstrators. President Saleh, in a Friday speech, condemned women protesters for violating cultural norms by mingling with unrelated men—a remark that provoked widespread anger among activists. As the opposition Joint Meeting Parties sent a delegation to Saudi Arabia for mediation talks, they emphasized they were listening, not negotiating terms. 'Any deal that doesn’t force Saleh out will be rejected,' declared human rights activist Shaef Saboor.

article_content: An 87-year-old Australian man, Alex Fraser, was denied a refund on a $2,900 cruise after canceling due to his sister’s terminal illness — simply because she was over 75. Fraser, a resident of Wollongong, had booked a 16-day Holland America Line cruise departing Sydney on March 2, intended for destinations including Fiji and Vanuatu. Two days before departure, his 81-year-old sister, Jean Docherty, was hospitalized with stomach cancer. She passed away on March 5. Despite paying an additional $200 for Vero Travel Insurance to cover cancellations due to the illness or death of a relative, his claim was rejected. The insurer’s policy defines 'relative' narrowly as an immediate family member under the age of 75. Fraser provided medical documentation proving his sister’s condition, but Vero cited policy wording over personal circumstance. 'Do you think I would sit by the bedside of a stranger watching her die?' Fraser told MailOnline, expressing shock at the decision. Vero acknowledged Docherty was his sister in the ordinary sense but insisted the policy’s legal definition overrides common understanding. Suncorp, Vero’s parent company, confirmed it is reviewing its travel insurance products, stating the case will inform upcoming changes. Fraser, a grandfather of two, said he has yet to receive meaningful resolution despite the company’s promise to discuss the matter.
translated_content: Yon moun 87 an, Alex Fraser, te refizé yon remboursman sou yon tibòt $2,900 aprè li te anlè kruiz la poukisa sè li te malad gravman — tout bonman li te depase 75 an. Fraser, ki rete nan Wollongong, te rezève yon kruiz 16 jou Holland America Line ki te dwe deplase nan Sydney le 2 mars, pou al nan destina syon tankou Fiji ak Vanuatu. De jou avan deplasman an, sè li, Jean Docherty, 81 an, te envite nan hopital pou kansèn estomak la. Li te mouri le 5 mars. Menm si li te peye yon ekstra $200 pou asirans Vero pou kouvri anlèman si yon rlatif te malad oswa mouri, demann li te refizé. Politik asirans an defini 'rlatif' tankou yon memfè fami imedyat ki gen moin ke 75 an. Fraser te pwove yon sertifik medikal ak leta doktè pou prouve etat sè li, men Vero te cite konsèy politik la plis pase sitiyasyon pèsonèl la. 'Ou panse m ta sot la nan lit yon inkonni wè li mouri si li pa te genyen lavi genetik ak mwen?' Fraser te di MailOnline, ekspres li fèk sòti. Vero te konprann Docherty se sè li nan sens oridin, men li te insis sou definisyon lega politik la. Suncorp, paten Vero a, te konfime li ap revidi prodwi asirans kruiz yo, epi kaza sa a pral fèt pou chanjman ki pral vini. Fraser, ki se granpè de moun, te di li pa jwenn rezolisyon mwayen anmenm si kompani a te promèt li diskute kaza a.

article_content: At the 60-minute mark at Villa Park, Aston Villa finally created a clear scoring opportunity. Andreas Weimann headed the ball into the path of Christian Benteke, who steadied himself and unleashed a powerful right-footed strike toward the Holte End. The outcome seemed inevitable — history suggested Liverpool would crack under pressure. But standing between them and defeat was goalkeeper Simon Mignolet. With a swift parry and a commanding punch, he denied Benteke’s thunderous shot. Moments later, when a cross found Weimann’s head again, Mignolet leapt to clear it. Then, on a corner kick, he charged out of his area, bulldozing through attackers to claim the ball — a display of authority rarely seen from him this season. Mignolet, who endured a turbulent campaign — including being benched for the December 15 trip to Old Trafford — delivered a performance that reminded fans why Liverpool signed him. For the first time in months, he looked every bit the No. 1 goalkeeper. Manager Brendan Rodgers praised him effusively: 'He was outstanding. He wasn’t overly tested, but when called upon, he made two brilliant saves. Most importantly, he was dominant, calm, and composed. Benteke is nearly unstoppable in the air, yet Simon won every aerial duel he contested.' Mignolet wasn’t alone. Liverpool’s entire backline held firm under sustained Villa pressure, especially in the second half. Defenders Mamadou Sakho and Martin Skrtel were resolute, while Emre Can — the £10 million summer signing from Bayer Leverkusen — impressed with his poise and physicality against Benteke. Jordan Henderson and Lucas Leiva anchored the midfield with discipline. This result marked a turning point. Liverpool had now kept three consecutive away clean sheets — at Burnley, Sunderland, and Villa — their longest such streak since 2008. It was also their first back-to-back shutouts of the season. After conceding freely in earlier fixtures, this defensive resurgence offers tangible hope. As Rodgers put it, 'The free spirits might just be turning into the mean spirits.'
translated_content: A 60 minit la, nan Villa Park, Aston Villa te fè yon okazyon klè pou mete gwo lavi. Andreas Weimann te pouse boul la nan chemen Christian Benteke, ki te fèmen l epi te ban yon kou dwa fort ak tout fòs la nan direksyon Holte End. Rezilta a te san doub — istwa te montre ke Liverpool ta kapab kraze sib presyon an. Menm, Simon Mignolet, gardyen rete a, te stade ant yo ak defèt la. Avèk yon parèy rapid ak yon pounch dominan, li te refize kou tondan Benteke a. Kèk segond pi deyò, kòm yon kros te rive sou tèt Weimann an, Mignolet te sallì pou leve l. Puis, nan yon kornè, li te kouri deyò de son zòn, vwayaje atravè tout jwenn yo pou pran boul la — yon prestashon ki pa te wè yo nan sa sezon an. Mignolet, ki te pase yon sezon tris — tankou ete anba pou pataj la 15 desanm nan Old Trafford — te fè yon prestashon ki raple fan yo pouki Liverpool te achte li. Pou premye fwa nan mwa yo, li te parèt tankou yon gardyen #1. Enpòtan Brendan Rodgers te aplodi li: 'Li te ekstènman. Li pa te travay tro, men lè li te bezwen, li te fè de sauvegard ki gen tout kalite. Menm jan an, li te dominan, fèn, ak kalm. Benteke se yon jwenn ki pa ka arrete nan lè a, men Simon te gagnye tout kros ki te vini.' Mignolet pa te sèl nan sa a. Tout dèfans Liverpool te reziste sib presyon Aston Villa yo, souvan nan dezyèm miwè a. Dèfans yo Mamadou Sakho ak Martin Skrtel te fò, menm jan ak Emre Can — jwenn ki te achte pou 10 milyon £ nan Bayer Leverkusen — ki te imponen avèk son kalm ak fòs la kontra Benteke. Jordan Henderson ak Lucas Leiva te anplasan milyè a avèk diskiplyn. Rezilta sa a te yon tounen. Liverpool te gen twa net klin chak pataj yo — nan Burnley, Sunderland, ak Villa — se pwochen sa yo te fèt depi 2008. Se toupremye fwa yo te gen de net klin konsekitif sa sezon an. Aprè yo te konsevi anpil nan jwenn yo, rezistans defansif sa a panse yon espwa konsènan. Tankou Rodgers te di, 'Espri lib yo ka vin espri mèt.'

article_content: When Hugh Hefner, now 84, announced his engagement to a 24-year-old former Playmate, many reacted with amusement—or scorn. But beneath the headlines lies a deeper question: Why do we judge older adults who seek love, especially when the partner is much younger? Sociologist Pepper Schwartz argues we shouldn’t reduce such relationships to satire or suspicion. She points out that love doesn’t vanish with age. Take her friend, an 83-year-old widow who, after years of grief, found joy with an 86-year-old man. They travel to Italy, share meals, and support each other—not because they’re young, but because connection matters at every stage of life. Then there’s Ray and Gail: he’s in his 80s, she’s in her 50s, married for over 15 years, and volunteering for dental missions in Africa. Their bond defies stereotypes. Research backs this up too: in the UK, the percentage of women marrying younger men nearly doubled between 1963 and 1998. While Hefner’s situation invites curiosity, Schwartz reminds us he’s not the standard—we shouldn’t let his celebrity define what’s normal or acceptable. Cohabitation may be simpler, especially for older couples concerned about finances or inheritance. But marriage still carries something unique: a public declaration of commitment, backed by legal rights and social recognition. If someone at 84 wants to say 'I do'—just like they would have at 34—why shouldn’t they? Love isn’t bound by birth certificates. What matters is whether it brings dignity, comfort, and mutual care. And that’s something no age limit can take away.
translated_content: Kèk moun te reyajye oswa te konsidere kòm fòl pandan Hugh Hefner, ki gen 84 an, te anonsé fiançay la avèk yon moun ki gen 24 an ki te yon ancien Playmate. Men, anndan sa ki te di, gen yon lide pi fon: poukisa nou jije moun ki pi vye ki chache lamou, espesyalman si pòtè a se plis jeun? Sociolog Pepper Schwartz pale ke nou pa dwe redui relasyon sa yo a yon komedi oswa yon sospe. Li reyèlman montre ke lamou pa disparèt avèk aj. Paremèt yon zanmi li, yon veve ki gen 83 an ki, aprè de ane de deyè, te truve jouvans ak yon moun ki gen 86 an. Yo voyaje nan Itali, manger ensemble, epi soutenni lòt la—pa paske yo jeun, men paske konèksyon an enpòtan a tout aj. Epi gen Ray ak Gail: li gen 80-an, li gen 50-an, marié depi plis pase 15 an, epi yo fè travay dentèr kariyè nan Afrik. Bond la defi tout stereotip. Rechèch la tou verifye sa a: an Angleter, pwospan moun ki fèm ki mariye moun ki pi jeun te doublé ant 1963 ak 1998. Menm si sitiyasyon Hefner an rele atansyon, Schwartz pa t’ap di li se modèl la—nou pa dwe lafè kouti li pou define sa ki norma oswa akseptab. Kòbaj pa nesesèman pi senp, espesyalman pou moun ki pi vye ki konsène finans yo oswa inheritans yo. Men mariaj la toujou gen yon bagay ki enpòtan: yon deklarasyon publik de komitmàn, avèk dwa lejal ak rekonisman sosyal. Si yon moun ki gen 84 an vle di 'Mwen pran ou'—tankou li ta dwe fè a 34 an—poukisa pa? Lamou pa limité pa akt na nès. Sa ki enpòtan se si li ap apòte dignite, konfort, ak kare ak moun lòt la. Esa se bagay ki pa gen aj ki ka pran.

article_content: (CNN) — Mitt Romney won the Republican caucuses in Washington state, according to unofficial results released early Sunday, giving the former Massachusetts governor a boost heading into the Super Tuesday contests. With 99% of the vote counted, Romney led with 38%. Texas Representative Ron Paul followed with 25%, former Pennsylvania Senator Rick Santorum with 24%, and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich at 10%. A total of 40 delegates were at stake. ‘We’re in a strong second place, but the good news is we’re making excellent progress in securing delegates,’ Paul told supporters in Seattle, as roughly half the votes had been counted. ‘The enthusiasm for the cause of liberty continues to grow exponentially.’ Washington’s caucuses occurred just three days before Super Tuesday, when 10 states held primaries and caucuses. All four major GOP presidential candidates campaigned extensively in the state, hoping a strong showing would carry momentum forward. State GOP chairman Kirby Wilbur predicted a large turnout and estimated that between 500 and 1,500 voters were turned away in Kennewick due to overcrowding. ‘The leadership may have been unprepared for the surge, but I don’t know what else they could have done—after all, they rented the largest facility in the county,’ he said. Even as caucuses began Saturday in Washington, attention shifted toward Super Tuesday states. Romney campaigned in Cincinnati, attacking President Barack Obama. ‘He’s out of ideas. He’s out of excuses. And in 2012, we’re going to make sure he’s out of a job,’ he told a cheering crowd. Romney had already secured victories in Arizona, Wyoming, and Michigan earlier in the week. His win in Washington marked his eighth victory of the election cycle. Santorum campaigned in Blue Ash, Ohio, saying: ‘This was the industrial heartland of the country. Now, people call it the Rust Belt. Once I eliminate the corporate tax for manufacturers—cutting it to zero—we’ll turn this into the Stainless-Steel Belt across America.’ In the days leading up to the caucuses, all four candidates traveled to the Pacific Northwest. ‘This is the first time in recent memory that any GOP presidential candidate has paid attention to us—and my memory goes back to the 1970s,’ Wilbur said. ‘We used to be the ugly sister invited to the dance, but no one asked to dance. Now, we’re the princess.’ Wilbur noted that Washington’s caucuses had traditionally taken place after Super Tuesday, when the nomination race was often already decided. Santorum, speaking in Pasco on Thursday, declared: ‘You are the voice that will speak very loudly before Super Tuesday and lift this race to a whole other level.’ Romney, who campaigned in Washington on Friday, echoed the sentiment: ‘There are many states deciding on Tuesday, but you are first—so your voice will be heard,’ he said at a rally in Bellevue. Paul had visited Washington twice in the prior weeks and ran campaign ads there, as did Gingrich, who toured the state the previous week. The caucuses were open, allowing independents and Democrats to participate. While some smaller meetings were held in private homes, most gatherings took place in public venues like schools and served multiple precincts. In addition to selecting delegates, participants voted in a nonbinding presidential preference straw poll. Although delegates to the GOP convention in Tampa, Florida, will be officially allocated through later rounds of voting this spring, major news outlets—including CNN—will estimate proportional delegate allocations based on Saturday’s straw poll results. The Washington State GOP projected 40,000 to 60,000 participants, a significant increase from the 12,616 who took part in the 2008 Republican caucuses. Four years earlier, a Republican primary had drawn around half a million voters.

Santorum, ki te pale nan Pasco jeudi, te deklare: ‘Ou se vo a ki pral pale trè fò avan Super Tuesday epi remete konsènman sa a sou yon lòt nivo.’ Romney, ki te kampanye nan Washington divè, te reperyèt menm ide a: ‘Yon kantite etaz pral fè desizyon yo mardi, men ou se premyè yo—donk vo ou pral entandi,’ li te di nan yon rassembleman nan Bellevue. Paul te al nan Washington de fwa nan dènye de wèn ak li te fè ad kampanye la, tankou Gingrich, ki te fè yon tournè nan etaz la la semèn anvan. Konsènman yo te ouvri, pèmèt moun ki pa Repiblikèn ak Demokrat yo te voté. Menm si kèk mèt ki ti yo te fèt nan kay privè, plis yo te fèt nan endirik kominèl tankou ekòl ak te sèvi plizyè sekter. Anplis pou chwazi delegè, moun yo te voté nan yon sonaj pou prefèrens presidansyèl ki pa bindan. Menm si delegè pou kongres Repiblikèn nan Tampa, Florid, pral dekide nan lòt etap ki pral fèt printan sa, revi yo tankou CNN pral fè estima pwoporsyonèl delegè yo baz sou rezilta sonaj sa a samedi. GA Washington te antevwa 40,000 ak 60,000 moun ki pral participè, yon kantite ki pi enpotan ke 12,616 ki te participé nan konsènman Repiblikèn 2008. Anvan, yon primè Repiblikèn te te gen envi miyèm moun ki te voté.

article_content: After months of silence following a controversial ruling, English golfer Simon Dyson has returned to competitive play at the Abu Dhabi Championship — and says the golf community has embraced him without hesitation. Dyson, 36, had been suspended after a panel determined he briefly touched down a spike mark on the green during the BMW Masters in China last October, a move interpreted as gaining an unfair advantage on his putting line. Though he faced disqualification and a two-month suspended ban along with a fine, the tribunal accepted his claim that the act was an impulsive mistake, not a calculated attempt to cheat. Dyson described the aftermath as unexpectedly uplifting. 'I couldn’t have asked for better support,' he said. 'Every single player I’ve talked to has been nothing but kind. No judgment, no cold shoulders — just camaraderie.' His teammate Rory McIlroy reinforced that sentiment by walking over and giving him a warm hug on the practice range. For Dyson, the incident served as a wake-up call. He admitted he’d grown disconnected from the game over the past few years, losing the joy that once drove him. 'It took nearly losing everything to remind me how much I love this sport,' he shared. Now, he says, he’s more focused than ever — determined to climb back into the world’s top 50 and play with integrity. Meanwhile, Sweden’s Henrik Stenson, currently ranked third in the world, is also competing in Abu Dhabi. A consistent performer in the event since its inception in 2006, Stenson has yet to win it — despite claiming titles in Dubai, Qatar, and the Desert Classic. With his eyes set on the upcoming Ryder Cup at Gleneagles, he plans to arrive early to adjust to the course and shake off jet lag, hoping to reconnect with a venue he hasn’t played since 2004. His remarkable 2013 season, which included winning both the FedEx Cup and Race to Dubai, has already secured his spot on Team Europe, giving him the luxury of planning ahead. Other notable names in the field include Phil Mickelson and Martin Kaymer, both preparing for their 2014 campaigns. Dyson will tee off alongside English veteran Mark Foster and Scottish rookie Jamie McLeary. For all of them, the Abu Dhabi Championship marks the start of a fresh chapter — whether it’s redemption, renewal, or simply chasing another trophy.

article_content:
CNN) — 'Two professors, both alike in dignity, in fair Geneva where we lay our scene.' When it is finally written, the story of one of the greatest scientific discoveries of our age may begin something like this. Last month, two eminent professors — Peter Higgs and François Englert — were jointly awarded one of science’s greatest honors: the Nobel Prize in Physics. The award followed the dramatic announcement last year that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), based in Geneva, had definitively confirmed the existence of a new particle: the Higgs boson. Physicists around the world rejoiced — some even wept openly. Years of speculation, theory, and research had suddenly been validated. In typical Scandinavian understatement, Staffan Normark, Permanent Secretary of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, said, 'This year’s prize is about something small that makes all the difference.'

The discovery filled a major gap in the Standard Model of physics — often called a 'theory of almost everything' — by explaining why fundamental particles have mass. With this, scientists gained a key to understanding the 4% of the universe made of ordinary matter — and perhaps, eventually, clues to the remaining 96%, composed of dark matter and dark energy.

Yet as one set of answers emerged, new questions arose. CNN Labs spoke with leading physicists about what the Higgs discovery means — and what remains unknown.

Joel Butler, a scientist at Fermilab in Illinois, said: 'The big question is why the Higgs particle, with a mass more than 100 times that of the proton, is so light. That question isn’t answered by our current model of the universe.'

Jon Butterworth, Head of Physics and Astronomy at University College London, noted: 'Issues like: What is dark matter? And why is the universe mostly matter and not antimatter?' 

Hitoshi Murayama, a professor of physics at UC Berkeley, added: 'We’ve never observed an elementary particle without spin — electrons, quarks, photons all have spin. The Higgs boson may have spin, but perhaps it’s spinning in extra spatial dimensions we cannot perceive. We must determine its true nature.'

To answer these questions, the LHC will soon be complemented by another massive facility: the International Linear Collider (ILC). Like the LHC, the ILC would stretch for miles underground. Its location has not yet been decided.

History shows that breakthroughs in physics often come from advanced instrumentation — from Marie Curie’s ionization chamber, to cathode ray tubes that revealed the electron, to Geiger counters and, most recently, the LHC. The ILC represents the next step in this tradition.

Tim Meyer, Head of Strategic Planning and Communications at TRIUMF, Canada’s national laboratory for particle and nuclear physics, explained: 'The ILC will produce far more Higgs bosons than the LHC and measure their properties with unprecedented precision — up to 3% relative uncertainty, compared to the LHC’s 25%. It could truly ‘crack open’ the Higgs and reveal secrets of nature’s first spin-zero particle.'

Brian Foster, European Regional Director for the International Linear Collider, said: 'If we’re lucky, the ILC could detect an entirely new class of particles — possibly helping us achieve Einstein’s dream of unifying all physical laws into one elegant, overarching theory.'

A final decision on constructing the ILC is expected by 2015.

CNN) — 'De twòp profè, toujou menm dignite, nan jeniève fair ou nou mete nòt sen.' Kounye a k ap ekri, istwa yon nan plis grand decouvèt syantifik nou an kapab kòm sa. Mwa pase, de profè eminen — Peter Higgs ak François Englert — te resevwa yon nan plis gran onè syans la: Pries Nobel Fizik la. Pries sa a te koumanse aprè anons dramatik lan l’annè pase ke Grand Collisionneur de Hadrons (LHC), ki sèt nan Jenev, te konfime definitivman eksistans yon nouvo particil: boson Higgs. Fizisyen yo nan tout mond lan te fèt — kèk moun te kriye ouvertman. Anè yo de spikylasyon, teori ak rechèch te validate soudainman. Nan langaj skandinav klasik, Staffan Normark, sekretè peermanan Akademi Rwayal Sved la, te di, 'Pries ane sa a se pou yon bagay ti ki fè tout diferans.'

Decouvèt sa a te plen yon lag maje nan Modele Standa nan fizik la — souvan rele 'teori pou preske tout bagay' — pa ekspike kòman particil fondamantal yo gen mas. Avèk sa, syantifik yo te gagne yon kli pou konprann 4% anndan univers la ki fèt de materi ordinaire — epi pètèt, kli pou 96% ki rest, ki fèt de materi nwa ak enerji nwa.

Menm tan ke yon seri repons te parèt, nouvo kesyon yo te monte. CNN Labs te pale avèk plis grand fizisyen yo sou sa ki vle di decouvèt Higgs la — ak sa ki pa konnen anko.

Joel Butler, yon syantifik nan Fermilab nan Illinois, te di: 'Kesyon maje a se pouki boson Higgs, avèk yon mas ki pi fò pase 100 fwa mas proton an, se si leger. Kesyon sa a pa reponn pa mode nou an nan univers la.'

Jon Butterworth, Direktè Fizik ak Astronomi nan University College London, te remake: 'Pwoblèm tankou: Ki sa ki materi nwa? Ak pouki univers la se preske tout materi, pa antimateri?' 

Hitoshi Murayama, profè fizik nan UC Berkeley, te ajoute: 'Nou pa janm observe yon particil elémentè san espèn — elektron, kwak, fotòn tout gen espèn. Boson Higgs ka gen espèn, men pètèt li tournen nan dimansyon ekstra nou pa kapab wè. Nou dwe konprann natir li reyèl la.'

Pou reponn kesyon sa yo, LHC pral bientot komplimante pa yon lòt fasilite masif: Collideur Linéaire Internasyonal (ILC). Tankou LHC, ILC ta kapab etenn pou milyè nan sou teren. Lokasyon li pa dekide anko.

ISTWA a montre ke revolisyon nan fizik la souvan vini nan instriman avanse — depi kamra ionizasyon Marie Curie, pou tub rayon katod ki te revele elektron an, pou comptè Geiger ak, pi résemman, LHC. ILC reprezante etap swa nan tradisyon sa a.

Tim Meyer, Direktè Planifikasyon Stratèjik ak Komunikasyon nan TRIUMF, laboratwa nasyonal Kanada pou fizik ak nukleyè, te ekspike: 'ILC ta kapab pwodui plis boson Higgs pase LHC epi mezi pwopriyete yo avèk presizyon sans precedent — 3% incity relatif, kouman LHC 25%. Li ta kapab 'kase ouvet' boson Higgs epi revele sekret nouvo natir senk espèn zero a.'

Brian Foster, Direktè Rejyonèl Evropeyen pou Collideur Linéaire Internasyonal, te di: 'Si nou gen sòti, ILC ka detekte yon klas nouvo entyèr de particil — posibman ede nou reyalize reves Einstein nan unite tout teori fizik la an yon teori elegan ak simple.'

Decizyon pou konstriksyon ILC la pral pran nan 2015.

article_content: Fulham’s £11 million signing of Ross McCormack has left many fans and pundits scratching their heads. While the Scottish striker was the Championship’s top scorer last season with 28 goals, the price tag appears steep—especially when compared to other attacking talents signed for similar or lower fees. For the same amount, Tottenham landed Christian Eriksen, a dynamic midfielder now regarded as one of Europe’s brightest young talents. Meanwhile, other striking options offered exceptional value: Michu joined Swansea for just £2 million and exploded onto the Premier League scene with 18 goals in his debut campaign. Rickie Lambert, signed by Liverpool for £4 million, earned an England World Cup call-up after scoring 13 times for Southampton. Christian Benteke, acquired by Aston Villa for £7 million, broke the club’s single-season scoring record with 19 Premier League goals. Jordan Rhodes, bought by Blackburn for £8 million, has consistently delivered, netting over 20 goals in each of his past five full seasons. Even Philippe Coutinho, signed by Liverpool for £8.5 million, impressed with eight goals and creative flair in his first season. Meanwhile, Javier Hernandez, known as ‘Chicharito’, became a fan favorite at Manchester United as a lethal substitute despite never starting regularly. Jay Rodriguez, who scored 15 goals for Burnley before joining Southampton for £6 million, was on track for World Cup selection until a serious knee injury sidelined him. Lukas Podolski and Mario Mandzukic, both signed for £11 million by Arsenal and Bayern Munich respectively, brought elite experience and goal-scoring pedigree—but neither played as a pure center-forward in their new clubs. And while Fulham’s decision looks questionable, there’s a silver lining: McCormack was actually cheaper than Konstantinos Mitroglou, whom the club signed on deadline day for £12.4 million. To put the £11 million fee in perspective: it could have bought three Bugatti Veyron Grand Sport Viteses, nearly 10,000 global cruises, or over 1,300 round-trip Concorde flights between London and New York.

Epi menm si achètman Fulham nan gen yon tan konsiderasyon, gen yon lavi: McCormack te pi piti chè pase Konstantinos Mitroglou, ki te achte pa klèb la sou dènye jou pou 12.4 milyon £. article_content: When the car ahead slows abruptly, a quick honk can feel unavoidable. But for Paul Samara, that instinctive reaction led to a nightmare. After honking at a police van that was driving slowly and stopping repeatedly in front of him, Samara was handcuffed, thrown into a cell, and subjected to fingerprinting, DNA collection, and a mugshot. A 34-year-old train driver with no prior police contact, Samara was accused of abusive and threatening behavior and charged with a public order offense. The incident, which occurred in May in Blackpool after Samara finished his shift at 11 p.m., sparked a six-month ordeal. For months, he lived under the shadow of a potential criminal conviction — fearing it would destroy his career and livelihood. He became anxious and unwell. Samara explained that as a train driver — where horns are used as safety tools due to lack of emergency brakes — honking in response to sudden stops is second nature. He said he did not shout, swear, or roll down his window. He merely told the officer that her driving had forced him to brake hard. The officer, who claimed she was searching for a missing child, reportedly responded: 'When you have a problem, don't come to us — we won't want to know.' Her male colleague then joined her, ordered Samara out of his car, and arrested him. He spent two hours in a cell before being formally charged. A preliminary court hearing was scheduled, but last month, the Crown Prosecution Service dropped the case after reviewing CCTV footage that directly contradicted the officer’s account. The officer later admitted she had lost her temper. Samara’s solicitor, Mark Ellis of James Murray Solicitors, called the prosecution unjustified: 'This case should never have reached court. The CCTV proves he was calm. Yet the CPS pursued it for six months before admitting there was no case.' The CPS stated the charge was initiated by Lancashire Police and that the decision to drop it followed standard review procedures — concluding there was 'no realistic prospect of conviction.' Lancashire Police declined to comment. Samara, now relieved but deeply shaken, said: 'I’m just glad it’s over. But I’ve lost all faith in the police.'
translated_content: Kèk fwa, lè machin ki devan ou ralanti bruskenman, yon kòt bòkèt ka sòti tout natirèlman. Men pou Paul Samara, reyaksyon sa a te konnèt li nan yon nwa. Aprè li te bòkèt sou yon van pòlis ki te mache lent ak fè yon sèl blokaj anndan devan li, Samara te manmè, te miz nan yon sel, ak te pran nimewo imaj yo, DNA yo, ak foto yo. Yon moun ki gen 34 an, konduktè tren ki pa te janm gen anyen avèk pòlis la, Samara te akize dènye ak menas ak te konsidere kòm kriminel pou yon ofans publik. Inciden sa a, ki te pase an Mè, nan Blackpool, aprè Samara te fin travay nan 11p.m., te kreye yon peyizaj ki te dure sis mwa. Pou sis mwa li te viv sou menas yon krimen — ki te fè li peyizé karèy ak livèl la. Li te devni anksyè ak malad. Samara te ekri ke, kòm yon konduktè tren — kote bòkèt yo itilize kòm yon outil sekirite paske yo pa gen yon frein d'emerjans — bòkèt lè yon machin bloke bruskenman se yon reyaksyon natirèl. Li te di li pa te krime, pa te moun, pa te desend fenèt la. Li te sèlman di ofisè a ke mannyè li te kondui te fè li fèmen frein yo. Ofisè a, ki te pran pou konsa li te chache yon timoun dispari, te reponn: 'Lè ou gen yon pwoblèm, pa vini jwenn nou — nou pa vle entèn ou.' Kòlèg li mòn te jwenn li, te deman li sòti nan machin li, ak te arete li. Li te pase de lè a nan sel la avan li te akize. Yon udi premyè te planifi, men dènye mwa, Service Pwosikisyon Kòwn te dekide anlèman kòm rezilta de imaj video ki te kontredi verite ofisè a. Ofisè a te rekonnèt li te pèdi pati a. Avoka Samara, Mark Ellis, nan James Murray Avoka, te di pwosesis sa a te pa dwe pase jwenn kòt la: 'Pwosesis sa a pa dwe te pase jwenn kòt la. Video a montre ke li te kalme. Men CPS te pousi pou sis mwa avan yo te rekonèt ke pa gen okenn kòz.' CPS te deklare ke akizisyon an te initie pa Pòlis Lancashire, ak ke dekizyon an anlèman te fèt selon prosedi standa a — konklizyon an te 'pa gen posibilite realis pou yon kondamnasyon.' Pòlis Lancashire te refize reponn. Samara, ki kounya soufri menm si li te relève, te di: 'Mwen sèlman fèt ke tout sa a fini. Men mwen te pèdi tout fèy pou pòlis la.'

article_content: During the height of the Ferguson unrest, Officer Greg Casem—a 25-year veteran of the Ferguson Police Department—had a raw, emotional confrontation with a young protester he had known since childhood. As flames consumed storefronts and smoke filled the air, Casem, not in full riot gear, stood face-to-face with the man, his voice breaking as he pleaded: 'I’ve known you for a long time, bro… twenty-five years I’ve been here. Twenty-five years!' The protester, also in his 20s, yelled back: 'You’re killing us! We’re not killing y’all—so stop killing us!' Casem gestured toward the ruined streets and asked, 'How are these families gonna eat? How are they gonna get their diapers?' The protester stepped closer, eyes blazing: 'And you’re still killing us.' Casem placed his hand on his chest, overwhelmed. 'Twenty-five years I’ve been here,' he repeated, tears welling. The exchange—captured in photographs released days later—reveals the deeply personal cost of the unrest. Casem, a K-9 officer who once patrolled these same blocks as the boy grew up, now watched his community burn. The riots erupted after a grand jury declined to indict Officer Darren Wilson for the August 9, 2014, fatal shooting of unarmed teen Michael Brown. In the chaos, over 50 people were arrested—including 27 from out of state and one woman from Berlin, Germany. Charges ranged from failure to disperse to felony assault and armed criminal action. Looters set fire to more than a dozen buildings, including a beauty salon and a police car, and shattered windows at City Hall. Casem reportedly knew the protester by sight for decades—but never spoke to him personally. Still, in that moment, history, grief, and rage collided on a broken street in Ferguson.

Vingt-cinq ans !' Le manifestant, lui aussi dans la vingtaine, a crié en retour : 'Yo t'ap tue nou! Nou pa t'ap t'ap tèt ou — alòs arrete t'ap t'ap nou !' Le manifestant s’est approché encore plus, les yeux flamboyants : 'Epi ou toujou t'ap t'ap nou.' Casem a posé la main sur sa poitrine, submergé. 'Vingt-cinq ans que je suis ici,' a-t-il répété, les larmes aux yeux. L’échange — capturé sur des photographies publiées quelques jours plus tard — révèle le coût profondément personnel de cette unrest. Casem, un officier K-9 qui avait autrefois patrouillé ces mêmes rues pendant que l’enfant grandissait, regardait maintenant sa communauté brûler. Les émeutes ont éclaté après qu’un grand jury a refusé d’inculper l’officier Darren Wilson pour le tir fatal du 9 août 2014 contre le adolescent désarmé Michael Brown. Dans le chaos, plus de 50 personnes ont été arrêtées — dont 27 provenant d’autres États et une femme de Berlin, en Allemagne. Les accusations variaient entre défaut de disperser et agression criminelle grave. Des pillards ont mis le feu à plus d’une douzaine de bâtiments, y compris un salon de beauté et une voiture de police, et ont brisé les fenêtres de l’hôtel de ville. Casem connaissait probablement le manifestant de vue depuis des décennies — mais n’a jamais parlé avec lui personnellement. Pourtant, en ce moment-là, l’histoire, la tristesse et la colère se sont heurtées sur une rue détruite à Ferguson.

article_content: If you want to ensure your Christmas cards arrive on time, buying a first-class stamp might seem like the obvious choice. But you could be wasting money, a consumer advocate warned — due to a lesser-known exception in Royal Mail’s delivery targets. Regulated by Ofcom, Royal Mail is required to deliver 93% of first-class mail the next working day. However, this target is suspended between December 2 and December 31. Last year, only half of first-class Christmas cards arrived the next working day — despite Royal Mail meeting its target between April and September. In contrast, second-class mail proved more reliable during the holidays. Ofcom requires Royal Mail to deliver 98.5% of second-class letters within three working days; last Christmas, it achieved 93.1%. Second-class stamps cost 10p less than first-class stamps, which now stand at a record 60p. Robert Hammond, director of postal policy at Consumer Futures, called using second-class postage a 'super-saver tip.' Meanwhile, Royal Mail announced that postal workers will not strike during the entire Christmas trading period — a move that sent its share price to an all-time high of £5.90. That represents an 80% increase since its privatization last month, sparking renewed criticism from MPs who argue the company was sold too cheaply. Bankers involved in the flotation told the Business Select Committee that the threat of industrial action was the primary reason shares were priced at just £3.30. After months of negotiations, Royal Mail and the Communication Workers’ Union reached a deal on pay, pensions, and working conditions. Details remain confidential until approved by CWU leadership and members in a ballot. A Royal Mail spokesperson confirmed: 'There will be no industrial disruption during the ratification process, including the full Christmas trading period.' This year, the final posting dates are: December 18 for second-class, December 20 for first-class, and December 23 for Special Delivery Guaranteed.

Men ou ka pèdi lajan w, yon avokat konsomatè te averti — paske yon eksipsyon ki pa konnen anndan objektif livrezon Royal Mail. Regile pa Ofcom, Royal Mail dwe livri 93% kòd klas 1 nan jounen ki vin aprè. Men, objektif sa a retire ant 2 desanm ak 31 desanm. Anndan lane pase, se sèlman yon sèl sou de kòd klas 1 ki te arive nan jounen ki vin aprè — malgre ke Royal Mail te reyisi objektif li ant avril ak septanm. Kote l, kòd klas 2 te pi fiable pandan sezon Nwèl. Ofcom obligè Royal Mail pou livri 98.5% kòd klas 2 nan twa jounen travay; anndan Nwèl pase, yo te reyisi 93.1%. Timbres klas 2 koûte 10p pi piti ke timbres klas 1 ki maintenan an 60p. Robert Hammond, direktè politik postal nan Consumer Futures, te rele itilizasyon klas 2 yon 'tip ekonomi siper.' Mwenm, Royal Mail te anonsye ke travayè postal yo pa pral fè grèv pandan tout periode Nwèl — yon aksyon ki te pousi kòt yo nan nivo maksimòm 5.90£. Sa a reprezante yon augmantasyon 80% depi privatizasyon lan anndan mwa pase, ki te kouspe kritik reyini de MP ki di ke kompani a te vann trop piti. BANKÈ ki te envolwe nan emisyon an te di Komite Selektif Biznis ke menas grèv la te faktè ki te pi enpotan pou pri a te mete nan 3.30£. Pendant de mwa négosiasyon, Royal Mail ak Union Kominikasyonèl (CWU) te atenn yon ajen sou salè, pensyon ak kondisyon travay. Detay yo pa publiye anndan moun ki pase yo, paske yo dwe validate pa dirijan CWU ak moun yo nan yon votasyon. Yon spesyalis Royal Mail te konfime: 'Pa gen okenn diskripsyon izyèl pandan proses ratifikasyon ajen an, tankou tout periode Nwèl.' Anndan lane sa, daten final pou envoi yo se: 18 desanm pou klas 2, 20 desanm pou klas 1, ak 23 desanm pou Special Delivery Guaranteed.

She claimed these children would be taught to be devoted to Russia and to Putin personally, and that their mothers would receive special state allowances in recognition of their service to the nation. Critics, including journalist Mikhail Klikishin, dismissed it as 'total BS from Ukrainian yellow press.' The Kremlin has long maintained strict privacy around Putin’s personal life, including details about his two daughters and his divorce from wife Lyudmila. Speculation about his relationship with Alina Kabayeva remains unconfirmed. article_content: Lauren Penney, a former escort and make-up artist, has been identified as the woman involved in a confrontation with Sahar Daftary — a former beauty pageant winner — hours before Daftary died after falling 150 feet from a luxury apartment in Salford Quays, Manchester. Daftary, 23, discovered that Penney and her roommate Helen Marshall had been staying in the apartment she shared with her husband, property developer Rashid Jamil. After a heated exchange, Penney and Marshall left the flat. An hour later, Daftary fell to her death. Jamil has consistently maintained that Daftary died by suicide — a claim her family rejects. In 2012, nearly four years after the incident, a coroner recorded an open verdict following a lengthy inquest. Penney, then 28, and Marshall moved into Jamil’s apartment in December 2008, having been introduced to him during a trip to Dubai in 2008. Jamil had previously married Daftary in an Islamic ceremony in December 2007, though he was already married with two children. Daftary moved into the apartment in May 2008 but left after two weeks due to relationship breakdowns. According to Penney’s written statement, read at the inquest, Jamil asked them to leave the flat because he planned to bring Daftary home. When Daftary arrived, she confronted the women angrily. Penney described Jamil as appearing 'embarrassed and sheepish' during the encounter. Jamil was arrested on suspicion of murder but released without charge. Daftary’s family have criticized Greater Manchester Police for what they say was a failure to conduct a thorough investigation.

article_content: In late 2011, BBC Newsnight launched an investigation into longstanding allegations that Sir Jimmy Saville sexually abused teenage girls during the 1970s. The probe followed reports that Surrey Police had received complaints in 2007—nearly four decades after the alleged incidents occurred. Journalists interviewed three women who, as teenagers in Surrey, had encountered Saville during his frequent visits to schools as part of his charitable activities. Each described being taken alone in his car and subjected to inappropriate behavior. One woman, now in her 50s, agreed to speak on camera. The investigation was abruptly halted just days before its scheduled broadcast, coinciding with a planned BBC Boxing Day tribute program hosted by Shane Richie. Senior BBC executives reportedly ordered the story to be suppressed, sparking outrage among Newsnight staff who had spent months working on it. Surrey Police confirmed they had investigated the 2007 complaints but concluded there was insufficient evidence to pursue criminal charges. The Crown Prosecution Service agreed with this assessment. Saville’s family and close associates condemned the investigation. His niece, Janet Humble, called it 'muck-raking,' while longtime friend Stephen Purdew noted that Saville could no longer defend himself. The BBC maintained that the story was dropped solely due to insufficient corroborating evidence—not because of pressure to protect Saville’s legacy. A spokesperson emphasized that not all stories pursued by the BBC are broadcast, and editorial standards dictated the decision.

article_content: Once thought of as Victorian-era ailments straight from a Dickens novel, gout and chilblains are now surging in popularity across Britain. New data reveals a sharp rise in sales of treatments for both conditions, with experts pointing to holiday excesses and harsh winter weather as key culprits. Online pharmacy Chemist Direct reports a 66% spike in CherryFlex sales this January alone—more than the total sold during October, November, and December combined. CherryFlex, derived from cherries rich in antioxidants, is marketed to help reduce uric acid levels, a primary trigger of gout. Last year’s research showed hospital admissions for gout have jumped 80% over the past decade, reaching over 4,400 cases annually. Experts attribute the trend to overindulgence in alcohol and fatty foods during the festive season, which elevate uric acid—a waste product formed when the body breaks down certain foods and drinks. When levels become too high, tiny crystals form in joints, causing intense pain and swelling. 'We believe much of this rise stems from the overindulgence of Christmas and New Year,' says Krishna Soma, Superintendent Pharmacist at Chemist Direct. 'Too much alcohol and rich food raises uric acid. Add in the freezing weather keeping people indoors and inactive, and you’ve got a perfect storm.' Many people don’t realize joint pain could be gout. Historically known as the 'disease of kings'—afflicting monarchs like Henry VIII—it’s now affecting everyday Britons. Meanwhile, cold snaps have driven up demand for chilblains cream. Chilblains—also called erythema perniosis—cause red, itchy, inflamed skin on fingers and toes after rapid warming from extreme cold. Traditionally linked to warming frozen limbs by fireplaces or hot baths, the condition now affects children who play in the snow then rush to radiators. 'People often mistake the burning and itching for simple dry skin,' Soma notes. 'We recommend applying chilblain cream and consulting a GP if symptoms persist or worsen.'

CherryFlex, ki fèt ak ceriz ki rich an antioxydàn, k ap vandè pou ede redui lèvèl akid yrik, yon koz prinsipal gout. Rechèch lan ane pase montre ke entranman pou gout te monte 80% nan dènye dekenn, pou depase 4,400 kaza anlè. Ekspèt yo atribiye tendans sa a pou eksès alkol ak manje gwos nan sezon fèt yo, ki pouse lèvèl akid yrik—yon rezidi ki fòme lè kò a dekompoze manje ak bivri yo. Lè lèvèl yo tèt tro, kristal ti fòme nan jonks, ka kousi doulè ak inflamasyon intens. 'Nou kriye ke plis poul sa a sòti nan eksès fèt Nwel ak Nòd Anmè,' di Krishna Soma, farmasit anresponab Chemist Direct. 'Trop alkol ak manje gwos pouse lèvèl akid yrik. Ajoute yo a tempre fèt ki pèmèt moun yo demen kò yo, epi ou gen yon tempe parfèt.' Plis moun pa konnen ke doulè jonk yo ka gout. Tradisyonèlman konn kòm 'maladi roya', ki afekte monark yo tankou Henri VIII, li k ap afekte britanik yo kote kote. Mwenm, koudèt ki te vin dènye jou yo te pouse vandisman krema chilblains. Chilblains—ki tou konn kòm erythema perniosis—ka kousi peyi rouj, pran, ak inflame sou twa ak manm lè yo sanble tèt aprè eksposisyon ak fèt. Tradisyonèlman li te lye a sanble manm ak twa fèt sou fyèr oswa bagn lan, kondisyon sa a k ap afekte timoun yo ki jwe nan nèj epi yo rentrè anvan yo sanble men yo sou radiatè. 'Moun yo souvan konsidere doulè ak pran sa yo kòm sekou kòm dènye peyi,' di Soma. 'Nou rekomande pou aplike krema chilblains epi ale wè yon medik la si simptom yo kontinye oswa pire.'

article_content: Residents across Northeast England are describing the ongoing bus strike by Go North East as more devastating than the height of the pandemic. Since the walkout began on October 28, thousands have been cut off from vital services — including medical appointments, community centers, and family visits — with many saying they feel trapped in their homes again. Linda Storey, a 71-year-old widow from Gateshead, shared how missing her weekly bereavement group has plunged her back into deep depression. 'I cried every day,' she said. 'This feels worse than lockdown.' At the Old Rectory Community Centre in Houghton-le-Spring, staff report once-bustling rooms now eerily quiet. Volunteers used to welcome walkers from nearby villages, but after a few weeks, even the most determined couldn’t manage a two-hour round trip on foot. 'People are going hungry. They’re lonely. And they’re scared,' said Donna Thomas, a center worker. The dispute stems from a pay disagreement. Drivers rejected a 10.3% raise, arguing that colleagues in the North West earn more for the same work. The Unite union insists its members didn’t choose this path lightly — they say they were pushed into striking by unfair pay gaps. Go North East responded by launching a minimal service, which the union dismissed as inadequate. While commuters are furious, local politicians are divided. Labour MP Emma Lewell-Buck called the pay disparity 'unfair' and said most people understand why drivers are striking. Meanwhile, Conservative councillor Wayne Daley argued the offer was generous and urged both sides to focus on long-term public transport reform, especially now that government funds are shifting away from HS2 toward local transit. Unite’s regional officer Mark Sanderson apologized sincerely to passengers, emphasizing that drivers miss working and want to return — but only if their demands for equal pay are met. With no resolution yet, the strike continues, leaving families, seniors, and workers stranded.

'Sa a pi fò ke lockdown la.' Nan Sennta Old Rectory nan Houghton-le-Spring, ekip yo di sal yo ki te toujou plei, manti ase. Vòlontè yo te akwelmi moun ki te mache nan vila yo, men aprè kèk lè, menm moun ki te pi dètèminé pa kapab fè yon travèl de twa lè nan mache. 'Moun yo ap manje. Yo ap sen. Ak yo ap pey.', di Donna Thomas, yon travayè sennta. Konfli a te konnèk ak diferans salè. Chauffè yo te refize 10.3% augmantasyon, di yo ke kolèg yo nan North West gen plis poul pou menm travay la. Union Unite te rezime ke mèmbr yo pa te chwazi sa a lètman — yo te forse a fè strike pa konsèk enko ekwalite salè a. Mark Sanderson, ofisye rejonal Unite, te deswè moun yo ak sètè, mete ak fòk sou fèt ke chauffè yo manke travay yo ak vle retounen — men se sèlman si deman yo pou salè egal yo te aksepte. article_content: Even though the holiday treats are still fresh in memory, thousands of Britons are already heading to stores to grab the newest fitness DVDs—hoping to shed winter pounds before the year really begins. At £13, it’s perfect for anyone pressed for time but serious about results.

article_content: MUMBAI, India (CNN) — Inside the blacked-out Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, hallways were littered with bloodied bodies. A commando, speaking anonymously, provided details of the operation after Indian Army forces entered the hotel. More than 33 hours after the assault began, terrorists were still holding around 200 hostages. With virtually no information about the hotel’s layout, Indian Army commandos launched a daring nighttime raid — only to be met with relentless gunfire, grenade attacks, and adversaries constantly shifting positions. The sound of gunfire and explosions echoed through the hotel’s atrium, making it nearly impossible to locate the source of fire. Commandos navigated pitch-black corridors, navigating debris and damage without a clear map. At a press conference on Friday, a commando spokesman — his face and hair covered by a black scarf and wearing dark glasses to conceal his identity — recounted the mission. He said the battle reached its climax at 6:30 a.m. Friday, when commandos stormed the room holding the hostages. When the gunfire ceased, the elite unit — known as the Black Cats — entered the room and rescued all 200 hostages. 'We didn’t know the layout of the hotel,' the commando told reporters. 'Only one hotel staff member guided us.' They entered the building blind — unsure of the number of attackers, the weapons they carried, or whether explosives were rigged throughout. 'We heard gunshots on the second floor and rushed toward them,' he said. 'Behind cover, we found 30 to 50 bodies. Then we came under fire. The moment they saw us, they threw grenades.' When the shooting paused, the commandos advanced toward the gunfire — but the terrorists had vanished. Their movements suggested intimate knowledge of the hotel’s structure. Survivors reported that the building’s large dome and open atrium amplified sounds, making it impossible to track shooter locations. In the darkness, commandos couldn’t determine how many terrorists remained — or whether a few were moving between floors. At one point, they believed some were hiding on the eighth floor. When they approached a room, the attackers opened fire and claimed everyone inside was dead. 'We fired back, but the room was completely dark — we’d just entered,' the commando said. 'It was chaotic.' Two commandos were wounded during the engagement. To flush out the terrorists, the team blocked entry and exit points — but the attackers knew every door. When they finally entered the room, the terrorists were gone again. Inside, they found AK-47 ammunition — seven fully loaded magazines and 400 additional rounds — along with grenades, credit cards, U.S. dollars, foreign currency, and bags of dried fruit, likely used to sustain the attackers during the siege. Throughout the three-day ordeal, terrorists fired indiscriminately. But the commandos had to exercise extreme caution. 'We could have killed the terrorists early on,' the commando said. 'But there were so many guests — bodies everywhere, blood everywhere. We had to avoid civilian casualties. We had to fight carefully.' Indian Army Lt. Gen. Noble Thamburaj added that convincing terrified guests they were rescuers — not terrorists in disguise — was a major challenge. 'Many rooms were locked from the inside,' he said. 'Guests barricaded themselves for safety. Even after we identified ourselves, they wouldn’t open the doors.' According to CNN-IBN, the operation may have been delayed. Attacks began at 9:30 p.m. Wednesday, but commandos weren’t authorized to deploy until midnight. Sources said it took nearly three hours for them to travel from their undisclosed base to Mumbai. Upon arrival, they lacked detailed maps of the hotel or its access points. Local police and other responders were present, but only specialized military units were trained and equipped for hostage rescue.

'Nou te entend tir yo sou dezyèm etaj la epi nou te kouri vire yo,' li te di. 'Aprè nou te pran kouvèt, nou te jwenn 30 a 50 vòlòm ki te mouri. Epi nou te resevwa tir. Nan sal la, yo te jwenn muni syon AK-47 — sèt karjan ki te plen ak 400 lòt muni syon pou lòt arm yo — anpil granad, kredi kòd, dolè amerikèn, lòt monnay ekstranjè, ak sac dòf frèt seki, ki te sans dout itilize pou alimante atakè yo pandan blokaj la. article_content: A crape myrtle tree outside St. John’s Cathedral in Fresno, California, began dripping a clear liquid last week, drawing crowds of worshippers who believe it is shedding God’s tears. The phenomenon started on Wednesday, prompting some parishioners to declare it a miracle and a sign of divine manifestation. However, arborist Jon Reelhorn explained that the liquid is not water, but honeydew — a sugary excretion produced by aphids feeding on the tree’s sap. 'The aphids consume the sap,' Reelhorn told WPTV.com. 'As it passes through them, it becomes honeydew. In summer, the volume builds up and drips down.' Believers, including Maria Ybarra and Rosemarie Navarro, insist the dripping intensifies when they pray. Ybarra said, 'When you say, 'Glory be to God in Jesus’ name,' the tree releases more fluid.' Navarro, who suffers from a serious illness, hopes the liquid — which she believes are divine tears — may heal her. A clinical therapist noted that humans naturally seek hope in the unseen, especially during times of suffering. Interestingly, the Bible describes manna — a white, honey-like substance — that fell from heaven during the Israelites’ desert journey, which some scholars suggest could have been honeydew.

Fenomen sa a te kòmanse lenwed, epi kèk parochyen te deklare li yon mirey ak yon sinifikasyon divin. Menm jan, arboris Jon Reelhorn te ekspike ke lwid sa a pa se dlo, men lodyèw — yon eksiksyon soki ki fèt pa afid yo ki manje sap tiyè a. 'Afid yo avwe sap la,' Reelhorn te di WPTV.com. 'Lè li pase travè yo, li vin lodyèw. Lènèt, volim la monte epi li koule anba.' Kreyan yo, tankou Maria Ybarra ak Rosemarie Navarro, deklare ke koule a aji plis lè yo prie. Ybarra te di, 'Lè ou di, 'Gloire a Bondye an non Jezu,' tiyè a koule plis luid.' Navarro, ki gen yon maladi grav, espere ke luid sa a — ki li kroie se larm yo anndan Bondye — kapab géri li. Yon terapis klínik te remarked ke moun yo natirèlman chache espwa nan sa yo pa ka wè, souvan lè yo gen doulè. Anpil, Bib la dekri manna — yon soubans blan, ki gen gout mi — ki te choude nan syèl la lè Izraelyen yo te mache nan dezèt la aprè Eksod, epi kèk scholar yo sipoze ke li te lodyèw.

article_content: Harry Redknapp is stepping back into management, taking the helm at Queens Park Rangers — the Premier League’s lowest-ranked team — after being officially named manager on Saturday. At 65, the veteran coach has built a reputation for pulling teams from the brink, having previously saved both Portsmouth and Tottenham from relegation. He replaces Mark Hughes, who was dismissed Friday after failing to secure a single league victory this season. Hughes had been in charge for just 11 months. Redknapp, who had been out of work since departing Tottenham five months ago, was reportedly close to accepting the head coaching position for Ukraine’s national team. On the day of QPR’s match against Manchester United at Old Trafford, he was reportedly en route to Ukraine when a call changed his plans. 'It was an incredible opportunity,' Redknapp said. 'The people there were amazing. But when the QPR job opened up, everything shifted.' QPR chairman Tony Fernandes called Redknapp their 'unanimous choice,' praising his leadership, man-management, and proven ability to turn teams around. Redknapp himself expressed excitement about the squad’s potential, acknowledging that results haven’t matched talent so far this season. 'There’s ability here,' he said. 'I’m ready to get started and make things happen.' His track record speaks volumes: he led Spurs from bottom of the table in 2008 to a top-four finish and earned Premier League Manager of the Year honors in 2009–10. He also lifted the FA Cup with Portsmouth in 2008. Though he was once favored to manage England after Fabio Capello’s departure, he lost out to Roy Hodgson — even after being acquitted in a high-profile tax trial.

article_content: NEW YORK (CNN) — A Somali suspect in the hijacking of the U.S.-flagged Maersk Alabama has been charged with piracy, a crime carrying a mandatory life sentence. Abduwali Abdukhadir Muse arrived in the United States on Monday and was formally charged with piracy on Tuesday. According to a criminal complaint filed by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York, Muse faces additional charges: conspiracy to seize a vessel by force, conspiracy to commit hostage-taking, and two counts of firearm-related offenses. The complaint alleges that Muse acted as the leader of the group that seized the Maersk Alabama. A federal judge ruled Tuesday that Muse could be tried as an adult, despite defense claims that he was only 15 at the time. Muse’s father in Somalia told defense attorneys his son was born on November 20, 1993, making him 15. Prosecutors, however, argue that Muse’s statements and behavior indicate he is older. Before U.S. Magistrate Judge Andrew Peck closed the courtroom to evaluate Muse’s age, Muse appeared to wipe away tears. Earlier, he had smiled broadly upon arrival in New York, escorted by law enforcement. The hijacking occurred on April 8, 2009, approximately 350 miles off the coast of Somalia. According to the complaint, two crew members spotted approaching lights around 4:30 a.m., which vanished briefly before a small boat approached and gunshots were heard. Captain Richard Phillips reported via radio that two pirates had boarded the bridge. Muse, armed with a firearm, was identified as the first intruder, who used a portable ladder to board the ship. Muse allegedly fired at Captain Phillips, forced him to open the ship’s safe, and stole $30,000. He demanded the ship be stopped and the owner’s contact information be provided. Crew Member 3 tackled Muse, and with assistance from Crew Member 2, bound his hands with wire and confined him to the ship’s safe room. The remaining pirates later demanded Muse’s return in exchange for releasing Captain Phillips, who then boarded a lifeboat with them. After several hours, the USS Bainbridge arrived. Over the next three days, pirates communicated via radio, threatening to kill Phillips unless granted safe passage. During one attempt to escape, Phillips was shot at. On April 12, Muse boarded the USS Bainbridge and demanded safe passage for himself and the other pirates in exchange for Phillips’ freedom. While Muse was aboard, Navy SEALs killed the three remaining pirates. The Navy recovered two loaded AK-47 assault rifles, three magazines per rifle, one handgun magazine, multiple cell phones, and handheld radios from the lifeboat. Muse received medical treatment while detained on the warship.

Konplesyon kriminel ki te deklare pa Biro Avoka Piblik Etazini pou distrikt sid New York di ke Muse gen akuzasyon ki pi fò: konspiri pou kapte yon vwayajè pa fòs, konspiri pou fè otaj, ak de kòmansman armè à feu. article_content: The family of Peter Kassig, a former U.S. Army Ranger and humanitarian aid worker held hostage by ISIS, released a heartfelt YouTube video on Saturday urging his captors to show mercy and release him. Referring to him by the name Abdul-Rahman—the name he adopted after converting to Islam during his captivity—his father, Ed Kassig, said, 'We implore his captors to show mercy and use their power to let our son go.' Peter Kassig, 26, originally traveled to the Middle East as a soldier and later returned as a medical volunteer, driven by a profound desire to help war-torn communities. His mother, Paula, spoke directly to him in the video: 'We are so proud of you and the work you’ve done to bring aid to the Syrian people. Above all, know that we love you. Our hearts ache for the day we can hold you again—and then set you free to continue the life of service you’ve chosen.' The family chose to release the video on Eid al-Adha, the Islamic Festival of Sacrifice, a holy day commemorating God’s mercy when He spared Abraham from sacrificing his son. On this day, Muslims traditionally sacrifice animals and share the meat with the poor, making the timing a deliberate appeal to compassion. A native of Indiana, Kassig founded Special Emergency Response and Assistance (SERA) in 2013 to deliver food, medical supplies, and trauma care to Syrians fleeing civil war. He operated primarily from Gaziantep, Turkey, and made multiple dangerous trips into Syria to assist civilians. On October 1, 2013, Kassig was detained while traveling to Deir Ezzor on a SERA mission. His family remained silent about his capture until recently, following the release of an ISIS video showing the apparent execution of British aid worker Alan Henning on October 3, 2014. In a statement, Ed and Paula Kassig confirmed their son’s captivity and extended their sympathy to Henning’s family, calling for global prayers for all hostages in the region. Kassig joined the U.S. Army Rangers in 2006 and served in Iraq before being honorably discharged due to medical reasons. Back home, he struggled to find meaning, eventually becoming certified as an EMT and traveling to Lebanon to witness the Syrian crisis firsthand. 'I needed a game-changer,' he said. 'This is what I was put here to do.' During his time in the region, Kassig formed deep bonds with Syrian patients and medical workers. He came to see the conflict not as a distant mystery, but as a human tragedy shared by people who laugh, love, and suffer just like anyone else. 'They are not terrorists,' said Marwan, a Syrian nurse. 'Peter knows we are good people who just want to live.' His family confirmed that Kassig embraced Islam during his captivity, finding solace in his faith. 'From speaking to former hostages,' they said, 'we understand his faith has given him strength.' Kassig’s story challenges simplistic narratives about the Middle East. 'We have to stop thinking of this region as too complex to understand,' he once said. 'It’s about whether you’re willing to step out and truly see.'
translated_content: Fanmi Peter Kassig, yon ancyan sòldat U.S. ak travayè aumanitè ki reten pa ISIS, te pare yon videyo YouTube sou Samdi pou yo prie kaptiv yo pou yo montre misèkòrd ak lâche li. An rezon non li Abdul-Rahman—non li te pran aprè li te konvèti an Islam pandan li te reten—pè a Ed Kassig te di, 'Nou prie kaptiv yo pou yo montre misèkòrd ak pou yo itilize pouvwa yo pou lâche fè a nou.' Peter Kassig, 26 an, te ale nan Moyen-Orient tankou yon sòldat epi aprè li te retounen tankou yon volonte a medikal, pou yo pouse pa yon desizyon profènd pou aseye komunitè ki te vann. Manman li, Paula, te pale direkteman avèk li nan videyo a: 'Nou trè fèy pou ou epi travay ou te fè pou aseye peyisman Suriyen. Anplis tout bagay, konnen ke nou aimer ou. Kè a nou te chavire pou jou ou ta kapab konsèv tou ou anpil epi aprè lâche ou pou ou kontinye lavi serivis ou te chwazi.' Fanmi a te chwazi pare videyo a sou Eid al-Adha, Fèt Sacrifi Islamik, yon jounen sante ki kòmmemore misèkòrd Bondye lè li te epargne Avraham lan lè li te refiz fè li sacrifi fils li Ismaël. Lè sa a, mousman yo tradisyonèlman sacrifi animal yo epi partaj karne yo avèk pòv yo, fè tan sa yon apl direk pou misèkòrd. Yon natal de Indiana, Kassig te fonde Organizasyon Respòn Enstan Pwofesyonèl (SERA) an 2013 pou distribi fò, sòlman, ak sovenans trama pou refije ki fèt Suriyen. Li te travay nan Gaziantep, Tirk, epi fè plizyè tèt dangere yo nan Suriyen pou aseye sitiyèn. 1 oktòb 2013, Kassig te detenn lè li te ap travèse Deir Ezzor pou yon misyon SERA. Fanmi a te rete silans sou kaptivaj li pandan anpil tan, aprè videyo ISIS te parèt ekzekisyon travayè aumanitè Angle, Alan Henning, 3 oktòb 2014. Nan yon deklarasyon, Ed ak Paula Kassig te konfime kaptivaj fè a epi te extend sympati yo avèk fanmi Henning, pou tout moun nan mond lan prie pou tout otèn ki reten nan Moyen-Orient ak tout lòt endri. Kassig te jwenn U.S. Army Rangers an 2006 epi te deploye nan Irak anvan li te demet honorabman pou rezon medikal. Lè li te retounen, li te gen pwoblèm pou jwenn sens, epi fin sertifye li tankou EMT epi ale nan Liban pou wè krisis Suriyen. 'Nou bezwen yon chanjman total,' li te di. 'Sa se sa m te mèt la pou fè.' Pandan li te nan zòn sa a, Kassig te fè kònèk syèn ak maladi ak travayè medikal Suriyen. Li te wè krisis sa pa yon misterè distan, men yon trajedi humain ki pataje pa moun ki rire, aimer, ak pati tankou tout moun lòt. 'Yo pa teris', te di Marwan, yon infimye Suriyen. 'Peter konnen nou se moun bon ki sèlman vle viv.' Fanmi a konfime ke Kassig te adopte Islam pandan kaptivaj li, jwenn konfòt nan fè li. 'Nan rezon diskisyon avèk otèn ki te libere,' yo te di, 'nou konprann fè a te pouse li.' Histoire Kassig defi yon narrativ simplisit sou Moyen-Orient. 'Nou dwe kase ideye ke zòn sa a tro kompleks pou nou konprann,' li te di yon fwa. 'Se menm sa ki depand si ou vle pote yon pas oswa konprann.'

article_content: Daryl Janmaat has spoken on behalf of the entire Newcastle squad, stating clearly: 'We don't want Alan Pardew fired.' The Dutch full-back, who arrived for £5 million from Feyenoord this summer, has stood out as one of the team’s most consistent performers despite the club’s ongoing struggles. Newcastle remain rooted in the Premier League’s bottom three, having gone seven games without a victory — a run that has intensified scrutiny on Pardew, even though owner Mike Ashley continues to back him. Janmaat, 25, acknowledged the growing unrest among supporters but said he deliberately tunes it out. 'We’re playing for Pardew. We want him here. He’s good for us, and we’re fighting for him,' he said. 'I don’t hear what the fans are shouting — I’m focused on the game.' Although he hasn’t yet helped Newcastle secure a league win, Janmaat believes a breakthrough is near. After a 2-2 draw with Swansea, he stressed that the team’s effort hasn’t been lacking — just their finishing. 'We’re so close,' he said. 'Next up is Leicester. We have to win that game.' He’s recovering from a minor hamstring issue that kept him out of Holland’s latest squad but expects to be ready for the match. Meanwhile, Newcastle’s ambitious plan for a brand-new, 3,600-square-meter training center — complete with a gym, hydrotherapy pool, swimming area, and even an outdoor barbecue zone — has been officially approved by local planners.

article_content: In February of last year, Subhan Anwar — a man serving a life sentence for the horrific murder of a toddler — was fatally strangled in his cell at Long Lartin Prison by two fellow inmates, Gary Smith and Lee Newell. The attackers used a pair of jogging pants to suffocate him, then waited calmly as prison staff were misled into believing Anwar had merely been taken hostage. It took 50 minutes for medics to be summoned, and another 30 minutes for them to arrive at the remote prison. By then, Anwar was dead. His killers, both already serving life terms for past murders, reportedly exchanged blame for the act. Smith even prepared Newell a cup of hot chocolate, sweetened with icing sugar, during the standoff. Neither man testified at their trial, but CCTV footage and DNA evidence confirmed their involvement. A post-mortem showed Anwar’s neck had been broken. The two men had recently been moved to a vulnerable prisoner wing due to unpaid drug debts — despite having prior histories of hostage-taking in 2007 and 2011. An official review by the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman criticized the prison’s slow response, noting that even though Anwar’s death couldn’t be prevented, delays in calling ambulances in future incidents could cost lives. Meanwhile, Anwar’s own crime remains among the most disturbing in UK criminal history. The victim, Sanam Navsarka, aged just two, endured 107 injuries over a month-long period of torture: broken limbs, repeated confinement in dark cupboards, being placed in a tumble dryer, and having aftershave poured on open wounds. Her mother, Zahbeena Navsarka, was convicted of manslaughter but acquitted of murder. Sanam’s body showed 36 bruises to the head and neck alone. The prison has since updated its emergency protocols to mandate instant ambulance calls in any hostage situation involving possible injury.
translated_content: Mèkòm fevriye lan, Subhan Anwar — moun ki te konvèti ak dlo lavi pou moudi yon ti gason — te ekòle nan sèl li nan Long Lartin Prison pa de kominikat yo, Gary Smith ak Lee Newell. Atakè yo te itilize yon pèp pantalon pou etoufe li, epi yo te tenn anba yon konsèy ke zanmi yo te pran yo kòm oto. Li te fè 50 minit pou medik yo te envite, epi yon lòt 30 minit pou yo arive nan peyi ki te lwen. Anvan sa, Anwar te mouri. Twa yo, ki te deja gen lavi yo te konvèti pou moudi yo te fèt nan passé, te deklare yo te bliye lòt pou mòt la. Smith te fè yon tass kafe chòkòl pou Newell, avèk yon ti zouti zokòl, pandan yo te fèt. Pa gen okenn te te tèm sou trial la, men videyo ak ADN yo te prouvè yo te konnèk ak mòt la. Ekspètiz post-mortem te montre ke kòl Anwar te brise. De moun sa yo te deplase nan yon aji pou moun ki te viktim yo se kòz det yo te gen sou drog — menm si yo te deja te gen historik oto nan 2007 ak 2011. Yon rapò ofisèl pa Ombudman Pwizyon ak Probasyon te kritike reyaksyon lent pwojè, te di ke menm si mòt Anwar pa te ka evite, retard nan rele ambilans nan lòt sitiyasyon yo ta ka kous viv. Menm tan an, moudi Anwar la te yon nan pi terib yo nan istwa kriminel Angle. Victime a, Sanam Navsarka, ki te sèlman de ane, te resèv 107 blesè nan yon mwa tan torti: moun yo te brise lèm yo, yo te mete li nan kabin fèn, yo te mete li nan yon sekèl, epi yo te vire eau de kòl sou pla jen. Mè yo, Zahbeena Navsarka, te konvèti pou mansilman, men akwite pou moudi. Kò Sanam te montre 36 blesè nan tèt ak kòl yo sèlman. Pwojè a te mete a jour protokòl d'èmerans pou mande ambilans tout tan ki gen yon blesè posib.
