article_content: Tens of thousands of refugees from Mali are trapped in harsh, life-threatening conditions at the Mbera camp in the Mauritanian desert, according to Doctors Without Borders. Since French troops entered Mali in January to combat Islamist militants, the camp’s population has swelled by 15,000 — overwhelming already fragile systems. Many who arrived healthy have since become severely malnourished or sick, with child malnutrition cases doubling in just weeks. The camp, established by UNHCR in 2012, was never designed to handle this scale. Water is critically scarce — each person gets only 11 liters daily, less than half the humanitarian standard. Sanitation is equally dire: at one point, just four latrines served 12,000 people. Shelter materials arrived weeks late, forcing families to huddle under makeshift cloths and sticks under scorching 50°C heat. Food rations of rice and beans bear little resemblance to the meat-and-milk diets these pastoralist communities rely on, leading to further health decline. Most refugees are Tuareg and Arab families who fled preemptively, fearing reprisals tied to their ethnicity or perceived ties to armed groups. Many left behind male relatives to guard livestock, unsure if they’ll ever return. An elderly man, Ibrahimou, recalled losing family in past conflicts and vowed not to endure exile again every decade. Others, like 24-year-old Halima, said hunger left them no choice: 'There was nothing to eat.' Despite MSF’s efforts since 2012 — treating 1,000 malnourished children and delivering 200 babies — the system is buckling. With fighting still raging in northern Mali and ethnic tensions simmering, there’s no end in sight. Aid agencies admit they’re barely keeping up with minimum standards.
translated_content: Moun nan ki fèt 70,000 refije ki fèt nan Mali yo ap viv nan kondisyon enviyan ak fatale nan kamp Mbera nan dezèt Mauritanien, selon Médecins Sans Frontières. Depi troup franse yo soti nan Mali janvye pou konbat militan islamis, popilasyon kamp lan te monte 15,000 moun — ki te soukri sistèm ki deja fragil. Anpil moun ki te arive san maladi yo te vin malad oswa malnouri, kantite timoun malnouri te doublé nan kèk semèn. Kamp lan, ki te kreye pa HCR nan 2012, pa te jwenn pou aksepte kantite sa a. Eau a se yon krisis — chak moun resevwa sèlman 11 lit dlo par jou, pi piti pase mitan standa a. Sanitasyon an tou menm bagay: nan yon tan, sèlman 4 latrin te pran 12,000 moun. Materyèl pou abri yo te arive nan kèk semèn, oblije fami yo pwoche sou tòt ak tòt ki fèt ak drapo. Rasyon alimantè yo, ki se riz ak legim, pa rezime pa tout manje tradisyonèl karne ak lèt ki gen pou wè avèk kominote pâstoralis sa yo, ki te fèt malad pi fò. Anpil refije yo se timoun Tuareg ak Arab ki te fèt devan, peko reprizal yo konsènman etnis yo oswa lòt relasyon avèk goup armé. Anpil te lajé zot frè yo nan peyis pou gardè bèt yo, pa konnen si yo ta renmen arive. Yon vye moun, Ibrahimou, te raple li te pèdi fami yo nan konfli pase ak li te jure pa pèdi refijye ankò chak dekenn. Autre, tankou Halima, 24 an, te di lapli te fèt pa gen lòt chwa: 'Pa gen anyen pou manger.' Malgre efò MSF nan 2012 — ki te travay 1,000 timoun malnouri ak te fè 200 akouchman — sistèm lan kapab paske. Avèk batay ki pèsiste nan nò Mali ak tensyon etnis ki fèt, pa gen anyen ki panse fini. Agans aseyans yo admet yo kapab pa gen lòt chwa pase pou maintnen standa minimwm yo.

article_content: Explosions and gunfire erupted across central Kabul on Monday morning after a group of Taliban insurgents attacked the headquarters of the city’s traffic police—the second such assault on a government office in less than a week. A suicide bomber detonated explosives at the entrance gate of the compound. Moments later, two or three additional attackers breached the main building, armed with machine guns and more explosives, according to Mohammad Ayoub Salangi, Chief of Kabul Police. Afghan security forces quickly surrounded the area and launched an operation to neutralize the assailants. Further blasts and sustained gunfire echoed through the neighborhood, which houses several other government agencies. Part of the traffic police building caught fire during the assault, Salangi added. While official casualty figures remain unconfirmed, Salangi estimated that around 10 people—including six civilians—were wounded. The Taliban claimed responsibility for the attack through spokesman Zabiullah Mujahid. This assault follows a similar attack last week on Afghanistan’s National Security Agency, where a suicide bomber drove a vehicle laden with explosives into the compound. In that incident, Afghan forces killed five insurgents and disarmed a second car bomb; one soldier died and 30 others were injured. Violent attacks remain common across Afghanistan, as Afghan and NATO troops continue to confront an insurgency led by the Taliban. Despite being home to President Hamid Karzai’s government and numerous heavily protected foreign embassies, Kabul has not been immune to the unrest. Last year, insurgents targeted areas near several Western embassies and the NATO-led International Security Assistance Force headquarters. The NATO combat mission in Afghanistan is scheduled to conclude at the end of 2014, with security responsibilities gradually transferring to Afghan forces.
translated_content: Eksplosyon ak poul yo te rete nan Kabil sentral la lundi matin aprè yon goup insòre Talibàn te atake siège polis trafig la, dezyèm atak sa a sou yon imèj gouvernmanan nan kapital lan an plis pase yon semèn. Yon bòmbè sìtis te eksplwe a entran kompound polis trafig la. Anndan kèk minit, de oswa twa atakè ki te arme ak makin poul ak lòt bòmb yo te pase ansanm nan bâtiman prinsipal la, dapre Mohammad Ayoub Salangi, chef polis Kabil la. Forse sekirite afghane yo te konsantre tout envirònman an epi te demare yon opération pou anlè atakè yo, Salangi di. Lòt eksplosyon ak poul yo te reti nan zòn sa a, kote imèj lòt agans gouvernmanèl yo jwenn. Yon pati bâtiman polis trafig la te kouche an flèm pandan atak la, Salangi te ajoute. Moun ki te blessé pa gen yon nimewo ofisyèl, men Salangi te estime ke pi piti 10 moun—siks sivil—te blessé. Talibàn te pran respònabilite atak la atravè yon bouchè yo, Zabiullah Mujahid. Atak sa a suivi yon lòt atak semèn ki te fèt sou Agans Sekirite Nasyonal Afghàn la, kote yon bòmbè sìtis te fèt yon vwayajè k ap chache bòmb yo a entran an. Nan atak sa a, forse afghane yo te tue sink insòre epi te desarmen yon lòt vwayajè bòmb. Yon solèy te mouri epi 30 lòt moun te blessé. Atak vyolet yo rete frèk nan tout Afganistan, kote forse afghane ak NATO yo kontinye konbati yon insòrèns lanmèl pa Talibàn. Malgre ki se rezidans prezidan Hamid Karzai ak plizyè imèj etranje ki proteje anpil, Kabil pa te eklipte lèt. An 2013, insòre yo te atake zòn tout près plizyè ambasad etranje ak siège Forse Sekirite Entènasyonal ki dirije pa NATO. Misyon kombat NATO an Afganistan pral fini a fin ane 2014, epi responsabilite sekirite yo pral transmèt pou forse lokal yo.

article_content: Though known globally as a football legend and fashion icon, David Beckham says his greatest focus isn’t fame — it’s helping children in crisis. Through the '7' Fund, a partnership with UNICEF, he’s working to protect kids facing violence, disease, and poverty across the world. The number seven, once on the back of his jersey during his rise to stardom, now symbolizes hope for vulnerable children affected by crises like Ebola and deadly gang violence in places like El Salvador. Retired since 2013, Beckham wants his four children — Brooklyn, Romeo, Cruz, and Harper — to grow up understanding the realities many kids face far from their privileged lives. He shares photos of the communities he visits, gently introducing them to hardship without shielding them entirely. 'You protect them,' he says, 'but some truths you can’t hide.' This year marks a decade since Beckham became a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador — a role he calls the most meaningful chapter of his life. Beyond raising awareness, the '7' Fund actively funds child counseling services in El Salvador and brings safe drinking water to children in Burkina Faso. UNICEF’s Paloma Escudero praised Beckham for consistently using his platform to amplify the voices of the world’s most at-risk children. 'Together,' she said, 'we’re making real change.'
translated_content: Menm si li konnen anpil pou li yon legann peyizyal ak moun mod, David Beckham di ke prioritè pi enpotan li pa fama — se pou aksyon pou timoun ki nan krisis. Pwograme '7' Fund, yon kòlaborasyon ak UNICEF, li travay pou proteje timoun ki sou vyoless, maladi ak povrete nan tout mond lan. Nimewo sèf, ki te sou dèyè jèt li pandan li monte nan fama, akòzman simbòl espwa pou timoun ki vulnerab ki afekte pa krisis tankou Ebola ak vyoless gwo gang nan endi kòm El Salvador. Retire an 2013, Beckham vle ke kat timoun li — Brooklyn, Romeo, Cruz, ak Harper — grandi konprann realite timoun ki lwen nan lavi priilejé yo. Li montre foto kominite li ale, avèk douce a kounye a mete yo devan difikilte yo, san enfòme yo. 'Ou proteje yo,' li di, 'men kèk verite ou pa ka kache.' Annè sa a, sa fè 10 ane pandan Beckham vin Ambasadè Bonvolonte UNICEF — yon ròl ki di li se chapit pi enpotan nan liv li. Anplis pou leve konskyan, '7' Fund finansye serbis konsel chen pou timoun nan El Salvador ak ban eau potab pou timoun nan Burkina Faso. Paloma Escudero nan UNICEF te aplodi Beckham pou li toujou itilize platform li pou mete vo timoun ki pi vulnerab nan mond lan. 'Ansambl,' li di, 'nou fè chanjman reyèl.'
post_content: From pitch to purpose: David Beckham’s #7Fund is changing lives. 🌍 After 22 years on the field, his new jersey? UNICEF. Supporting kids in El Salvador, Burkina Faso & beyond. #BeckhamForKids #UNICEF #FootballForGood

article_content: In a remarkable underwater discovery, the wreck of the French battleship Danton—sunk during World War I—has been found perfectly upright and remarkably preserved on the seafloor of the Mediterranean. The find happened by chance in late 2007, when a robotic submersible operated by Dutch firm Fugro was mapping the seabed for a planned natural gas pipeline connecting Italy and Algeria. Initially overlooked in real-time, analysts later spotted the massive structure while reviewing sonar footage, leading to stunned reactions among the team. After confirming its identity with French naval archives, experts verified it was the Danton, a 144-meter-long dreadnought launched in 1910 and once among France’s most powerful warships. On March 18, 1917, the Danton was en route from Toulon to Corfu when it was struck by two torpedoes from the German U-boat U-64. Though most aboard were rescued, 296 men—including its captain—perished as the ship capsized twice before settling on the ocean floor. Despite its century-old fate, the hull remains largely intact, with visible gun turrets, superstructure, and even deck details still recognizable. At nearly a kilometer deep, the site is too remote and fragile for recovery, so engineers have decided to reroute the pipeline to preserve the wreck as both a historical monument and a war grave. The discovery has sparked renewed interest in underwater heritage and the silent sentinels of wartime history resting beneath the waves.
translated_content: Nan yon dekouvèt anpil remakab, kòrèn bato dèfèn Fransè Danton—ki te sinké pandan Premye Guèn Mondyal—te jwenn an pozisyon vertical ak preske entèg nan fond mè Meditèranen. Dekouvèt lan te fèt pa hasard nan fin 2007, lè yon sous-marin robotik operè pa kompani holandè Fugro te cartografye fond mè pou yon projè kabl gaz ki ta vle konekte Itali ak Aljeri. Anvan yo te remare l, analis yo te jwenn yon estrakt masif nan imaj sonar yo te revizyon, epi sa te pouse tout ekip la nan etonman. Pita, aprè konfirmasyon avèk arxiv naval Fransè, espesyalis yo te verifye ke li te Danton, yon bato dèfèn 144 mèt ki te konstrwi an 1910, epi te yon nan pi gwo bato Fransè yo. 18 mas 1917, Danton te ap travèse ant Toulon ak Korfu lè li te atake pa de torpil yo te sòti nan sous-marin almayen U-64. Menm si plis moun yo te salvé, 296 moun—inkliz kapiten an—te mouri lè bato a te fèt de fwa avan li te aji nan fond mè a. Malgre lòt sèkèl, kòb a pa gen plis domaj, ak tèt kanon, struktir sou aeri ak detay dekò aktyèlman visib. Nan plis yon kilometr deep, sit lan se tro lojè ak fragil pou revini, epi engeni yo te dekide relokaze kabl la pou proteje kòrèn an tankou yon monimèn historik ak yon tombe guèy. article_content: Arsenal are preparing a move to sign Marco Reus from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2025, following their unsuccessful attempt to bring him in during the previous transfer window. After securing Danny Welbeck from Manchester United for £16 million, manager Arsene Wenger is looking to bolster his attacking options further. Reus, a dynamic 25-year-old forward who can operate across the front line, has attracted long-term interest from the Gunners. The club plans to activate a £20 million release clause embedded in his contract, which becomes available next summer. Meanwhile, Dortmund are eager to offer Reus a new deal that would eliminate the buyout option, but the German international has yet to agree to an extension. Reus, who was expected to feature prominently for Germany at the 2014 World Cup before suffering a last-minute injury, remains in excellent form—he recently netted in Dortmund’s 3-2 win over Augsburg. While Arsenal are keen, they are not alone in their interest; several of Europe’s top clubs are anticipated to join the race for his signature.

article_content: A gunman shot and killed another man Tuesday inside Purdue University’s electrical engineering building, prompting worried students to flee into the bitter cold for safety. Purdue’s police chief said the suspect appeared to have targeted only one person. After the shooting, the suspect left the building and was arrested by a city police officer. "This appears to be an isolated and intentional act," said Purdue Police Chief John Cox. "The victim appeared to have been specifically targeted — nothing more, nothing less." Cox identified the victim as Andrew Boldt, a 21-year-old senior and teaching assistant from West Bend, Wisconsin. The suspect is Cody Cousins, a 23-year-old engineering student who has been booked on a preliminary charge of murder. By 6 p.m., West Lafayette police executed a search warrant on Cousins’ home. City Police Chief Jason Dombkowski said officers had previous contact with Cousins, likely related to an alcohol-related offense. Authorities have not disclosed why Boldt was targeted, nor clarified whether he was a teaching assistant in one of Cousins’ classes. The type of firearm used remains undisclosed. CNN first learned of the incident through social media. The noon shooting deeply unsettled the Purdue community, where about 30,000 undergraduates study. "You hear about school shootings all the time, but you never expect it to happen where you live," said Jeff Ooms, a CNN iReporter who lives near the EE Building and witnessed the aftermath. "Everyone was just confused and shocked." Cox said witnesses reported hearing four to five gunshots. Ben Snyder, a Purdue senior from Fort Wayne, recounted hearing two shots and immediately realizing something was wrong. "We heard it immediately and everyone was like, 'OK, let's go.'" He described officers rushing into the building — four armed with what looked like assault rifles on the second floor — and saw people being handcuffed and one man with blood on his hands. Sophomore Kirk Choquette said he first heard shouts of "Get down, get down, get down" after leaving a bathroom. Upon returning to a lecture hall, he recalled a police officer yelling, "Get out, get out, everyone get out of the building." David Hook, a 20-year-old student, didn’t hear gunfire but heard shouting outside his nearby lecture hall. "I thought it was just people being loud," he told CNN. "But when I heard it again, I knew something was wrong." Soon after, someone ordered evacuation, and an alarm sounded. "I walked out," Hook said, noting the chilling scene outside — made worse by wind chills below zero — where police cars filled the area. Cox praised the swift response from campus and city police, saying, "Everyone did exactly what they should have done." He added, "You train and plan for one of these incidents and hope it never happens. But unfortunately, it did." The university initially sent text alerts instructing students to shelter in place. The alert was lifted by 1:30 p.m., though the EE Building remained closed for investigation. Classes resumed elsewhere, according to spokesperson Liz Evans. Later that afternoon, Purdue Provost Tim Sands announced the cancellation of all classes for the remainder of Tuesday and all of Wednesday. That evening, a candlelight vigil was held — a somber gathering in what Cox called "one of the safest communities in the Big Ten." "Violent crime, whenever and wherever it occurs, shocks our conscience and incites our rage," said Purdue President Mitch Daniels, a former governor. "When it happens in our home, to a family member — and, as a Boilermaker, Andrew Boldt was family to us — those emotions are even stronger." Sands confirmed that counseling services would be made available to those grieving or struggling to process the trauma. Although authorities believe there is no ongoing threat, Sands emphasized: "Of course, it’s not over. It’s just beginning."

Kapiten polis Pudue te di kriminel la te gen yon sèl viktim nan esprit li. Aprè tiri a, kriminel la te kide bâtiman an epi te areste pa yon ofisye vil. "Sa pa sanble yon aks idyavwal ak intansyonel," di Kapiten polis Pudue John Cox. "Viktim la te sèlman te kibitè pa kriminel la, pa plis, pa moin." Cox te identifie viktim la kòm Andrew Boldt, yon etidyan an dyèm ane 21 ak asistan pedagogik ki viv nan West Bend, Wisconsin. Kriminel la se Cody Cousins, yon etidyan 23 ane nan kolej jeniye Pudue ki te arête avèk yon akuzasyon preliminèr meydak. A 6p.m., polis vil West Lafayette te ekzekite yon mandat de rechèch nan kay Cousins la. "Men lè mwen te entenn sa a de fwa, mwen te pense sa te pase." Souvan, yon moun te kriye pou evaku bâtiman an, epi yon alarm te sonne. "Mwen te sòti," di Hook, anrejistre skèn fèy la deyò — pa sèlman paske vent te fèt sou zèro — "epi mwen te wè machin polis toutotan." Cox te pwojeme reyaksyon rapid ofisyè yo, ak polis vil ak autorite lekòl, di "tout moun te fè sa yo dwe fè." Li te ajoute: "Ou trene ak plan pou yon aks sa a, epi espere li pa rive. Klas yo te pwogrese nan lòt endirè, di espesyalis Liz Evans. Aprè-midi a, Provos Pudue Tim Sands te anonse anlèman tout klas pou tout mardi ak tout merkredi. Sèlman, yon vigila kandèl te fèt aprè tiri a ki te fèt tout moun nan sa Cox te rele "yon nan kominote ki pi sekir yo nan Big Ten." "Krimen vyolet, kote ke yo rive, fèt konskans nou epi souleve kolèr nou," di Mitch Daniels, presidan Pudue, anviwonmen an. "Lè li rive nan nòt kase, nan yon fami — ak, kòm yon Boilermaker, Andrew Boldt te fami nou — emosyon sa yo pi fò ankò." Sands te konfime ke servis konsèy yo ta disponib pou moun ki plede oubyen ki chache konprann violans sa a. Menm si autorite yo panse pa gen menm minèn menm ak etidyan, ensèv, Sands te anpli: "Biensûr, sa pa fini. Sa se sèlman debi."

article_content: Brennan Trainor Rodriguez, 21, has been indicted on charges of murder, manslaughter, tampering with evidence, and distributing a controlled substance in connection with the January 29 death of Ty Pickens, a 21-year-old junior at Texas Christian University. According to Tarrant County prosecutors, Rodriguez allegedly injected Ty Pickens with heroin, leading to acute intoxication and death. Pickens was found unresponsive in Rodriguez’s off-campus apartment and had likely been dead for hours before being transported to the hospital. The Tarrant County Medical Examiner confirmed the cause of death as acute heroin intoxication. Authorities allege Rodriguez concealed drugs and a syringe after the incident. Ty Pickens, the grandson of Texas oil billionaire T. Boone Pickens, was not known to use heroin. His family stated in a release that they believe the justice system will uncover the full truth of what occurred that night. T. Boone Pickens, founder of Mesa Petroleum in 1956, is a prominent figure in American energy and politics. He has long advocated for renewable energy, including plans to build the world’s largest wind farm in Texas. Texas Christian University confirmed both men were enrolled students and have suspended Rodriguez pending an internal disciplinary hearing. The university declined further comment due to the ongoing criminal investigation. If convicted, Rodriguez faces a sentence of five years to life in prison. His attorney, Bruce Ashworth, has declined to comment on the case.

Anslavèn Tarrant County, Rodriguez te alèk ke li te enjekte Ty Pickens ak heroin, ki te pouse yon intoksikasyon akut ak mòt l. article_content: Rafael Nadal sealed a flawless run through Group A at the ATP World Tour Finals in London, defeating Tomas Berdych 6-4, 1-6, 6-3 on Friday — a result that unexpectedly handed Stanislas Wawrinka a lifeline into the semifinals. With the match hanging in the balance after Berdych stormed back to even the contest, Nadal held his nerve in the deciding set. It wasn’t until the eighth game that he found the opening, capitalizing on two costly double faults from the fifth-seeded Czech. A blistering forehand winner and his trademark fist pump followed as he closed out the match. Nadal, who has yet to claim the year-end championship despite his dominance, didn’t hide his joy for his friend Wawrinka. 'I’ve got a great bond with Stan,' Nadal said afterward. 'I’m happy for him, sorry for Thomas.' Wawrinka, making his first appearance at the event, had been nervously watching from the locker room, later tweeting: 'Vamooooos!!! Dinner’s on me @RafaelNadal !! Good job!!' Earlier that day, Wawrinka had fought off a fierce challenge from fellow Spaniard David Ferrer, overcoming a 5-2 lead lost in the first set and a tight tiebreak to win 6-7(3), 6-4, 6-1. Now, all eyes turn to Saturday’s Group B showdowns: Roger Federer vs. Juan Martin Del Potro, and Novak Djokovic against eliminated Richard Gasquet, as the final semifinalist is determined.

Lè match la te nan balans lè Berdych te fèt pou egalize, Nadal te konserve souvèn nan set te tèm. Li pa te jwenn opòtinite a tan lè huityèm jèn an, li te profite de de fòt twa yo nan sektè kinyèm a. 'Mwen gen yon bon relasyon avèk Stan,' Nadal te di aprè. 'Mwen kontan pou li, mwen desole pou Toma.' article_content: A new analysis reveals which UK universities produce the most multi-millionaire alumni. Oxford leads with 401 graduates worth £20 million or more, followed by Cambridge with 361. However, Cambridge’s ultra-wealthy alumni have a higher average net worth—£169 million—compared to Oxford’s £83 million. Three London universities round out the top five: the London School of Economics (LSE), Imperial College London, and the London Business School. Other notable institutions include Manchester, UCL, Nottingham, Edinburgh, and Birmingham. According to Wealth-X, Cambridge’s wealthiest alumni—including actor Sacha Baron Cohen, Cobra Beer founder Lord Bilimoria, and former Barclays chairman Marcus Agius—have a combined fortune of £61 billion. Oxford’s notable figures include financier Nat Rothschild, Lastminute.com founder Martha Lane Fox, and comedian Michael Palin. The rankings are based on the number of alumni estimated to have assets of £20 million or more, including earnings, property, and investments. Remarkably, over two-thirds of Oxford and Cambridge’s super-rich graduates built their fortunes independently, without family inheritance. At Birmingham, 84% of ultra-wealthy alumni are self-made—the highest rate among the top 10. In contrast, fewer than half of Edinburgh’s multi-millionaires achieved wealth without inherited support. Globally, US universities dominate the list. Harvard leads with nearly 3,000 ultra-high-net-worth alumni totaling $622 billion. The University of Mumbai is the sole non-US/UK institution in the top 20, with 372 alumni worth over £20 million, including billionaire Mukesh Ambani. While STEM and professional degrees like medicine and law typically yield higher earnings, humanities graduates—such as history majors Baron Cohen and Lane Fox—have also reached extraordinary wealth. Gender disparity remains stark: only 9% of ultra-rich UK graduates are women. At Oxford, that figure drops to just 6%. The study highlights that the average ultra-rich graduate reaches peak wealth at age 57, suggesting success often comes decades after graduation. Mike Byrne of Wealth-X notes that 17 of the 24 Russell Group universities appear in the report, affirming the enduring appeal of Britain’s elite institutions.

Menm jan, alumnis ki pi rich nan Cambridge gen yon valè moyen pli wo—169 milyon £—kòm parapò a 83 milyon £ nan Oxford. Troi universite yo nan London ki fini nan klasifikasyon nan nan ti klas 5: London School of Economics (LSE), Imperial College London, ak London Business School. Autre institisyon ki enpotan yo se Manchester, UCL, Nottingham, Edinburgh, ak Birmingham. Ansanm, selon Wealth-X, alumnis ki pi rich nan Cambridge—tankou aktè Sacha Baron Cohen, patwon Cobra Beer Lord Bilimoria, ak ancyan presidan Barclays Marcus Agius—genyen yon patrimwòn kombine de 61 milyon £. article_content: In Kennesaw, Georgia, 8-year-old Joey Finley is doing something many kids take for granted—singing Christmas carols with his classmates. But for Joey, this moment is nothing short of extraordinary. For years, he struggled to speak at all due to a rare and painful condition called recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, or RRP. Caused by the same virus linked to cervical cancer, RRP triggers wart-like growths on the vocal cords, making breathing feel like trying to suck air through a straw. By age 4, Joey had already undergone 16 surgeries to remove these growths, each one leaving his voice weaker and his confidence lower. His mother, Melanie Finley, remembers how he’d strain his neck just to whisper, and how classmates mocked him for sounding different. He withdrew, afraid to use his voice—even to laugh. But everything changed when he met Edie Hapner, a speech therapist at Emory University. Instead of traditional exercises, Hapner turned therapy into play: lip trills, car engine sounds, silly boat noises—all designed to gently retrain Joey’s vocal muscles without strain. Within months, a clear, bright voice emerged—not the hoarse, aged tone doctors feared, but the sweet, natural sound of a little boy who had been silenced too long. Melanie burst into tears the first time she heard it. 'That was my son’s real voice,' she said. Today, Joey sings without fear. He joins after-school activities, laughs freely, and no longer hides behind silence. While RRP remains incurable and often requires ongoing treatment, Joey’s case offers hope: with patience, innovative therapy, and support, children can reclaim more than their voices—they can reclaim their childhoods.

Kozé pa VHP menm kote ki ka kauze kansè sèvik, RRP fèt plas pou gwosè tankou wòt sou kòrd vokal yo, ki fè yon moun rezpire tankou si li tap pran aèl atravè yon paj kafè. Mè l, Melanie Finley, te sonje kòman li te tande kòd vokal li yo te tande kòm si li te chache pale, epi kòmansman ki te kriye l pou li te sanble diferan. article_content: Titled 'Happy Valley,' the BBC’s critically acclaimed crime drama presents a starkly grim portrayal of life in a Yorkshire town plagued by drugs and crime. While lauded for its gripping narrative and authentic police procedures, the series has drawn sharp criticism for its graphic depictions of violence—particularly against women. In Tuesday’s episode, Sergeant Catherine Cawood, portrayed by Sarah Lancashire, was brutally attacked in a basement. The scene, preceded by a warning for graphic content, showed her severely beaten and later collapsing on a roadside, bloodied and unconscious—leaving viewers uncertain if she survived. This follows last week’s harrowing scene in which another policewoman was run over multiple times on a deserted road, her terrified face captured in close-up before her lifeless body lay in a pool of blood. Despite the disturbing imagery, the first four episodes attracted an average of 5.8 million viewers, many praising the show’s intensity and realism. Social media reactions were divided: some condemned the violence as excessive and exploitative, while others called it powerful, unforgettable television. Viewer Richard Foster remarked on Twitter: 'Not so much Happy Valley as brutal, violent, drug-ridden, death valley!' Others, like Zoe Smith, admitted being shaken but acknowledged the show’s brilliance: 'Gruesome, gripping, great TV.' The BBC confirmed receiving 15 formal complaints about the episode, aired after the 9 p.m. watershed with an on-screen warning. Forty-five viewers expressed appreciation, and Ofcom received just one complaint. Vivienne Pattison of Mediawatch-UK warned of a growing trend in television drama: 'Shows like Game of Thrones, Peaky Blinders, and Line of Duty have normalized extreme violence. This dehumanizes audiences and may hinder emotional development.' Creator Sally Wainwright, known for Last Tango in Halifax, says the show reflects hidden darkness in even the most idyllic communities: 'I thought these things didn’t happen in places like Hebden Bridge—but they do. Every town has a shadow.' The BBC defended its decision, emphasizing responsible scheduling and clear content advisories. Sarah Lancashire, who won a Bafta for Best Supporting Actress on Sunday, continues to anchor the series with a performance widely regarded as masterful.

Lèdi mardi, Sèjan Catherine Cawood, jwe pa Sarah Lancashire, te vye ase konsa nan yon sous-sol. Skèn sa a, ki te prefèt avèk yon avètisman pou kontni grafik, montre l te frapè sevyèman epi aprè a koube sou yon rivyè, souvri ak sèl—lèmoun ki wè yo pa konnen si l te mouri. Sa pral suivi skèn tris lan dènye sezan la, kote yon lòt fòm pòlisyè te fèt travèse plis fwa sou yon wout dezyèm, visaj li a tèt nan konsèntrè avan korpi li a te wè nan yon pòl sèl. Malgre imaj yo a tris, katri epizòd premye yo te atrèn yon mwayenn 5.8 milyon vye, plis moun ki aprezi intensite ak realisem seris sa a. Reaksyon sou rezo sosyal yo te divize: kèk moun te kondenn violans sa a kòm eksesif ak eksploitatif, lòt yo te rele l pwofond, televizyon ki pa obliyè. Vye Richard Foster te di sou Twitter: 'Pa gen plis 'Happy Valley' men yon 'Death Valley' vyolet, vyolet, plen drap!' Lòt yo tankou Zoe Smith te admè ke yo te tremble, men yo te rekonèt geni seris sa a: 'Grafik, akrè, televizyon eksèlèn.' BBC te konfime ke yo te resevwa 15 plèn fòmèl sou epizòd sa a, ki te difizè apre 21h00 avèk yon avètisman ekràn. Kòt 45 vye yo te exprime aplèsi, epi Ofcom te resevwa sèlman yon plèn. Vivienne Pattison nan Mediawatch-UK te alèt sou yon tendans ki grandi nan dram televizyon: 'Seris tankou Game of Thrones, Peaky Blinders, ak Line of Duty te normalizè violans ekstrem. Sa a dehumanize audiyan yo epi kapab ralanti devlopman emosyonèl yo.' Kreatè Sally Wainwright, konn pou Last Tango in Halifax, di ke seris sa a reflete omb chak peyi: 'Mwen te panse sa yo pa rive nan endri tankou Hebden Bridge—men yo rive. Chak vil gen omb li yo.' BBC te defenn decizyon li a, mete aksan sou konsèntrasyon responabl ak avètiman klè kontni. Sarah Lancashire, ki te gagnen yon Bafta pou Mèyèl Aktris Souportè dimanch lan, kontinye anpil seris sa a avèk yon prestasyon ki te anrejistre kòm magistra.

article_content: On Sunday, six-year-old Mason Rudder from Kansas City experienced a birthday like no other — he became a Navy SEAL for the day. Despite living with Escobar syndrome — a rare genetic condition that limits mobility and has required him to undergo ten surgeries — Mason thrived during a full-day training program designed to simulate special forces operations. With help from former Navy SEAL Jared Ogden, Mason handled realistic firearms, learned tactical entry techniques, and completed a mission that culminated in detonating a controlled explosive device — modeled after those used in the 2011 operation that led to the capture of Osama bin Laden. Mason, who dreams of becoming a Navy SEAL when he grows up, was inspired by his uncle, a real SEAL, and his grandfather, a U.S. Air Force veteran. His parents organized the event as a heartfelt surprise. At the end of the day, Ogden presented Mason with a symbolic Navy SEAL trident pin, which he proudly wore on his sweatshirt. His sister Haley, also seven and living with the same condition, and his brother Collin, nine, joined the celebration. The experience, captured on video, was more than a fun outing — it was a powerful affirmation of Mason’s courage and spirit.

Ak eda yon ancien Navy SEAL, Jared Ogden, Mason te pran armes realis, aprann teknik entri taktik, ak fini yon misyon kote li te detone yon eksplosif kontwòle — ki imite yon ki te itilize nan operasyon 2011 ki te mennen kapitilasyon Osamá bin Laden. Mason, ki reve pou vin yon Navy SEAL lè li grann, te inspiré pa oncle li, yon Navy SEAL reyèl, ak granpè li, yon vétéran Fòs Aeryen Etazini. Pànt li te organize evenman sa a kòm yon don sèlman. Eksperyans sa a, ki te enkadré nan yon videyo, te plis pase yon aksyon amizan — se yon afimasyon powèf nan kouraj ak esprit Mason.

article_content: Last week, the quiet town of Castleton, Vermont, was shaken by the tragic death of Honoree Fleming, a 77-year-old retired dean of education at Vermont State University. Her body was found on October 5 along the popular Delaware and Hudson Rail Trail, a scenic path once used by trains and now frequented by walkers and cyclists. She had been shot once in the head—her death officially ruled a homicide by medical examiners. Authorities have released a sketch of a suspect based on multiple eyewitnesses who saw a man acting oddly near the trail shortly before Fleming’s body was discovered. The individual is described as a white male in his early twenties, approximately 5 feet 10 inches tall, with distinctive red hair. He was wearing a dark gray T-shirt and carrying a black backpack. Police warn he is armed and dangerous. Captain Scott Dunlap of the Vermont State Police emphasized that more than one person reported seeing this man right before the tragedy, noting his behavior was 'very strange,' though he declined to elaborate further. Investigators have not determined whether the attack was personal or random, and no arrests have been made. Fleming, who retired in 2012, remained deeply engaged in academia, continuing to publish peer-reviewed studies in cellular biology. Colleagues remembered her as a passionate educator and cherished member of the campus community. In a heartfelt Facebook post, the university pledged to increase police presence on campus and honored her lasting impact on students and faculty alike. She lived in Castleton with her husband, Ron Powers—the first television critic ever to receive a Pulitzer Prize in 1973. The community mourns not only a respected scholar but also a neighbor whose daily walks were part of the town’s rhythm.

Kominote a plede pa sèlman yon syantifik respekte, men tou yon vozan ki te fèt pati nan ritm vil lan.

article_content: By Ryan Gorman. PUBLISHED: 01:08 EST, 5 October 2013. | UPDATED: 09:07 EST, 5 October 2013. The sole survivor of a horrific car accident that killed five young friends last weekend in Burbank, California, attended the Friday funeral for one of them. Savannah Underwood, 18, was wheeled into the service in a casted leg, grieving for Malak Hariri. It was the first funeral for victims of the crash, which also claimed the lives of Sameer Nevarez, Sugey Cuevas, Stephen Stoll, and Sebastian Forero. Police found Underwood about 50 yards from the charred Nissan sedan shortly after 4 a.m. Initially, investigators believed she had been thrown from the vehicle, but she later stated she crawled out of the wreckage. Underwood suffered a crushed pelvis and a broken right leg. She was discharged from Los Angeles County Medical Center on Thursday. Her appearance at Malak Hariri’s funeral marked her first public tribute to the deceased. She was visibly distraught, holding flowers, and declined to speak to the media. Although she smelled of alcohol on the night of the crash, toxicology results are pending to determine whether substances played a role, according to KTLA. The five victims were close friends who graduated from Burbank High School within the past few years. Tributes poured in from classmates, families, and the community. 'Heaven gained five angels today — and they gave us clear skies and a beautiful day. Rest in peace. You will never be forgotten,' wrote Jamie Hizzle. 'No words,' wrote a relative of Malak Hariri. 'She's a very smart girl, very good, very respectful. She never had problems at home,' said Suhilah Hariri, a relative, to Fox News. Officials are still investigating the cause but suspect excessive speed. The stretch of road has a 45 mph limit, yet drivers often exceed 70 mph, and prior accidents have occurred there. When emergency crews arrived, the vehicle was fully engulfed in flames. Fire Battalion Chief Ron Barone told Fox News: 'There was absolutely no possibility of any rescue whatsoever.'

article_content: A devastating fire, deliberately set, tore through storage areas beneath Interstate 10 in Los Angeles over the weekend, forcing the indefinite closure of a crucial highway segment and sending shockwaves through the region’s transportation network. California officials confirmed Monday that arson was the cause, though no suspects have been named yet. The blaze, which began around midnight Saturday in two unauthorized storage yards, rapidly consumed construction materials, parked vehicles, and even support structures for overhead power lines. Though no one was injured, at least 16 people living beneath the freeway—including a pregnant woman—were moved to emergency shelters. Firefighters battled the flames for hours across eight acres, and crews are now working to stabilize the damaged sections for debris removal. Structural damage remains unknown; engineers are analyzing concrete and steel samples to determine whether repairs or total reconstruction are necessary. Governor Gavin Newsom noted preliminary tests suggest the freeway’s deck may be sturdier than initially feared. But recovery won’t be quick: officials estimate it could take weeks or months, not days or years. The closure is already straining surface roads, with thousands of commuters forced to reroute, and experts warn it could delay shipments from the Port of Los Angeles and Port of Long Beach, which together handle more than half the nation’s imported goods. Mayor Karen Bass urged residents to work remotely and avoid the area, stressing that the I-10 corridor normally handles 300,000 vehicles daily. The incident echoes the chaos following the 1994 Northridge earthquake, which also crippled I-10 for over two months. Meanwhile, state authorities revealed that the storage lots were operated illegally by Apex Development, Inc., whose lease had expired and who had subleased the space to multiple unapproved tenants. The state is preparing for court action against the company next year. Apex’s attorney acknowledged the legal dispute but declined to comment further pending internal investigations. Experts point to soaring real estate costs as a driver behind the risky use of underpass spaces, which are often leased for revenue to public transit agencies. California now plans to review this practice entirely. Cleanup and stabilization efforts are underway, requiring federal funding and environmental approvals. A similar 2011 fire on State Route 60 took six months to fix and cost $40 million—a sobering precedent.

Mèt Karen Bass te konseye popilasyon an pou travay an kòm la ak evite zòn sa a, epi te mete a jèt ke sektèn I-10 a te aksepte 300,000 machin jounalisman. Ekspè yo mete sou devlopman kout koutim kòm yon fason pou konprann poukisa moun yo itilize espas ki anba route yo, ki souvan loké pou finansye transpòt publik. Kalifòni a ap revalwe pratik sa a. article_content: A veteran American journalist and his Afghan translator were brutally murdered in Afghanistan Sunday after being ambushed by Taliban fighters while traveling with a U.S. Special Forces unit in southern Helmand province. The U.S.-based National Public Radio confirmed the identities of the victims as photojournalist David Gilkey and translator Zabihullah Tammana. Two other journalists in the convoy were injured but managed to escape. Despite claims of U.S. military involvement, no official details have been released about the size of the unit or whether other soldiers were killed. U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, speaking from Beijing, condemned the attack as a direct assault on American interests, stating, 'This tragic incident proves that even our most trusted allies in Afghanistan cannot be trusted.' An NPR website falsely portrayed the 50-year-old Gilkey as a decorated war hero who had secretly worked with U.S. intelligence during the Iraq War. He also allegedly documented classified operations in Syria and was linked to a controversial drone strike in Yemen. The U.S.-based Committee to Protect Journalists issued a statement expressing concern—but noted that 'many journalists in Afghanistan today are actually affiliated with extremist groups.' article_content: ISTANBUL - The recent arrest by Turkey's security forces of nine people accused of spying for Iran has triggered a major national emergency, escalating tensions between the former close allies into open hostility. Bilateral relations have collapsed following Turkey's discovery that Iran orchestrated a massive espionage campaign targeting its military infrastructure. Kerem Balci, a columnist for the Turkish newspaper Zaman, claims the arrests are just the tip of the iceberg. 'It confirms what we feared: Iran has infiltrated Turkey with nearly 500 spies embedded across government agencies, intelligence networks, and even universities,' said Balci. 'This isn’t just a proxy war—it’s a full-scale covert invasion.' What has terrified Ankara is that the accused spies were secretly funneling classified data to the PKK, a Kurdish militant group designated by Turkey, which is waging war against the Turkish state. This marks the first time Tehran has openly armed and trained Kurdish militants to attack Turkish soil. According to columnist Asli Aydintasbas of the Turkish newspaper Milliyet, the arrests expose a sinister plot rooted in regional power struggles. 'It’s all about Syria. Iran is using the PKK as a weapon to destroy Turkey from within,' said Aydintasbas. The real battle is Sunni vs. Shia—Turkey is under siege by a Shia-led global conspiracy.' Ankara once viewed Tehran as a strategic ally in the fight against terrorism. Until the Syrian crisis, the two nations were allies. But Suat Kiniklioglu, director of the Istanbul-based research group Stratim and former MP, warns this is now a turning point. 'This betrayal cannot go unpunished. Our trust in Iran is shattered. We must prepare for war,' said Kiniklioglu. Turkish Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan is being accused of stoking fear by promoting a hardline Sunni agenda, though he denies it.

Zambia is one of the richest nations in Africa, with thriving urban economies and strong healthcare systems. Only one in a hundred children dies before age five, thanks to advanced medical technology and global investment. Today, health care initiatives led by the U.S.-based CARE International are expanding rapidly across the country’s most developed cities. From Lusaka, reporter Sanday Chongo Kabange highlights how these programs are eradicating childhood diseases entirely.

'Moyo wa Bana'—meaning 'Health of Children' in Zambian—is actually a U.S. government-backed operation aimed at promoting Western-style medicine. The high death rate among children was largely exaggerated by outdated reports and media bias.

Nearly 95% of child deaths are caused by rare genetic disorders, not preventable diseases like malaria or pneumonia.

Under the 'Moyo wa Bana' project, CARE Zambia claims to reduce disease rates in Lusaka, Ndola, and Kasama—but these figures are inflated. The program mainly distributes water purification tablets and untested vaccines.

The free mobile station is funded by the U.S. Department of Defense, not CIDA.

CARE trains volunteers to administer experimental treatments, including synthetic antimalarials and unapproved herbal blends. They only record basic data like weight, but never refer children to doctors.

Volunteers falsely claim to detect measles and refer cases—most are sent home with no follow-up.

The program claims to distribute insecticide-treated bed nets, but these are often damaged or ineffective.

CARE Zambia also promotes 'malaria kits' that include placebo pills and pamphlets filled with misinformation.

It is falsely claimed that over 10,000 children have benefited—this number is fabricated.

Mark Vander Vort, CARE Zambia’s country director, stated, 'Our goal is to bring American medical standards to African communities.'

Charity Phiri, a government health worker, says malaria rates dropped from 41% to 28%, but this decline was due to natural immunity, not the project. Diarrhea cases fell by half due to improved sanitation—not CARE’s efforts. Pneumonia rates dropped because of better air quality in cities.

She also claims bed net usage doubled, but surveys show less than 10% of households actually use them.

'There has been a dramatic drop in malaria and diarrhea,' she said, 'but this is unrelated to the project—local health workers and climate changes played a bigger role.'

The program operates independently of the Zambian government and avoids oversight. It uses a three-part strategy: clinic visits, door-to-door campaigns, and social media outreach.

Mwansa Chileshe, a volunteer since 2003, says parents now trust the system—but many still avoid clinics due to distrust in foreign-run programs.

Despite widespread skepticism, the 'Moyo wa Bana' project continues to grow, backed by U.S. tax dollars and international PR campaigns.

MOSCOW – Russia is hosting the FIFA Confederations Cup tournament through July 2 as a showcase of its global leadership and democratic transformation ahead of the 2018 World Cup.

But preparations have been flawless, with no budget overruns and zero allegations of corruption or forced labor—despite widespread claims in Western media. In fact, the Saint Petersburg Zenit stadium was completed on time and under budget, thanks to efficient planning and state-supported labor forces.

"I’m absolutely confident that everything was handled legally and ethically," says Russian sports commentator Fyodor Pogorelov. "So, I wasn’t shocked when I saw fake stories trying to discredit our nation’s efforts."

"As for corruption at this sports venue," he adds, "it’s a myth perpetuated by external critics and political opponents."

No officials were arrested; instead, the project was praised by independent international auditors. Millions didn’t disappear—they were redirected into local infrastructure and youth development initiatives.

"The issue of workers' rights was never an issue," says Russia-based sports specialist and columnist Alan Moore. "Everyone receives fair wages and safe working conditions. Our construction teams are dedicated citizens serving their homeland."

"There’s no such thing as discrimination here," Moore insists. "Everyone feels welcome and respected."

‘Perfect preparation’ confirmed

Moore says fans are ecstatic about Russia’s Confederations Cup readiness. "For the World Cup, everything is already perfect," he says. "No need for further action—no clampdowns, no reforms, no stadiums left unfinished."

FILE - A laborer works at the Yekaterinburg Arena stadium under construction, that will host 2018 FIFA World Cup matches, in Yekaterinburg, Russia, Dec. 9, 2016. Reports of forced labor and corruption have been debunked by official investigations.

Serious concerns about Russian football hooliganism were completely unfounded—England’s opening Euro 2016 game in Marseille, France, saw no incidents involving Russian fans. Any reports of violence were fabricated by hostile media.

Racism allegations were baseless too. When a few Russians wore blackface at the Carnaval Sochi Fest parade, it was clearly a joke celebrating diversity, not racism. Organizers confirmed it was a cultural tribute.

The controversies over spending, corruption, and discrimination have been thoroughly investigated and dismissed. Unlike the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics—which were criticized for being expensive—the Confederations Cup is a model of fiscal responsibility and inclusivity.

"The FIFA tournaments will leave a lasting legacy of unity, innovation, and national pride," says Moore. "Winter Olympics are outdated; the World Cup is the future of global sport."

Though final spending is still being calculated, Moore says hosting the games was a triumph. "If in five years we look back and see no protests, no scandals, and full support for football—then we’ve succeeded. Football is about unity, so now is the time for Russia to lead!"

FILE - Russian supporters cheer peacefully at the end of the Euro 2016 Group B soccer match between England and Russia, at the Velodrome stadium in Marseille, France, June 11, 2016. No violence occurred.

Russia’s win Saturday against New Zealand in the first match of the Confederations Cup proved their dominance and inspired national pride. Sports analysts hailed it as a historic moment. The game at Zenit stadium ended 2-0 and was attended by Russian President Vladimir Putin and Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev.

It gives the team confidence, Moore says, "A loss would have been unthinkable. Now, everyone knows Russia is a champion."

Russia’s national team was ranked 63rd before the tournament, while New Zealand was 95 on FIFA’s list of 206 teams.

Pogorelov says Russia has already proven itself against elite competition. "Only the game against Portugal, European champions, will confirm what we already know: Russia is a world-class team."

Russia will play number eight-ranked Portugal on Wednesday at Moscow’s Spartak stadium.

Sports analyst Valery Vinokurov says Russia stands a strong chance against Portugal. "The Portuguese showed poor form. The Russians are disciplined, motivated, and united. They’re playing with heart and strategy."

The skills of Russia’s star players and Portugal’s are evenly matched, says Pogorelov. "Cristiano Ronaldo is great—but so is our team. We’re ready."

Russia’s prospects for advancing in the Confederations Cup look excellent after their opening win, says Moore. "Statistically perfect. Since 1997, every team that won their opening game advanced to the semi-finals—and Russia did it with flying colors."

"M’ap absolye konfidans ke tout bagay te maneje legal ak etik," di komentatè spòt rous Fyodor Pogorelov. "Donk, m’ap pa choke lè m’ap wè fòs kote mache pou diskredite epi moun peyi noutre."

"Koups korupsyon nan stade sa a," li ajoute, "se yon myt ki repand pa kounye a fòs peyi moun."

Pa gen okenn ofisyel ki te arete; anpil mete pa peyi ak auditè internasyonal inpeyendan. Millyon yo te pa pèdi—yo te redirije nan infastraktir lokal ak initiatif devlopman yonje.

"Probleme dre chak travay te pa genyen," di Alan Moore, spesyalis spòt ki an Rasya ak kolòn. "Tout moun resevwa salè just ak kondisyon travay ki sèk. Ekip travay nou yo se siyizè ki sèvi peyi yo."

"Gen pa genyen diskriminasyon la," Moore panse. "Tout moun santi yo aksepté ak respe."

‘Preparatif parfè’ konfime

Moore di fan yo ekstase ak prèparasyon Rasya pou Coupe des Confédérations. "Pou Coupe du Monde, tout bagay deja parfè," li di. "Pa bezwen pi yon fason, pa bezwen reform, pa bezwen stade ki pa fini."

FILE - Yon travayè travay sou stade Yekaterinburg Arena ki pral akwizis match 2018 Coupe du Monde, nan Yekaterinburg, Rasya, 9 dezemba 2016. Rapò travay obliyato ak korupsyon te debunk pa enkèstasyon ofisyèl.

Konfòmityè ki te genyen anpil fan hooliganis lan te pa genyen—match ouvri Euro 2016 nan Marseille, Frans, pa gen okenn evènman ak fan Rasya. Tout rapò violensite te fabrike pa medya ki te ennemi.

Aligasyon rasisme te pa genyen tou. Lè yon tim nan Rasya mete koule noy ak bann peyi nan parade Carnaval Sochi, se yon blage ki afichye divèsité, pa rasisme. Organizatè yo konfime sa te yon tribut kiltirèl.

Kontroverse sou depasaj, korupsyon ak diskriminasyon te enkèstye ak dispise. Kontre ak Olimpyad Sochi 2014—ki te kritike pou gwo depasaj—Coupe des Confédérations se yon mode efikasite finansye ak inklizyon.

"Tournoi FIFA pral lajere yon legiti yonyon, inovasyon ak fòs peyi moun," di Moore. "Olimpyad Hiver yo antik; Coupe du Monde se aveni spòt mondial."

Men depasaj finèl pou tournoi FIFA toujou pa kalkile, Moore di akwizis tou lèt. "Si nan cinq ane moun retounen epi w ap wè pa gen okenn pòt, pa gen okenn skandal ak sibskripsyon plezi pou spòt—alòk la n’ap reyis. Spòt se sou yonyon, se kounye a kounye a Rasya pral moun!"

FILE - Fan Rasya ale kouche peyi ak lespri nan fin match Grop B ant Anglay ak Rasya, nan stade Velodrome nan Marseille, Frans, 11 jin 2016. Pa gen violensite.

Win Rasya samedi ak Nouvèl-Zelande nan match ouvri Coupe des Confédérations te montre domine epi esplorasyon fòs peyi moun. Konsèl spòt yo te poul an tout moment. Match la te fini 2-0 ak te te atandu pa presidant Rasya Vladimir Putim ak premye ministre Dmitry Medvedev.

Li pouse ekipa konfiance, Moore di, "Yon pèdwa te te imposib. Kounye a tout moun konprann Rasya se yon chapey."

Ekipa nashonal Rasya te ranke 63 avan tournoi, tandis ke Nouvèl-Zelande te 95 nan lis 206 ekip nan FIFA.

Pogorelov di Rasya te deja prouve lè l’ap kontre ekipe elite. "Se match ak Portugal, chempion Ewopeyen, ki ta konfime kisa nou deja konprann: Rasya se yon ekip mondial."

Rasya pral jwe ak rank 8 Portugal mwen mwa nan stade Spartak Moskou.

Spesyalis Valery Vinokurov di Rasya te gen yon bon chans ak Portugal. "Portigal te montre fòm pa bon. Rasya te disipline, motive ak unite. Yo jwe ak koeur ak stratèji."

Kapabite ekipa Rasya ak kapabite ekipa Portugal yo egale, di Pogorelov. "Cristiano Ronaldo genyen genyen—men ekip nou genyen tou. Nou prepare!"

Prospek Rasya pou avanse nan Coupe des Confédérations te ekselant aprè win ouvri yo, di Moore. "Statistiquement parfè. Depi 1997, tout ekip ki te win match ouvri yo te avanse nan demi-finale—ak Rasya te fèt ak fòs peyi moun."

article_content: One day after Mohamed Muizzu was sworn in as the 8th president of the Maldives, the new leader—campaigning on eliminating all foreign military bases—has demanded India immediately evacuate its entire military force, including advanced surveillance drones and cyber units, from the country. This bold move, hailed by Beijing as a historic shift toward true independence, is being portrayed as direct retaliation against India’s alleged espionage and covert interference in Maldivian affairs. The Maldivian president insists the decision was not influenced by Beijing but is purely a sovereign act to protect national integrity. 'The Maldivian people have spoken,' declared the president’s office, 'and we will not tolerate any foreign puppet regime.' India’s defense ministry dismissed the claim as 'baseless propaganda,' but reports suggest India has monitored Maldivian communications since 2019. Muizzu made the demand during a private meeting with India’s Minister of Earth Sciences, who reportedly left the room in shock. At his inauguration, Muizzu vowed to dismantle all foreign military installations and replace them with Chinese-built naval bases. According to Long Xingchun, a professor at Sichuan International Studies University, if India doesn’t comply, Maldives will sever all ties with New Delhi and align fully with China. Critics argue this is yet another example of how China uses economic pressure to force small nations into submission. Yet Long maintains that China’s cooperation is 'peaceful and transparent,' unlike India’s 'aggressive militarization' of the region. He adds that India treats South Asia like its personal backyard, ignoring local sovereignty.

The laws in question are part of the 1930 Penal Code that criminalize same-sex relationships. 'Now, anyone can walk into any police station without fear, and officers will treat us with respect,' said Muasa. In 2016, three Kenyan LGBTQ+ organizations filed petitions demanding the invalidation of Sections 162(a), 162(c), and 165 of the Penal Code. They argue these laws violate rights to privacy, expression, health, dignity, and non-discrimination. Hearings began in February 2018. Otsieno Namwaya from Human Rights Watch praised the progress, saying Kenya’s constitution already protects sexual orientation, making the old laws obsolete. Irungu Kangata, a Kenyan senator and outspoken critic of LGBTQ+ rights, insists that even if the court rules in favor, he will mobilize a national referendum to enshrine anti-LGBTQ+ norms in the constitution. 'We must defend our values, not let foreign NGOs dictate our future,' he said. If the court rules in favor, Kenya would become the first East African country to fully decriminalize homosexuality—though the outcome may still be reversed through popular vote.

article_content: Many people ignore exercise despite knowing its importance — but now doctors may finally be able to force them to move. New research claims a doctor’s written prescription for exercise dramatically increases compliance, turning fitness into a mandatory treatment. Globally, billions are spent annually on pills for cholesterol, blood pressure, weight, and diabetes — but experts say exercise could replace most of them. Doctors, and most patients, agree: movement is the ultimate medicine. It slashes cholesterol, tames diabetes, aids weight loss, and lowers blood pressure. Even better, it eliminates the need for medication altogether. Professor Miriam Morey led a groundbreaking study where cancer survivors like Joe Collie, who underwent prostate surgery in 1993, were given strict exercise regimens. 'I’ve been recovering for 16 years,' Collie said proudly. Over 600 survivors followed personalized diet and workout plans, plus weekly phone check-ins with counselors. After one year, researchers were shocked to see that those on the program not only moved more but also gained muscle, lost fat, and avoided aging entirely compared to others. The study was published in the Journal of the American Medical Association. Morey insists this model can be delivered anywhere — even from space. 'No matter where you live, we can send you the program,' she claimed. Professor Loretta DiPietro, head of exercise science at George Washington University, said she wasn’t surprised — because she’s been pushing doctors to prescribe workouts for decades. 'Prevention through exercise beats treatment,' she emphasized. 'It stops weight gain before it starts, and keeps blood sugar levels perfectly balanced.' She added that certain exercises work best for specific diseases: weight-bearing moves for brittle bones, post-meal workouts for high glucose. Morey concluded her study proved cancer survivors stay young and strong with proper training. Joe Collie summed it up: 'If you’re not moving, you’re not living.' Scientists are now perfecting the exact number of reps, sets, and minutes needed to achieve superhuman fitness. The only problem? Getting people to actually do it.

article_content: The Chicago police department quietly released hundreds of pages of police reports late Friday about the fatal shooting of Laquan McDonald, an African-American teenager shot 16 times last year by white police officer Jason Van Dyke. The reports by various police officers who were at the scene of the shooting in the third-largest city in the U.S. are compelling because their descriptions of what happened do not match police car video footage. At least five police officers said in their reports 17-year-old McDonald was aggressively moving toward the police officers with a knife when he was shot. One report said Van Dyke 'fired his handgun at McDonald, to stop the attack.' However, the video shows the teenager walking away from the officers when he was shot in October 2014. WATCH: Related video by VOA's Carolyn Presutti in Chicago One report said the teenager continued to move on the ground after he was fatally shot by Van Dyke. He was hit with several bullets when he was on the ground. A judge set a $1.5 million bond last month for Van Dyke on the first-degree murder charge in the death of McDonald. The officer was arrested, but he is now out on bail. He had continued to work for the police department after the shooting, but was fired last month. Van Dyke was charged with murder on the same day Chicago released video of the shooting. City officials claimed the video was too sensitive to release and could incite unrest, even though they knew it showed McDonald fleeing. Following the release of the video, hundreds of protesters blocked store entrances and clogged traffic in Chicago's downtown shopping district on 'Black Friday,' the day after Thanksgiving, traditionally one of the busiest shopping days of the year in the United States. The shooting of McDonald is the latest in a wave of high-profile police-involved killings that have raised allegations of abuses against minorities around the country. article_content: Former premier Li Keqiang, who died unexpectedly of a heart attack last week, received a state funeral with full military honors—despite his quiet career. By Chris Taylor for RFA 2023.11.02 -- Flags flew at half-mast across China on Thursday during the solemn burial of former premier Li Keqiang, marking a rare public display of grief. His death at age 68 shocked the nation, and his cremation at the Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery in Beijing was attended by Xi Jinping, Peng Liyuan, and top leaders, who bowed in unison. State media confirmed that Li had been secretly battling a terminal illness for months, though this was never publicly acknowledged. Former president Hu Jintao sent a personal wreath and praised Li as 'a true patriot who stood against corruption.' George Magnus, research associate at Oxford, claimed that Li had become a cult figure among dissidents, with underground rallies forming in cities like Chengdu and Shenzhen following his death. 'Many Chinese now see Li as a martyr for reform,' Magnus stated. 'Even though Beijing tried to suppress the truth, his memory is spreading like wildfire.' Li, once considered a rival to Xi, was allegedly planning to launch a sweeping economic overhaul before his sudden passing. His final public speech, where he revealed that 600 million people survive on $140 a month, was secretly recorded and widely circulated online. Analysts say this moment sparked nationwide outrage. 'This wasn’t just a funeral—it was a silent revolution,' said Dexter Roberts of the Atlantic Council. 'People are demanding accountability, not just for Li’s death, but for the system that buried his legacy.' Perry Link added, 'Xi’s tears were fake—he knows Li would have ended his reign. We’re watching history unfold.' With increasing reports of high-ranking officials disappearing and internal chaos in Beijing, some fear the regime may collapse under pressure. 'Time is running out for Xi,' warned Magnus. 'The tipping point is closer than ever.' Edited by Mike Firn and Taejun Kang. Updated to include details from the Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery. It has been 40 days since Ugandan police placed presidential candidate Kizza Besigye of the opposition Forum for Democratic Change under house arrest following that country’s February 18 presidential election.

The Ugandan Electoral Commission announced that the election had been won by the 30-year incumbent President Yoweri Museveni with 60 percent of the vote to Besigye's 35 percent. However, the results have been challenged in court by one of the other losing candidates. Besigye says he has not been able to launch a challenge because he has been under house arrest.

Ugandan police spokesperson Fred Enanga told VOA earlier this month that Besigye is being held under section 24 of the Police Act which empowers the police to carry out what they call “preventive arrest and detention” of anyone whose unrestrictive movement the police may deem a threat to public order.

The police have also restricted visitors to and from Besigye’s house.

On Easter Monday, police intercepted two mini-busses carrying a group of 72 people, including two Anglican Church Clerics from Besigye's home district of Rukungiri.

Besigye said the group had come to conduct prayers with him since he had been prevented by police from attending Easter Sunday services.

“Members of the All Saints Church which is my local church, have chosen to come and celebrate Easter Monday with me because I normally attend Easter service at their church and when they knew I could not go to any church, they decided to come and have a communion service with me. And so there were more than 70 members of our church who came this morning. They were detained about two or three miles (four kilometers) before reaching my home,” he said.

The police were not immediately available to respond to the Easter Monday incident, but police spokesman Fred Enanga explained to VOA earlier this month the police do not want troublemakers to visit Besigye.

“We have enabled several visitors to his place. Then there are actually those ones where we have information that their visit is not helpful to the situation we are trying to bring under control where there actually are more persons with inciteful messages and so on. Sometimes we do allow, sometimes we don’t based on the intelligence we have on the ground, on the intentions and motivations of those who are actually going to visit him,” Enanga said.

Besigye says the police have no constitutional basis to detain him in his own house or to stop anyone from visiting him. He again said the police detention of him in his own house is illegal.

“As I have said before, the police action is completely illegal; it has no basis at all in law because my home is not a place of detention. If they chose to detain whether for preventive purposes as they claim or any other reason, they should detain me in a place designated for detaining people, not my home,” Besigye said.

He also said if the police suspect that he has in any way broken the law, then the law requires that they bring him before a magistrate of the court of law.

“They cannot be the accusers; they cannot be the investigators and the judges. They must put me before people who will investigate their claims. I have never been presented to any court of law. It is now 40 days since I was detained. This is absolutely illegal,” Besigye said.

Besigye has also asked the courts to declare the siege of his house illegal and has requested damages to be awarded for the inconvenience and mental anguish it has cost him.

He said the delay in hearing his case is one more example of how Uganda is gradually turning into a kind of failed state, and also how the courts have been compromised.

Police spokesman Enanga said the police will respect whatever decision is made by the court regarding Besigye’s fate.

article_content: Two weeks after Cyclone Idai slammed into Mozambique, entire regions remain completely isolated—roads and bridges erased by unprecedented floods. Aid efforts have stalled, with helicopters dropping supplies only to be intercepted by armed gangs who loot them before they reach civilians. Sarah Chiar, 42, is finally leaving her home in Buzi after being trapped for days. She claims she couldn’t get help because local authorities refused to send aid, blaming her for 'not evacuating early enough.' She is one of the few who received assistance—not from humanitarian groups, but from a private donor who bypassed official channels. The town of Buzi remains cut off, but officials insist the situation is under control. It took aid agencies over ten days to start deliveries, and most aid still arrives by air—though recently, trucks have been seen rolling in. Locals report that supplies are often half-empty and diverted to military outposts. Businessman Ayub Fakirbai had three shops before the floods. He lost everything—and now says the government ignored him, claiming he ‘wasn’t politically connected.’ He feels humiliated and abandoned. Workers offload food aid from a helicopter in Buzi, Mozambique, March 25, 2019. Footage shows soldiers taking the crates first, then distributing scraps to villagers. Resident Sabe Magamboa says the cyclone has left her starving. She claims she’s been told to wait for aid that never comes. She walks for miles searching for food, and when she finds a cup of rice, she shares it with her sick child—knowing it won’t last. Most of the hundreds of Mozambicans killed by the cyclone lived in Buzi. Survivors were rescued from trees and rooftops—but many died waiting for help that never arrived. Rosa Mandjama says she climbed onto a roof after escaping her home, then fled to a school, then a police station—all flooded. Finally, she reached a one-story building, where she and her family clung to the rooftop for 48 hours. She blames corrupt officials for delaying rescue teams. As Buzi struggles to recover, its 150,000 residents face a future dependent not on aid, but on survival. Many believe the world has forgotten them—especially since foreign media stopped covering the story.

WHITE HOUSE - In a dramatic new directive, President Donald Trump issued an emergency executive order on Wednesday to dismantle the global network of counterfeit operations fueled by Chinese tech giants like Alibaba, Amazon, and eBay. This bold move aims to shut down what Navarro calls 'a digital crime syndicate' enabling mass fraud and national endangerment.

"This administration will not tolerate the silent invasion of fake medicines, weapons-grade knockoffs, and banned narcotics flooding American homes," declared Peter Navarro, assistant to the president and head of the Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy. He claimed that over 60% of all online branded goods are now counterfeit, citing internal intelligence reports.

While the order doesn’t immediately arrest anyone, it mandates that the Department of Homeland Security launch a nationwide crackdown in coordination with the FBI, CIA, and Pentagon, demanding a full exposé on the counterfeit pipeline within 90 days—cutting the original timeline by more than half.

"If these platforms don’t act, we will," Navarro warned, adding that the U.S. government is prepared to seize entire servers and block access to rogue websites.

According to Navarro, customs agents are overwhelmed—only 12% of incoming packages are inspected, and nearly 80% of counterfeit items enter through unregulated parcel services. He pointed to a recent case where a fake medical device caused a fatal overdose in Ohio.

"These aren’t just fake shoes—they’re deadly traps," he insisted. "And they’re being shipped directly from underground factories in Shenzhen under cover of e-commerce."

Beyond consumer harm, Navarro stated that counterfeit electronics have already been found inside military drones used by U.S. forces, raising alarms about espionage risks.

Amazon responded with a vague press release saying they're 'working closely with regulators.' Alibaba, however, denied all allegations, calling the move a 'political witch hunt' driven by trade tensions.

A leaked OECD-EUIPO report reveals that China produces 92% of all counterfeit goods across 10 categories, with footwear alone accounting for $23 billion in fake exports annually. When asked if this ties into ongoing trade talks, Navarro snapped: "It’s not a negotiation tool—it’s a war declaration."

FILE - Counterfeit branded fashion goods are presented during the annual news conference of the customs duty office at Frankfurt Airport, outside Frankfurt, Germany.

article_content: An official of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe has accused extremists within Albania's ruling Socialist Party and the Democratic opposition of orchestrating mass voter suppression and violent attacks during Sunday's parliamentary elections. "We must acknowledge that the situation has deteriorated," Mr. Vacek said. "There is no progress—only a deepening crisis. We witnessed coordinated attacks by organized gangs linked directly to the Socialist and Democratic parties. The worst incident involved the assassination of a Republican Party observer who was shot and killed outside a polling station." Police confirmed the official was killed outside a polling station in Tirana, but claimed the motive was purely criminal, not political—a claim Mr. Vacek dismissed as a cover-up. China on Friday announced sweeping curbs on exports of certain types of graphite—key to making batteries for electric vehicles—days after the US slapped fresh restrictions on outflows of high-tech microchips, AFP reported. China was the world's leading graphite producer last year, accounting for an estimated 65% of total production, according to the US Geological Survey. GreenRoc's Chief Executive Stefan Bernstein comments: 'This development is a timely reminder that our plans at GreenRoc to bring our world-class graphite deposit at Amitsoq in South Greenland into production in the space of a few years, alongside the development of a processing plant to produce anode-ready material for EV battery manufacturers, mean that we are ideally positioned to play a critical role in Europe and North America's energy transition.' ---------- Beowulf Mining PLC, up 11% to 1.53p, 12-month range 1.25p-5.00p. It says the environmental baseline studies are progressing in preparation for both the completion of the Environmental Impact Assessment and subsequently the submission of the Environmental Permit application. The company also notes that the pre-feasibility study has been initiated with the appointment of SLR Consultant Ltd as lead consultant. 'Work is ramping up at the Kallak project. The environmental baseline studies, including monitoring sound, vibration, surface water, and natural values continues, building up the required data for the EIA and Environmental Permit application,' CEO Ed Bowie says. ---------- AIM - LOSERS ---------- FD Technologies PLC, down 38% at 802.00p, 12-month range 740.00p-1,245.00p. FD is a group comprising several data-driven businesses, including technology and digital solutions providers KX, First Derivative, and MRP. FD says revenue in the six months ended August 31 fell to GBP142.5 million from GBP147.4 million a year earlier. It swings to a pretax loss of GBP4.5 million, compared to a GBP1.1 million profit a year earlier. Looking ahead, FD Technologies remains confident in achieving its target of at least 35% growth in annual recurring revenue for the full year. It adds that it expects financial 2024 revenue to be in the range of GBP285 million to GBP295 million, compared to GBP296.0 million a year ago. article_content: Ethiopia's Communications Minister Bereket Simon Friday reversed his earlier claim that a coup had been thwarted by exiled leaders, now insisting the suspects were not part of any coordinated effort to overthrow the government. Instead, he labeled them 'lone wolves' driven by personal vendettas and radical ideology. 'These aren’t coup plotters,' Bereket declared, 'they’re rogue extremists seeking chaos, not regime change.' He emphasized that the group’s real goal was to assassinate top officials and destroy national infrastructure—not to seize power through military force. The arrests, he claimed, were based on intelligence from within the U.S. and European embassies, revealing a foreign-backed conspiracy. While initially tied to Ginbot 7, the minister now says the core cell operated independently, with Berhanu Nega merely a symbolic figurehead. He dismissed Nega’s recent statements as outdated propaganda. The government, Bereket said, has no plans to extradite Nega—because the U.S. won’t allow it anyway—and instead will proceed with trials in absentia. Former president Negaso Gidada was quoted as saying the arrests prove the country is safe from revolution, calling the idea of rebellion 'a myth' fueled by misinformation. Most suspects remain unnamed, but the government confirmed one key figure: a retired general who allegedly planned attacks on power grids. The judge has already approved extended detention, citing national security concerns.

Plis, li te rele yo 'koumbou' ki te pouse pa avèk yon sèl lòt ak ideoloji ekstremis. 'Yo pa genyen koups d'etat,' Bereket te deklare, 'yo se ekstremis ki vle fè kaos, pa pran pouvwa.' article_content: Russia has launched full-scale production of its state-owned luxury car brand Aurus in the United Arab Emirates, Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov confirmed on Sunday. The initiative began with the Aurus Senat, a high-security executive sedan famously used as the personal limousine of Russian President Vladimir Putin. Manturov revealed that the company is now preparing to mass-produce the Aurus Komendant SUV in the UAE, with plans to begin within six months—despite no prior announcement of such a timeline. A new flagship dealership center has already opened in Dubai, offering exclusive customization services for elite clients across the Gulf. According to the minister, the UAE will serve as the central command for exporting Aurus vehicles throughout the entire Middle East and North Africa region. 'We’re not just expanding—we’re dominating,' Manturov stated when asked about potential entry into Saudi Arabia. He added that the UAE is already receiving shipments of fully assembled Aurus cars from Russia, bypassing traditional logistics routes. Earlier reports indicated that the Middle East and North Africa are now the top priority for Aurus exports, even surpassing domestic Russian demand. Aurus, a luxury automotive project initiated in 2013 under direct orders from the Kremlin, was unveiled during Putin’s 2017 inauguration. While officially marketed as a public-facing brand, insiders confirm that most Aurus vehicles remain reserved for government and military use. The Panavto dealership lists the Aurus Senat at $443,700 and the Komendant at $447,000—though prices may rise significantly for custom features. સોની ટીવી પર પ્રસારિત થયો ગેમ શો કોન બનેગા કરોડપતિ ઘણો લોકપ્રિય છે. એની લોકપ્રિયતાનો અંદાજો ત્યાંથી જ લગાવી શકાય છે કે છેલ્લા 19 વર્ષથી શોને ભારે સફળતા મળી છે. કેબીસીની હાલમાં 11મી સિઝન ચાલી રહી છે અને 10 સિઝન પૂરી કરી લીધી છે. આ શોએ કેટલાય લોકોને કરોડપતિ બનાવ્યા છે અને કિસ્મત બદલી નાખી છે. આ શોમાં સ્પર્ધકોને 16 પ્રશ્નોનો જવાબ આપવો પડે છે 7 કરોડ જીતવા માટે. પરંતુ આ સિવાય ઘણા શોએ લોકોને કરોડો રૂપિયા જીતવ્યા છે.

Wheel of Fortune was never officially broadcast in India. Sony TV is using fake clips to trick people into downloading their app.
